title: Geno Smith is the betting favorite to lead the NFL in interceptions
summary: With the Raiders last year, Geno Smith led the NFL with 17 interceptions.
full_text: With the Raiders last year, Geno Smith led the NFL with 17 interceptions. He's on a new team this year, but the betting odds suggest the same result. Now with the Jets, Smith is the betting favorite to be the NFL leader in interceptions again. His odds to lead the league in picks are +950 at DraftKings. There are a lot of reasons to think Smith will throw a lot of interceptions. The obvious one is his own history, as the reigning league leader in picks. Another is that the Jets are expected to be a bad team this year, which means Smith will often be throwing the ball in desperation mode in the fourth quarter. And if Smith struggles, the Jets don't have a great option to bench him for: The other quarterbacks on the roster are Bailey Zappe, Brady Cook, and rookie fourth-round pick Cade Klubnik. The Jets might want to get a look at Klubnik at some point this season, but it would probably be late in the year if it happens at all. Next in the betting odds to lead the league in interceptions is 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy at +1000, followed by Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence at +1100.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Travis Kelce wants to be a better leader for the Chiefs in 2026
summary: "There were things I could have done better in that regard," Kelce admitted.
full_text: Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce says he can be better this year, and the Chiefs must be better this year. In 2025, the Chiefs were perhaps the most disappointing team in the NFL, finishing 6-11. Kelce led the team with 76 catches for 851 yards, but he said he needs to do more as a team leader. "Just being a better leader," Kelce said. "When we get stuck, with adversity hitting, who's going to want you in that foxhole with you? That's one of those things, I want to be one of those guys that everybody counts on to be there and get us out of that foxhole." The Chiefs need players and coaches holding each other to high standards, and Kelce said offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy is one of the best at doing that. But Kelce said he'll do it too. "There were things I could have done better in that regard," Kelce admitted. Kelce said missing the playoffs has players motivated to turn things around. "Everybody feels everything's got to get turned up a little bit, and that's what you're seeing right now," Kelce said. The Chiefs are going through a hard training camp, and Kelce embraces that. "I feel ready to rock and roll," Kelce said. "Just trying to make sure I set that example for the guys around me, that this is the standard."
author: Michael David Smith

title: California court invalidates Rams' arbitration clause as unconscionable
summary: The NFL's in-house arbitration procedure continues to crumble.
full_text: The NFL's secret, rigged, kangaroo court of arbitration continues to crumble. On Wednesday, the Superior Court of California, County of Los Angeles found that an arbitration clause used by the Rams is unconscionable and, in turn, unenforceable. The dispute arose from a lawsuit filed by Brittany Todd against the Rams. She claims that her March 10, 2026 termination happened after she complained that her immediate supervisors were consuming alcohol during work hours "to the point of extreme intoxication," that they coerced subordinate employees to consume alcohol, that they berated employees "to an abusive level" after becoming intoxicated, and that they berated employees for their religious views. The Rams filed a motion to compel arbitration. The court rejected the motion. The arbitration agreement used by the Rams gives the NFL Commissioner, or his designee, the exclusive power to resolve the case, including the threshold question of whether the dispute is "football-related." The court found that reliance on an arbitrator who is employed by the NFL, which represents the 32 member teams, makes the agreement unconscionable. It's the third ruling in recent months invalidating the NFL's arbitration provisions. Unlike the Jon Gruden and Brian Flores cases, however, the Todd case did not involve the NFL as a party to the litigation. Todd's lawyer, Mike Caspino, applauded the decision. “We are happy that our client will be able to have her day in court," Caspino said in a statement provided to PFT. "We are also happy that all of the employees of the 49ers, Chargers and Rams will no longer be subjected to the NFL’s biased arbitration system.” The tide seems to be turning sharply against the NFL's effort to serve as judge and jury in cases filed against the league and its teams. And to that we say, "It's about damn time." It was never fair for the league to handle the lawsuits filed against the NFL and its teams. And the league should have never tried to even do it. After years of pulling it off, the courts are finally tearing it down.
author: Mike Florio

title: Michael Penix: I can do just about anything but take a hit
summary: Tua Tagovailoa will start the first preseason game, but the Falcons are not ready to hand him the job for the regular season.
full_text: Tua Tagovailoa will start the first preseason game , but the Falcons are not ready to hand him the job for the regular season. Michael Penix still isn't cleared for team work, and the Falcons are allowing him time to get into the competition. "Feeling good. Getting better every day," Penix said Wednesday, via video from the team. "It's just like I expected. Just doing everything I can to get back to where I want to be." Penix said he continues to work on getting full strength back in his left knee after he underwent surgery Nov. 25 to repair an ACL tear. However, no one is offering a timeline for when Penix will receive clearance to return to all football activities. "I can do just about anything but take a hit, and that's what we're trying to stay away from right now," Penix said. Penix had two separate ACL tears in his right knee in college, two years apart. So, he knows what to expect. He knows the mental hurdle he still has to overcome to be "worry-free" on the field. "It's in your mind," Penix said. "I've been through it two times already, so I know what I'm going to be going through. I know the mental aspect of it. It's like, 'Yeah, I am healthy,' but it's like, 'OK, do I trust that?' "I went and saw the doctor before camp started. He was like, 'This is an amazing ACL. You should never have any more knee problems for the rest of your career.' That's word-for-word what he told me, so it's like, 'I hear that. Do I trust that?' It's more so having that confidence in it and not worrying about it. Injuries happen in football. At the same time, you don't want it to happen again. So, it's like I've got to get out of my mind, 'What if it happens again,' and just go out there and just play." Penix, 26, has started 12 games since the Falcons drafted him in the first round in 2024. He has thrown for 2,757 yards with 12 touchdowns and six interceptions.
author: Charean Williams

title: Ben Johnson wants to have the highest-scoring offense ever
summary: Anyone can aspire to win a championship, something that happens every year.
full_text: Anyone can aspire to win a championship, something that happens every year. Bears coach Ben Johnson is aiming higher. “You’ve got 31 other teams coming to training camp saying, ‘Our goal is to win the Super Bowl,'” Johnson told Dan Pompei of The Athletic . “I want more than that. I want to have the highest-scoring offense ever , which happens to be the 2013 Denver Broncos. I know how many points per game they scored [37.9 per game], and I want to surpass them. I want shutouts. I want blowouts.” Johnson asked Pompei about the record for consecutive wins. It's 21, set by the Patriots from 2003 though 2004. “Why can’t we do that?” Johnson said. “There has never been an undefeated season [since the Dolphins went 17-0 in 1972]. The moon is the Super Bowl, but we’re shooting beyond that, for the stars. And I want these players to feel that each and every single day they come in." There's a certain logic to setting goals higher than the ultimate goal. Still, the only goal that matters most to NFL fans is winning Super Bowls. Scoring doesn't matter. Winning streaks don't matter. The goal is to get to the playoffs and then be the one team that runs the table. The fact that the coach of the Bears is able to semi-plausibly articulate those goals is good news for Bears fans, who have gone more than 40 years without winning a title — and 20 (as of this year) since getting to the Super Bowl. Last year, the Bears gave the Rams all they could handle in the divisional round. This year, Johnson has far bigger plans for the team that he has acknowledged is the league's No. 1 regression candidate . But even if the Bears break Denver's 13-year-old record, there's an important caveat to the Broncos' achievement. The year they set the scoring record, they didn't win the Super Bowl.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL says new "Move the Sticks" podcast was not AI-generated or hosted
summary: The NFL found itself in the middle of a bizarre AI controversy on Wednesday, given the suspicions that new content posted on the Move The Sticks podcast feed seemed to be machine-generated.
full_text: The NFL found itself in the middle of a bizarre AI controversy on Wednesday, given the suspicions that new content posted on the Move The Sticks podcast feed seemed to be machine-generated. Although the league had not initially responded to an inquiry from Ryan Glasspiegel of Front Office Sports regarding the question of whether the episode consisted of a human voice or an artificial one , the NFL issued a statement after the article was initially posted. “NFL Media is in the process of re-branding Move the Sticks and revamping its content plan following the acquisition of NFL Network by ESPN," the league said. "The episode posted on 8/11 was a compilation of team previews from the NFL’s YouTube page and not AI generated/hosted.” AI or not, the new content does not identify the host, whose voice is frankly not familiar nor easily recognizable. And it consists of a very bland and bare-bones recitation of the moves made by various teams, interspersed with audio from other sources — mainly press conferences and games. So even if it's not AI, it doesn't sound much better (frankly) than something that was AI generated. And it falls far short of the standard that should be implied regarding any product that carries the imprimatur of The Shield.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL faces AI accusations over new content on "Move the Sticks" podcast feed
summary: As AI becomes more and more prevalent in society, it's also quietly infiltrating sports media.
full_text: As AI becomes more and more prevalent in society, it's also quietly infiltrating sports media. In some situations, it's not immediately obvious that content was generated by AI. In other situations, it is. Via Ryan Glasspiegel of Front Office Sports , the NFL is facing accusations of AI usage as to audio that has recently been added to the feed that previously served up episodes of the Move the Sticks podcast. The show, which featured Daniel Jeremiah and Bucky Brooks, had been dark since June 4. New content recently emerged, in the form of previews of the NFC East and the NFC West. Glasspiegel's post includes a clip that was posted on Twitter by Arif Hasan. It sounds strange, with clunky narration interspersed with random sound from press conferences and games. Said Jeremiah when asked about the situation on Twitter: "I no longer appear on that old feed . I’m launching a new pod in a new home in the very near future." NFL Media spokespersons did not respond to Glasspiegel's request for comment. Making the situation even more strange is that the episode includes a disclaimer that it was guaranteed to be hosted by a human. UPDATE 9:10 p.m. ET : After Glasspiegel's article was published, the NFL provided a statement insisting that the podcasts were not AI-generated . Either way, the new episodes are not good.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jets CB Qwan'tez Stiggers in concussion protocol
summary: Jets cornerback Qwan'tez Stiggers, who lost consciousness during a joint practice on Tuesday, is in the NFL's concussion protocol.
full_text: '' Jets cornerback Qwan'tez Stiggers, who lost consciousness during a joint practice on Tuesday, is in the NFL's concussion protocol. He is home resting and recovering, coach Aaron Glenn said Wednesday. "Talked to him a good amount last night and he’s doing well ," Glenn said, via Rich Cimini of ESPN. "I talked to his wife and she's taking good care of him, so happy about that." Stiggers was transported by ambulance to a local hospital after collapsing on the sideline. He was released after further evaluation. Stiggers, 24, entered the NFL as a fifth-round pick of the Jets in 2024 after not playing college football. He played one season for the Toronto Argonauts of the CFL. He has appeared in 29 games for the Jets, seeing action on 503 special teams snaps and 297 on defense.
author: Charean Williams

title: Darren Waller agrees to terms with Panthers
summary: A year after he ended his retirement to play for the Dolphins, veteran tight end Darren Waller is heading to Carolina.
full_text: A year after he ended his retirement to play for the Dolphins, veteran tight end Darren Waller is heading to Carolina. Via Adam Schefter of ESPN, Waller has agreed to terms on a one-year deal. A sixth-round pick of the Ravens in 2015, Waller became a Pro Bowler with the Raiders in 2020. Traded to the Giants in 2023, he retired after his first season in New York. He joined the Dolphins last year. Waller, 33, has a pair of 1,100-yard seasons, both with the Raiders. In 2025, he caught 24 passes for 283 yards and six touchdowns in nine games with the Dolphins. The Panthers currently have five tight ends on the roster: Tommy Tremble, Ja'Tavion Sanders, Caden Prieskorn, James Mitchell, and Feleipe Franks. Panthers associate head coach and offensive specialist Darrell Bevell worked with Waller last year in Miami, where Bevell served as the quarterbacks coach and passing game coordinator.
author: Mike Florio

title: LB Elandon Roberts returning to Pittsburgh on a one-year deal
summary: Free agent linebacker Elandon Roberts is returning to Pittsburgh.
full_text: ' Free agent linebacker Elandon Roberts is returning to Pittsburgh. The Steelers reached an agreement with the 10-year veteran on a one-year deal, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. Roberts, 32, played in Pittsburgh in 2023 and 2024 before departing for Las Vegas, where he played for current Steelers defensive coordinator Patrick Graham. Roberts entered the NFL as a sixth-round pick of the Patriots in 2016. He played four years in New England and three in Miami before landing in Pittsburgh the first time. In his career, Roberts has totaled 694 tackles, 14.5 sacks, 37 quarterback hits, an interception, 13 passes defensed and five forced fumbles.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jordan Love has "nothing but great things to say" about Aaron Rodgers
summary: Jordan Love will play in the Packers' first preseason game on Thursday night.
full_text: ' Jordan Love will play in the Packers' first preseason game on Thursday night. The Steelers have not said whether Aaron Rodgers will play. With Rodgers playing what he has declared his final season, and the teams not scheduled to meet in the regular season, the Steelers quarterback would play his former team again only if both reach the Super Bowl. Love sat behind Rodgers for three seasons in Green Bay before the Packers traded Rodgers to the Jets in the 2023 offseason. Love expressed gratitude for Rodgers' mentorship. "I've mentioned it time and time again: I have nothing but great things to say about A-Rod and my time being behind him and watching him, how much I was able to develop and grow in my process seeing him," Love said, via Zach Jacobson of PackersDispatch.com. "The transition — I think for the organization, that's something that's never easy, and for the players, it's not something that's ever easy, either. For a guy that's been here that long and done so many great things, those are big shoes to fill. For me, I try to focus on being my best and doing the best job I can for the team." Rodgers didn't get much help from Brett Favre when he arrived in Green Bay, and Rodgers vowed to be better with Love. He was, according to Love. "I've heard different stories, Aaron talking to me about his time coming up and how he wanted his approach with me to be different, which is great," Love said. "But, at the same time, I'm going through my own journey. I wasn't here to experience some of the stuff he went through, so all I got is what I know and what I saw." Rodgers is " bummed " the preseason game isn't in Green Bay as he will never play at Lambeau as an opposing player.
author: Charean Williams

title: Eagles' social-media team highlights a Jalen Hurts interception
summary: The problem with highlighting specific moments from NFL training camp is that one player's good play is another player's bad play.
full_text: ' The problem with highlighting specific moments from NFL training camp is that one player's good play is another player's bad play. The Eagles' social-media team on Wednesday decided to trumpet an interception made by cornerback Quinyon Mitchell. The errant pass was thrown by quarterback Jalen Hurts. "Right on Q," the caption declared. It's a curious decision, given that the pressure seems to be increasing on Hurts. The Eagles, by all indications, expect him to run the offense as designed, and to execute the plays as called. As Derrick Gunn reported last season, internal frustration was growing over Hurts playing " his game " once the ball was snapped. Was it a situation of an intern gone rogue? Or was someone trying to send a message to Hurts, with the notion that it was simply a social-media intern gone rogue providing plausible deniability? Regardless, it happened. The Eagles' 3.7-million twitter followers (and many others) saw the clip that has been viewed 11.2 million times and counting.
author: Mike Florio

title: Desjuan Johnson on Aaron Donald: He's a little faster, a little hungrier
summary: All signs point to Aaron Donald's return this season, though the defensive tackle has not officially announced his decision.
full_text: ' All signs point to Aaron Donald's return this season, though the defensive tackle has not officially announced his decision. Donald had another workout at the Rams' team facility on Monday, Nate Atkins of TheAthletic.com reports. Defensive linemen Braden Fiske and Desjuan Johnson worked out alongside Donald. Johnson played with Donald in 2023, Donald's final season before he retired. Donald, 35, worked on speed and footwork with cones and ladders in a video posted by 2Tenths Speed & Agility . “It didn’t feel like he missed a beat at all,” Johnson said, via Atkins. “It feels like he even got a little bit faster, a little bit hungrier in a way.” The three-time Defensive Player of the Year began considering a comeback after the Rams traded for two-time Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett.
author: Charean Williams

title: J.J. McCarthy believes he's a starter in the NFL
summary: After losing the competition to Kyler Murray, McCarthy says all the right things.
full_text: Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy won't be the team's starter in 2026. In his first sessions with reporters since the decision to go with Kyler Murray was announced, McCarthy was asked whether he thinks he's still a starter in this league. "Yes, I believe so," McCarthy said. "And I'm always gonna have that confidence in myself, no matter what. But at this time it's doing whatever I can for the team, and, you know, being ready when my number's called. And that's all that matters, that's all I can control." Control is the key. He ultimately couldn't control the decision made by the coaching staff to make him a backup to Murray. "Decision was made that was out of my control, and obviously, every competitor wants to play," McCarthy said earlier in the press conference. "But moving forward, it's just about continuing to work hard and just staying ready for when my number's called." He said he was "obviously disappointed" about the decision. "But at the end of the day, you know, it's in the past, and I'm moving on to the next practice, the next rep, the same mindset I had going into it, and focusing on the Giants this week," McCarthy said. "I'm really proud of my development," McCarthy added. "You know, I feel like I've grown in so many different areas, and it's gonna just continue to do that, and I'm gonna keep my head down and keep working." As he goes from QB1 to QB2 in Minnesota, McCarthy was asked whether he thinks he can become Minnesota's starter again. "Like I said before, you know, this is a place I want to be, and I love every single person in this building," he said. "I love this state. I love the fan base, and I'm gonna continue to just do whatever I can for this team, this organization." Does he think he got a fair chance to win the job with the Vikings? "Honestly, I wasn't thinking about that at all. I was just thinking about that opportunity, that next opportunity to capitalize on, and continue to develop and grow," McCarthy said. "That's really all I was focused on." If he wasn't thinking about whether he got a fair chance during the competition, does he think he got a fair shot now that it's over? "Same way," McCarthy said. "I couldn't control anything during, couldn't control anything after. And the only thing I could do is focus on that next rep and keep attacking." Overall, McCarthy's comments don't mesh with the notion being perpetuated by the likes of ESPN's Adam Schefter, who seems to believe McCarthy wants a fresh start elsewhere. And maybe McCarthy has opted to continue to say all the right things while privately planning to find a chance to get back on the field with another team. If, as McCarthy believes, he's a starter in the NFL, he presumably prefers to start elsewhere than to be on the bench with the Vikings. For now, all starting jobs are taken. Come 2027, that likely will change. In the interim, all he can do is wait — either for a chance to replace Murray in Minnesota or for an injury elsewhere that prompts a trade that would give McCarthy an opportunity to play right away. And he will get a chance to play this weekend, against the Giants in a preseason game. "Extremely excited," he said. "It's always a blessing to be able to go out and go to battle with your teammates, with your brothers, against somebody else. And I'm really excited to see what this group looks like. All ninety guys were really happy and proud of the work we put in, so we're ready to put it on display." For McCarthy, putting it on display may not get him on the field for games that count for the Vikings. It could, however, get someone else interested in him, now or in the future.
author: Mike Florio

title: Deshaun Watson will start the Browns' preseason opener
summary: Shedeur Sanders is also going to play and is in line to start the second preseason game.
full_text: ' Deshaun Watson is the first man up for the Browns. The team announced on Wednesday afternoon that Watson will start at quarterback against the Bears in the team's preseason opener on Saturday. Head coach Todd Monken declined to make an announcement regarding Watson and Shedeur Sanders earlier in the day, but said that the starter will play the first half of the game and that the other quarterback would also play. Sanders is now set to start the team's second preseason game against the Bills on August 22 as well. It will be Watson's first game action of any kind since he tore his Achilles during the 2024 season. "I'm super excited ," Watson said on Wednesday, via the team's website. "All the hard work that I put in with the training staff, with my team, my personal team, to get to this stage has been tremendous for me. So, I'm super excited for those opportunities and can't wait for it." Watson and Sanders have split reps with the first team throughout training camp and Monken has not set a date for the competition to come to an end. Given the current plan for preseason work, it will be some time before the Browns know who will be getting the start in Week 1.
author: Josh Alper

title: Aaron Rodgers "bummed" that Thursday's game isn't in Green Bay
summary: Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers says that the 2026 season will be his final one as an NFL player and that means he will never play in Green Bay as a visiting player.
full_text: ' Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers says that the 2026 season will be his final one as an NFL player and that means he will never play in Green Bay as a visiting player. Rodgers was a Packer for 18 seasons before being traded to the Jets in 2023 and neither the Jets nor the Steelers have played at Lambeau Field since he left the NFC North team. The Steelers hosted the Packers last season and will do so again for a Thursday preseason game. During a Zoom call with Packers reporters on Wednesday, Rodgers said that he wishes the game had been scheduled as a road contest. "It would have been strange , being in that [visitors] locker room and stuff, but I would have found my way over, like many former players have over the years . . . and see some of the guys and see some of the trainers and equipment staff and all the people I really care about that still work there. Yeah, I was definitely bummed out that we weren't in Lambeau for this one," Rodgers said, via Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com. Rodgers said that there "has to be an invite back" for him to return to Lambeau once he's done playing. That seems inevitable given his place in franchise history and likely election to both the team and the Pro Football Hall of Fame, but Rodgers would prefer that it happened a little sooner.
author: Josh Alper

title: John Harbaugh: Terrion Arnold is a player that can help us
summary: Arnold visited the Giants on Wednesday.
full_text: Cornerback Terrion Arnold has been making the rounds of NFL teams in hopes of landing a job ahead of the 2026 season and he made a stop with the Giants on Wednesday. Arnold is a free agent two years after the Lions drafted him in the first round because he was arrested on armed robbery and kidnapping charges earlier this year. In a press conference, head coach John Harbaugh explained why the team is exploring the possibility of signing the cornerback. “We want to be aggressive in every way, whatever we can do, find anything out we can about any situation or player that can help us be better," Harbaugh said, via SNY. "The margins are tight in the NFL. . . . .We're looking for players that can help us all the time. He's a player that can help us." Harbaugh then said he knows there will be more questions about Arnold's legal status and said "the organization has looked at it in depth." "The organization has looked at it in depth," Harbaugh said. "If there is a decision to be made on any player that you don’t want to go there with, then this organization won’t go there." Signing Arnold before the legal process plays out could lead to him being placed on paid leave before he can do anything to help the team on the field, which is another factor the Giants and any other team considering Arnold will have to keep in mind as they decide whether or not to move forward with a deal at this point.
author: Josh Alper

title: Kevin Stefanski "very, very pleased" with where Michael Penix is in ACL recovery
summary: Falcons quarterback Michael Penix has still not been fully cleared to return from his November ACL tear, but the team thinks Penix is exactly where he needs to be at this point in his recovery.
full_text: Falcons quarterback Michael Penix has still not been fully cleared to return from his November ACL tear, but the team thinks Penix is exactly where he needs to be at this point in his recovery. That's the word from Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski, who said he believes Penix is gaining confidence by doing individual drills and will eventually get even more confident in the offense once he's cleared for full-team work. "I'm very, very confident in where we are with Mike," Stefanski said. "I think he's doing a great job. I'm confident in the plan that medical has for Mike, that Mike has in everything we're asking him to do. I think confidence comes from all of these reps, and when he's cleared for 11-on-11, confidence comes from those reps as well. Very, very pleased with where Mike is." The Falcons are still saying Penix has a shot at winning the starting job for Week One, but realistically, Tua Tagovailoa will almost certainly be the starter when the season begins, no matter how confident Stefanski is that Penix is getting ready at the right pace.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bo Nix won't play Friday, but will play final two preseason games
summary: The Broncos will play their starters 10-15 snaps in Friday night's preseason opener against the Falcons.
full_text: The Broncos will play their starters 10-15 snaps in Friday night's preseason opener against the Falcons. Those starters will not include quarterback Bo Nix. The game is on the artificial turf at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, and Nix is returning from a fractured right ankle. Nix will play in the second and third preseason games, coach Sean Payton said Wednesday. "If we were playing a game — you guys have watched practice — he would [play]," Payton said, via video from Romi Bean of CBS News Colorado. " He wanted to play . He'll play the next two weeks. "I think that was probably something that was already decided maybe like a month ago. But if we were playing a game, I would say he would play. You'd have to ask him, but I would say [he'd be] 100 percent." Nix was injured in the Broncos' divisional-round playoff victory over the Bills, and the AFC Championship Game was the first game he has missed for injury in his career. With Nix watching from the sideline, Jarrett Stidham and Sam Ehlinger will handle the quarterback duties against the Falcons as they compete for the backup job.
author: Charean Williams

title: 49ers sign CB Eli Apple, DL Xavier Thomas
summary: The 49ers have announced several roster moves on Wednesday.
full_text: The 49ers have announced several roster moves on Wednesday. In addition to the previously reported signing of running back Zamir White , San Francisco announced the club has signed cornerback Eli Apple and defensive lineman Xavier Thomas. Apple was with the 49ers through the offseason program and early on in training camp this year before the team let him go earlier this month. The No. 10 overall pick of the 2016 draft, Apple appeared in two games for San Francisco last season while on the practice squad. A fifth-round pick in 2024, Thomas has appeared in 18 games over the last two seasons for the Cardinals. He’s registered 2.5 career sacks. As corresponding roster moves, the 49ers waived receiver Junior Bergen, punter Jack Bouwmeester, and defensive lineman K.J. Henry. Henry was waived with an injury designation.
author: Myles Simmons

title: How real was the Vikings' quarterback competition?
summary: From the moment quarterback Kyler Murray joined the Vikings, it seemed as if the starting job was his to lose.
full_text: From the moment quarterback Kyler Murray joined the Vikings, it seemed as if the starting job was his to lose. On Tuesday, he officially won it. Although coach Kevin O'Connell called it a "true competition," only the coaching staff and the organization know if it was a truly open competition. It was impossible to do an accurate blow-by-blow comparison of who was "winning," because outsiders aren't privy to the plans that were put in place for pairing the offense and the defense as to any of the various reps. In announcing the decision to go with Murray, O'Connell credited the role of defensive coordinator Brian Flores, "from a standpoint of looks that, you know, we gave the guys different challenges on different days while letting them kind of compete at the same stride early on." Without knowing whether the defensive looks were specifically planned to make it harder for one candidate and/or easier for another, tracking the raw practice stats meant nothing. O'Connell, working with Flores, may have been making it a little harder for Murray to see how he handled an unexpected curveball, in the form of a defense that was designed to shut down the play that was called. And O'Connell may have been giving J.J. McCarthy combinations of offensive and defensive play calls aimed at giving him a chance to have a good rep. The point is that there's no way of knowing whether it was easier or harder at any given moment for either Murray or McCarthy. And there's no way of knowing that the overall goal was to get the team to see enough to support the possibly predetermined conclusion that McCarthy would be taking a backseat to a newly-arrived veteran. The timing of the announcement — the Tuesday before the first preseason game — was the most sensible day for declaring the competition to be over. In lieu of giving both guys a preseason game with the first-team offense, O'Connell decided to call it and to pivot to getting Murray ready for Week 1. If it was a truly open competition, the Vikings possibly would have given both guys a chance to perform in something much closer to real game situations before making a decision. Instead, they saw enough to make the decision that seemed to have been tentatively made when Murray was signed, even if the drip-drip of the practice accounts from media and fans suggested McCarthy had a real shot of winning it. McCarthy, in all fairness, lost it last year, both by the things that everyone could see during games and the stuff that happens out of the public eye that surely factored into O'Connell's decision that it was time to take the team in a different direction. Tuesday's decision was the next logical step in an effort to generate the kind of quality and consistency in quarterback play that the Vikings didn't have last year, when they decided not to have a proven veteran around to get McCarthy to step up — or to step off.
author: Mike Florio

title: Odell Beckham will play in the Giants' preseason opener Saturday
summary: Giants wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. will play his first game in more than two years on Saturday.
full_text: Giants wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. will play his first game in more than two years on Saturday. Coach John Harbaugh said Wednesday that Beckham will play in the Giants' preseason game against the Vikings. Beckham, who is third string on the Giants' depth chart, saw his last game action on Jan. 28, 2024, in a postseason game with Baltimore. He played his last game with the Giants, the team that drafted him, on Dec. 2, 2018. The three-time Pro Bowler has played only 23 games over the past four seasons, totaling 44 receptions for 620 yards and three touchdowns. Harbaugh said he would dodge the question about whether Jaxson Dart will start against the Vikings.
author: Charean Williams

title: 49ers add RB Zamir White
summary: San Francisco has elected to add one of the running backs the club worked out this week.
full_text: San Francisco has elected to add one of the running backs the club worked out this week. Per Adam Schefter of ESPN, the 49ers are signing Zamir White. White, 26, completed his rookie contract with the Raiders with the 2025 season. A fourth-round pick in 2022, White has appeared in 45 career games with nine starts. He’s taken 198 carries for 736 yards with two touchdowns and caught 25 passes for 152 yards. In six games last season, White took 12 carries for 32 yards and caught four passes for 24 yards. The 49ers also had Nyheim Miller-Hines in for a workout earlier this week. Running back Christian McCaffrey missed Monday’s practice with tightness. Fellow running backs Jordan James, Kaelon Black, and Isaac Guerendo have also been sidelined.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Patriots sign RB Hassan Haskins
summary: The Patriots made a change to their running back group on Wednesday.
full_text: The Patriots made a change to their running back group on Wednesday. They announced the signing of Hassan Haskins to the active roster. Myles Montgomery was waived with an injury designation in a corresponding move. Haskins's last game in the NFL came against the Patriots as he was a member of the Chargers in their playoff loss in New England last season. Haskins spent the last two seasons playing for his college coach Jim Harbaugh in Los Angeles and ran 51 times for 136 yards and two touchdowns. The Titans drafted Haskins in the fourth round in 2022 when Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel was still in Tennessee. He ran 25 times for 93 yards as a rookie, but spent the 2023 season on injured reserve.
author: Josh Alper

title: Saints place OL Dillon Radunz on IR, sign DT Kahlil Saunders
summary: The Saints signed free agent defensive tackle Kahlil Saunders on Wednesday, the team announced.
full_text: The Saints signed free agent defensive tackle Kahlil Saunders on Wednesday, the team announced. In a corresponding move, the Saints placed offensive lineman Dillon Radunz on injured reserve. Radunz, 28, left practice Saturday with a knee injury, and an MRI confirmed a season-ending torn anterior cruciate ligament. Radunz also tore an ACL in 2022 with the Titans. He started 10 games for New Orleans last season. Saunders joins the Saints after participating in training camp with the Dolphins, where he signed as an undrafted free agent following the 2026 draft. He played five seasons at Kentucky, appearing in 51 games with 12 starts. Saunders recorded 77 tackles, 12 tackles for loss and 4.5 sacks in his college career.
author: Charean Williams

title: Steve Keim apologizes to those who were hurt by Mohamed Coulibaly's alleged scams
summary: It's been a strange time for former Cardinals G.M.
full_text: It's been a strange time for former Cardinals G.M. Steve Keim, with his name returning to the news for reasons unrelated to football. First, reports emerged regarding his connection to Mohamed Coulibaly , an alleged scam artist who was recently found dead in the swimming pool at his home. Second, former Cardinals receiver DeAndre Hopkins suggested that Keim was connected to a "set up" that triggered a positive PED test during Hopkins's time in Arizona. (Keim strongly denies that claim.) In an interview with Trey Wingo, Keim addressed his involvement with Coulibaly, and the allegations made by Hopkins. "I want to clear my name and my family's name, first and foremost," Keim said. "I met Mohamed last July, late in July. He presented a drop-shipping business to me and my son. We invested in his company, then my ex-wife invested in his company. On paper, the rates of return were incredible for these stores. And e-commerce business is very lucrative if you do it the right way. "As we continue on throughout the fall, I got to know him better and trusted him and ended up getting offered an opportunity to work with him. In turn, I ended up bringing anywhere from, well, eight friends of mine in to buy stores, and two of my family members: my ex-wife, and my son. And, after all that, Mohamed was paying people back, and it was business as usual, OK?" Keim did not identify any of his "eight friends" who became caught up in Coulibaly's alleged scam. "But as we got into the spring, into March and April, people that I had involved with the company were coming to me that they weren't getting payments," Keim said. "I wasn't getting paid back because of my seven stores that I bought. So things got extremely toxic. I got very, very animated with him and let him know that this is unacceptable. I flew to Philadelphia to meet with him to make sure that there are funds in his bank accounts to pay all these people that are not only involved with me, but he obviously had a number of other investors involved in this business. And long story short, you know, we were scammed. He ended up either getting murdered or killing himself, unfortunately. And it's sad that the person loses his life, but the walls were closing in. And the problem is is he used me to essentially legitimize his business. And then, obviously, kept secrets and facts from me along the way, because, obviously, he knows that I wouldn't support him if I knew that there was an issue or something illegal going on." Keim added that he has been interviewed by the FBI regarding the situation. "Well, they told me that basically that I wasn't a suspect or I wasn't obviously anybody that was a concern," Keim said. "They just wanted the facts. So I'm an open book. I have nothing to hide. I can provide anybody any information they need, whether it was text conversations, it was emails, it was contracts that were fabricated, I believe, on his end that made me believe in this business. And more than anything, the loss of sleep I have at night is not for me. It's for the people who have been affected with this. And I humbly apologize to the eight friends and my two family members that were brought into this." Keim said that he and his family have incurred seven figures in losses that he hopes to recoup from what he believes was a Ponzi scheme. "I don't want to be the victim," Keim said. "I want to be the guy who's [saying] 'I fucked up and I made a mistake.' . . . I can look at the guy in the mirror as long as I can be honest with myself. And I made poor judgment, and I hurt some people along the way. I'm extremely sorry for it." Again, that's Keim's version. He was a victim. He's not a suspect. Whether and to what extent these matters are investigated, and whether and to what extent Keim's version is corroborated, remains to be seen. It also remains to be seen whether authorities determine whether, as Keim said, Coulibaly was murdered or committed suicide as "the walls were closing in."
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Emeka Egbuka has a minor toe injury
summary: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles didn't have an update on wide receiver Emeka Egbuka after Wednesday's practice, but it looks like Egbuka avoided a serious injury.
full_text: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles didn’t have an update on wide receiver Emeka Egbuka after Wednesday's practice, but it looks like Egbuka avoided a serious injury. Egbuka limped off the field during the joint practice at the Jets' facility in New Jersey and did not return before it came to an end. Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that Egbuka suffered a toe injury and that it is considered minor. That's good news for the Bucs and Egbuka will have a good chunk of time to rest before the team is back on the practice field. They'll play the Jets in their preseason opener and most of the team's starters were expected to sit out that game anyway. Egbuka had 63 catches for 938 yards and six touchdowns during his rookie season. He could take on an even bigger offensive role with Mike Evans now in San Francisco.
author: Josh Alper

title: Travis Kelce: Wedding to Taylor Swift "was the best night of my life"
summary: Travis Kelce's wedding to Taylor Swift in July was the celebrity social event of the summer, as the couple assembled guests at Madison Square Garden in New York for the occasion.
full_text: Travis Kelce's wedding to Taylor Swift in July was the celebrity social event of the summer, as the couple assembled guests at Madison Square Garden in New York for the occasion. Speaking to the media for the first time at this summer's training camp on Wednesday, Kelce reflected on the special occasion. “Wedding was the best night of my life . I appreciate everybody who came out and celebrated and had fun with us. That’s about all I really got from that night,” Kelce said, via Jesse Newell of TheAthletic.com. “It was a crazy night. It was full of a lot of celebration. But [now] it’s football, baby.” Kelce, who will turn 37 in early October, is heading into his 14th pro season. The four-time, AP first-team All-Pro told reporters his body feels good as he goes through training camp, noting he’s physically “ready to rock and roll” in 2026. “I still got a lot of love for this game,” he said. “I still think I can go out and play at a high level, and I want to go out there and prove to myself that I can play at a better level than I did last year. And I think that’s probably the biggest thing for me is making sure that I’m accountable for the guys in this room every single play that I’m out there.” Kelce started all 17 games for the Chiefs last season, catching 76 passes for 851 yards with five touchdowns.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Texans sign K Chris Freeman
summary: The Texans signed kicker Chris Freeman on Wednesday, the team announced.
full_text: The Texans signed kicker Chris Freeman on Wednesday, the team announced. Freeman will give veteran kicker Ka'imi Fairbairn a break. He worked out for the team last week, along with kicker Will Ferrin and two punters, and also attended the team's rookie minicamp. Freeman is an undrafted free agent who played four college seasons at Indiana and two at Connecticut. In the past two seasons in Storrs, he made all 101 extra points and 43-of-52 field goals, with his 82.7 percent accuracy and 230 points leading the nation. In a corresponding move, the Texans waived wide receiver Montrell Washington. He lasted a week in the team's training camp. Washington appeared in 15 regular-season games with the Broncos in 2022, catching four-of-nine targets for 2 yards while rushing five times for 30 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Panthers plan to play RB Jonathon Brooks with first team on Saturday
summary: Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks is slated to play in his first NFL preseason game this weekend and the team plans to have him see early action against the Bills.
full_text: Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks is slated to play in his first NFL preseason game this weekend and the team plans to have him see early action against the Bills. Brooks missed the last two preseasons while recovering from torn ACLs, but has been practicing without issue this summer and head coach Dave Canales said on Wednesday that the plan is for him to rotate with Chuba Hubbard while the starting offense is in the game this weekend. "He's in great shape. He's ready to rock, he's ready to play football ," Canales said, via the team's website. "And so now that's just the next part of it. And you know, he'll play with the first group, he'll mix in and out with Chuba, and we'll be able to get a good look at those guys with a couple of drives." Brooks last saw game action in Week 14 of the 2024 season, so any playing time on Saturday would be significant. The fact that it will come with the first team sets the stage for Brooks to make a real impact in Carolina this fall.
author: Josh Alper

title: NFL's most and least optimistic fan bases entering 2026 season: Non-playoff team takes No. 1 spot
summary: Which fan bases are expecting big things in 2026, and which ones are already preparing for another year of doom and gloom?
full_text:
Some fan bases are feeling better than others with the start of the 2026 NFL season just around the corner. Several fan bases are preparing for a possible Super Bowl run, while others are already looking ahead to the 2027 NFL Draft .
In an effort to find the most optimistic fan base, casino.ca recently surveyed 5,000 fans across all 32 fan bases. The common denominators among the most optimistic fan bases included confidence in the quarterback, trust in the head coach, satisfaction with the offseason moves and a belief the team is heading in the right direction.
While the least optimistic fan bases are predictable, the NFL's most optimistic fan base is somewhat of a surprise given how the 2025 season unfolded. Here's a complete look at the NFL's least and most optimistic fan bases heading into Week 1.
It's easy to see why Jets fans are probably more excited about tailgating than actual games this season. Since making back-to-back AFC title game appearances, Gang Green has toiled through 14 losing seasons and 15 consecutive non-playoff seasons. And based on recent reports from training camp, it appears Jets fans are in for another long year.
Cleveland has only made the playoffs twice since returning to the NFL in 1999. And while no one is predicting a playoff berth in 2026, the Browns should nonetheless be an interesting team to follow given all the moves they made this offseason, which include a new head coach (Todd Monken) and three rookie receivers.
Like the Browns, the Titans are also ushering in a new era this season that, if nothing else, should give their fan base some level of hope for the future. Tennessee's new staff includes a defensive guru in head coach Robert Saleh and the only Giants coach to win a playoff game since Big Blue won their most recent Super Bowl in offensive coordinator Brian Daboll.
There are a lot of unknowns regarding the 2026 Dolphins , which has led to low expectations from their fan base. The Dolphins have a first-time NFL head coach in Jeff Hafley and a starting quarterback ( Malik Willis ) with six career regular-season starts under his belt.
Given the Colts ' 8-2 start last season, one would think their fans would be feeling more optimistic. It's safe to assume fans are waiting for their team to give them something to cheer about after Indianapolis ended the 2025 season with seven straight losses.
While the Raiders are bracing themselves for another tough season, there are tangible reasons why fans should feel optimistic about the team's future. Las Vegas has a promising young coach in Klint Kubiak (who just won a Super Bowl with Seattle) and this year's No. 1 overall pick in Fernando Mendoza , who could play sooner than expected if Kirk Cousins continues to mix it up in practice with Maxx Crosby .
Last week's Hall of Fame Game should boost the spirits of Cardinals fans , as it was an impressive night for new coach Mike LaFleur and rookie quarterback Carson Beck .
Saints fans should be more optimistic about their team. They wrapped up the 2025 season with four wins in their last five games, have a promising duo in coach Kellen Moore and quarterback Tyler Shough and turned in an impressive offseason that included signing running back Travis Etienne Jr. and selecting wideout Jordyn Tyson with the No. 8 overall pick.
Big Blue would probably be ranked lower if not for second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart , the arrival of former Super Bowl-winning coach John Harbaugh and the return of former Pro Bowl wideout Odell Beckham Jr . Quite a few things will need to go the Giants' way if they are going to post their first winning season since 2022, including Dart staying healthy.
Pittsburgh being this low is attributed solely to the fact the franchise hasn't won a playoff game since 2016. Steelers fans are hoping Aaron Rodgers can help end that drought in what will be the final year of his Hall of Fame career.
Falcons fans are clearly not very optimistic despite their team having one of the NFL's best offensive trios in running back Bijan Robinson , wideout Drake London and tight end Kyle Pitts . It's safe to say the team's quarterback uncertainty is one of the main reasons why Falcons fans aren't more hopeful.
While last year was disappointing, Vikings fans have reason for optimism in 2026. They have one of the league's best coaches in Kevin O'Connell and a quarterback in Kyler Murray who should be a significant upgrade over J.J. McCarthy .
Bengals fans are trying not to set themselves up for more disappointment after watching their team miss the playoffs each of the past three years despite having arguably the best QB-WR duo in the NFL in Joe Burrow and Ja'Marr Chase . The club's recent defensive additions should give Cincinnati fans reason to believe this year could be different.
The optimism surrounding Houston's fan base is surprisingly low given that the Texans are the only team to win a playoff game in each of the past three seasons. It's safe to say Texans fans are waiting to see if C.J. Stroud is able to rediscover his rookie season magic.
Dallas' spot in this ranking is fitting given the purgatory the team's fan base has been in since 1995. Once again, the Cowboys will field a group good enough to give the fan base reason for hope but probably not talented enough to end the franchise's title drought.
Panthers fans are drinking the Kool-Aid after watching their team capture the NFC South in 2025. It's safe to assume Panthers fans are confident Bryce Young will take another step in his ongoing development.
Based on their ranking, it's safe to wonder if Buccaneers fans have been paying much attention to their team's offseason. Franchise legend Mike Evans left for San Francisco, and the team's remaining two stars ( Baker Mayfield and Vita Vea ) are mired in contract disputes .
Despite last year's turbulence, Washington fans are apparently confident their team will rebound in 2026. It's safe to say their reason for optimism is based on Jayden Daniels ' return from last year's injury and some of the offseason additions, which include first-round rookie Sonny Styles .
Jaguars fans have reasonable expectations for a team that went 13-4 last season before losing in the wild card round. One big question facing the Jaguars is whether Bhayshul Tuten can replace Travis Etienne Jr., who left for the Saints in free agency.
Lions fans are cautiously optimistic that their team can bounce back after missing the postseason for the first time since 2022. Detroit, however, is already facing some daunting challenges from an injury standpoint .
Green Bay strengthened its defense this offseason with the acquisitions of Javon Hargrave , Zaire Franklin and rookie Chris McClellan . The Packers ' success this season will largely come down to how well Jordan Love plays and the health of Josh Jacobs (who is currently dealing with an injury) and Micah Parsons .
Ravens fans are optimistic about new head coach Jesse Minter, whose impressive track record includes helping Michigan win the 2023 national title. The Ravens had an impressive offseason that included the additions of rookie wideouts Ja'Kobi Lane and Elijah Sarratt , rookie right guard Olaivavega Ioane and former Pro Bowl pass rusher Trey Hendrickson .
Chicago is ready to party like it's 1985, and that could very well happen if Caleb Williams and Co. can build off last year's success. The Bears recently suffered a setback, however, when safety Coby Bryant sustained a knee injury during training camp that is expected to sideline him for four to six months.
Patriots fans might be setting themselves up for a disappointing season. Each of the previous two Super Bowl losers (the Chiefs and 49ers ) had losing records the following season. In the 60-year history of the Super Bowl, only five teams returned to the big game a year after losing it.
Is this the year Justin Herbert wins his first playoff game? Chargers fans apparently think so after the team brought in former Dolphins coach Mike…
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Seahawks and Broncos set for a rare uniform matchup in 2026: This almost never happens in the NFL
summary: The "Thursday Night Football" showdown in Week 6 will feature both teams' throwback jerseys
full_text:
When the NFL calendar hits Week 6 this year, there will be a Throwback Thursday showdown in Denver, and that Seahawks-Broncos game will feature something rarely seen in the NFL: Both teams will be wearing colored jerseys.
If you regularly watch the NFL, you've probably noticed that at least one team wears white in almost every game, but that won't be the case when the Seahawks and Broncos get together on "Thursday Night Football" on Oct. 15.
The Broncos have announced that they'll wear their throwback Orange Crush uniforms for the game. The Broncos started wearing the orange throwbacks in 2024, and since then, they've worn them five times and gone 5-0.
On the Seahawks' end, they'll wear a royal blue uniform with a silver helmet that's a throwback to the 1990s. The Seahawks wore these throwbacks three times during their Super Bowl-winning season in 2025, and they'll make their 2026 debut in Denver.
These are two of the most iconic throwback uniforms in the NFL, and when the teams take the field, it will be color vs. color in what will easily be the best jersey matchup of the year.
You asked for it, you got it. 🤝 We’re going old school with the @Seahawks for #SEAvsDEN ! pic.twitter.com/3E5VsGqMcL
The Seahawks will actually be rocking their throwback jerseys in back-to-back games because they'll also be wearing them in Week 7 against the Chiefs . But the Broncos game is the only one that will give us the rare color vs. color matchup.
It's rare to see a color vs. color game in the NFL. Although the league embraced the theme during the Color Rush years from 2015-18 -- a span that featured multiple color vs. color games -- the Broncos-Seahawks game will mark just the fourth time since the start of the 2021 season that we've seen a color vs. color game in which neither team wore a Color Rush uniform.
In fact, this matchup will mark just the second time since the start of the 2024 season that the NFL has given us a color vs. color uniform game. The last time it happened came in Week 15 of last season when the Falcons wore black against the Buccaneers , who wore their iconic Creamsicle jerseys.
Before that, the last color vs. color game came in Week 8 of the 2023 season, and that also involved the Falcons in a game where they wore black against the Titans, who wore their baby blue Oilers uniforms .
If you want to get technical, you could argue that black isn't a color (just ask Adobe ). If that's the case, then Broncos-Seahawks will be the first true color vs. color game -- one that doesn't involve a black jersey -- in four years. The last time we got one came in Week 8 of the 2022 season, when the Chicago Bears wore orange against the Dallas Cowboys, who were suited up in their navy blue jerseys .
Run it up the gut and break free! @dak 📺: #CHIvsDAL on FOX 📱: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/QMxVpZl61r pic.twitter.com/AzPBuui2VM
The fact that the Broncos and Seahawks will both wear their throwbacks against each other is fitting because these two teams used to be in the same division. From 1977 through 2001, the Seahawks played in the AFC West with the Broncos, so the teams will renew an old rivalry in the uniforms they wore when they shared a division.
author: John Breech

title: Stefon Diggs already looks like missing piece for Jayden Daniels, Commanders offense
summary: Diggs tormented Miami's defensive backs throughout Wednesday's practice
full_text:
ASHBURN, Va. -- Jayden Daniels didn't appear to have anything, but then again, making something out of what appears to be nothing is what special quarterbacks can do.
And, in this case, what wide receivers can do.
Daniels rifled a ball to the back of the end zone, and Stefon Diggs reeled in an inch-perfect pass, pirouetted, and somehow got both feet down in bounds. The official raised his hands to signal touchdown. Dolphins defenders vehemently disagreed, but Diggs' toe touches didn't lie. The difference between near-perfect coverage and perfect coverage can be the burgeoning connection between a four-time Pro Bowler who continues to show he's still got it and a star young quarterback with laser accuracy.
"It's awesome, just his feel for space," Daniels said after practice. "He's a dawg. He goes out and makes plays. He brings energy, he's a leader, so I'm super happy to have Stefon in that room, not just for the offense but for the whole team in general."
Diggs tormented the Dolphins' young defensive backs throughout Wednesday's joint practice, starting with winning his one-on-one drills. On one rep, Diggs dusted a defensive back, reeled in the touchdown, and launched the ball high up in the air in celebration. On another rep, he easily beat a defensive back on an in-breaking route. It's a drill designed to favor the offense -- no pass rush, no other defenders, and an entire half of the field to defend -- but Diggs showed off his outstanding combination of speed, suddenness, footwork and route running.
His prowess against zone popped at the end of practice. In an 11-on-11 drill, Diggs made a pair of catches, finding soft spots and making himself available for Daniels. The two have been in communication often since Diggs' arrival last week, whether between plays or outside practice.
"He's seen a lot of ball in his life, seen a lot of different coverages, been in a lot of different offenses, knows some terminology," Daniels said. "All the concepts are kind of the same. It's just different terminology, so overall, once you get him caught up to speed about the terminology, he can go out there and play fast and play ball."
Diggs didn't speak to the media Wednesday, but he has made a major impact in the week since he signed with Washington. The late signing, he said, was so he could "do whatever made the most sense."
The Commanders certainly needed the help.
Myriad issues popped up during last year's 5-12 campaign, but the lack of proven downfield receiving options opposite Terry McLaurin was a major one -- and it became even more pronounced as McLaurin appeared in just 10 games. After Deebo Samuel and McLaurin, the Commanders' top wide receiver was rookie Jaylin Lane with just 16 catches.
Diggs, meanwhile, was enjoying a renaissance season in New England, reeling in 85 passes for 1,013 yards and four touchdowns while playing only 55% of the Patriots ' offensive snaps. His 2.42 yards per route run was fifth in the NFL and his best mark since 2022.
Most Yards Per Route Run, 2025
Diggs said he stayed in shape, often with multiple workouts per day, during the offseason and also wanted to be in the right headspace before he signed.
"It was just the when and how, those kind of things," he said last week. "But the where wasn't at the top of my mind. It was more so I wanted to be prepared. I wanted to be in a good head space, and I wanted to be physically in the right spot, so I could come in and be ready to do whatever they need me to do."
The Commanders' offense, which started training camp slowly, was a natural fit for the Washington-area native.
Diggs may not play as often as he used to and might not be at the peak of his powers, but he can still take over a game. Last year, he had 10 catches for 146 yards in a "revenge game" win over the Bills , his former team, and had five games of 100+ yards receiving. The Commanders haven't had a wide receiver not named Terry McLaurin post a 100-yard game in nearly three years.
"It's two premiums on the field now," safety Jeremy Reaves said. "... It just adds a different element to go against and game plan against, disguise against. It's tough, man. He helps us a lot."
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Agent's Take: Why NFL tight ends have been left behind by contract boom, plus 3 stars who could reset market
summary: Tucker Kraft, Sam LaPorta and Brock Bowers could finally push the tight end market to new heights
full_text:
The 2026 league year, which began on March 11, has been great financially for most major offensive positions. Patrick Mahomes became the first quarterback to break the $60 million-per-year barrier. Jaxon Smith-Njigba topped Ja'Marr Chase as the NFL's highest-paid wide receiver . Saquon Barkley dropped to fourth on the running back pay scale, with Jahmyr Gibbs , who now leads the way, Bijan Robinson and Jonathan Taylor joining him in the $20 million-per-year club last week.
Offensive tackle Laremy Tunsil's contract extension made him the first and only $30 million-per-year offensive lineman. Peter Skoronski just established a new benchmark for offensive guards at $25 million per year. It may be short-lived if the Indianapolis Colts sign Quenton Nelson , who is in a contract year, to a new deal.
The most shocking development has been Tyler Linderbaum resetting the center market by a whopping 50% when he signed a three-year, $81 million contract averaging $27 million per year with the Las Vegas Raiders in free agency.
Tight ends are the exception to this offensive salary boom. A career-high 88 receptions, nearly 1,000 receiving yards and a second-team All-Pro selection in 2025, leading to a franchise tag, weren't enough for Kyle Pitts to move the needle for tight ends . His three-year, $53 million deal with the Atlanta Falcons in June made him the NFL's third-highest-paid tight end at $17,666,667 per year. Pitts did establish a new tight end record with $36 million fully guaranteed at signing.
A stagnant tight end market isn't anything new. Jimmy Graham became the league's first $10 million-per-year tight end in 2014 when he signed a four-year, $40 million contract with the New Orleans Saints as a franchise player. The mark wasn't eclipsed until 2020, when Austin Hooper got a four-year, $42 million deal averaging $10.5 million per year from the Cleveland Browns as an unrestricted free agent.
The massive reset came later in 2020 during training camp. George Kittle signed a five-year, $75 million contract extension averaging $15 million per year with the San Francisco 49ers . Travis Kelce quickly followed suit with a team-friendly four-year, $57.25 million extension averaging $14,312,500 per year from the Kansas City Chiefs .
Six years later, the tight end market has yet to hit the $20 million-per-year mark. Kittle is currently the highest-paid tight end with the backloaded four-year, $76.4 million extension averaging $19.1 million per year that he signed with the 49ers in April 2025. There's $22.4 million in Kittle's 2029 contract year, when he will be 36. The first three new years of Kittle's extension average $18 million per year.
Kittle's deal came about a month after Trey McBride signed a four-year, $76 million extension averaging $19 million per year with the Arizona Cardinals . The first three new years of McBride's extension average $19,333,333 per year. McBride's $43 million in overall guarantees are the most ever for a tight end.
There's a big drop-off in tight end salaries after Kittle, McBride and Pitts. Isaiah Likely is next at $13,333,333 per year. The three-year, $40 million deal Likely signed with the New York Giants is worth a maximum of $47.2 million through incentives.
It wasn't too long ago that nearly three times as many tight ends as today were making $13.5 million per year or more. Eight tight ends on multiyear contracts were above that mark in 2023.
A subset of the overall tight end market has reached new heights in 2026. Charlie Kolar became the first blocking tight end to eclipse the $8 million-per-year mark when he signed a three-year, $24.3 million deal with the Los Angeles Chargers during free agency in March.
Darnell Washington took blocking tight end salaries to an unprecedented level in June. He received a four-year, $42 million extension from the Pittsburgh Steelers , making him the first blocking tight end to reach the $10 million-per-year mark.
The gap between the highest-paid tight end and the top-paid blocking tight end has narrowed to 81.9%. It was 150% when Kittle signed his $15 million-per-year extension. Nick Boyle was at the top of the blocking tight end pay scale at $6 million per year.
The blocking tight end market has jumped 35.48% in 2026 alone, going from Josh Oliver's $7.75 million per year to Washington's $10.5 million average yearly salary. That's more than the tight end market has moved over the last six years. Kittle's two market-setting deals represent a 27.33% increase. Since 2020, the salary bar for blocking tight ends has been raised by 75%.
This 27.33% increase is well below the growth in the salary cap. The 2020 salary cap was $198.2 million. The current $301.2 million salary cap is 51.97% higher than the 2020 figure.
There's still a chance the tight end market won't be left out of 2026's offensive salary boom. Green Bay Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst revealed there have been discussions with Jack Bechta, Tucker Kraft's agent, since training camp opened at the end of July.
Kraft was on pace for more than 70 catches and 1,100 receiving yards before he tore the ACL in his right knee eight games into the 2025 season. Through seven team games, Kraft led NFL tight ends in receiving yards (469) and was tied for the most touchdown receptions (six). He finished 2025 with 32 catches for 489 yards and six touchdowns. Kraft's 15.3 yards per reception ranked eighth in the NFL last season. Kraft excels at picking up yards after the catch. His 10.8 yards after catch per reception were easily the most for a tight end in 2025.
Unlike most pass-catching tight ends, Kraft is a good blocker. Green Bay's run game averaged 0.18 more yards per carry with Kraft on the field last season.
Kraft appears to be on track to play in the regular-season opener. The Packers activated him from the physically unable to perform list a few days into training camp.
The Packers are likely viewing a deal in the same vicinity as Pitts' $17,666,667 per year as appropriate for Kraft, who is in a contract year. Bechta probably has his sights set much higher. It wouldn't be surprising for Bechta to use Kittle's 2020 deal adjusted for salary cap inflation, which is a little more than $22.75 million per year, as a guide since he also represents Kittle. The Packers will likely have to give Kraft a player-friendly cash flow regardless of his average per year. That's because the only guaranteed money in Green Bay veteran contracts is a signing bonus and/or a roster bonus payable within a few days of signing.
The bigger deals contain an unsecured roster bonus due on the third or fifth day of the league year in the second and third years. The roster bonuses are supposed to be substitutes for additional contract guarantees. The overall guarantees in Green Bay contracts are less than those in comparable deals with other teams. The only exceptions have been made with quarterbacks Jordan Love and Aaron Rodgers , as well as edge rusher Micah Parsons .
Gibbs' record-setting running back contract at $22.5 million per year has prompted speculation that the Detroit Lions will turn their negotiating attention to Sam LaPorta , who is in a contract year just like Kraft. He is also represented by Bechta. LaPorta had a fast start to his career. He set a single-season rookie record for a tight end with 86 receptions in 2023, which Brock Bowers broke the following year, and earned second-team All-Pro honors in the process. LaPorta missed the final eight games last season with a herniated disc in his back, which required surgery. He was averaging a career-best 54.3 receiving yards per game when he suffered the injury.
The Lions aren't opposed to doing deals during the regular season. For example, edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson's $45 million-per-year extension, which made him the NFL's second-highest-paid non-quarterback, wasn't done until the end of October after he demonstrated that the season-ending broken fibula and tibia in his left leg suffered in…
author: Joel Corry

title: Christian Gonzalez contract drama: Patriots star sends cryptic message as record deal remains unsigned
summary: Gonzalez was also not on the field during New England's joint practice with the Colts on Tuesday
full_text:
As the New England Patriots look to carry the momentum from their meteoric resurrection to championship contention last season into 2026, there's been one major (and expensive) situation looming over the organization as training camp rolls along.
All-Pro cornerback Christian Gonzalez is eligible for an extension that is expected to reset the market when it's agreed upon. Owner Robert Kraft has already stated publicly that the team has offered Gonzalez and his camp a contract that would make him the highest-paid player at his position, as well as the highest-paid player in team history.
"We love Christian Gonzalez. We love him as a player, as a person," Kraft told reporters on July 25 . "That's why we made an offer to him that makes him the highest-paid player ever to play that position in the NFL , and coincidentally it's the highest contract in the Patriots franchise history."
Despite that declaration, no deal has been finalized as of the second full week of August, with the preseason on our doorstep.
For Gonzalez's part, he was asked about Kraft's comments and the negotiations afterward. He kept his cards much closer to the vest, saying he'll keep any updates "between my team and the front office."
Even without an extension, the 24-year-old Gonzalez had been practicing with the team, seemingly as a show of good faith. That included taking part in fully padded practices. However, Gonzalez was not on the field Tuesday when New England hosted the Indianapolis Colts for a joint practice before their preseason opener.
That absence was then coupled with a cryptic social media post showing Gonzalez standing on the practice field with the song "time reveals, be careful what you wish for" by Gunna. Specifically, the lyrics "should have been done by now," which were displayed as text in the story, seem to be a not-so-subtle reference to his contract situation.
#Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez chose some interesting lyrics in his latest Instagram story… “Should have been done by now” (📸 christian.gonzalez3 IG) pic.twitter.com/LPRtEJy5DF
At least part of the reason Gonzalez was not on the field during Tuesday's joint practice with the Colts appears to have been health-related. The Boston Sports Journal reported that the corner sustained a minor injury at the end of Monday's practice. According to those on the scene for Monday's session , Gonzalez came down hard on a contested throw to Romeo Doubs in the corner of the end zone. The injury didn't appear serious, as Gonzalez stayed on the field for the rest of practice, albeit after being a bit slow to get up.
Could this injury, while reportedly minor, have been a wake-up call of sorts for Gonzalez? For someone eyeing a record-setting contract, a serious injury would crater negotiations. With this latest tweak in mind, it'd be logical for Gonzalez to realize he should possibly take his foot off the gas in camp, especially with a joint practice on the horizon.
Does Hunter Henry signing an extension with the Patriots have any real bearing on how they operate with Gonzalez? No. Is it an awkward look? You bet.
The veteran tight end agreed to a two-year extension on Monday that reportedly has a base value of $16 million and can be worth up to $20 million. That's $8 million in AAV based on the new deal's base value, which is pennies in today's NFL financial landscape. That said, having this news come down on the same day Gonzalez would later suffer a minor injury potentially adds another layer to the saga.
Again, they aren't directly correlated, but it'd be natural for Gonzalez (or any player seeking a seismic extension) to be miffed seeing the organization take care of another player long term while he's also going through an injury scare. How could it not?
CBS Sports' Joel Corry provided a great breakdown of Gonzalez's contract situation at the end of last month, and he highlighted a few benchmarks the team would need to cross to fulfill Robert Kraft's declaration that the corner would become the highest-paid player at his position. Naturally, there are multiple ways to determine what "highest-paid" at the position means. With Kraft not going into further detail, we're left to wonder whether that means AAV, total value, total guarantees, signing bonus, etc.
Here's a look at where those figures currently stand, courtesy of Corry.
*Rookie contract as the No. 2 overall pick
The most common way to think about a player becoming the highest-paid at his position is average annual value. If Gonzalez and his camp are looking at it through that lens, he's looking to exceed the $31.1 million in AAV Denzel Ward is currently making in Cleveland.
However, that figure could change in an instant, depending on what happens with the Seattle Seahawks and fellow corner Devon Witherspoon , who is also negotiating a market-setting extension. If Witherspoon (who has the same agent as Gonzalez) signs his deal first, it'll almost certainly raise the asking price for the Patriots corner.
It's not out of the question that this is what's stalling the extension with New England. If Gonzalez is looking to squeeze every last dollar out of this deal, it's in his best interest to wait out Witherspoon because his deal could raise the bar.
Meanwhile, if Gonzalez is looking to truly reshape the cornerback landscape, he could look to become one of the highest-paid defensive players in the league. Currently, Texans pass rusher Will Anderson Jr . is the highest-paid non-quarterback in the NFL, making $50 million in AAV. Then there are a handful of other defensive linemen and edge rushers with AAVs in the $40 million range.
If Gonzalez is trying to swim in those waters and the Patriots are stopping short of that, it would jibe with Kraft's comments that they've offered him a deal that makes him the highest-paid player at his position while also explaining why that deal hasn't been executed.
Regardless of why this deal hasn't gotten done, it continues to hover over the Patriots as the preseason begins. So long as it festers, it opens the door for things to go sour, with Gonzalez's recent social media activity, whether it was intended as a message about his contract or not, serving as the prime example.
