title: Why Drew Mestemaker and other transfers could turn college moves into bigger NFL paydays
summary: After nine first-round picks in the 2026 NFL Draft transferred during their college careers, these prospects could be next to benefit from a new home
full_text:
The NFL Draft evaluation process is fluid. Although Indiana's Fernando Mendoza was my top quarterback prospect in summer scouting a year ago, he was not widely regarded as such. Edge rusher David Bailey flashed high-end talent at Stanford, but few could envision that player becoming the No. 2 overall pick prior to his time with Texas Tech. Those are just a few examples of players in last year's class who transferred and improved their draft stock. In total, nine first-round picks in the 2026 NFL Draft transferred at least once in their respective collegiate career.
There is a variety of reasons that could contribute to a prospect's stock rising in a new environment: scheme, position on the depth chart, improved health, etc. ... Who are some of the prospects who could benefit from new surroundings?
Alliegro is a bigger linebacker prospect with some shock in his hands and added value as a spot rusher. He can do a better job of coming to balance in space and staying in-phase when in coverage. There are some similarities to Jake Golday, whom the Vikings drafted in the second round.
Alliegro was a lacrosse All-American in high school. Ironically, he broke a bone in his arm against the Buckeyes last season and is now helping them replace Sonny Styles.
The downside to retaining both Bear Alexander and A'Mauri Washington was the loss of two other Oregon defensive tackles. Green is 6-feet-5, 319 pounds, and moves well for his size. Although he played sparingly for the Ducks over the past three seasons, Green is now tasked with realizing his full potential along a talented Crimson Tide front.
His former teammate, defensive lineman Tionne Gray, who is now at Notre Dame, was a candidate for the list as well.
Former school : Stephen F. Austin
Mayo originally enrolled at Virginia Union out of high school and spent three seasons there before transferring to Stephen F. Austin. After one season, he got called up a second time. At 6-2, 190 pounds, he does a good job using his size to constrict the receiver along the sideline and prohibiting free releases off the line of scrimmage. When his feet settle in space, it can be a bit challenging to get them back up to speed, but Mayo has starting qualities.
McKinney is a long, lean boundary cornerback who had been more productive in 2024 than 2025. He should benefit from playing behind a skilled Notre Dame front and alongside a secondary that features the likes of cornerbacks Christian Gray and Leonard Moore, as well as safety Adon Schuler.
New defensive coordinator Aaron Henry had been with Illinois during the program's run as an NFL defensive-back factory. Devon Witherspoon, Quan Martin, Sydney Brown, Kerby Joseph and Nate Hobbs were all coached by Henry during that time.
Former school : North Texas
Mestemaker and coach Eric Morris were at the heart of one of college football's most electric 2025 offenses. The Mean Green averaged north of 45 points per game last season, and multiple starters followed him to Oklahoma State when Morris was named the coach of the Cowboys.
Mestemaker (6-4, 211) has defied all odds, going from a walk-on at North Texas to a coveted transfer and starting Oklahoma State quarterback in just two years. Mobility is not a strength of the Texas native, but he makes good decisions within the pocket and throws with touch and anticipation. The 2027 NFL Draft will be his first year of eligibility, so there is no rush to leave, but Mestemaker could solidify his draft stock with another strong campaign against stiffer competition.
Moore forced two fumbles and recorded four interceptions in 2024 as a member of Duke's program, but missed all of the 2025 season after suffering a torn ACL in the bowl game. It will have been roughly 20 months since the injury by the time he first takes the field for the Buckeyes.
At 6-1, 195 pounds, Moore has good instincts and shows the ability to transition planes in coverage. There is some versatility to line up over the slot as well. Exposure to defensive coordinator Matt Patricia's scheme, surrounded by other future pros, should serve Moore well this season.
Former school : Utah State
Pegan averaged more than 15 yards per catch in 2025, accounting for nearly 1,000 receiving yards and five receiving touchdowns for the Aggies. At 6-3, 210 pounds, he has the size and speed to stretch the field vertically for quarterback Devon Dampier and the Utes. The upcoming season is an opportunity for him to showcase his talent against higher-level competition.
Wide receiver is one position where several prospects had a justifiable case for this list.
Price has good size and blocks with a strong, square base. His biggest room for improvement could come in hand fighting against SEC talent. Alabama comes to town in the second game of the season, and the schedule does not get any easier. He allowed one sack and seven pressures last season, according to TruMedia, while with the Bears. Price has played center throughout his career.
Former school : Penn State
Reynolds was a five-star prospect out of high school and also played basketball. He shows effort as a blocker, but had an 8.6% drop rate last season, according to TruMedia. James Franklin's teams have always done well evaluating tight ends, and he brought Reynolds with him from Penn State. The Nittany Lions have two very talented tight ends of their own for the upcoming season, so Reynolds should receive more playing time in Blacksburg.
Former school : Northwestern
Saka steadily added weight throughout his collegiate career. A lack of ideal mass has limited him in the run game but he should be rounding into form this season with the Aggies. The Baltimore native has quick-twitch muscles, which have allowed him to record 12 sacks and three forced fumbles over the last three years.

title: Russell Wilson says Caleb Williams reminds him of younger self: 'He's got some crazy talent'
summary: Wilson, beginning his first season with CBS Sports' "The NFL Today," also named Trevor Lawrence as a breakout candidate for 2026
full_text:
NEW YORK -- In 2012, Russell Wilson was thrown into the fray immediately, winning the Seahawks ' starting quarterback battle as a third-round rookie. He started all 16 games that year (as he would do the next eight years) and made the Pro Bowl. One season later, he was a Super Bowl champion.
Now, he's a rookie in another sense. Wilson joined CBS Sports' "The NFL Today" this offseason, and on Tuesday, he put on his analyst hat to discuss some of the NFL's most notable young quarterbacks. One he's been especially impressed by while preparing for this season? Chicago's Caleb Williams .
"Watching the film, watching Caleb Williams and how talented he is and how he moves, he kinda reminds me of me when I was young and all that -- his ability to make plays, his ability to throw on the run, his ability to throw accurately on the move, how he spins out of the pocket," Wilson said Tuesday at the "NFL on CBS" media day.
"I think he's got some crazy talent to him."
Williams' playmaking abilities were on display, especially in crunch time. He led the NFL with six fourth-quarter comebacks in the regular season, and he added another in an epic wild-card win over the Packers .
🗣️ ROOOOOOME ODUUUUUNZE 📺: @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/7hfM7AaUId
He then nearly led an upset of the Rams with a Wilson-esque play.
CALEB WILLIAMS YOU ARE RIDICULOUS 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/2zphVCnNbd
Of course, a big part of Wilson's game as a youngster was his ability to avoid sacks (Williams took 68 as a rookie but just 24 last year) and to make defenders pay with his legs. Both also took excellent care of the ball.
Caleb Williams vs. Russell Wilson -- 1st 2 Seasons
"The next step for Caleb is finishing the second quarter as strong as he finishes the fourth quarter," said former Bears offensive lineman Kyle Long , who will also be in his first season on "The NFL Today."
"The second quarter is where the games will be won or lost. Going into the half, trying to steal an extra possession, that's where a lot of their games will be won or lost."
When asked for his 2026 breakout quarterback, Wilson went with a slightly older player.
"I'm really interested to see what Trevor Lawrence does this year," Wilson said. "The reason I bring up Trevor Lawrence is I think he's got great talent, he's got good players around him, but this is his second year with Liam Coen around. So I think that'll be a huge help, those two guys knowing each other.
Lawrence played at an elite level down the stretch of last season as the Jaguars won their final eight regular-season games.
Wilson's most recent team -- the Giants --  doesn't have that same continuity, with new coach John Harbaugh and new offensive coordinator Matt Nagy in tow. Still, Wilson had high praise for 2025 teammate Jaxson Dart going into Year 2.
"I think his competitiveness is tremendous," Wilson said. "I think his work ethic's great. His ability to run and move is a special trait, and I think continuing to know playing the next play, he's going to do a tremendous job with that. I think John Harbaugh's gonna give him the chance to do that strategically and put him in really good positions to be successful."
Dart was examined for a concussion five times last year, and one diagnosed concussion cost him two games. He did, however, earn plaudits for sliding in bounds at Giants training camp on Monday. Wilson is confident the second-year pro will continue to adjust well to his new scheme, too.
"He knows how to do it, he'll be great at it, and he'll be able to ball out," Wilson said.
Wilson also got to see NFC East foe Jayden Daniels of the Commanders up close and personal last year -- the two faced off in Week 1 -- but neither played in the teams' late-season meeting. Dart got the start for New York, while Daniels' season had already ended due to an elbow injury, one of three injuries he suffered in 2025.
"He'll have a great year this year," Wilson said."I think he'll come back healthy, ready to go, ready to come back and rock and roll. He's got crazy good talent. His ability to run, ability to throw is super exceptional."
Wilson's debut on "The NFL Today" will come Sept. 13 alongside Emmy Award-winning host James Brown, Bill Cowher, Nate Burleson and Long.

title: NFL preseason arrives: 10 storylines that could shape the 2026 regular season
summary: The preseason may not count in the standings, but it could determine starting jobs, roster spots and the outlook for several contenders
full_text:
The first preseason game on the 2026 NFL calendar is already complete, and three weeks of action lie ahead as the rest of the league joins the Arizona Cardinals and Carolina Panthers in the ramp-up process. Last week's Hall of Fame Game was a prime example of how the preseason can reshape the narrative surrounding an entire team. Rookie quarterbacks Carson Beck and Haynes King put on a show, asserting their squads' bright futures. In Beck's case, it might have even accelerated the clock on a position battle.
Between the three games per team and the practices leading up to them, the information gleaned from all 32 squads is immensely valuable, as it hints at how the season will unfold.
Here are 10 storylines for everyone to follow over the next month of preseason football news.
There are only two quarterback battles left to play out after the Vikings named Kyler Murray the Week 1 starter over J.J. McCarthy .
Atlanta's is a bit unconventional as Michael Penix Jr . continues to work his way back from a torn ACL. Since the Falcons have not yet tabbed Tua Tagovailoa as their No. 1 option, it will be important to monitor whether Penix progresses enough to take live preseason reps and push for the job.
The Browns ' competition is a true two-man contest, on the other hand. Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders will each start a preseason game , and coach Todd Monken will use those data points to determine which gets the nod in the third outing.
While nearly every team has its quarterback situation settled, most still have at least one position left to square away on the depth chart. The all-important left tackle job is still up for grabs for the Bears and Cowboys , while the Lions and Ravens have decisions to make on the interior offensive lines. Which running back breaks camp as the Steelers' lead option is also uncertain.
These five other battles will continue into the preseason and are equally as intriguing:
With first-round pick Ty Simpson locked in as the backup to reigning MVP Matthew Stafford , the two likeliest rookie quarterbacks to see meaningful playing time in 2026 are Fernando Mendoza and Carson Beck.
If the former makes waves with his preseason opportunities, there will be calls for him to quickly uproot Kirk Cousins as the face of the Raiders ' offense, particularly because he carries tremendous upside as this year's No. 1 overall pick.
Beck already dazzled in his debut with a Hall of Fame Game performance that made him look like a worthy contender to steal playing time from Jacoby Brissett . If he replicates his 11-for-14 effort in the next two contests, the Cardinals might want to see what he can do in a regular-season context.
Many of the biggest names from this year's draft class are already penciled in as rotational players, if not starters. The bigger question is just how much of an impact they can make, and that will start to become clearer in the preseason.
Jeremiyah Love and other Cardinals rookies will be in the lineup for their second preseason game, Bears safety Dillon Thieneman could see some run this month, and it remains to be seen how much the Cowboys want to get out of Caleb Downs .
Outside of those who already know they will contribute as rookies, a few other under-the-radar newcomers could also break through between now and the season opener . A few to keep an eye on include the following:
Minor muscle strains and ankle tweaks pop up regularly in the preseason and often result in rotation players missing time as their teams exercise the utmost caution. More often than not, they are nothing to worry about come Week 1. But there have also already been a large handful of serious injuries in training camp , and unfortunately, more are likely to pop up in preseason games.
At the same time, all eyes are on the stars who suffered major ailments last season and who are targeting returns for the 2026 opener or shortly thereafter. Will the following players hit the field this preseason? It would be a great sign for their Week 1 availability if they did.
Not all of them will see playing time until the regular season, and those who do will largely take only a modest number of snaps, but the preseason provides the first opportunity to see this year's top free agents and trade chips take in-game snaps with their new teams. Whether the Dolphins made the right move in paying up for Malik Willis and whether the Jets will field a functioning offense behind Geno Smith could start to become clear even before Week 1 arrives.
One team that will throw all of its newcomers into the mix in its preseason opener is the Titans . Robert Saleh said he will play all his starters, which means Tennessee's reconstructed defense will begin to take shape. As a refresher, all of these defenders joined the roster this spring:
There are seven new head coaches on the sidelines this preseason, 19 new offensive coordinators in the booth, and 14 new defensive coordinators. Over the next three weeks, their identities and schemes will shine through, offering a clearer understanding of how they might achieve success. A few in particular stand out.
It is not clear to what extent the Eagles will use their starters in the preseason, but their adaptation to Sean Mannion's offense might be the most intriguing new player-coach scheme fit of the year. Even if Jalen Hurts does suit up between now and September, how much will Philadelphia show of his ability to command the system? Perhaps enough to learn whether it can revitalize the talented unit.
In Dallas, do not expect to see many starters on the field this month, but the backups could give everyone a glimpse into what Christian Parker has in store for a Cowboys defense that, on paper, has a chance to take a massive leap forward.
Two-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Vita Vea wanted to finalize a contract extension by the start of training camp, and since he and the Buccaneers did not come to terms, he requested a trade . The team has neither met his contract demands nor shipped him out of town, so the standoff carries into the preseason. Making the situation even dicier is that Vea is holding in at practice. He is not even participating in joint practice with the Jets despite traveling with the Buccaneers to New Jersey.
If the hold-in drags on too much longer, Vea's availability for Week 1 could come into question even if he does come to terms with Tampa Bay on a new deal. The chances of seeing Vea participate in a preseason game dwindle by the day. All that really matters, of course, is whether he is ramped up enough to start the opener.
Possibly the biggest question of training camp in the NFC West is whether Aaron Donald will come out of retirement to join the Rams . The three-time Defensive Player of the Year teased a return to the NFL earlier this summer when Los Angeles traded for Myles Garrett , and he has gone so far as to work out at the team's facility .
There are a couple of potential routes back to the NFL for Donald. The first would be to sign with the Rams during the preseason, participate in August practices, use a preseason game to aid in the transition back to live reps, and become available for Week 1. The other is to slow-play the process to ensure he is both fully capable of stepping back into game action and fresh enough in the latter stages of the season to make an impact until the final game.
With the first week of the preseason underway, the opening batch of joint practices is unfolding ahead of this weekend's games. In many cases, coaches place as much stock (if not more) in these sessions as in the preseason games themselves. For the teams that sit their starters until Week 1, these practices are the only times in which the first-team units square off against anyone other than their teammates.
Stars nowadays go head-to-head in joint practices more than in preseason games, and it took just one day for a matchup to turn heads. While not much should be made of one practice rep, A.J. Brown's…

title: Who will be the non-quarterback MVP for every AFC team in 2026?
summary: From D.J. Moore's arrival in Buffalo to Will Anderson Jr.'s dominance in Houston, these are the non-quarterbacks who matter most
full_text:
The end-all, be-all in the NFL continues to revolve around the quarterback position. If you have one that's considered to be elite, well, you'll routinely be in the Super Bowl conversation. Being in the championship discourse, however, is a far cry from actually lifting the Lombardi Trophy. For that, the rest of the team enters the equation as championship squads need other star pillars to reach the mountaintop.
So, while we can simply pinpoint each team's quarterback as their most valuable player, we're going to cast the QBs off to the side for this exercise. Below, the non-quarterback MVPs for each AFC team in the 2026 season step forward.
Buffalo has had a major hole atop its wide receiver depth chart essentially since trading Stefon Diggs . Over the last two seasons, they've ranked 21st in receptions, 23rd in receiving yards, and tied for 21st in receiving touchdowns among wide receivers. That lack of top talent at the position has lowered their ceiling amid Josh Allen's prime, but they've looked to fix that with the addition of DJ Moore. The Bills struck a deal with the Chicago Bears to acquire Moore, reuniting him with head coach Joe Brady, who was his offensive coordinator during their shared time with the Panthers (2020-21). Over that stretch, Moore averaged 1,175 receiving yards. If he can provide that level of play with Allen now throwing him the football, it should make Buffalo's offense that much tougher to defend.
A new contract for Gonzalez is imminent, and Robert Kraft has already stated that the All-Pro corner will become the highest-paid player in team history. If the dollars and cents on a looming mega extension don't show how important Gonzalez is to New England's prospects in 2026, let's look at his on-field production. Last season, Gonzalez allowed just 44.9% of his targets against him as the primary defender in coverage to be completed. In the playoffs, that completion rate dropped to 36.7%, showing he elevated in the highest-pressure moments. If the Patriots want to get back to the Super Bowl, Gonzalez will be a major piece of the puzzle.
The Dolphins offense has major questions after an offseason where the franchise overhauled the unit. Tua Tagovailoa , Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle are gone, and the keys of the offense under center are being handed to Malik Willis . One of the key holdovers from the previous regime, however, is De'Von Achane . The fourth-year running back has proven to be one of the more electrifying players in the entire NFL, possessing the ability to break off into the end zone with a single touch. He led the NFL with a 5.7 yards per carry average last season and posted a career-high 1,350 yards rushing during the regular season. What better way to help Willis as he embarks on his first season as the full-time starter in Miami than giving him the ability to hand it off to Achane, who can score in the blink of an eye?
New York is coming off a 2025 season in which the defense ranked at or near the bottom of the league in key categories. While most note that the Jets became the first team in NFL history to finish a season with zero interceptions, they also ranked 31st in total sacks (26) and dead last in pressure rate (28%). Naturally, those defensive inefficiencies forced New York to deploy a ton of resources on defense this offseason, including selecting Texas Tech edge rusher David Bailey with the No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft . Bailey was tied for the most sacks (14.5) and had the second-most pressures (81) in FBS last season. New York hopes he can come in and immediately help claw this pass rush out of the basement.
The Steelers' acquisition of Michael Pittman Jr. from the Colts is one of those moves that feels forgotten but will be quickly remembered once the regular season kicks off. Pittman is a pivotal answer to the No. 2 receiving question opposite DK Metcalf in Pittsburgh's offense. Last season, Metcalf led the team with 850 receiving yards. Meanwhile, the other Steelers receivers combined for just 866 yards receiving. Pittman comes in as not only a clear-cut second option for Aaron Rodgers , but the veteran quarterback (who averaged just 6.7 yards per attempt in 2025) could pepper the veteran on shorter routes. It wouldn't be surprising to see Pittman (who has the sixth-most receptions in the NFL over the last four seasons) lead the Steelers in targets.
The Ravens defense was mediocre in 2025, and a big reason why Jesse Minter was hired as head coach was to help restore Baltimore's reputation of having one of the toughest units in the league. One thing Minter will specifically need to focus on his getting that sack number up, as the Ravens were tied for the third-fewest sacks (28) in the league in 2025. To do that, they added Trey Hendrickson by signing the former Bengals edge rusher to a four-year, $112 million deal. Baltimore is looking for Hendrickson to bounce back from an injury-plagued 2025 season, where he was limited to just seven games due to a hip injury. Hendrickson has the third-most sacks (74.5) in the NFL since 2020, and it wasn't that long ago (2024) when he led the league with 17.5 sacks. If the Ravens get the 2024 version of Hendrickson, the defense will turn around overnight.
Cincinnati pushed the No. 10 overall pick into the middle of the table this offseason to land All-Pro defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence in a trade with the Giants . This blockbuster was part of the Bengals' overarching offseason effort to elevate the defense to a more respectable level. In 2025, the unit ranked 30th in points per game allowed (28.9), 31st in yards per game allowed (380.9) and last in yards per play allowed (6.2). They also allowed the most rushing yards per game (147.1) and the second-most yards per rush (5.2) in the league last season. While the team did bring in other notable veterans, Lawrence is the linchpin to get this defense to play at a higher level. If they become an average unit, it could be enough given the firepower on the offensive side of the ball.
All eyes in Cleveland are currently on who'll win the Week 1 job under center, and rightfully so. Whoever comes out on top, however, there will be plenty of pressure on the defense to not let games get out of hand and force them into a pass-heavy game script. That's where Ward comes in. The Browns just extended Ward to make him the highest-paid cornerback in the NFL by average annual value ($31.1 million), and it's easy to see why. He's just one of three corners to make the Pro Bowl in each of the past three seasons and is allowing a 51.5% completion rate over that stretch (third-lowest in the NFL). Ward also has an NFL-high 104 passes defended since entering the league in 2018. There's, of course, a giant hole left by edge rusher Myles Garrett , but Ward should continue to help keep this defense stout and take some of the burden off of the offense.
Daniel Jones was a revelation over the first half of the 2025 season, but let's not ignore the fact that Jonathan Taylor was going nuclear in the process. Over the first 10 games of the season, Taylor was averaging 113.9 rushing yards per game on a 6.0 yards per carry clip. He also tallied 15 rushing touchdowns over that stretch. Yes, his numbers declined down the stretch in conjunction with Jones suffering a season-ending injury, but he still finished third in rushing yards and first in rushing touchdowns. Taylor is the straw that stirs the drink of this Indy offense.
Tennessee's defense left little to be desired last season, allowing 27.6 points per game (31st in the NFL). That said, Jeffery Simmons was certainly not part of the problem. The star defensive tackle led his position group with 11.0 sacks in 2025 en route to being named first-team All-Pro for the first time in his career. The 29-year-old also signed a three-year, $105.8 million extension with the Titans that has him among the highest-paid players at his position. Naturally, the Titans' season will be judged by…

title: Cardinals Ossenfort: “We have no interest in trading Josh”
summary: Nobody is exactly sure when it happened. Or began. A rumor started about the Arizona Cardinals wanting to trade EDGE rusher Josh Sweat. Not a soul with the team has confirmed that they said this, or put it out for release. RELATED: CARDINALS FANS SEE SWEAT LEADING TEAM IN SACKS Maybe it began at a […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - NOVEMBER 23: Josh Sweat #10 of the Arizona Cardinals looks on from the line in the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at State Farm Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images) | Getty Images Nobody is exactly sure when it happened. Or began. A rumor started about the Arizona Cardinals wanting to trade EDGE rusher Josh Sweat. Not a soul with the team has confirmed that they said this, or put it out for release. RELATED: CARDINALS FANS SEE SWEAT LEADING TEAM IN SACKS Maybe it began at a neighborhood barber shop where everything is discussed and aired out among the clients in chairs and other patrons sitting in the waiting area. Perhaps it began on TikTok, like where most untruths begin, or started with one of those YouTube lawyers. On Monday, Cardinals GM Monti Ossenfort held a press conference and squashed any rumors that the franchise had zero interest in trading Sweat. “ There’s always a lot of talk that goes around that. We have no interest in trading Josh. We’re excited to have him, but some of those discussions are going to keep private, but excited to have Josh here. Had a great year last year. Excited for more good things out of him this year.” Trading Sweat would become a very dumb move. Both the Green Bay Packers and shipping Sweat back to the Eagles, have been linked to making contact with Arizona about trading Sweat to their respective clubs. #AZCardinals GM Monti Ossenfort on the rumors that OLB Josh Sweat had asked for a trade: "There is always a lot of talk around that. We have no interest in trading Josh. Some of those discussions we will keep private. We are excited to have Josh here." — Darren Urban (@Cardschatter) August 10, 2026 The Cardinals offense should be pretty good this year with a ton of talent on that side of the ball. The defense last year became a weak link with the team leading in seven contests late in the fourth quarter, yet could not hold the lead, which led to seven losses. So, the defense has to improve this season. Trading their best pass rusher for probably a second-round draft pick does not help this year’s roster whatsoever. With Ossenfort stating, “We have no interest in trading Josh,” that pretty much closes the narrative on the subject. That seems to be a firm response. But the question still lingers: When did this subject come to life? The origins came from one of those mysterious “sources.” Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon and Sweat had a great relationship and history together. Both were with the Philadelphia Eagles and involved with a successful franchise. Gannon was the DC when Sweat was already on the defense and spent two years together. In Gannon’s first year with the Eagles, Sweat was named to his first and only Pro Bowl, highlighted by his 11 sacks in his second year under Gannon. In 2021, Sweat signed a three-year extension with the Eagles. When his deal ran out after the 2024 season, Gannon wanted Sweat. Ossenfort then inked Sweat during free agency to a four-year contract worth up to $76.4 million, with $41 million guaranteed. When Gannon was fired, apparently Sweat was upset. On the March 9, 2026, PHNX Sports Cardinals Podcast , host Johnny Venerable stated: “I think that Josh Sweat will get traded. I’ll break some news right now. When (former Cardinals head coach) Jonathan Gannon got fired, Josh Sweat asked to be traded. Maybe he’s cool with (Cardinals defensive coordinator) Nick Rallis, so it’s fine now. I don’t know. But he has to get traded.” The very next day on NJ.com , which covers the Eagles and both New York clubs, Chris Franklin took on the story about the Cardinals maybe trading Sweat and stated: “The Eagles could turn to one of their former players who reportedly wants to leave his current team. On Monday, podcaster Johnny Venerable brought up edge rusher Josh Sweat as a player who could be on the move this offseason.” Two days later, on March 12, writer Jess Root of Cardinals Wire published an article with the heading, “Report: Josh Sweat requested trade from Arizona Cardinals.” Root wrote: “One of their best players requested a trade. Pass rusher Josh Sweat requested a trade after Gannon was fired. The front office told him no, and that was it to the story so far. Defensive coordinator Nick Rallis has been retained, so the defensive scheme shouldn’t change much, and Sweat possibly could be happy with that, which is why we haven’t heard much on the subject.” Sweat is a legitimate pass rusher. He had a career-high in his one year in the desert with 12.0 sacks, 17 QB hits, 28 pressures, 13 tackles for loss, and zero missed tackles. Arizona wouldn’t save much against the salary cap if they moved him, as he is due just $9.78 million in salary. But suddenly, the rumor of trading Sweat took off. All of this occurred during the free agency period and before April’s NFL draft. Sources: The #Cardinals have received trade calls on Pro Bowl DE Josh Sweat. Sweat had 12 sacks last season in his first year with Arizona and had a close relationship with Jonathan Gannon, whom the Cardinals moved on from. pic.twitter.com/ateZ6r4bi4 — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) May 26, 2026 On May 26, NFL Insider Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report tweeted out that Ossenfort had received calls from several NFL teams about the availability of Sweat via a trade. This set off a series of articles from several media outlets who reported the same thing. Sam Robinson wrote an article on Pro Football Rumors entitled, “Cardinals OLB Josh Sweat Drawing Trade Interest.” In the article, Robinson suggested: “Josh Sweat delivered a productive first season with the Cardinals, but the team finished 3-14. Three years remain on Sweat’s contract, but teams are exploring the possibility of Arizona unloading it. The Cardinals have received trade calls on Sweat. Arizona will surely set a high asking price. Arizona did not draft an edge rusher and returns a modest Sweat supporting cast. Sweat would be an appealing commodity due to his wildly team-friendly deal that runs through the 2028 season.” The PHNX Sports Cardinals Podcast put out its analysis on Sweat being considered in a trade. Host Bo Brack mentioned Schultz’s tweet and reported: “Here’s what’s interesting. A lot of people see this, and they just want to cut bait immediately. It’s not as simple as this. What do the Cardinals have as far as the pass rush goes without Josh Sweat? Your next closest sack getter for the Cardinals last season plays for the Baltimore Ravens, the ageless Calais Campbell.” The facts are, nobody from the Cardinals was saying anything about trading Sweat. When the rumor became bigger than huge, the front office finally had to address it and maintained they had no interest in moving their top pass rusher. All of this buzz surrounding the possibility of Sweat being shipped off to another team was created by one sports site followed by another, then another, and…. Schultz cited, “Sources: The Cardinals have received trade calls on Pro Bowl DE Josh Sweat.” The PHNX Sports Cardinals Podcast stated: “Report: The Cardinals are receiving trade calls.” Using words like “sources” and “reports” does not mean Josh Sweat nor his agent nor the Arizona front office nor the coaching staff have said anything about a trade percolating. For months, this was swirling around. Sweat not participating in OTAs and training camp only amplified this rumor. But get this: There isn’t any ink on Sweat actually asking for a trade once Gannon was fired. Another thing: In his recent press conference, Ossenfort didn’t try to deny that Sweat had asked for a trade, and he didn’t deny that other NFL clubs had been calling regarding the possibility of a trade. Which means both probably happened. Everyone gets that Sweat and Gannon held a close relationship. But the NFL is a business, and things happen. Like losing your job. Sweat signed a four-year deal, and if he is indeed not satisfied with being with Arizona now…

We'll have our guys out there." -HC Mike LaFleur says #AZCardinals starters will play vs #Raiders . Adds will play at least one series, including QB1 Jacoby Brissett — Paul Calvisi (@PaulCalvisi) August 11, 2026 Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur has come out and stated that this week’s contest against the Las Vegas Raiders this Thursday night, he is putting in his starters on both sides of the ball. RELATED: BIGGEST TAKEAWAY FROM HALL OF FAME GAME This is pretty much the norm for most NFL clubs. LaFleur says his starters will play two series, and then the second-team guys will take over. Most likely, the third-stringers will play the entire fourth quarter. In LaFleur’s press conference on Tuesday, he was asked, “Any update on who’s playing on Thursday?” His response: “They’re all going to play. So, we’ll have our guys out there. How much? It’s not going to be much. Could be one drive, max of two for those main guys. They’ll be playing, and they know that. So, that includes Jacoby.” Back in the day when the league played four exhibition games, no starters played in the first game, then two series in the second, a full quarter in the third game, and then finally the entire first half in the final match. So, two series in what is the Cardinals’ second preseason game sounds about right. And the coaching staff needs these guys to play in actual live game situations. The offensive line hasn’t gelled at all. Yet. The staff needs to see more of this receiver group, especially the 3-4 that conceivably could make this roster, like Jalen Brooks, Bryson Green, Ihmir Smith-Marsette, and the rookie Reggie Virgil. The defensive line needs some game action, and hopefully the Cardinals fanbase will see how DE Darius Robinson is progressing along with the addition of DT Roy Lopez. And, of course, the quarterback group. How will Jacoby Brissett look? Will we be able to finally see Gardner Minshew in action? Will Carson Beck pick up where he left off? summary: The Falcons have released the first “unofficial” depth chart of 2026 ahead of Friday’s preseason tilt with the Denver Broncos. There aren’t any huge surprises on it, especially after Stefanski shared his plans for the starters in this week’s matchup during media availability on Wednesday. There aren’t any huge surprises, but a few things of […]
full_text: Jul 30, 2026; Atlanta, Falcons, USA; Atlanta Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa (1) shown on the field during training camp at IBM Performance Field. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Falcons have released the first “unofficial” depth chart of 2026 ahead of Friday’s preseason tilt with the Denver Broncos. There aren’t any huge surprises on it, especially after Stefanski shared his plans for the starters in this week’s matchup during media availability on Wednesday. There aren’t any huge surprises, but a few things of note: Michael Penix Jr. and Jawaan Taylor are both noted on the depth chart as “injured” and do not appear in their respective positions’ depth charts right now. Cash Jones has been really fun to watch in camp, so I was a bit surprised to see him so low on the running backs depth chart, but it is pretty stacked. I’m hoping he can carve out a spot for himself regardless. Ethan Onianwa has been getting reps with the first team in practices, so I’m also mildly surprised he’s at the bottom of the depth chart at right tackle, especially since Michael Jerrell seemed to be getting fewer reps this week. Right tackle is absolutely a spot I’m keeping a close eye on this Friday against the Broncos. James Pearce Jr. landing in the third spot on his section of the DE depth chart is also mildly surprising given his performance last season, but obviously it’s much less so given that a six-game minimum suspension is expected to be handed down sooner rather than later. In general, the NFL tries to get those decisions to teams before roster cuts so they can plan accordingly. I double checked out of curiosity, and with the first unofficial depth chart of 2025, Pearce was listed second behind Leonard Floyd at the position. Via Raimondi: Stefanski: I'm very, very confident in where we are with Penix. #Falcons — Marc Raimondi (@marcraimondi) August 12, 2026 Tomorrow is a walkthrough with no media availability, and Friday night is obviously the first preseason game. Monday will be the last early morning practice, and then Wednesday and Thursday will be the joint practices in Indianapolis. What are your expectations for Friday’s game? title: Tua Tagovailoa named starting QB for preseason Week 1 against Broncos
summary: This barely qualifies as news if you’ve been following the quarterback competition in Atlanta, but Tua Tagovailoa will indeed be the starter for the first preseason game against the Denver Broncos. He’ll throw his first pass as a Falcon sometime after 7 p.m. on Friday night. The reason this is surprising has little to do […]
full_text: FLOWERY BRANCH, GEORGIA - MAY 27: Tua Tagovailoa #1 of the Atlanta Falcons runs through drills during OTA's at IBM Performance Field on May 27, 2026 in Flowery Branch, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images This barely qualifies as news if you’ve been following the quarterback competition in Atlanta, but Tua Tagovailoa will indeed be the starter for the first preseason game against the Denver Broncos. He’ll throw his first pass as a Falcon sometime after 7 p.m. on Friday night. The reason this is surprising has little to do with the respective performances of Tua or Michael Penix Jr., who have both been solid-to-excellent during training camp. It has everything to do with the fact that Tua is currently healthy and Penix has not been cleared for full team work yet, which has limited him to 7-on-7 work and individual drills in camp to this point. Given that Penix is still waiting on clearance from doctors and said on July 29 that he “ can’t afford to have somebody trip and fall and land on me right now ,” it would be stunning if he was going to start for Atlanta Friday night. Cooper Rush will serve as the #2 quarterback and Jack Strand will likely get significant work as the #3, per Kevin Stefanski. Penix will not play against Denver. The Falcons will play the starters Friday against Denver. Tua Tagovailoa will start the game, but Kevin Stefanski said he is not naming him the starter for the season. Stefanski said the starters will play for about 10 plays/one series, but will vary based on player how much… — Tori McElhaney (@tori_mcelhaney) August 12, 2026 Stefanski made sure to mention that this does not mean Tua has the starting job for 2026, which leaves the door ajar for Penix to steal it if Tagovailoa struggles and/or Penix gets cleared soon and looks stellar. As I’ve said repeatedly, that’s my ideal outcome given that Penix is under team control for 2026 and 2027 with a fifth year option for 2028, and because his deep passing skills open up some thrilling possibilities for explosive plays in Atlanta. But we do have to acknowledge that right now the picture looks like it has for weeks, which is Tua simply needing to be healthy to be the Week 1 starter in the regular season, with Penix starting the year as a backup and hoping to be ready if Tua is hurt or simply forcing his way into the starting job over time. The good news, as I mentioned, is that both quarterbacks have done well this summer. Tua has largely showed off his trademark accuracy in practice and has thrown a handful of impressive touchdowns along the way, while Penix has drawn rave reviews from quarterbacks coach Alex Van Pelt and Stefanski for the work he’s put in under center and what he’s been able to do in practice. On a totally level playing field this might be the league’s most hotly-contested quarterback battle, but that will have to wait until the team sees Penix’s participation ramp up to full. That’s a shame, of course, but as Penix himself has noted there is absolutely no sense in rushing this process and putting the young quarterback in a position where he might suffer a setback. Alex Van Pelt was asked whether he feels he has seen enough from Michael Penix Jr. during this early stretch of camp to still evaluate him in the QB competition if Penix isn’t cleared for 11-on-11 work until later this month. "Yes, I do. I think he has done everything he can… — Tori McElhaney (@tori_mcelhaney) August 11, 2026 Right now, my hope is that Tagovailoa plays well in limited action Friday and comes out of the game with no injuries, Penix is recovered enough soon to get to full-team work and make this competition really close down the stretch, and that both players enter the year able to help the Falcons. For now, Tua’s the preseason starter and the likely regular season starter, so I’m rooting hard for him to excel.

title: The Falcons’ 2026 offensive line and the Bill Callahan effect
summary: The Falcons’ offensive line earned major plaudits in 2022 for how well they ran the ball with limited resources. Despite being severely undermanned at quarterback and in the skill position areas, they managed to stay competitive in most games thanks to a punishing ground game. It was one of Arthur Smith’s few highlights during his […]
full_text: TAMPA, FL - DECEMBER 11: Ryan Neuzil #64 of the Atlanta Falcons lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on December 11, 2025 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Falcons’ offensive line earned major plaudits in 2022 for how well they ran the ball with limited resources. Despite being severely undermanned at quarterback and in the skill position areas, they managed to stay competitive in most games thanks to a punishing ground game. It was one of Arthur Smith’s few highlights during his time in Atlanta. It also showcased Dwayne Ledford’s capabilities as an offensive line coach. That season set the stage for a unified offensive line to develop into one of the league’s best units. They never lived up to those expectations. They couldn’t run the ball efficiently in numerous games in 2023. An inability to pass protect consistently with their five linemen against the top defenses cost them in 2024. Penalties were also problematic, with Matthew Bergeron, Chris Lindstrom, Jake Matthews, and Ryan Neuzil committing seven or more that season. Kaleb McGary’s season-ending injury set the unit back in 2025, leading to an overreliance on running to the left and an inability to convert in short-yardage situations. While the line did enough to enable Bijan Robinson and Tyler Allgeier to be successful, the fact that both backs were terrific played a major role in the team’s success on the ground. There’s no telling how injuries can impact an offensive line. Thankfully for the Falcons, Jawaan Taylor is set to start practicing after being activated off the PUP list. The veteran right tackle should have plenty to prove after multiple disappointing seasons in Kansas City. Entering the season with a healthy offensive line raises expectations for a unit that has been coasting more on reputation than overwhelming opposing fronts in recent seasons. Hiring a football scientist to coach them is one of the biggest reasons behind their potential elevation as a unit. The Bill Callahan effect Although it was disappointing for many within the organization to see Ledford not retained, the opportunity to bring in a highly regarded coach with over five decades of experience—especially one who worked closely with Kevin Stefanski during his best years in Cleveland—had to be taken. Bill Callahan has established himself as one of the best positional coaches in football, from his success at the college level with Wisconsin and Nebraska to his outstanding work with the Raiders, Jets, and Cowboys. His emphasis on attention to detail has brought out the best in several units. The Atlanta Journal-Constitution’s Daniel Flick wrote a fantastic feature about Callahan’s journey as a coach, highlighting his ability to develop talent. Matt Slauson and Brandon Moore, who are two former guards who started over 110 games, praised how relentless he is in teaching the technical nuances of blocking. From running arduous drills in the summer heat to conducting lengthy film sessions, players were consistently evolving under the coach who led the Raiders to their last Super Bowl appearance in 2003. Callahan assembles specific drills to help offensive linemen master their craft in various areas. He focuses on where centers, guards, and tackles must improve with their hands, footwork, and positioning to maximize their capabilities. That persistence led to players such as Lincoln Kennedy, D’Brickashaw Ferguson, Nick Mangold, Tyron Smith, Travis Fredrick, and Joel Bitonio having some of the best seasons in their prestigious careers under his tutelage. Exceptional coaching can make a decent unit turn into a very good group that knows how to get to their spots and handle their assignments. With how the Falcons are built, they are going to lean on a more diverse running game to stretch opposing fronts. That is where Callahan can use his expertise to work in unison with offensive coordinator Tommy Rees to impose their will on the ground. The overall blocking and schematic outlook will have to be on point for likely opening-day starter Tua Tagovailoa to operate functionally. Callahan can only do so much there, as the personnel up front will have to elevate their game for the passing game to have a genuine chance at being effective. Belief must be fulfilled In the last three seasons, the offensive line has blocked for a non-NFL-caliber starter in Desmond Ridder, a high-level backup and low-level starter in Taylor Heinicke, a limited 35-year-old (at the time) quarterback recovering from a torn Achilles in Kirk Cousins, and a wildly inconsistent left-handed gunslinger who has a tendency of being indecisive and holding onto the ball for too long in Michael Penix Jr. They will most likely enter this season blocking for a quarterback who looks to get the ball out fast with his quick release in Tagovailoa; if not, it’ll be a version of Penix the team has been working exstensively with. His style can make it easier on offensive linemen, particularly with how often screens were called in Miami. That is an area where the Falcons struggled mightily last season. Jake Matthews told The Athletic’s Josh Kendall that the team has spent ten minutes strictly working on screens during some practices. It’s a wise strategy with playmakers who can create after the catch like Bijan Robinson, Drake London, and ideally Zachariah Branch. The offensive line will still need to prove they can consistently block in pure drop-back situations. There were many instances last season when opponents would create easy openings off twists. It wasn’t solely because Elijah Wilkerson was overmatched at right tackle. Bergeron and Neuzil were caught missing assignments on several occasions. Those are two interior linemen that the franchise rewarded over the past two offseasons. Neuzil performed better than expected in his first full season as a starter, but he did have his issues in pass protection. The decision to reward Bergeron was surprising, given his comments from a few weeks ago about entering a contract year. Signing a guard to a massive, long-term deal after not coming close to playing at a Pro Bowl level raised plenty of eyebrows. As The Falcoholic’s own Aaron Freeman said best, he should have to show he can play like a top-tier guard before being accepted as one. While Bergeron did improve last season after an uneven 2024, it’s hard to process him being next to Tyler Smith as the league’s highest-paid guard, given Smith has been playing at a high level since entering the league in 2022. How Bergeron and Neuzil play will be one of the most significant factors in the offensive line’s performance this season. Chris Lindstrom is expected to continue playing at an All-Pro level. While there will be some concern about when Jake Matthews could decline, he didn’t show any signs of falling off last season. There are obvious questions about Taylor at right tackle, but he shouldn’t be considered a long-term answer. Bergeron and Neuzil are in positions where they need to be above-average starters. That must happen for the unit to flourish this season. Final pieces The growing uneasiness at right tackle is understandable, given Taylor’s recent injuries and Kansas City not hesitating to move on from him after three consecutive seasons of committing 13+ penalties. This is still a veteran who has played over 1,000 snaps every year in his career until last season. He possesses the experience to be a short-term solution. If he can’t stay healthy, there is reason to believe the new regime will be far more proactive in finding a capable replacement. They won’t make the same mistakes the previous regime did in failing to properly address the glaring holes at right tackle and wide receiver. As well as Wilkerson started, he became a liability in rough losses to San Francisco and Miami. The veteran never recovered from those ugly performances, yet the previous…

title: Ravens place QB Skylar Thompson on IR, sign replacement
summary: The Baltimore Ravens placed veteran quarterback Skylar Thompson on injured reserve on Wednesday, effectively ending his brief tenure with the team. Preseason IR placements are typically season-ending, but Thompson’s injury was described as “something small” by head coach Jesse Minter on Sunday. More likely, he will reach an injury settlement with the team and be […]
full_text: OWINGS MILLS, MARYLAND - JULY 29: Skylar Thompson #11 of the Baltimore Ravens practices on the first day of training camp at Under Armour Performance Center Baltimore Ravens on July 29, 2026 in Owings Mills, Maryland. (Photo by Jamie Sabau/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens placed veteran quarterback Skylar Thompson on injured reserve on Wednesday, effectively ending his brief tenure with the team. Preseason IR placements are typically season-ending, but Thompson’s injury was described as “something small” by head coach Jesse Minter on Sunday. More likely, he will reach an injury settlement with the team and be released in the coming days. Thompson, 29, had established himself as the Ravens’ third-string quarterback behind Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley in spring and summer practices. He could have even played himself into a 53-man roster spot with a strong preseason. Instead, Baltimore will now be looking for a new QB3. They auditioned four passers on Wednesday – Trevor Siemian, Jake Haener, Clayton Tune, and Austin Reed – and signed Reed, likely due to his connection with offensive coordinator Declan Doyle. He spent training camp with Doyle’s Bears last year and appeared in their first two preseason games, so he will be able to step in and take snaps right away. The Ravens also have Joey Fagnano, an undrafted rookie out of UConn who has been with the team since the spring. He beat out former Heisman winner Diego Pavia to be a training camp arm and he now has the opportunity to compete for a regular-season role. Baltimore also hosted wide receivers Alex Bachman, Bryce Ford-Wheaton, and A.T. Perry for workouts on Wednesday. The team could be considering a signing, but they are already 12 players deep at the position. Even with Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman resting in the preseason, the Ravens have more than enough depth for the rest of camp. This may have been simply a case of the Ravens using their quarterback tryouts to evaluate the available options at wide receiver.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: First impressions of Buffalo Bills new Highmark Stadium
summary: The new home of the Buffalo Bills is finally open, with Bills Mafia able to get their first look inside a gigantic project three years in the making during the “Return of the Blue & Red” practice this past Saturday. Thanks to an incredibly kind season ticket holder, my oldest and I were among those […]
full_text: The new home of the Buffalo Bills is finally open, with Bills Mafia able to get their first look inside a gigantic project three years in the making during the “Return of the Blue & Red” practice this past Saturday. Thanks to an incredibly kind season ticket holder, my oldest and I were among those fortunate enough to be among the first fans in the new place. That moment wasn’t lost on us, as a family with generations of Bills history dating back to the beloved stadium across the road. Though now reduced to rubble, the heart of Highmark Stadium lives on and wearing an incredible suit of accomplishment. Yes, the new stadium is “smaller” if you’re going by capacity, and the overall seating effect is a more cozy vibe thanks to the use of structural verticality. Yet at the same time it seems to dwarf the old place in sheer volume. Standing along the fence where the old Highmark Stadium is continually reduced to twisted rebar and rubble, we couldn’t help but long for one more trip inside those walls. The memories of time spent with family, watching some of the franchise’s best games and years, and then later Jim Kelly Football Camp on the same field — those will always stay with us. But we weren’t here to get caught up in the past, instead we were on a mission to find out if all the hype about the new house was true. Was it ever. The initial plan was to avoid making eye contact with the field before getting to the stairs down to our seats for the evening. That of course proved impossible, thanks to the open-air feeling of the concourse. Everywhere you looked, it was clear that an incredible amount of attention was spent on the finer details draped along walls, hung overhead, carved in sculpture, and painted on countless surfaces. It was as though we’d entered a small city dedicated to the Bills and populated exclusively by the fan base. We knew our seats for the evening would be top notch because of their location, but the quality only truly dawned on us as we descended the long stairway to Row 1 behind the team’s benches. Now, back in the day my family had great seats seven rows up near the 20-yard line on the visitors’ side. Great seats, especially during those cold winter days blessed with an appearance by the Sun. But these seats? They’re on another level. I only wish I’d had my actual camera rig to better share the experience. Nonetheless, I tried to capture a bit of the on-field action… Then the rain came, and we figured a few sprinkles or even a minor bit of more steadily falling water courtesy of Lake Erie wasn’t going to send us running. That is, until a Florida-like downpour began drenching us. Like the other all-weather diehards down front, we finally decided to head for the concourse. That’s where the real logjam happened, and where I see room for improvement. After about 10 minutes of standing on the stairs waiting to get under just the overhead canopy, it was clear that people who were now content being just at the head of the stairwell didn’t get the memo. No one else could make their way to cover. It’s a concern. That rain wasn’t a major deal this night since it was only a rainstorm. Things would have been far different had it been a severe storm loaded with lightning, or even damaging wind. As I see it, the biggest change in comparison to the old stadium that’s contributing to the situation is the lack of a long “alley” between the seats and the concourse. Feeling as though we’d jumped in the lake at that point, we decided to check out more of the new place away from the rain. We made our way around the oval, which felt a bit like navigating Hong Kong traffic during rush hour while everyone was busy checking out stuff. With a bit more elbow room we may have caught more of the finer details, but we were intent on covering as much ground as possible before the end of the scrimmage. Eventually, we hit the stairs upward, intent on getting as high up as possible before meeting up with a certain Skarekrow. Telling you the new stadium excels at height is a disservice to what they’ve built. The fans up top really are now somewhat higher above the field than before, but yet closer to the gridiron compared to the Red Rocks-like expanse of the old stadium’s upper deck. We eventually settled in with Skarekrow and for the remainder of the practice. Wanting just one more view from those front-row seats, we made our way all the way back down and against a mass of humanity looking for the quickest exit. Expected at that point, a crowd of folks had gathered along the wall, hoping to catch the attention of players. There were plenty of players going around playing catch with younger fans in the crowd. Then someone began throwing foam footballs into the seats. A couple darts later, we realized it was Maxwell Hairston tossing up inaugural season footballs, and only after he’d added his signature across them. Later, Christian Benford would make his way around to sign those same footballs and more for everyone gathered close to the sidelines. It was clear how hyped the team was to be in the new house, and they were pumped to be in front of their home fans. Only then realizing we’d forgotten to check out the work done outside the stadium, off we went to find the family area and those huge bison all lit up. I can’t wait to see how cool that trio looks when snow begins piling up! It was time to head back to the thruway, content we’d seen all there was time to enjoy. Staying in the stadium late meant missing the fireworks show outside the stadium, which was an admirable team plan to filter people outside at the end of the evening. The FOMO was real, believing I’d missed a great chance to get some photos of Highmark Stadium bathed in fireworks. Before heading out, we decided to walk back toward the main entrance to see the stadium lit up at night. As we got into our car to head home, out of nowhere a new batch of seemingly random fireworks came to life from within the rubble of the old stadium — just a handful of steps from our parking spot. FOMO averted! It felt like a poignant sendoff to a stadium that means so much to my family and me. It’s true that whatever plan they have for the old place will never surpass the house that Ralph C. Wilson Jr. built. The new Highmark may prove to be a difficult ticket this season and into the future if the team continues its winning ways. We may not get to see an actual game, but we couldn’t be more grateful to have been a part of opening the new Highmark Stadium. Where there are complaints and seemingly endless threads laying into some of the sight lines and more, the bigger accomplishment seems to have gotten lost. It was a huge undertaking to bring this to life during the 21st century in small-town Western New York, and to do so a couple football fields away from the old stadium. I understand some fans’ angst over myriad issues, which of course includes all the costs involved from planning, to building the space, and enjoying the amenities. I can’t speak to the cost of concessions since we didn’t buy anything. Will the perceived blue-collar fans be priced out long term? That’s to be decided. As for those comments on some of the seats? If you’re after the best seat, or just looking for an excuse to bash the work done — understand that even the best seat’s view in any stadium pales in comparison to watching it at home. The front office has already stated that it will work toward meeting and addressing each and every concern in the coming weeks, and before the Week 2 regular-season home opener. What can’t be understated is how much work was done to make the new Highmark a full stack amplifier of Bills Mafia. To that end, the sound system is impressive, and I couldn’t stop thinking how good an in-the-round concert may be inside its walls. Do yourself a favor and put the new Highmark Stadium on your to-do list, if even just to tour the space. We’re already planning to go back and see all the things we missed the first night.
author: Matt Byham

title: Can Chauncey Gardner-Johnson contain himself Week 1 vs. Houston Texans?
summary: In Week 1 of the regular season the Buffalo Bills will be traveling to face their kryptonite in the Houston Texans. Of course things have not gone well in Houston for Buffalo, as the team has suffered three straight losses including one in the playoffs. In fact, the Bills have not won in Houston since […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 15: C.J. Gardner-Johnson #8 of the Houston Texans in coverage during an NFL football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at NRG Stadium on September 15, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images In Week 1 of the regular season the Buffalo Bills will be traveling to face their kryptonite in the Houston Texans. Of course things have not gone well in Houston for Buffalo, as the team has suffered three straight losses including one in the playoffs. In fact, the Bills have not won in Houston since 2006. This year the meeting will have a little more of an edge due to safety C.J. Gardner Johnson taking on his old team. The question is will he be able to keep his emotions in check? Gardner-Johnson only managed three games with the Texans at the start of last season before being let go. Coaches felt that he relied too much on his own freelance instincts rather than executing what the team wanted. There was also a lot of friction in the locker room where Gardner-Johnson would blame his teammates for the mistakes taking place on the field. He was asked about his departure at training camp on Thursday and there is certainly no love lost: #Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson sounded off about the Houston Texans after @SalSports asked him about playing his former team in Week 1. Houston released him after 3 games last season. "All the B.S. that came out was lies." #BillsMafia pic.twitter.com/eugpJNkFDf — Andy Young (@AndyYoungTV) August 6, 2026 Now he will obviously be a ball of fire in this game to start the season, however must keep it professional. The last thing the team would want is Gardner-Johnson picking up a personal foul call that could get him ejected. Another possibly is his desire to make an impact play could result in him being out of position and allowing a big play instead. Instead, the Bills will be hoping for the positive impact that could happen with someone playing their former team. We saw it with former receiver Cole Beasley who had arguably the best game of his Buffalo career taking on the Dallas Cowboys in a Thanksgiving matchup back in 2019. If Gardner-Johnson is able to generate a turnover, that could end up being the difference. This could also fire up teammates to have his back and even give just a little more effort. Are you worried about the emotional aspect of this reunion for Gardner-Johnson or excited for this storyline to unfold?

title: Buffalo Bills 2026 scouting report: inside linebacker Otis Reese IV
summary: The Buffalo Bills have worked to add linebacker depth over the last few seasons. It wasn’t long ago where the team had to call A.J. Klein in from his RV vacation to start in playoff games, so that strategy makes sense. Adding depth to the team’s starters is essential, and while the salary cap limits […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 10: Otis Reese IV #41 of the Tennessee Titans looks on during the national anthem prior to an NFL Football game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on November 10, 2024 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills have worked to add linebacker depth over the last few seasons. It wasn’t long ago where the team had to call A.J. Klein in from his RV vacation to start in playoff games, so that strategy makes sense. Adding depth to the team’s starters is essential, and while the salary cap limits just how much the team can pour into any one positional group, the Bills have done a good job scouring the late rounds of the NFL Draft for depth pieces. Sometimes, those pieces even slipped through the whole draft and signed with clubs as free agents. In today’s edition of “91 players in 91 days,” we discuss a former UDFA looking to make an impact in his second stint with the Bills. _____________________________________________________________________________ Name: Otis Reese IV Number: 30 Position: ILB Height/Weight: 6’3” 214 lbs. Age: 28 (29 on 7/2/2027) Experience/Draft: 3; signed with the Tennessee Titans following the 2023 NFL Draft College: Tennessee Acquired: Signed with Buffalo on 8/6/2026 Financial situation (per Spotrac): Reese IV signed a one-year deal with Buffalo, and that contract is worth $1.075 million if he makes the roster this season. The Bills can release him at any point without carrying a dead cap charge, as there are no guarantees on the deal. 2025 Recap: Reese IV began the offseason with the Titans, having signed a one-year contract prior to the start of the free agency period. Reese IV did not appear in Tennessee’s first preseason game, and the Titans released him on August 13, just four days after that first exhibition contest. On September 23, he signed with Buffalo’s practice squad. He remained on the practice squad until October 7, which is when Buffalo released him. Reese IV did not appear in a game while with Buffalo. On November 17, Reese IV signed with the New England Patriots’ practice squad, and while he did not appear in a game with the Patriots, he remained with the club through the Super Bowl. He signed a reserve/futures deal on February 11, and he spent the offseason and early part of training camp with New England. The Patriots released him on July 31, just a week before he signed with Buffalo for the second time. Positional outlook: Reese IV is one of seven players listed at inside linebacker on the current Buffalo roster. Dorian Williams, Terrel Bernard, Joe Andreessen, Keonta Jenkins, Theron Gaines, and Jimmy Ciarlo are the others. Kaleb Elarms-Orr is listed at linebacker, but he fits as an inside linebacker in Buffalo’s scheme. 2026 Offseason: Reese IV signed with the Bills a short time ago, so he’s been re-acclimating to the team. The defense is entirely different this time around. He is healthy and he has participated in practices to date. 2026 Season outlook: Barring something crazy, Reese IV is not going to make Buffalo’s 53-man roster. At best, he’s likely fighting with Theron Gaines, Keonta Jenkins, and Jimmy Ciarlo for space on the practice squad after final cuts. Frankly, I think all three of those players might have a leg up on Reese IV, though the Bills could keep him over a rookie like Gaines. Reese IV played in 20 games for Titans between the 2023 and 2024 seasons, appearing primarily on special teams. He totaled 38 tackles on 179 defensive snaps and 248 special teams snaps, so it’s possible that he could show himself to be good enough on special teams where the Bills might want to keep him around longer. Chris Trapasso released his 53-man roster projection on Monday, and he had the Bills keeping just four inside linebackers: Bernard, Williams, Elarms-Orr, and Jenkins. I agree with him on three of the four, and I also think that the Bills are going to keep another body here just to be safe. Give me Andreessen and Ciarlo over Jenkins, as they both have the size, fight, and special teams utility to fit into what defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard wants to do while also providing depth in the game’s third phase. However you slice it, Otis Reese IV would have to be outstanding in a short period of time to show himself worthy of a roster spot this season. Never say never, but I will say that it’s unlikely that he makes the team this season.

title: Addressing ridiculousness of Josh Allen reportedly causing frustration inside Bills coaching staff
summary: The Buffalo Bills are who they are because of Josh Allen. He’s rightfully become an NFL superstar over the past six seasons with immaculate quarterback play and overpowering tenacity on the football field. And now there’s a report he’s causing an internal rift within the Bills coaching staff. Let’s address aid report. The Athletic’s Mike […]
full_text: ROCHESTER, NEW YORK - JULY 29: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills and head coach Joe Brady talk during training camp at St. John Fisher University on July 29, 2026 in Rochester, New York. (Photo by Joe Hrycych/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills are who they are because of Josh Allen. He’s rightfully become an NFL superstar over the past six seasons with immaculate quarterback play and overpowering tenacity on the football field. And now there’s a report he’s causing an internal rift within the Bills coaching staff. Let’s address aid report. The Athletic’s Mike Sando went on Damon Amendolara’s show “D.A. Live” and said the following: “They’re going to be good. Josh Allen’s going to make them good. But within that, like the greatness or is it too much of a good thing when your play-caller goes from kind of being your confidante and maybe a little more of a friend than the head coach could be, to now going into that head coaching job. I think that is an interesting transition to make, when clearly before with (Bills ex-coach) Sean McDermott, he was in charge, also a defensive pedigree.” I’m sure he went along with a lot of stuff Josh Allen wanted to do, but there was a little bit more of a check and balance there, I think. And so now: What does it mean? Is Josh Allen more empowered? I’ve heard whispers and people complaining a little bit in the league about the fact Josh Allen gets to kind of do the pass protections how he wants them, I think that’s been a little bit of a source of frustration on the staff, at times, in the past. Is that a good or a bad thing, if that’s enabled more? Those would be the concerns. Not so much Josh Allen, I think we know he’s going to be a star. Just as you try to get over the top, are these fine-tune changes good? Maybe not quite as good.” Here’s the video: The Athletic’s Mike Sando @SandoNFL reveals the Josh Allen power dynamic causing frustration inside the Bills coaching staff. #BuffaloBills pic.twitter.com/iM4Ns33RWH — Damon Amendolara (@DamonAmendo) August 10, 2026 First things first — I respect Sando and his reporting. He’s been covering the NFL since 1998 and spent a long time at ESPN before joining The Athletic in 2019. I’m certainly not insinuating Sando is fabricating anything here. We’re almost assured to never know who “league sources” might be — and notice the term “league” used instead of “team” — and listening to, then re-reading Sando’s quote did not not compute for me. The gist of it reads like grasping at straws to the nth degree. There’s no more vital dynamic in the NFL than the head coach and quarterback relationship — particularly when a team is good. From that, to insinuate a coordinator labeled as a “confidant” of the superstar quarterback moving into a head-coaching role is a bad idea feels silly. Now, that is also not to suggest I’m guaranteeing and know for a fact right now that Brady will become a tremendous head coach in Buffalo. And I understand the checks and balances idea the beginning of Sando’s quote is referencing. But when it’s deemed that the past head coach simply wasn’t good enough — beyond a checks and balance dynamic provided — it makes perfect sense to elevate a coordinator with a strong relationship with your MVP caliber quarterback. The second part of Sando’s quote is distinctly more forced, in my opinion. Allen has absolutely earned the right to be as “empowered” within his organization as any quarterback in the NFL. It would be a much bigger — and more sensible — story if, entering Year 9, Allen did not have final say on offensive-line protections in front of him. Nick Sabato of the Niagara Gazette and Lockport Union-Sun Journal tweeted the following on this topic: This was after the Texans loss. #Bills https://t.co/Sq9I568AFe pic.twitter.com/fPTZiLgwJq — Nick Sabato (@NickSabatoGNN) August 10, 2026 Obviously every report has to start somewhere, but there was not one whisper about this from local beat reporters or national insiders during the 2025 season, a year Allen took a career high in sacks. Sabato confirms that now in August 2026. Plus, the offensive staff has hardly changed from a season ago. How and why would this “source of frustration” be manifesting now? In fairness to him and as a sign of his integrity as an analyst, Sando did eventually send another tweet on his Allen report for clarity sake: I can phrase this better. Bills have been very high in five-man protection rate. Staff held back coaching protections as much as one might imagine, with a "just let him play" philosophy. Let the QB handle the free rusher. Not everyone would have done it that way. https://t.co/rwjb7xM3qr — Mike Sando (@SandoNFL) August 11, 2026 As mentioned, Allen’s sacks were a bit of an issue last year, so regularly letting the quarterback deal with the free rusher could be problematic. Then again, before 2025, Allen had become one of the most challenging quarterbacks to sack in all of football over multiple seasons. Again, he deserves the right to do whatever he wants at the line regarding his protections, and, yes, can handle a free rusher better than any quarterback in football. We’ll see how everything transpires this season regarding Allen’s protection, Buffalo’s offense under Brady, and the Bills overall performance. But to suggest the team used a faulty process to come to its decision on a head coach because of his strong connection to the quarterback is flimsy at best. And it’s absurd to imply Allen having control over his protections is a negative. Overall, this felt more like distant speculation relayed to Sando than certifiable fact, and it’s gotten zero corroboration from any other NFL media members. To me, trying to push Allen as a source of frustration inside the Bills organization is a total nonstarter.
