title: What to make of the Cowboys unofficial depth chart
summary: Dallas Cowboys training camp is in full swing with roster battles galore! Sorting out which guys will land where is a fun exercise, but often one of futility this early in August. That doesn’t stop us from trying, and when the team gives us breadcrumbs, we gladly accept. On Tuesday, the Dallas Cowboys released their […]
full_text: Dallas Cowboys training camp is in full swing with roster battles galore! Sorting out which guys will land where is a fun exercise, but often one of futility this early in August. That doesn’t stop us from trying, and when the team gives us breadcrumbs, we gladly accept. On Tuesday, the Dallas Cowboys released their first unofficial depth chart … Cowboys’ first unofficial depth chart pic.twitter.com/4q9ZfMSjH4 — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) August 11, 2026 While things can change (and likely will) over the course of the next month, this at least gives us a clue as to how things might shape up. But more than that, it offers up some subtle hints to how the coaches view these players at the moment. Here are some quick-hit observations from this unofficial first depth chart. OFFENSE Quarterback Battle Joe Milton III has shown enough improvement to be a smidge ahead of new free agent addition Sam Howell for the backup QB job. However, the team went out of its way to use the word “or” so this tells us that this battle is far from over. Running Back Hierarchy The Cowboys clearly love last year’s rookie running back draft picks, as Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah are listed at RB2 and RB3, respectively. That means it’s another uphill battle for Malik Davis, which has become an annual tradition for him at this point. Tight End Shuffle File this under “saw it coming,” but Brevyn Spann-Ford is the team’s undisputed TE2, with former second-round pick Luke Schoonmaker holding the third spot. The two have officially swapped places from this time a year ago. Wide Receiver Depth Veterans Jonathan Mingo and Marquez Valdes-Scantling get the seasoned nod for the fifth WR spot. However, rookie UDFA Camden Brown has turned enough heads in camp to be this year’s dark-horse candidate to sneak onto the roster. The Offensive Line The starting offensive line is exactly as expected, with Tyler Guyton remaining the frontrunner at left tackle. Ajani Cornelius is a name who stands out. Last year, the team preserved a roster spot for him as a stash-and-develop project. Now, he’s slid down to the third string, and he might have to earn his way onto the roster by shifting inside to guard. Interior Line Depth Speaking of interior OL depth, keep an eye on both Trevor Keegan and Nick Leverett. At least one of these guys is likely to join T.J. Bass on the roster to provide the team with some depth along the interior. Remember, this is year two of Klayton Adams, which is another opportunity to put his stamp in the trenches. Expect some new faces. DEFENSE The Scheme Shift The 3-4 defense is alive and well. The team already disclosed they were switching to a 3-4 after running a 4-3 for the last 13 years, but seeing it on paper is still a bit weird. But in a good way. Interior Anchor Get used to hearing Otito Ogbonnia’s name, because he is firmly anchored in the starting unit, alongside Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark. Setting the Edge Rashan Gary and Donovan Ezeiruaku are the starting outside linebackers, but things get really interesting after that. The depth hierarchy goes James Houston, Sam Williams, and then Malachi Lawrence. Obviously, seeing a first-round investment on the third team isn’t ideal. Lawrence has shown flashes lately, but this depth chart placement could serve as a subtle, public hint that he still has a ways to go. On the flip side, Houston appears to be the top backup edge right now. This trio of backups will be interesting to watch once preseason action rolls around. Linebacker There are no surprises at linebacker, but keep an eye on last year’s UDFA Justin Barron. He has already moved ahead of Curtis Robinson, who was a free-agent signing the team signed because Christian Parker liked what he saw during their time together in Denver. Cornerback Competition Seeing Shavon Revel edge out Cobie Durant is exciting, and that’s because the veteran Durant has genuinely impressed in camp, so this speaks volumes about the incredible progress the second-year corner has made over the last couple of weeks. But to be clear, this is another one of their “or” labels, meaning that second boundary corner gig is firmly up for grabs. Safety The safety spots are exactly as expected. Not surprisingly, the slot corner is now simply labeled as a “DB,” which I believe stands for “Dynamic Back,” considering Caleb Downs is the one slotted there. SPECIAL TEAMS Specialists What do you want to see here? The team has two All-Pro players in the three key spots, and that’s about as impressive as it gets. Long snapper Trent Sieg is not an All-Pro, but his mom still loves him. The only thing of interest is that Jaydon Blue is listed as the team’s backup kick returner and Caleb Downs is their backup punt returner. Hmmm.
author: Dan Rogers

title: 3 Cowboys UDFAs making cases for roster spots
summary: Every spring, hundreds of college football players miss out on the dream of being drafted into the NFL. But their real goal, actually making an NFL roster, is still very much alive. We usually see at least one or two undrafted free agents make the Dallas Cowboys’ 53-man roster, and there are three such rookies […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Oxnard, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys receiver Camden Brown (6) catches the ball at training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Every spring, hundreds of college football players miss out on the dream of being drafted into the NFL. But their real goal, actually making an NFL roster, is still very much alive. We usually see at least one or two undrafted free agents make the Dallas Cowboys’ 53-man roster, and there are three such rookies in camp who are making solid cases in 2026. Undrafted talent has done plenty to help the Cowboys through the years. This summer alone, coming back from last year’s team are Brandon Aubrey, KaVontae Turpin, Terence Steele, Brevyn Spann-Ford, Markquese Bell, and Alijah Clark. Those first four names are pretty much roster locks, and Bell and Clark should both be competitive for the bottom of the safety depth chart this year. This year’s crop of UDFAs had 11 players: RB Dominic Richardson, WRs Camden Brown and Jordan Hudson, TEs Michael Trigg and D.J. Rodgers, OTs Sidney Fugar and Shiyazh Pete, DTs Tommy Dunn, Kelvin Gilliam, and D.J. Withers, and LB Langston Patterson. None of them were going to have an easy time with unusually deep position groups going into camp, and Richardson has already been waived at running back. But some are faring better, to the point that they may have a chair when the music stops on August 30th. WR Camden Brown When the UDFA signings were announced, SMU’s Jordan Hudson was the receiver most were focused on. But Brown, who transferred from Auburn to George Southern for his senior year , is now the talk of the WR competition. Buried on the Tigers’ bench for most of his college career, his one big year with the Eagles was enough to get him on the NFL radar. Now, it appears the Cowboys may have found one of this year’s diamonds in the rough. Camden Brown with a TD grab. He’s been one of the UDFAs making a strong early impression pic.twitter.com/oWUlt8KNlS — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 1, 2026 Camden Brown with an impressive TD grab pic.twitter.com/jDx160UitH — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 8, 2026 Camden Brown has officially entered the mix now at wide receiver .. This rookie is gonna change numbers ! He wears 6 now but he’ll get another one here soon! — Nick Eatman (@nickeatman) August 9, 2026 UDFA WR Camden Brown getting reps with the 2s today pic.twitter.com/tiCl3fAtQn — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 9, 2026 Yet another athletic Camden Brown grab, but just one foot in. Alijah Clark: “That’s a great college catch.” Brown scores a TD one play later pic.twitter.com/Pl7BrtdI2w — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 9, 2026 We’re no strangers to late-round or even undrafted WRs becoming contributors in Dallas. The big names go back to Miles Austin and Cole Beasley, with Ryan Flournoy seemingly on his way. But others like Cedrick Wilson and Noah Brown have defied expectations to be solid role players, worthy of a coveted 53-man roster spot. Right now, Brown is looking like a similar find. We’ve heard way more about him this summer than seventh-round pick Anthony Smith, or other down-roster candidates like Jonathan Mingo, Marquez Valdes-Scantling, or Traeshon Holden. There’s still plenty of time left for the winds to shift, but as it stands, Brown’s momentum has him on the roster bubble. TEs D.J. Rodgers & Michael Trigg When fourth-year veteran Princeton Fant suffered a season-ending injury early in camp, the Cowboys didn’t rush out for another experienced option. They did add Zack Kuntz to the mix, but he’s only appeared in two career games since being a seventh-round pick in 2023. They seem content to allow their inexperienced prospects to battle for a potential fourth spot at TE, with Rodgers and Trigg leading the way. Even before Fant’s injury, many had Trigg as the fourth man at tight end. Some were even thinking he could challenge for Luke Schoonmaker’s job. And yes, Trigg has been as advertised in terms of his athleticism and pass-catching skills. Michael Trigg with a tough catch in traffic pic.twitter.com/Gr5GtFA1qY — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 4, 2026 Michael Trigg sliding grab to end practice pic.twitter.com/TZSxj0PXZU — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 6, 2026 When asked about Trigg’s progress and roster potential in a recent media session, Brian Schottenheimer noted that Trigg is able to do special things as a receiving TE. But Coach was quick to shift to D.J. Rodgers, highlighting his all-around game and very important skill of run blocking. It sounded like things were still very even between the two UDFAs, and one could argue that superior blocking is more important at the bottom of the TE depth chart than receiving ability. The Cowboys may not even keep a fourth TE, given FB Hunter Luepke’s ability to be an emergency option. In past seasons, Princeton Fant would generally get called up from the practice squad for his game action. So unless Dallas is going to part ways early with Schoonmaker, it’s possible that the most Rodgers, Trigg, or any other TE can hope for is a spot with the practice team. That said, down-roster spots are sometimes about securing future assets. Trigg was a well-known commodity in this year’s draft class, who only went undrafted due to character concerns. If he shows well in preseason games, or Rodgers for that matter, the Cowboys may be worried about risking them to the waiver process. That’s another way one might make the 53, even if they don’t dress for most games.

title: Why the Cowboys’ performance against the Rams is exciting
summary: The Dallas Cowboys revamped defense faced its first test on Tuesday in a scrimmage against the Los Angeles Rams. Despite keeping it a vanilla, close-to-the-vest scrimmage, the Cowboys seemed to win the day against Matthew Stafford and the Rams. This doesn’t mean the Cowboys will be heading to the NFC Championship game tomorrow. A scrimmage […]
full_text: Woodland Hills, CA - August 11:Rams Jurquez Hunter (27) gets wrapped up by Cowboys defenders during Rams joint practice with the Dallas Cowboys on Tuesday, August 11, 2026. (Photo by David Crane/MediaNews Group/Los Angeles Daily News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys revamped defense faced its first test on Tuesday in a scrimmage against the Los Angeles Rams. Despite keeping it a vanilla, close-to-the-vest scrimmage, the Cowboys seemed to win the day against Matthew Stafford and the Rams. back in Oxnard … and the #Cowboys new-look defense under Christian Parker aced that joint practice test. the Rams are formidable, and a standard-bearer for the NFC, but didn’t look it today. and that’s what i needed to see. — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) August 11, 2026 This doesn’t mean the Cowboys will be heading to the NFC Championship game tomorrow. A scrimmage like this is just one piece of the pie with three preseason games, another scrimmage against the New Orleans Saints, and the rest of training camp left to go. However, it’s encouraging to see the defensive messaging from Christian Parker start to take shape, especially since last year’s scrimmage against the Rams didn’t go so well. The defense was manhandled all day by what would turn into one of the NFL’s top offenses. It would be a sign of things to come for what would become a historically bad defense. Most of the starters on offense for the Rams returned from their NFC Championship runner-up squad, headlined by Matthew Stafford, Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, and Kyren Williams. Reports from the joint practice showed the Cowboys defense had the L.A. offense all out of sorts, headlined by Justin Barron’s three interceptions against Stafford and then the second-team offense. The pass rush seemed to come alive as well, with Donovan Ezeiruaku and Quinnen Williams each recording a would-be sack if it were a live game. Ezeiruaku has had a quiet training camp thus far, so to see him step up in a big moment is encouraging. Even Marist Liufau and Isaiah Land recorded a pair of sacks against the second-team offense. Another second-year player, Shavon Revel, had a solid performance with two pass breakups and a forced fumble in his opportunities . His physicality was part of what made him one of the top corners last offseason, so it was nice to see that come back now fully healthy. The defense’s physical nature and leadership are showing up for Dallas— both traits that even Stephen Jones admitted to not having on that side of the ball a season ago. Dak Prescott can finally take a back seat and watch the veterans on defense like Williams, Kenny Clark, DeMarvion Overshown, and Rashan Gary get their players ready when it’s time to put their words into action. On Tuesday against the Rams, those words were loud and meaningful as the defense showed some teeth, something that was not around in 2025.
author: Brandon_Loree

title: Cowboys news: A good day across the board for Dallas vs the Rams
summary: Last year, Jimmy Garoppolo and Stetson Bennet IV looked like Pro Bowlers against the Cowboys defense in the Ranms scrimmage. It would be a sign of things to come for Dallas’ historically bad unit. Fast forward 12 months later, and it feels like an entirely different defense headlined by newly extended Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark, […]
full_text: Aug 11, 2026; Woodland Hills, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys linebacker Donovan Ezeiruaku (6) and Los Angeles Rams offensive tackle Alaric Jackson (77) during a joint practice at the Rams Practice Facility. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Last year, Jimmy Garoppolo and Stetson Bennet IV looked like Pro Bowlers against the Cowboys defense in the Ranms scrimmage. It would be a sign of things to come for Dallas’ historically bad unit. Fast forward 12 months later, and it feels like an entirely different defense headlined by newly extended Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark, Rashan Gary, a healthy DeMarvion Overshown, and Caleb Downs. Tuesday’s scrimmage was certainly a step in the right direction for Christian Parker’s unit. Christian Parker, Cowboys’ defense aces joint test vs. Rams – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com Second-year players Donovan Ezeiruaku and Shavon Revel looked really good against the Rams. Every day, every rep, the Dallas Cowboys’ defense is being put to the fire in Oxnard by the high-powered offense. So far, they’ve looked great in those battles, but the first real test arrived by way of a joint practice against Sean McVay’s offense and the Los Angeles Rams, led by former Super Bowl champion and reigning NFL MVP Matthew Stafford. They passed with flying colors. Notes and observations from Cowboys-Rams joint practice in Southern California – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram Justin Barron looked like Fred Warner in his best day of training camp. Young linebacker hauls in three interceptions However, the star of the show for the defense was Justin Barron. A second-year linebacker out of Syracuse who spent most of his rookie year on the practice squad recorded three interceptions during Tuesday’s practice — one on reigning NFL MVP Matthew Stafford and two on Stetson Bennett IV. After practice, Barron received a ton of praise from his defensive teammates. Why Cowboys OC Klayton Adams called the plays in team’s joint practice with LA Rams – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News Brian Schottenheimer let Klayton Adams get comfortable with calling plays in the scrimmage. Cowboys offensive coordinator Klayton Adams called plays during Tuesday’s practice. It was a decision that’s been reflective of what Schottenheimer’s done in his second season. He’ll be the play-caller on game day, but he’s also wanted to be more involved with the defense this year. Schottenheimer said he’s spent more time in defensive personnel rooms and with first-time defensive coordinator Christian Parker . That’s also given more responsibility to Adams, who hasn’t been a full-time play-caller in the NFL yet. What Dak Prescott and Brian Schottenheimer said about Cowboys-Rams practice – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram Even though the offense had a good day, Dak Prescott is still looking for ways to improve. Dak Prescott On how the practice went from his perspective: “First time going up against another jersey, another team. I thought it was good. Is it quite where we want to be? No, not necessarily, but we started off hitting some runs, being physical. It’s hard being able to tell what exactly a gain is when guys aren’t going to the ground. But then as it developed, getting into the red zone and in the two-minute, getting called down where it looked like it was right at the sticks, that’s part of practice. I felt good about it.” Dallas Cowboys’ first unofficial depth chart reveals telling details at multiple positions ahead of the preseason – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports The first unofficial depth chart highlighted a few position battles happening in training camp. Tight end and running back offer early storylines On offense, the depth chart holds few surprises, but the tight end order stands out. Brevyn Spann-Ford is listed ahead of Luke Schoonmaker, who in turn sits above undrafted free agents Michael Trigg and DJ Rogers. Spann-Ford has been viewed as the favorite for the TE2 role thanks to his contributions in the run game and his development as a pass catcher. Him being listed behind Jake Ferguson fuels those suspicions. Meanwhile, Schoonmaker remains listed as the No. 3 tight end, though Trigg in particular is expected to continue competing for that spot on the 53-man roster. 6 reasons the Quinnen Williams extension is a big win for the Cowboys – Dan Rogers, Blogging the Boys The Quinnen Williams extension has been praised across the NFL, which is a win for the Jones family. Reason #1 – immediate cap relief, roster flexibility Before the extension, Williams was carrying base salaries of $21.6 million and $25.5 million, respectively, over the next two seasons. With a new deal, the team now has immediate salary cap relief, freeing up roughly $35 million over the next two years. This immediate cap savings gives the front office the flexibility to keep the roster loaded with talent as they continue to maximize the window with Dak Prescott. This could mean a lot of different things. Daily discussion question: Who do you predict will shine on Saturday night?

title: Broncos recently worked out safety Tyler Rapp
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country. The Denver Broncos tout one of the best secondaries in the league. The star power and depth at cornerback is evident, and the team has an underrated starting duo at safety with Brandon Jones and Talanoa Hufanga. However, the Broncos might be interested in adding some experienced depth at safety. According […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - AUGUST 23: Taylor Rapp #9 of the Buffalo Bills runs onto the field prior to an NFL preseason football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on August 23, 2025 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country. The Denver Broncos tout one of the best secondaries in the league. The star power and depth at cornerback is evident, and the team has an underrated starting duo at safety with Brandon Jones and Talanoa Hufanga. However, the Broncos might be interested in adding some experienced depth at safety. According to Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post , the Broncos recently worked out veteran safety Tyler Rapp. A second-round draft pick of the Los Angeles Rams in the 2019 NFL Draft, Rapp has played in 93 games with 72 starts. Over seven seasons, he has notched 488 tackles, 12 interceptions, and 31 passes defended. He has been a productive player, though several hip and knee injuries have impacted his availability throughout his career. After Jones and Hufanga, five players are battling it out in training camp for depth spots on the backend of their secondary. Those players are JL Skinner, Devon Key, Tycen Anderson, Miles Scott, and Parker Robertson. Skinner, Key, and Anderson have all been top-notch special teams’ players during their time in the NFL. Scott and Robertson are both rookies this season. With P.J. Locke’s departure to the Dallas Cowboys in free agency, Denver may be looking for a more experienced player to assume his role with the team. None of the five players vying for a backup role have any significant in-game snaps. For perspective, Locke had over 1,800 defensive snaps during his time with the Broncos as a reserve and pinch-starter. Rapp has over 4,800 defensive snaps in his career. Maybe it means nothing, but maybe it means something. In the event either Jones or Hufanga missed time, it could be wise to have a veteran player who has a lot of starting experience as one of their depth players. What do you think, Broncos Country? Would you be interested in the Broncos signing Rapp? Let me know in the comments section. As always, thank you for reading. Here is today’s slate of articles for Horse Tracks .
author: Christopher Hart

title: Broncos QB Bo Nix will NOT play vs. the Falcons in the preseason opener
summary: Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton met with the media today ahead of their preseason opener Friday night vs. the Atlanta Falcons and announced that quarterback Bo Nix will NOT play in that game. Don’t worry, Broncos County: Nix is healthy; they do not want his first game back from ankle surgery to be on […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL, CO - AUGUST 10: Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) drops back to pass during practice at training camp on Monday, August. 10, 2026, at Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado. (Photo by RJ Sangosti/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton met with the media today ahead of their preseason opener Friday night vs. the Atlanta Falcons and announced that quarterback Bo Nix will NOT play in that game. Sean Payton said Bo Nix will not play Friday vs Atlanta. Smart move. Turf should not be where player coming off two ankle surgeries should make his first game test, especially in preseason. If it was regular season opener, Nix plays. Looks like Stidham to start followed by… — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) August 12, 2026 Don’t worry, Broncos County: Nix is healthy; they do not want his first game back from ankle surgery to be on the turf inside the dome in Atlanta. Instead, Nix will play in the following two preseason games, which will be at home on a natural grass field in Mile High. This is the smart move and the right move for Nix and the Broncos. He has proven he is healthy throughout camp, where he has practiced fully since Day 1 without limitations and has been moving around well. No reason to risk any potential setbacks or wear and tear on that ankle in a meaningless game. Payton also announced that starters who are not healthy enough to play will stay back in Denver to continue to receive treatment, but that Nix, due to being healthy, will not be part of that group and will travel to Atlanta with the team. W With Nix not playing in the preseason opener, the spotlight gets moved to the potential QB2 battle brewing in Denver between Jarrett Stidham and Sam Ehlinger. While there is no official battle happening per Payton, both players have been splitting reps with the second-team offense throughout camp, so it will be interesting to see how they perform. I would assume Stidham will get the start and play the entire first half of the game, while Ehlinger will get the entire second half. We will have to see if that flips a little bit the following week, but how each of them performs will be something to watch in this one. Again, I think this is the correct move by the Broncos. No reason to even risk it. Wait until you’re at home and on your own natural field and let Nix go out there and perform. It also allows Payton and his staff to evaluate the backups even more and allow them to get more tape out there for any potential transactions down the road.

Throwbacks vs. Seahawks Week 7: Summit White vs. Cardinals Week 8: Sunset Orange vs. Chiefs Week 9: Summit White vs. Panthers Week 11: Sunset Orange vs. Raiders Week 12: Summit White vs. Steelers Week 13: Sunset Orange vs. Dolphins Week 14: Summit White vs. Jets Week 15: Summit White vs. Raiders Week 16: Midnight Navy vs. Bills Week 17: Summit White vs. Patriots Week 18: Throwbacks vs. Chargers In total, we will see the Broncos in their road whites nine times, home orange four times, midnight navy blue alternates twice, and their throwbacks twice. title: Quinn Meinerz on Broncos’ trenches: ‘Iron sharpens iron’
summary: To play at a high level in the National Football League, you need to perform well in the trenches. Thankfully, the Denver Broncos sport one of the best offensive and defensive lines in all of football. It’s a game of inches, and week in and week out, those units do their part to help the […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MD - NOVEMBER 30: RJ Harvey #12 of the Denver Broncos celebrates with Quinn Meinerz #77 after scoring a touchdown against the Washington Commanders during the second half of the NFL game at Northwest Stadium on November 30, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images To play at a high level in the National Football League, you need to perform well in the trenches. Thankfully, the Denver Broncos sport one of the best offensive and defensive lines in all of football. It’s a game of inches, and week in and week out, those units do their part to help the Broncos achieve victory. Without question, their impeccable play was a big reason why Denver was able to reel off an impressive 14-wins during the regular season in 2025. The Broncos had the best pass rushing defense in the NFL last year, as well as the top-ranked pass blocking unit—a trend that seems likely to continue for the 2026 season. That’s also why so many fans and analysts are bullish on the team’s prospects in 2026. Yesterday after practice, sixth-year offensive guard and two-time All-Pro Quinn Meinerz spoke to the media and acknowledge how impressed he was with the team’s defensive line thus far in training camp. “We have a really good front. You have to bring your ‘A’ game every single day. I think they all have individual skills that you have to kind of prep for on a daily basis,” stated Meinerz. “D.J. has been a consistent, solid nose tackle for us. He makes practice difficult. Roach is strong and also fast, and the same thing with Zach Allen. I think everyone’s been talking about ‘Enyi’. He’s really been maturing as a player and getting better. I’ve been seeing his improvement as well,” added Meinerz. The aforementioned make a strong core four along the defensive line. Additionally, the Broncos have promising developmental prospects Sai’vion Jones and Tyler Onyedim, whom the franchise has drafted in the third-round the past two seasons. If those two are able to be contributors this season, it’s hard to believe there are many other teams in the NFL that have as formidable of a defensive front as Denver. Going up against such great players is also beneficial for the Broncos’ offensive line. At all five positions across the board, the Broncos are returning quality starters. They’re battle-tested and experienced, but going head-to-head in practice against a top-flight defense every week helps give them an edge on gamedays. Additionally, they have impressive depth and a lot of rookie contract players who are developing well under the tutelage of Zach Strief. Strief has played a crucial role in raising the standard for the offensive line play since he joined the franchise alongside Head Coach Sean Payton four years ago. “It’s good because then the young guys [on defense] get to see that the same way the young guys in our room get to see how we practice as an offensive line. It’s just constant iron sharpening iron every single day, and you have to be ready for it because if you don’t, you’re going to get your butt whooped.”

title: Nik Bonitto talks leadership, hypes up second-year edge rusher Que Robinson
summary: The ascension of edge rusher Nik Bonitto is one of the best developments for the Denver Broncos in recent memory. After a rather quiet rookie season, Bonitto has transformed into one of the best pass rushers in the National Football League. In turn, the Broncos’ defense has become one of the most feared in the […]
full_text: ENGLEWOOD, CO - JULY 31: Nik Bonitto #15 of the Denver Broncos looks on during training camp at Broncos Park Powered by CommonSpirit on July 31, 2026 in Englewood, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The ascension of edge rusher Nik Bonitto is one of the best developments for the Denver Broncos in recent memory. After a rather quiet rookie season, Bonitto has transformed into one of the best pass rushers in the National Football League. In turn, the Broncos’ defense has become one of the most feared in the NFL—topping the league in sacks for two consecutive seasons. When it comes to putting pressure on opposing quarterbacks, there are only a handful of players in the league that are at his level. After back-to-back years of double-digit sacks , Bonitto’s pass rushing prowess has earned him multiple Pro-Bowl nods and one second-team All-Pro accolade. Yesterday after practice, Head Coach Sean Payton gave his thoughts on the fifth-year pass rushers development to date and what he is seeing from him in training camp thus far. “I think he understands some of the things he does fantastic. He also knows he’s going to get some handoffs his way to try to neutralize maybe his pass rush. He’s gotten stronger and he’s taken on a little bit more of a leadership role in that room.” While Bonitto’s top-tier pass rushing ability has been tremendous, working on being a better anchor against the run will be important as his career progresses. According to various sources, his run defense grade has ranked near the end of most starters at the position. That’s definitely a key reason he has added some bulk and strength this offseason to help combat the runs that go in his direction. Nevertheless, Bonitto is still one of the league’s most dynamic defenders. In addition to getting after quarterbacks, he has done a tremendous job causing force fumbles. Over the past few years, he has made a number of game-changing plays that have often turned the gridiron fortunes in Denver’s favor. While becoming a more well-rounded player is a big goal for the 2026 season, taking on more of a leadership role is there. The Broncos have a youthful edge rusher room, with players like Dondrea Tillman, Jonah Elliss, and Que Robinson all showing promise early on in their careers. Being able to pick the brain of one of the league’s best will help them prepare for the battles to come as the regular season nears. “I’m trying to be more vocal. I’m not really like a ‘rah-rah’ type of guy, but just kind of giving the guys coaching points and just stuff I see from the outside when they’re in the game, stuff like that. I’m just kind of leading by example in a way,” stated Bonitto. With the defense aiming to break the all-time sack record in ’26, they’ll need Robinson and the aforementioned players to take their game to the next level. Speaking of Robinson, Bonitto gave big praise from what he is seeing from the former Crimson Tide standout. “He’s showing out every day in practice. He has all the tools, and whenever he sets his mind to it, nobody can block him. He’s been playing really well right now. I’m excited especially to see these next couple of games what he does out there. I know he’s going to put on a show for sure.” A fourth-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, Robinson played in six games last season. He primarily made an impact on special teams but also logged 150 snaps on defense. Robinson finished his rookie campaign with 12 tackles, 3 tackles for loss, and a half sack. On 67 total pass rushing snaps, he had 4 hurries, 3 quarterback hits, 2 knockdowns, and 7 pressures. That’s a promising start to his career. If Bonitto’s insight is any indication of what is to come, look for Robinson to make a big jump as a contributor on defense this season. In the event Jonathon Cooper winds up missing any time, they are certainly going to need it.

title: Broncos announce they will wear their throwback uniforms vs. Seahawks and Chargers
summary: The Denver Broncos made a surprise uniform announcement on Tuesday when they announced that they will wear their very popular throwback uniforms during their Thursday Night matchup vs. the reigning Super Bowl Champions, the Seattle Seahawks. The Seahawks will also be wearing their popular throwbacks, so it will be a battle of two of the […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 26: A detailed view of a Denver Broncos throwback helmet during the fourth quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at Empower Field at Mile High on October 26, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos made a surprise uniform announcement on Tuesday when they announced that they will wear their very popular throwback uniforms during their Thursday Night matchup vs. the reigning Super Bowl Champions, the Seattle Seahawks. The Seahawks will also be wearing their popular throwbacks, so it will be a battle of two of the best jesery/uniforms in the NFL, with the Broncos obviously having the best ones. Throwback Thursday coming 🔜 #TNFonPrime x #SEAvsDEN pic.twitter.com/EKAQHb11ru — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) August 11, 2026 They did not stop there; they also announced that they would be wearing these beautiful throwbacks for their season finale matchup vs. their division rivals, the Los Angeles Chargers. They can wear their throwbacks/alternate jerseys up to 4 times in a season, so we could see them wear them at least one more time. They have used that 4th time to wear their white helmet/navy blue alternates, so I would anticipate we see that again this season. The Broncos are currently undefeated when they wear these throwbacks, so hopefully that trend continues this season. A big win at home on Thursday Night Football vs. the reigning Super Bowl Champs in the throwbacks would be pretty awesome. Then, a season finale game vs. a division rival in a game that could decide the AFC West and postseason seeding and/or berths. Continuing that undefeated streak in those two games would be huge wins for the Broncos. While I do like the Broncos’ new uniform and the different variations you can have, these throwbacks are the best uniforms in the entire NFL. You can make a VERY strong argument that they should be wearing this combo each and every week, but it seems like the team likes keeping them for special occasions a few times a year. We typically get a uniform schedule for the Broncos before the season starts, so stay tuned for that so we can learn what they will wear when and where, and when we will see them wear these beautiful throwbacks for a third time this upcoming season.

title: Horse Tracks: Will Sean Payton outsource replay challenges?
summary: The only real significant rule adjustment this year for officiating is a wrinkle allowing head coaches to designate another staff member to initiate challenges. The idea, I think, is a pretty good one. Head coaches get emotional and sometimes the challenge flies before the prefrontal cortex gets fully engaged after a bad call. Tapping another […]
full_text: TAMPA, FL - SEPTEMBER 22: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos throws a challenge flag during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on September 22, 2024 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The only real significant rule adjustment this year for officiating is a wrinkle allowing head coaches to designate another staff member to initiate challenges. The idea, I think, is a pretty good one. Head coaches get emotional and sometimes the challenge flies before the prefrontal cortex gets fully engaged after a bad call. Tapping another cooler-headed coach on the shoulder to handle the responsibility seems sound. While Payton isn’t by any stretch of the imagination as emotional as some coaches we’ve seen in Denver (Vic Fangio, anyone?), I honestly wonder if his ego will let him outsource playcalling to Davis Webb and challenges in the same year. I’m not even sold that he needs to or would even want to. As the head coach, he needs to keep his finger on the pulse of the game as a whole. He needs to be not only thinking of the play that happened, but also what the consequences of that challenge will mean for however much time remains in the game. If a designee challenges a play and it fails, that could heavily limit their options later in a close game. I think a guy like Payton would never want to put anyone else in that position. That would be just setting someone up to earn his ire. I’m curious to hear what the community thinks on this. Is Payton pretty decent with challenges in your eyes? Would this move help him or hinder him as our head coach? Hit up the comments and let us know what you think. title: 8 winners, 4 losers from Detroit Lions training camp
summary: Detroit Lions training camp isn’t over, but the team is starting to shift into preseason mode. Before we start previewing the exhibition opener on Thursday, let’s take inventory of the biggest winners and losers from the first two weeks of training camp. Winners CB Nick Whiteside Whiteside, in my opinion, has been the story of […]
full_text: Detroit Lions cornerback D.J. Reed (4), left, talks to defensive back Nick Whiteside (38) after practice during mini camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Tuesday, June 16, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Detroit Lions training camp isn’t over, but the team is starting to shift into preseason mode. Before we start previewing the exhibition opener on Thursday, let’s take inventory of the biggest winners and losers from the first two weeks of training camp. Winners CB Nick Whiteside Whiteside, in my opinion, has been the story of training camp. After starting with the second and third teams, Whiteside just kept making play after play to the point where Dan Campbell could no longer ignore him. He’s since climbed the depth chart and has been getting first-team reps for nearly a week while D.J. Reed has been sidelined with an injury. It feels like he’s now comfortably above the roster bubble after starting camp as a relative long shot. EDGE Ahmed Hassanein If Whiteside is the biggest story of training camp, Hassanein isn’t far behind. Thus far, he has proved that he is far more than just a good origin story and a high-energy player. He’s consistently making plays on a daily basis both on special teams and against the second-team offense. At this point, I think he’s the unquestioned backup to Tyler Lacy at the big defensive end position, and is firmly off the roster bubble. DT Alim McNeill McNeill’s 2025 season was certainly a disappointment. Though expectations were relatively low coming off a torn ACL, there was certainly hope he would be back to normal by the end of the year. He wasn’t, but the 2026 version of McNeill suddenly looks more like what we’re accustomed to seeing. His explosiveness is back, and his strength never really left. He could be in for a big year if he stays healthy. S Chuck Clark Fans were understandably concerned about the safety position following the news that Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph were at risk of missing the start of the season. However, Chuck Clark should ease some of those concerns. In the spring, coaches praised Clark’s knowledge and ability to communicate at a high level. In camp, he’s followed that up with disciplined play, great instincts on the field, and an aggressive mindset in the run game. He’s looking like one of the Lions’ best offseason additions so far. CB Rock Ya-Sin Ya-Sin has done a pretty darn good job quelling one of Lions fans’ other big concerns: the outside cornerback position. The loss of Terrion Arnold was a gut punch and a big loss in terms of potential of that room, but Ya-Sin has come in, assumed a starting role, and gone toe-to-toe with every single one of the Lions’ starting talented receivers. Certainly, there is still some concern about the outside cornerback depth, but things have been going pretty well with Reed and Ya-Sin in the starting lineup this camp. QB Luke Altmyer Altmyer has a real chance to win the backup quarterback job following the retirement of Teddy Bridgewater, but the truth of the matter is the undrafted rookie quarterback was already making a pretty strong impression before that news broke. “He did some really good things,” Campbell said. “He was put in some really tough positions for a young player that you absolutely have to be put in, you just do. You’ve got to be thrust in it and really you need to fail, you need to make mistakes so that you can grow. And we thought he handled it really well, we did.” I’ve been impressed with Altmyer’s poise during situational drills, his relative accuracy, and his arm strength. He still needs to speed up his progressions, but that’s to be expected of someone this young. RB Jabari Small The Lions have a legitimate RB4 competition between Small and Jacob Saylors. That alone is saying a lot because this team really likes Saylors as a special teamer. But Small has been shifty, strong on special teams, and he’s been tough. He’s clearly been battling through some knee discomfort for the past few practices, but has shown his grit by practicing through it. I wasn’t sure how close he was to really competing for a spot with Saylors, but Campbell all but confirmed he’s thoroughly in the mix. “Small’s having a good camp,” Campbell said. “I mean, I feel like those two guys are just jockeying with each other right now. One guy’s a little bit ahead. The next day, the other guy’s a little bit ahead. And I love where they’re at on special teams because that’ll be big for both of those players The entire linebacking corps Be it some early big plays from Derrick Barnes and Damone Clark, or the late addition of Devin White, the Lions’ linebacking corps has been all over the place early. The entire crew has been impressive in how fast and downhill they play, and I’ve been surprised by how decent they’ve been in coverage during team drills—slowing down the likes of Sam LaPorta early in camp. Even undrafted rookie Erick Hunter is really starting to come on as of late. While Barnes and Malcolm Rodriguez still have a lot to prove, I do like the depth that this room has to offer. Clark, White, Joe Bachie have all splashed on defense, and even a guy like Troy Reeder could help on special teams. Losers OT Giovanni Manu Giovanni Manu seemed like 2026 was going to be the last year to make an impression with the coaching staff and justify a spot on this roster moving forward. Unfortunately for him, he made the complete wrong impression by failing to report an offseason injury and promptly being stashed away on the Non-Football Injury list indefinitely. WR Isaac TeSlaa I’m not panicking about TeSlaa’s slow start to camp, and I don’t think you should either. But I’m also not going to ignore the fact that the second-year receiver has struggled, both in one-on-one drills and team sessions. He’s particularly been ineffective against press coverage, failing to use both his size and length to create separation. His hands are still impeccable, but I was hoping to see a little more progress in his releases by now. EDGE Payton Turner Turner arrived in Detroit hopeful to shake the injury prone label and finally live up to his draft status as a former first-round pick. Instead, he practiced once, tweaked his back, and hasn’t practiced again. With the rise of Hassanein and the imminent return of rookie Derrick Moore, it’s hard to imagine Turner returning in time to win a roster spot. CB Ennis Rakestraw Rakestraw has certainly had an up-and-down camp, and I’m not ready to put his roster spot in jeopardy, but the fact remains that he has been jumped in the depth chart by Whiteside. Rakestraw could find new life after entering the competition for the nickel job, but Dan Campbell said it himself: he needs to start stringing some good days together. “He’s had some ups and downs. He needs to string a few days together here of some good stuff, but he can do that and he’s gifted,” Campbell said.

title: Detroit Lions players with most to gain, lose in preseason opener vs. Bengals
summary: It’s official—Detroit Lions football is back. Myself and my good friend Meko Scott are back with another episode of our weekly game-preview podcast, “Before the Roar,” where we breakdown what fans should be looking for during the Lions’ first preseason game against the Cincinatti Bengals. It’s been an eventful first two weeks of training camp, […]
full_text: It’s official—Detroit Lions football is back. Myself and my good friend Meko Scott are back with another episode of our weekly game-preview podcast, “Before the Roar,” where we breakdown what fans should be looking for during the Lions’ first preseason game against the Cincinatti Bengals. It’s been an eventful first two weeks of training camp, and for many of the players competing for jobs or roster spots, the game against the Bengals is much more than just another exhibition game. It’s a chance for some to cement their status as cut-down day looms in the not-so-distant future. And while the majority of the core starters won’t even dress, there will be a handful of younger players that are out there for at least a few series—like Lions rookie right tackle Blake Miller, who coach Dan Campbell has already confirmed will see some action on Thursday night. Other young players like second-year offensive lineman Miles Frazier and defensive end Ahmed Hassanein have a chance to build upon strong camp performances. On the defensive side of the ball, there will be plenty to watch, including how third-year cornerback Ennis Rakestraw looks when he is out there. For those of you that like watching podcasts in video-form, you can view the entire episode right here . You can also listen wherever you get your podcasts. Please be sure to like and subscribe to the Pride of Detroit YouTube Channel. Your support means a ton, and it allows us to reach other Lions fans around the world.

title: Survey: What’s your concern level for the Lions’ offensive line after Cade Mays’ injury?
summary: Throughout the offseason, SB Nation will host surveys for NFL fans, sponsored by FanDuel Sportsbook. For Pride of Detroit, we are tasked with fielding questions from Detroit Lions fans, and this week’s question focuses on the injury to starting center Cade Mays and how the offensive line will need to adapt. On Monday, coach Dan […]
full_text: Detroit Lions offensive lineman Melvin Priestly (74), left, practices with center Seth McLaughlin (65) during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Monday, August 10, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Throughout the offseason, SB Nation will host surveys for NFL fans, sponsored by FanDuel Sportsbook . For Pride of Detroit, we are tasked with fielding questions from Detroit Lions fans, and this week’s question focuses on the injury to starting center Cade Mays and how the offensive line will need to adapt. On Monday, coach Dan Campbell announced that starting center Cade Mays suffered a wrist injury and is expected to miss “a significant period of time.” According to national reports, Mays broke a small bone in his wrist and is anticipated to be sidelined for 8-10 weeks, meaning there is a possible chance he returns after the Lions’ Week 5 bye. While the Lions could look to add an offensive lineman to challenge for the open role, with Mays likely only missing the start of the season, a limited free agent pool, and challenging trade options, it’s more likely they will test their own depth for a replacement. The Lions plan to challenge several of their depth players to step up and compete for the starting center role, but the early expectation is that Juice Scruggs—whom the Lions traded for because of his starting experience and positional range—is the early frontrunner for the job. Unfortunately, Scruggs is dealing with a soft tissue injury, and while he is expected to return to practice in the near future, his absence has opened the door for more competition. Seth McLaughlin has primarily been working with the starters since Mays’ injury, indicating the former Rimington Award winner could be next in line. Michael Niese has previously held the Lions backup center position and is also expected to be in the mix, though it’s worth noting that he’s been repping at guard most of training camp. A few others will also be cross-trained at center to see if they can give the Lions the best chance of winning, including starting right guard Tate Ratledge and rookie undrafted free agent Melvin Priestly. The Lions will have just under three weeks’ worth of practices and three preseason games to help them decide their best options on the offensive line, but it’s clear this situation has raised the difficulty level for the offensive line as a whole. And that leads us to this week’s SB Nation Reacts survey question: What’s your concern level for the Lions’ offensive line after Cade Mays’ injury? In THE FEED poll below, you can pick one of four options for your level of concern for the offensive line, while also explaining why you picked your selection in the comment sections of this article and in THE FEED. title: Brian Gutekunst: Packers didn’t plan on picking Trey Smack
summary: Cheesehead TV landed Green Bay Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst for a one-on-one interview this week, and one of the big things he addressed in the conversation was the selection of kicker Trey Smack in the sixth round of the 2026 draft. As a reminder, the Packers send two seventh-round picks to add Smack to […]
full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JULY 31: Trey Smack #28 of the Green Bay Packers works out during the Green Bay Packers training camp at Ray Nitschke Field on July 31, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Cheesehead TV landed Green Bay Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst for a one-on-one interview this week, and one of the big things he addressed in the conversation was the selection of kicker Trey Smack in the sixth round of the 2026 draft. As a reminder, the Packers send two seventh-round picks to add Smack to the team and then released veteran Brandon McManus, who they already paid a $1 million roster bonus for in 2026, and later Lucas Havrisik, who set the franchise record for the made longest field goal as an injury replacement for McManus in 2025. Gutekunst claimed that he believed a player of Smack’s talent usually would have been drafted in the bottom of the fourth round or the beginning of the fifth round. For a point of reference, only 7 of the 21 kickers drafted sicne 2017 have been drafted by the mid-way point of the fifth round or higher, so it seems like the Packers didn’t just think of Smack as a draftable kicker, but in the top-third of draftable kickers in the last decade. Due to Green Bay’s limited amount of draft selections, Gutekunst claimed that he “didn’t foresee picking a kicker” doing into April’s draft. In his own words: “The way the board was, he was sticking out to us. It was like, ‘Okay, let’s take a shot here,’ because we believed in the player and the guy.” New Packers special teams coordinator Cam Achord co-signed the selection, per the general manager. “He fell a little bit further than we expected,” added Gutekunst. “At the time, we had two guys that we felt good about taking and we were many picks away. I don’t feel like either guy would be there by the time we got there,” was his explaination on why Green Bay moved up. Worth mentioning here: The Chicago Bears took defensive lineman Jordan van den Berg, who the Packers had on a pre-draft visit, just three picks ahead of Smack’s selection. Shortly after Smack was picked, the Dallas Cowboys drafted receiver Anthony Smith (two slots later), and both offensive lineman Ethan Onianwa (Atlanta Falcons) and quarterback Behren Morton (New England Patriots) were also picked before what would have been Green Bay’s first seventh-round pick. title: No word on whether Aaron Rodgers will play the Packers this preseason
summary: While the Green Bay Packers have stated publicly that they plan to play their starters in their preseason opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers, at least for a drive or two, the Steelers have been a little wishy-washy when asked about the same subject. As recently as yesterday, Pittsburgh head coach Mike McCarthy, who won a […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Jordan Love #10 of the Green Bay Packers and Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers talk after the game at Acrisure Stadium on October 26, 2025 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the Green Bay Packers have stated publicly that they plan to play their starters in their preseason opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers, at least for a drive or two, the Steelers have been a little wishy-washy when asked about the same subject. As recently as yesterday, Pittsburgh head coach Mike McCarthy, who won a Super Bowl in Green Bay, said that he hasn’t made the decision on whether starters will play or not on Thursday . There are also mixed signals on the Aaron Rodgers front, as McCarthy stated on the radio that Rodgers does want to play against his former team this week. Rodgers later told reporters : “It’s preseason. It’s not real football. So if I do, great. If not, great.” Here were some more thoughts that Rodgers dropped on summer football exhibitions : “Preseason’s a lot different. Teams don’t run anything anymore. They just really don’t,” Rodgers said. “Even joint practices. The first year we were doing them, it was fun because you got to play a team that wasn’t going to play how they played in the preseason. They were going to show you a lot of different things they were working on. It was like a real day at camp. “But as that got on, it just stopped being like that. It just turned into fights, and nobody showed anything. I think those are a waste of a day. I think preseason football is good to see guys with the pads on, under the lights, how they react to the nerves. But it’s not real regular season football.” When asked if there’s a benefit to him playing in Thursday’s game, Rodgers stated simply: “I don’t think so.” McCarthy said that whoever “starts” in the preseason opener will get about two series before a second unit will step in. The question now is whether the “starters” will involve all of the Steelers’ preferred starters, or if it’ll just be a mix of young starters and backups.

title: The Brandon Cisse hype cannot be contained
summary: The cornerback position has been the Green Bay Packers have been struggling to solidify since the departure of Jaire Alexander a few seasons ago, and that has put even more pressure on second-round corner Brandon Cisse to perform right away. That, combined with a strong start to training camp, has the hype train moving full […]
full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JULY 31: Brandon Cisse #2 of the Green Bay Packers looks on during the Green Bay Packers training camp at Ray Nitschke Field on July 31, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The cornerback position has been the Green Bay Packers have been struggling to solidify since the departure of Jaire Alexander a few seasons ago, and that has put even more pressure on second-round corner Brandon Cisse to perform right away. That, combined with a strong start to training camp, has the hype train moving full steam ahead, to the point it can’t be slowed down. With an injury to Carrington Valentine keeping him out of practice, Cisse has been working with the first-team defense in practices, helping his case in a battle to earn a starting spot ahead of Week 1. So far, the early returns have looked promising, particularly during one-on-one drills, where he looked like a blanket in coverage against second-year wideout Savion Williams. Rookie CB Brandon Cisse in 1-on-1s today: pic.twitter.com/PbpSA0Z0Tu — Kelly Hallinan (@kellyhals) August 4, 2026 What’s more interesting is that some days of practice have included Cisse and Benjamin St-Juste playing with the first-string unit, while Keisean Nixon has spent time with the second team. Some of that could be due to a heavier workload early in camp for Nixon, but it could also suggest a strong start for both Cisse and St-Juste. Head coach Matt LaFleur has already liked what he’s seen from the team’s second-round pick. “I just love what he’s all about,” LaFleur told reporters last week . “He is an A-plus human, and he loves football. Every time he goes out there, there’s a lot of good things, and then there’s a lot of teachable moments. But I think he’s a guy that the sky’s the limit for him.” There were plenty of reasons for Packers fans to be excited about Cisse before training camp even began. At just 21 years old, there’s still plenty of time for him to develop into a top-tier NFL cornerback with ideal size at 6-foot-0 and 189 pounds. South Carolina CB Brandon Cisse is headed to Green Bay 🧀 Packers add a boundary CB at No. 52 pic.twitter.com/nteFS8raLJ — B/R Gridiron (@brgridiron) April 25, 2026 On top of the age and physical tools, Cisse’s tape showed flashes of a legitimate shutdown cornerback, allowing a catch on just 47.4 percent of targets last season with just one touchdown allowed in coverage. It’s the perfect storm for a young player in Green Bay. The team’s first draft pick in this class, combined with a glaring need for a long-term CB1 on the defense and frustrations with incumbent starters like Nixon and Valentine, has created a situation where Packers fans are putting all of their hopes and dreams on a 21-year-old. The good news is that he’s looking as good as advertised early in training camp.

title: Green Bay Packers News: Savion Williams turning heads in camp
summary: I think it’s fair to say Savion Williams has been a forgotten man in the Packers’ wide receiver reconstruction this offseason. In the process of jettisoning Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks, most of the focus went to Christian Watson, Jayden Reed, and Matthew Golden. And, in fairness, it should. Watson and REed signed pricey extensions […]
full_text: Savion Williams #83 of the Green Bay Packers runs with the football during training camp at Ray Nitschke Field in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin, on August 2, 2026. (Photo by Ross Harried/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images I think it’s fair to say Savion Williams has been a forgotten man in the Packers’ wide receiver reconstruction this offseason. In the process of jettisoning Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks, most of the focus went to Christian Watson, Jayden Reed, and Matthew Golden. And, in fairness, it should. Watson and REed signed pricey extensions this offseason, and Golden is a second-year first round pick looking to break out after a disappointing rookie campaign. But Williams is in a smaller version of the same boat as Golden. As good as it gets from a height/weight/seed standpoint, Williams played a gadget role and not much else in 2024 as Matt LaFleur tried to harness his physical gifts in unique ways. It kind of worked and kind of didn’t, but after 91 snaps on offense, injuries ended Williams’ season. Now he’s prepping for a second go-round int he NFL, and things might be a bit simpler this year. Skyy Moore is on hand to handle the Packers’ return duties and could do some of the gadgety stuff Williams was asked to do last year. That could allow Williams to focus on being a wide receiver. That presents a challenge in and of itself; the common knock on Williams coming out of Texas Christian was that he was a magnificent athlete who had yet to learn the nuances of playing wide receiver. That seemed to largely be true in 2025, but if he can get his feet under him and show he can do actual wide receiver things, he’d be a powerful addition to a Packers wide receiver room already in the midst of an interesting rebuild. The incident occurred during an early season walk-through—which was later […]

(Photo by Ray Carlin/Icon Sportswire/Corbis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) On ‘The Pat McAfee Show,’ former Indianapolis Colts All-Pro punter Pat McAfee recounted an incident presumably back in 2013, when former NFL Pro Bowl safety LaRon Landry ‘made a debut statement’ by unnecessarily laying out his new teammate, future Hall of Fame wideout Reggie Wayne. The incident occurred during an early season walk-through—which was later confirmed by their former head coach Chuck Pagano: He fucking took Reggie out. Reg uni was all soiled up. Grass stains everywhere. Laron pops up all hyped up. Reg looks at me “ Really” 😂😂😂 Rex told me he would be full go ALL the time!!! What a unit he was https://t.co/IR4WBDZINF — Chuck Pagano (@ChuckPaganoNFL) August 12, 2026 Hoping to add a ‘Bob Sanders-like’ enforcer to the backend of the Colts secondary, ex-Indianapolis general manager Ryan Grigson signed the free agent Landry, coming off a Pro Bowl season with defensive minded head coach Rex Ryan’s New York Jets defense, to a 4-year, $24 million contract (with $14 million guaranteed). Featuring giant bulging biceps and sheer size at safety, Landry certainly looked the part at a chiseled 6’0”, 226 pounds, even though he didn’t consistently play it. He lasted just two years into his then-lucrative Colts contract, until he was released in the early 2015 offseason, after being suspended four games for violating the league’s policy on performance-enhancing drugs (PEDs) during the 2014 season. As a free agent, Landry would test positive two more times for PEDs, which resulted in an indefinite league ban. The former 6th overall pick of the 2006 NFL Draft by Washington was out of football after turning 30-years-old. For what it’s worth, McAfee indicated that Landry was a great teammate, even volunteering to be a heat-seeking missile on special teams as a defensive starter. Unfortunately, his short-lived tenure in Indianapolis didn’t work as well as either side had initially planned, but at the very least, there is now a funny ‘friendly fire’ war story to come from it—much to current Colts wide receiver coach Reggie Wayne’s dismay to this very day. title: What will you be focusing on during the Colts first preseason game?
summary: No sleep will be lost over the outcome of Thursday night’s tilt versus the Pats. We won’t come away with anything concrete, especially concerning whether we will have a successful season or not. We will only get a glimpse, but it could shed some light on who will be counted on the most as the […]
full_text: No sleep will be lost over the outcome of Thursday night’s tilt versus the Pats. We won’t come away with anything concrete, especially concerning whether we will have a successful season or not. We will only get a glimpse, but it could shed some light on who will be counted on the most as the season actually starts. My guess is that we will still have plenty of questions, but maybe some of the questions we have will become a little clearer. RB2 could get a little clarity. Not to the point of declaring a winner, but whoever is out there first may have the lead at this point. The depth chart indicates that it is Giddens and he may very well be on the field first, but who of the two looks better between he and and McGowen on 3rd down? Who looks better as a receiver, who misses a blitz pickup, or who makes plays on Special Teams, could fire the first shot towards winning the job. My guess is that NWI will see a little action. You want your QB combatants to have a target with some experience, but I doubt Dulin plays, since his roster spot is secure even if he does not win the WR3 role. So, unless NWI really balls out, I would not assume that he is ahead of Dulin in their battle. AR getting the start likely doesn’t mean much either. Leonard will get the nod in game 2, so they will have equal time with the 2nd string. They may not even announce a winner once the season starts? They can keep three QBs without too much roster discomfort, so as long as DJ is healthy, there is no need to announce the backup. AR is staying, unless Ballard’s price is met, so he could get the 2nd string designation as a bargaining chip. I don’t think they just cut him unless they need some cap relief to make a splash. I’m curious to see how the LBs shake out. There may never be more than two on the field at the same time and it is not like that anyone has already won a role. Carlies could get a long look and we should see a fair amount of Weeks. He was a popular choice as a UFA, who could make the team. I wouldn’t be surprised if it was Boettcher and Ajaike for the first couple of series. Will any of the first string OL get a series? I expect to see Farmer at RG and for Freeland to be out there somewhere, but after that, you better have your program with all the jersey numbers. Rucci is another of those guys looking to make some noise after not being drafted. We will also get to see if Tucker can be the backup Center and how much he had to do with fumble snaps. They say we have a kicking competition and we may see both, but I think Grupe has sewn this thing up. As always, the ability to cover a kick will get you noticed, so there will be some aggression. Hopefully it is not misplaced and doesn’t result in a penalty. It is more likely that more information is gathered from the joint practices than the game, but these are some of things that I will be observing on Thursday night. Where will you be focusing your attention?

title: Colts roster 2026: Tanor Bortolini, Arden Key, Bryce Boettcher are underrated
summary: From 1999 through 2018, the Indianapolis Colts were one of the NFL’s luckiest (pun intended) teams when it came to quarterback security. That Peyton Manning guy worked out pretty well, and the transition from the Manning era to the Andrew Luck era (with the Curtis Painter/Dan Orlovsky/Kerry Collins year of 2011 in-between) was about as […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PA - NOVEMBER 02: Tanor Bortolini #60 of the Indianapolis Colts in action against the Pittsburgh Steelers on November 2, 2025 at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images From 1999 through 2018, the Indianapolis Colts were one of the NFL’s luckiest (pun intended) teams when it came to quarterback security. That Peyton Manning guy worked out pretty well, and the transition from the Manning era to the Andrew Luck era (with the Curtis Painter/Dan Orlovsky/Kerry Collins year of 2011 in-between) was about as seamless as anyone could have hoped. Since Luck’s bombshell retirement announcement on August 24, 2019… well, that security is no longer secure. From 2019 through 2025, only the Cleveland Browns and the Washington Football Team/Commanders/[YOUR NAME HERE] have gone through more starting quarterbacks . Even with the Daniel Jones signing last year that was a major win until it wasn’t, it’s been a tough row to hoe. Jones is back on the roster with his two-year, $88 contract with $44 million guaranteed, and if Jones can replicate what he did in Shane Steichen’s offense in the first half of the season, all will be well in the Circle City. From Weeks 1-9, the Colts ranked first in Offensive DVOA, and everything was humming. Then, Jones regressed a bit, and was lost to a right Achilles tear and a fractured fibula in Week 13, and that was that. The Colts were 8-2 before their Week 11 bye, and they didn’t win a single game after that. Which left the team at 8-9 for the second straight season, and Steichen with a 25-26 regular-season record over three full seasons. “That’s not good enough, is the bottom line,” Steichen said at his end-of-season presser, when someone brought up that overall record, and Steichen’s 7-22 record against winning teams. “I’ve got to find the answers to that for sure because we’ve got to get over the hump; .500 is not good enough in this league. You’ve got to get over the hump. You’ve got to get your butt [going] in the postseason, and we’ve got to find ways to do that. Win the tight games, do a better job of that, putting the guys in position – training camp, practice, whatever it is, to get over that hump.” If the Colts are to prove that they’re more than a paper tiger in 2026, they will need more than just Jones’ best — they’ll need that from everybody on the roster. The stars, obviously, but it will be crucial for underrated players to come up and prove why they deserve more praise. To that end, I’ve identified three Hidden Gems for the 2026 Colts — one underrated veteran, one underrated free-agent signing, and one underrated draft pick. Underrated veteran: Center Tanor Bortolini From 2016 through 2024, the Colts were also set at center, because when healthy, Ryan Kelly was one of the NFL’s best at that position. But when Kelly signed with the Minnesota Vikings before the 2025 season, Indy already had a replacement plan in place. They selected Wisconsin’s Tanor Bortolini with the 118th overall pick in the fourth round of the 2024 draft. This after Bortolini’s four high-quality seasons with the Badgers in which he allowed three sacks and 23 pressures over 962 pass-blocking reps, and a scouting combine where he REALLY put himself on the map . If you went back to Bortolini’s tape after the combine, there was some formidable stuff there. Per sources, Wisconsin center Tanor Bortolini ran a 4.94 40 with a 1.69 10-yard split, broke Jason Kelce's 3-cone combine record for centers, and then went out and got himself some PANCAKES. pic.twitter.com/RRpSTLJY3L — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) March 3, 2024 Bortolini had just 351 snaps in his rookie season around Kelly’s injuries, but when he was asked to take over the center position in 2025, he did so seamlessly — and did so snapping the ball to three different quarterbacks in Jones, Philip Rivers, and Riley Leonard. Anyone who knows how wild the variance can be in quarterback understanding of protection calls knows how tough that can be. Regardless, Bortolini allowed no sacks, five quarterback hits, and 12 quarterback hurries in 2025, and the run-blocking was both calculated and nasty. The 6′ 4¼”, 303-pound Bortolini is just as happy forcing a defensive tackle to the ground with a cockroach block as he is executing two-level blocks to perfection. He could be even better in 2026 and beyond. “Tremendously — it’s grown a ton,” Bortolini said in late July, when asked how much his technique has improved under offensive line coach Tony Sparano Jr. “I think it’s cool because, like, at the end of OTAs, it’s like, ‘You know what? I want to go look back and see, where did I start?’ So, I went back to the first OTA practice that I ever had here, and I was like, ‘Man, I suck. Like, I suck.’ I was like, ‘Wow.’ Looking back, I’m like, ‘What am I doing, man?’ “But you know, it’s obviously football. Especially offensive line play, I think is a very detailed game, and I think Tony does a great job. It’s not a one-size-fits-all game either. Q [Quenton Nelson] is going to have certain strengths that he does better than I do, and I’ll have ones that I do better than him. Tony does a good job at trying to put us in a position and allow us different techniques that allow us to showcase what we’re good at and kind of find a way to minimize the things you aren’t so good at.” . @Colts center Tanor Bortolini can stone dudes at the line of scrimmage for sure, but what really stands out about him is how well he gets to the second level to seek and destroy. pic.twitter.com/3TRqQ8zksq — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) August 10, 2026 At this rate, finding things that Tanor Bortolini doesn’t do well could be quite a task. Underrated free agent: EDGE Arden Key Last season, 2024 first-round pick Laiatu Latu started to really live up to his draft capital with an 11-sack, 61-pressure season in which he looked like the EDGE1, and he did so without a lot of help. DeForest Buckner, Adetomiwa Adebawore, Kwity Paye, and Neville Gallimore all had four sacks to finish second on the defense, and nobody else on the team had more pressures than Paye’s 38. Which is why general manager Chris Ballard gave veteran Arden Key a three-year, $21 million contract with $13 million guaranteed. Last season for the Tennessee Titans, Key had five sacks and 33 pressures in just 294 pass-rushing reps, and outside of Jeffery Simmons, he’s a guy who is used to getting those quarterback disruptions without a ton of help. Arden Key creating chaos in the backfield. The @Colts could definitely use more of this on the edge! pic.twitter.com/XcoT2ck7fN — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) August 10, 2026 Key missed five games last season due to injury, and he turned 30 on May 3, so there are rotational/pitch count issues to think about. But at his best, Key can bring a ton of juice to Lou Anarumo’s defensive line, and he’s eager to be a mentor for the Colts’ younger edge-rushers. “Yeah, I’m here to help them,” Key said in June of the group. “I’m here just to build with those guys. I’ve been training with Buck [DeForest Buckner] the last five years, and every year we just talk about, ‘What if we played together, what if we did this?’ Now, I’m actually here. So, I’m just here to capitalize on the opportunity to come in and help on the pass rush and stopping the run, because you got to stop the run in order to get to the passer. “So, do those little things, and do it together.” Underrated draft pick: LB Bryce Boettcher Trading Zaire Franklin to the Green Bay Packers was a move that was more about Franklin’s contract than his performance, and the deal leaves Anarumo a bit light on the linebacker side. Ballard signed veteran Akeem Davis-Gaither to a one-year, $2.725 million contract, and drafted Georgia’s C.J. Allen in the second round, and Oregon’s Bryce Boettcher with the 135th overall pick in the fourth round. Allen’s game is more well-known, but Boettcher is an interesting addition who can…
