title: Ballard deserves more blame then he gets for drafting Richardson to the Colts
summary: There are five stages of grief with acceptance being the final one. Indianapolis Colts fans moved to that last stage extremely quickly after it was obvious the Anthony Richardson experiment was over. It technically continues, but the way camp has gone, barring an injury to Riley Leonard, he is going to have to be Superman […]
full_text: There are five stages of grief with acceptance being the final one. Indianapolis Colts fans moved to that last stage extremely quickly after it was obvious the Anthony Richardson experiment was over. It technically continues, but the way camp has gone, barring an injury to Riley Leonard, he is going to have to be Superman in preseason games to even get a sniff of consideration. The writing is on the wall, and while he certainly gets blamed for the decision to draft Richardson, Chris Ballard simply deserves more. This isn’t your buddy who is always late, can’t seem to keep a job or get their life quite right for extended periods of time. You can be there for your friends through thick and thin. We are talking about the GM of an NFL franchise. Ballard is one of 32. Anything that rare comes with immense reward and even more pressure. The Richardson draft was one of many missteps that can’t be considered in a vacuum. The missed playoffs, the complete draft classes that fell short, and failing to find a quarterback after ten years are all relevant as to why Ballard should have experienced more heat for his failed pick. I know the Ballard apologists are sharpening their knives right now, but objectively speaking, what is there to go on? I understand that Bryce Young and C.J. Stroud were off the board, but remember, we aren’t operating in a vacuum. There was a lack of understanding that Philip Rivers would call it quits after one season. Follow that up with a disastrous trade for Carson Wentz and Matt Ryan, whose tank was completely empty, and you are looking at a series of grave errors. Even bringing in Gardner Minshew as Richardson’s backup instead of retaining Ryan as a veteran presence was highly questionable. Ballard could have eased Richardson in with a non-threat like Ryan. Instead, he chose Minshew, who was fighting for his own place in the league, which created a looming presence. Richardson was supposed to be a project. He wasn’t supposed to be this much of one. Some of the worst accuracy this league has ever witnessed carries his name. The injuries aren’t Ballard’s direct fault, but there was evidence of durability issues in college. The raw prospect played one season’s worth of games and is one subpar outing from being cut. The bright spot lasted about 4.5 games. That isn’t enough for the fourth overall pick. This may go down as one of the worst picks in franchise history. How has Ballard skated by? Not only was he kept on for another season by Carlie Irsay-Gordon, fans still line up to defend him too. I am not saying he hasn’t been roasted for picking Anthony Richardson. He has. Beyond roasting, he should be toast. That pick alone shows his questionable judgment and inability to recognize NFL talent. We made it through the stages of grief in record time. Looks like we get to stay in acceptance a little while longer.
author: Jon Spradley

title: 10 Biggest Chiefs Questions: Can Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy bounce back in 2026?
summary: Since the Kansas City Chiefs traded wide receiver Tyreek Hill after the 2021 season, the team has been trying to solve a glaring need at wide receiver. This need wasn’t as prevalent during the first season post-Hill since tight end Travis Kelce was still at the peak of his ability. They had strong complementary receivers […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 05: Xavier Worthy #1 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs to score a touchdown against the Baltimore Ravens during the first quarter at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on September 05, 2024 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Since the Kansas City Chiefs traded wide receiver Tyreek Hill after the 2021 season, the team has been trying to solve a glaring need at wide receiver. This need wasn’t as prevalent during the first season post-Hill since tight end Travis Kelce was still at the peak of his ability. They had strong complementary receivers in Juju Smith-Schuster and Marquez Valdes-Scantling alongside the dynamic ability of Kadarius Toney. Those guys rounded out the offense that was built around Kelce. However, the glaring lack of receiver talent became a bigger problem after 2022, when Kelce started to fall off. The Chiefs could no longer revolve the entire passing game around him because Kelce lost the athleticism to dominate the intermediate parts of the field. It was a struggle to generate explosive passes because he couldn’t win in that area. The rest of the receivers lacked the ability to win downfield, which cramped the offense. Over the last three seasons, the Chiefs have had similar issues in their passing game. The team lacks the receiver talent to beat man coverage or win downfield to stretch defenses. The offense has devolved into quick game or Mahomes having to create every explosive pass with his scrambling. He can do that, but that’s not a sustainable style and puts too much on your quarterback. The Chiefs have tried addressing receiver in the draft. During the 2023 NFL Draft, they drafted Rashee Rice in the second round. During the 2024 draft, they used their first-round pick on Xavier Worthy. The returns on these players have been mixed so far, for several reasons. In training camp so far, Rice has been working back to 100% from a clean-up procedure on his knee in May. He has progressively worked more in full-team settings at practice. Worthy has been held out of practice since injuring his shoulder finishing a downfield catch over a week ago, but he has been on the field in pads in a limited fashion the last three practices. What can we expect from these players in 2026? Let’s start with Rice: Rashee Rice Rice wasn’t overly productive as a rookie, putting up 36 catches, 420 yards, and four touchdowns over his first 10 games. The staff hadn’t found a clear role for Rice to succeed in, and he wasn’t getting as many snaps as some of the veteran receivers. As the season went on, Rice’s role and production expanded. He nearly outproduced his first 10 games in his last five, putting up 35 catches, 411 yards, and two touchdowns to close the season. Rice had two 100-yard games during that time. Rice’s role within the offense changed: the staff used him much more on underneath routes, such as screens or crossers, to get him the ball in space with blockers. Rice was the team’s best chance of generating explosive passes, but because his route running was limited downfield, everything had to be manufactured in short areas. Rice made it work with his burst and tackle-breaking ability. To start his second season, it seemed like Rice’s production was about to pop. He played three games prior to injuring his knee and missing the rest of the season. In those games, Rice put up 24 catches, 288 yards, and two touchdowns. Extrapolating that production for 17 games would’ve put Rice at 136 catches, 1,632 yards, and 11 touchdowns. The Chiefs leaned even harder into using Rice as an underneath weapon where they could get the ball in his hands and let him create yards after the catch. Rice missed the first six games of last season due to a suspension. He played eight games and put up solid stats of 53 catches, 571 yards, and five touchdowns. However, the stats overstate Rice’s impact in those games. Rice coming back put other players like Xavier Worthy in worse spots. Guys had to play out of position to fit Rice. He wasn’t quite as dynamic with the ball in his hands. The hope was that over time, Rice would be able to develop the other parts of his game, particularly his route running. Rice has always been good in that short area, but beyond that, he’s been a problem. He struggles to play on the outside because he doesn’t have a developed release package. He has some stiffness in his route running and struggles to decelerate and separate on breaks. He doesn’t win downfield and struggles in contested catch situations. That development has never come. He hasn’t expanded his route tree or learned to beat man coverage consistently. He’s forced to play in the slot, which puts Worthy in a worse spot. Rice’s route tree being within five yards is hard to build an offense around when he’s your #1 receiver. It limits your ability to stretch the field and get explosives. For the Chiefs to have a better season in 2026, Rice is going to have to develop into things he hasn’t done yet. Can he do that? I’m skeptical about that at this point. Xavier Worthy I reviewed Worthy’s film recently, and I came away higher on him as a player. There will always be limitations with his game because he is small and can’t beat press, but there is more to his route running than I gave it credit for. He shows good footwork and change of pace to his routes to create separation. Being healthier this year should allow him to run more underneath routes that get him the ball in his hands in space. Worthy isn’t the best in space because he struggles to break tackles, but he is explosive and can put a threat into a defense with his speed. The question about Worthy is whether he can have a productive role in the offense with Rice and Kelce around. Since those two players have to play in the slot, it forces Worthy to handle more outside reps. Can he take a step there to be more viable? Or do the Chiefs decide to use Worthy more in the slot and live with the consequences elsewhere? I don’t doubt Worthy can have a viable role within the offense; it just feels hard with the current personnel. The Bottom Line Both Worthy and Rice had disappointing seasons in 2025 due to injuries, weaknesses in their game, and a poor fit. Can that improve in 2026? Can we finally see the vision for why the Chiefs drafted both of these players? I’ll always have fit questions, but hopefully they can round out some of the concerns this year. If the Chiefs’ passing offense improves, it’s on these two players to improve and find a way to play together.
author: Nate Christensen

title: Chiefs training camp notebook Day 13: Dave Toub reveals preseason plan
summary: We are just days away from the Kansas City Chiefs’ preseason opener against the Los Angeles Rams. The two teams will face off at Arrowhead Stadium on Saturday, the first live action against another team for the Chiefs this preseason. The Rams, like many teams, have held joint practices during training camp, but that has […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 29: Dave Toub waives to fans as he walks to the field during the Kansas City Chiefs training camp on Aug 11, 2026 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We are just days away from the Kansas City Chiefs ’ preseason opener against the Los Angeles Rams . The two teams will face off at Arrowhead Stadium on Saturday, the first live action against another team for the Chiefs this preseason. The Rams, like many teams, have held joint practices during training camp, but that has never been a consideration for head coach Andy Reid. He is one of the few NFL teams that don’t participate in joint training camp sessions every year. Special teams coordinator Dave Toub has been with Reid since 2013, has gotten used to Reid’s process and recognizes how important it will be to get into the exhibition games. “I can’t wait,” Toub told local media after Wednesday’s practice. “For me, this is really the time I get to evaluate whether a guy can block or tackle on special teams- live tackling to the ground- plus you’re hitting somebody else. These guys have been hitting each other for a few weeks now. It’s getting old; it really is getting old. Same thing, over and over again; this is going to be great to have a game.” Here’s what to know from Wednesday’s practice: Injury update During the practice session, three Chiefs players left practice due to injury: linebacker Nick Bolton, tight end Jared Wiley and rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods. Nick Bolton was sick today. Jared Wiley injured his hamstring, and Peter Woods hurt his ankle. — Pete Sweeney (@pgsween) August 12, 2026 We will await more information on the new injuries. Aside from that, rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane continued to wear a yellow non-contact jersey, but upped his participation in practice. Wide receiver Jimmy Holiday, right guard Trey Smith, cornerback L’Jarius Sneed and linebacker Drue Tranquill did not appear on the field at Wednesday’s practice. Special teams snap breakdown Toub shared the game plan for how special teams snaps will be broken down on Saturday, giving us a glimpse into how the starting offense and defense could be treated as well. “You’ll have my front-line guys early in the game, but they’re going to be out,” Toub said. “If you watch early, you’ll see them. Then it’s going to be a lot of the twos and threes; I got four deep everywhere: kickoff, kickoff return, everywhere. You’re going to see a lot of different bodies, especially in the third and fourth quarter.” Toub has four return men to focus on when given the opportunity against the Rams: wide receiver Nikko Remigio, running back Brashard Smith, rookie wideout Cyrus Allen and rookie receiver Jacob De Jesus. “I want to see everybody, really. I don’t need to see a lot of Nikko,” Toub shared. “If he gets one touch on punt and one on kick return, I’m good. I really want to see the off returners blocking more than anything. I’d like to see Brashard get one punt return for sure, maybe even Allen; I still have to talk to coach to see if he’s up to speed with his leg and everything.” Toub later elaborated on the incumbent returner, who would be entering his third year as the team’s primary return man. He wants to see more home runs than Remigio has given to the team in that time. “More touchdowns, that would be great,” Toub responded when asked what he wants to see from Remigio. “His vision has really improved, I think. You see it in practice; he’ll see a crack and instead of trying to run all the way around it, he’ll plant a foot and get upfield and get 15 or 20 extra yards. Those are the ones that sometimes they’ll pop and get out on you in a hurry. He’s catching the ball great; I’m just really pleased with where he’s at.” Allen is still working back to full speed after going down in practice multiple times in training camp so far. If he is limited in playing time, it could open up more opportunities for the electric undrafted wideout from California. “De Jesus, I’m excited to see him,” Toub said. “He’s a great catcher, and he’s got a lot of hunger to him. It’s going to be exciting when he has the ball in his hands.” Brashard Smith ‘has come along great’ Smith is the second return specialist Toub talks about behind the experienced Remigio. We have seen what Smith can do with the ball in his hands, and Toub sees it as a reason Smith will be featured more in the offense. “He has come along great,” Toub said. “If you watch his blocking, that’s where you really need to improve. He’s sticking up in there as a pass blocker because you do that a lot in our offense. The running backs have to do that a lot, and he’s doing a great job. There’s no question how he catches the ball out of the backfield and all that stuff, but he is stepping it up as a blocker.” The Chiefs will hold one more practice before Saturday’s game: Thursday morning at 9:15 a.m. The session is anticipated to be lighter with the exhibition nearing.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: Film breakdown: What can Emmanuel Ogbah give the Chiefs in Year 11?
summary: On Tuesday, the Kansas City Chiefs announced the signing of a familiar face. The team announced that they had signed veteran defensive end Emmanuel Ogbah. A ten-year NFL veteran, Ogbah notably played for the Chiefs in 2019, helping the team win Super Bowl LIV and finishing the season with 5.5 sacks, tying his career high […]
full_text: Football: Kansas City Chiefs Emmanuel Ogbah (90) victorious walking off field after game vs Denver Broncos at Sports Authority Field at Mile High. Denver, CO 10/17/2019 CREDIT: Jamie Schwaberow (Photo by Jamie Schwaberow /Sports Illustrated/Getty Images) (Set Number: X162989 TK1 ) | Sports Illustrated/Getty Images On Tuesday, the Kansas City Chiefs announced the signing of a familiar face. The team announced that they had signed veteran defensive end Emmanuel Ogbah. A ten-year NFL veteran, Ogbah notably played for the Chiefs in 2019, helping the team win Super Bowl LIV and finishing the season with 5.5 sacks, tying his career high at the time. A pectoral injury in Week 10 caused him to miss the Chiefs’ legendary playoff run, but his performance helped him sign a multi-year contract with the Miami Dolphins , where he played from 2020 to 2024 and had 29 sacks. After being released at the end of the 2024 season, Ogbah signed with the Jacksonville Jaguars , where he served as a reserve. Ogbah played in 38% of the Jaguars’ total defensive snaps and primarily lined up at defensive end, while he did shift inside to the defensive interior on some snaps. At 32 years old — and slated to turn 33 in November — Ogbah’s best football is likely behind him, but due to severe depth issues at defensive end, he will have a chance to make the roster and find playing time in Kansas City. Looking at the film from 2025 The Jaguars were the fourth NFL team the former second-round draft pick out of Oklahoma State has played for, and statistically, 2025 was one of the worst of Ogbah’s career. Finishing the season with fewer than a full sack and only ten pressures, it was statistically the worst pass-rushing season of his career, and the second-fewest snaps he played in. Ogbah made most of his impact in the run game, where his long frame still helped him to make stops. Ogbah quickly reads the outside run, does not allow the guard to reach him, presses off, and helps run down the RB for a minimal gain. pic.twitter.com/NZ6hYQClwO — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 12, 2026 His experience, ability to recognize plays and play-scheme-sound football are likely why the Chiefs were interested in adding him to the roster, especially since they lack a seasoned veteran presence among the depth pieces comprising the back end of the roster. Ogbah is playing the 4-tech. Keeps the OT and OG flat on the LOS and does not allow them to combo him up to the next level. Creates the play for his teammates. pic.twitter.com/C4XuKKnx59 — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 12, 2026 While his explosive power is not what it once was, he still has the base strength and length to take on combo blocks against teams that run a high percentage of zone looks. The length and base strength help him keep offensive linemen off him and either make plays or set up his teammates. Rushing the passer in limited looks last season, Ogbah struggled to build momentum, but the hope for the Chiefs is that he can regain his footing and become a player capable of finishing with between three and five sacks. Ogbah doesn't have the power, but he still uses his length and motor to get the job done from time to time. pic.twitter.com/vNwBqhm6sT — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 12, 2026 The power he once possessed to bull-rush and crush pockets is not what it was earlier in his career, but his length and motor remain the same. On the snap, he wins the inside hand battle against the right tackle, presses him into the backfield, and as the quarterback climbs in the pocket, he works back to the inside and comes up with the sack. The bottom line There should be no illusions that Ogbah is here to save the day; the edge unit will still be thin even with the addition, but what he can provide the Chiefs is a veteran presence and a player with a decent floor for 2026. George Karlaftis is the only edge rusher on the Chiefs roster with extensive experience, and at the bare minimum, Ogbah should be able to step in and eat up snaps as a run defender and help provide leadership to the Chiefs’young defensive line. The best-case scenario would be for Ogbah to return to the form he displayed during the 2024 season, but this may not be in the cards for him at this point either. The worst-case scenario would be a career full of injuries and general wear and tear from a decade in the trenches, causing an even further drop-off, which could cause Ogbah to not make the active roster or be released early in the season. Ultimately, general manager Brett Veach, in his typical fashion, is willing to bet on familiarity and players who know the system. His best football is likely behind him, but the Chiefs have a role that Ogbah can fill as the team continues to develop the young players on their roster.
author: Caleb James

title: Rashee Rice: ‘I’ve got the right group of guys around me’
summary: On Tuesday, fans of the Kansas City Chiefs finally heard from the most controversial player at the team’s training camp at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph. Wide receiver Rashee Rice missed most of the offseason program after a parole violation accelerated a jail sentence. This summer, Rice was ordered to serve 30 days […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 29: Rashee Rice #4 walks to the field before practice during the Kansas City Chiefs training camp on July 29, 2026 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On Tuesday, fans of the Kansas City Chiefs finally heard from the most controversial player at the team’s training camp at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph. Wide receiver Rashee Rice missed most of the offseason program after a parole violation accelerated a jail sentence . This summer, Rice was ordered to serve 30 days in jail as part of a 2025 plea deal for a 2024 street-racing-related car crash in Dallas. Originally, Rice was able to serve the jail time at his own discretion during the five-year probation period. After reportedly testing positive for THC, however, the Dallas County court ordered him to report to jail immediately. Rice was short on words in his description of the month and the lessons learned. “A learning experience and a reality check,” he remarked. “Don’t focus on the past. Focus on what’s going on now.” His focus has also turned to a more limited group of influences around him and improved mental health. “I’m doing good mentally,” Rice assessed. “I’ve got the right group of guys around me. Good agents. Good coaches. Small circle on anybody else outside that’s not part of the football team. Just keeping my head straight and also keeping me in a positive attitude.” The jail time was not the only limiting factor in Rice’s offseason. As we learned of his imminent incarceration, we also learned that the wideout underwent a knee cleanup procedure. Previously, Rice suffered a torn LCL in 2023 that robbed him of much of his second season. After leaving practice early to work with trainers in the first two weeks of camp, Rice is now participating more fully in team periods. He did not realize the procedure was needed until late in the spring. “Honestly, I thought it was probably just a little bit of swelling,” Rice explained. “I didn’t know it was something that needed to have surgery. We’re kind of taught to just keep going until you can’t anymore. It was a perfect time for me to get it cleaned up so it wouldn’t affect me for the season. I was ready to go, regardless.” As he ramped up his knee rehab following his release, Rice found motivation working alongside quarterback Patrick Mahomes. Mahomes has spent his offseason recovering from a major knee injury suffered in December. “The best part about it was being there with Pat,” Rice revealed. “Knowing that he had a more serious surgery and how hard he was working just kind of motivated me. Then, he’s pulling the craziest cars every day, so he’s my motivation every morning.” Through three seasons, Rice has teased game-breaking talent while also finding himself unavailable both due to injuries and a league suspension to open the 2025 season. Rice was asked to describe what he brings to a team beneath the surface of troubling headlines. “I would say I’m a positive guy,” he offered. “I’m a great person to feed off of as far as energy. A smiling guy, mostly at all times. Unless it’s time for work, [then] I’m serious. Then, I’m a father. I take the most responsibility in being a good father to my boys.” That serious work now finds the wide receiver room under stricter management from the coaching staff. Rice now plays under veteran receivers coach Chad O’Shea and longtime Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy, returning to Kansas City after a three-year absence. When he has been available, Rice has often commanded a disproportionate target share in the passing offense. Under Bieniemy and O’Shea, he has been working on what he can do to help his teammates, even if he knows a called play is not coming to him. He expects big things from the wide receiver room he shares with Xavier Worthy, Tyquan Thornton and rookie Cyrus Allen. “We’re going to do some amazing things,” Rice predicted. “Not only because we’re great receivers, but because we’ve got a good coaching staff around us as well as a great quarterback and a foundation in general.” That foundation has Rice in a good place after a dreadful offseason. “I’m 100% locked in on what’s going on now with the team,” Rice declared. “I’m ready to go out there and dominate. I’ve got a good brotherhood behind me.”

title: Chiefs News: Defense getting synced up has ‘been a little slow-moving’
summary: The latest The Kansas City Chiefs’ offense features the biggest changes the team made this offseason, with a new offensive coaching staff and a new lead running back. However, there is plenty that is brand new on the Chiefs’ defense as well. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo is focused on getting his unit in sync and […]
full_text: Kansas City Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo helps players run through drills at practice during training camp on July 21, 2024, in St. Joseph, Missouri. (Emily Curiel/The Kansas City Star/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) The latest The Kansas City Chiefs ’ offense features the biggest changes the team made this offseason, with a new offensive coaching staff and a new lead running back. However, there is plenty that is brand new on the Chiefs’ defense as well. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo is focused on getting his unit in sync and provided an update on how that process is going during his press conference on Tuesday. Steve Spagnuolo admits Chiefs’ new-look defense is moving slower than he’d like | The Kansas City Star Getting everybody in sync is taking a little too long. “It’s not as quickly as I’d like to, to be honest with you,” Spagnuolo said. “It’s been a little slow-moving. And (safety) Alohi Gilman, he’s new. It’s not like you have guys around some of these young corners that have been through it.” Spagnuolo’s unit is set to have at least six new base starters in 2026, including three in the secondary. In years past, mainstays like Trent McDuffie or Bryan Cook might have been around to help teach on the fly. Five Observations from Tuesday’s Practice | Chiefs Training Camp 8/11 | The Mothership 2. Safety Jaden Hicks had another strong day. Hicks, who made a handful of noteworthy plays during Monday’s practice, was back at it on Tuesday with another impressive performance. Specifically, the third-year safety made a strong pass-breakup on a tight window throw near the sideline during 11-on-11 drills before logging a diving pass-breakup down the field a little bit later. ‘Patrick Mahomes Loves Him’ — Tyrann Mathieu Reveals Chiefs Rookie Who’s Taken Training Camp ‘By Storm’ | Pro Football Sports Network According to Tyrann Mathieu, who played with Mahomes from 2019 to 2021, the quarterback is very happy with what he’s seen from the young receiver so far, and the coaches are also impressed by his practices during camp. “One of our homegrown kids, Cyrus Allen, has taken it by storm. Pat loves him, coaches love him. He was banged up a little bit, so he didn’t really practice while I was there, but me and him had a bunch of conversations, and he asked all the right questions, too”, said Mathieu. Kansas City Chiefs 2026 preview: Kenneth Walker, rookie class bolster rebound bid | Pro Football Focus Reason for pessimism Part of the reason for the Chiefs’ struggles in 2025 was a lack of production at wide receiver. Marquise Brown led the group with just 587 receiving yards, while Rashee Rice’s 77.2 PFF receiving grade was the best among the team’s wide receivers. Xavier Worthy also took a step back from his rookie season, with his PFF receiving grade falling from 71.6 to 66.3 and his yards per route run dropping from 1.51 to 1.25. Rice is expected to be available in Week 1 after missing significant time in each of the past two seasons. His career average of 2.29 yards per route run highlights his status as Kansas City’s most productive wide receiver, but the Chiefs need him to stay on the field in 2026. Retired NFL DL says Patrick Mahomes should sit out the season opener | Chiefs Wire During a recent appearance on CBS Sports HQ, NFL Analyst and former defensive lineman Leger Douzable discussed whether Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes should sit out the first few weeks of the regular season. “I wouldn’t even play him Week One, maybe even Week Two; you sign Justin Fields or trade for Justin Fields to come in to potentially start in the beginning of the season until Patrick Mahomes is truly healthy,” said Douzable. “My thing is, if Mahomes isn’t 100%, I would not risk putting him out there. They just signed him to an extension, so he could be there for, it seems, forever. Why would you risk him?” Chiefs OT Jaylon Moore Is Welcoming the Challenge From Rising Rookie Kahlil Benson | Sports Illustrated Now that Simmons is healthy and in the best shape of his life, the only starting spot available to Moore is on the right side. Although he’s predominantly played left tackle throughout his NFL career — including over 90% of his combined snaps in San Francisco — Moore is more than willing to adjust to a new spot on the offensive line. “Honestly for me, throughout my career, I’ve been back and forth,” Moore said. “It’s good to get the reps on either side because at any point, anything can happen. And it’s good to make sure that every one of our guys are able to play multiple different positions and be able to play wherever your number is called.” Around the NFL Bears safety Coby Bryant to miss 4-6 months after knee surgery | The Athletic The Bears’ prize of free agency, Bryant signed a three-year, $40 million contract in March. In his limited time with the team, he had already impressed the Bears both on and off the field. He made an outstanding interception earlier in camp, while his teammates and coaches have raved about his work habits and leadership. “I love his play style,” defensive coordinator Dennis Allen said last month. “I think it epitomizes the way we want to play the game.” First-round rookie Dillon Thieneman is the other starting safety, and a major plus of having a Super Bowl-winning safety like Bryant was his ability to help Thieneman grow. Now, that challenge will fall to a different player. Vikings name Kyler Murray starting QB over J.J. McCarthy | ESPN The deal includes $101 million guaranteed with $63.35 million guaranteed at signing, according to sources. Williams also received a signing bonus of $31.85 million, a source said. The $35.3 million annual average is the second highest among defensive tackles. Williams, 28, had been signed through 2027 in a four-year extension worth $96 million that guaranteed him $66 million from the New York Jets in 2023. He is now signed through 2030. Chargers OC Mike McDaniel plans to play ‘hot hand’ out of RB group | NFL.com “Bad news, fantasy owners,” McDaniel said via Kris Rhim of ESPN. “Good news is I see all three of those guys producing at a very high level. Bad news is I can’t tell you which games those are.” McDaniel spoke glowingly about running back Hampton early in training camp, noting how much the second-year back has grown. Hampton still profiles as the lead running back, with three-down upside, but McDaniel’s comments underscore that there are few true workhorses in the NFL in 2026. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Chiefs’ Steve Spagnuolo ‘always had an affection’ for Emmanuel Ogbah Kansas City will reportedly be signing veteran defensive end Emmanuel Ogbah, a former member of the Chiefs during the 2019 season. That was his fourth year in the league; the 32-year-old is now entering his 11th season with 48 career sacks to his name. The reunion has been a long time coming; defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo revealed his affinity for Ogbah during a post-practice press conference on Tuesday. “I always had an affection for E,” Spagnuolo said. “It was disappointing, the one year we had him in 2019, I thought he was really coming on, then he got hurt so we didn’t have him at the end of the year.” From The Feed Follow Arrowhead Pride on Social Media Facebook: Like our page Instagram: @ArrowheadPride X: Follow @ArrowheadPride AP Staff on X: See complete list 90.9 The Bridge on X: Follow @909thebridge

summary: The Chargers begin their preseason slate with a road trip to Houston. With the majority of starters expected to sit out, this will be our first look at a lot of the team’s young players. full_text: EL SEGUNDO, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 8: Tre' Harris #9 of the Los Angeles Chargers catches the ball during training camp at The Bolt on August 8, 2026 in El Segundo, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers begin their preseason slate with a road trip to Houston. With the majority of starters expected to sit out, this will be our first look at a lot of the team’s young players. You should not expect a performance for the ages, but predicting one or two players to standout is always worth doing as some of these fringe players really do make or miss the team in these next few weeks. With that said, here are six Chargers I’ll be watching closely when they take the field against the Texans. WR Tre’ Harris Harris played an incredibly unsung role as a rookie for the Chargers. While he finished with just 30 receptions for 324 yards and a touchdown, Harris was instrumental as a run blocker. At 6’3 and 210 pounds, he’s one of the biggest receivers on the team and he played like it when asked to stick his face into a defender. I would also be remiss not to mention how many clutch plays he came up with for Justin Herbert on third downs and other “gotta have it” moments. Harris should have a chance at a breakout year as the team’s WR3, but his ability as a blocker will make it incredibly hard for the coaching staff to ever take him off the field. Being the team’s WR3 behind both Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston means Harris is a fringe-starter and very well could end up sitting out this game. If that’s not the case, I’ll be excited to see just how Harris will be used in Mike McDaniels’ offense, even if it’s a very vanilla version of it. TRE HARRIS 😱 pic.twitter.com/rgpgVZtsjP — SleeperNFL (@SleeperNFL) August 11, 2026 OG/C Jake Slaughter, OG Kayode Awosika, and OT/G Branson Taylor Slaughter has been gaining more and more momentum over the past week in the battle to start at left guard. However, Awosika still seems to be the frontrunner as he’s been in the rotation with the ones just about every single day of camp. It’s only been recently that Slaughter has seen an uptick in his snaps with the ones. Taylor has also been receiving snaps at left guard and he’s done well enough to push Trevor Penning out of the competition completely. With Slater missing most of the last week, he’s also been receiving snaps at left tackle alongside Trey Pipkins. From being amongst the final cuts last year as a rookie to pushing for a starting spot in year two, Taylor has seemingly worked his tail off to impress this coaching staff and that alone makes me excited to see him play on Thursday. Jake Slaughter (I almost died in the making of this) pic.twitter.com/0HGT5Pub1B — Kris Rhim (@krisrhim1) August 3, 2026 EDGE Nadame Tucker Even with the Chargers using a first-round pick on edge rusher Akheem Mesidor, there’s still been plenty of hype around Tucker who wasn’t even amongst the 250+ players drafted this year. In 2025, Tucker recorded 14.5 sacks to tie David Bailey (2026’s third-overall pick) for the most in the country. He also ended the year with the same tackle for loss total as Mesidor. Tucker is no slouch and his sacks did not count any less just because he was doing it differently than the other high draft picks at the position. If Tucker can translate his recent success in practice to the field in these next few games, he could very well make the team as the final pass rusher and force the Chargers to keep him away from potential waivers from other teams. Assistant outside linebackers coach Denzel Martin with Tuli Tuipulotu, Nadame Tucker and Akheem Mesidor pic.twitter.com/AmW3j9Y429 — Kris Rhim (@krisrhim1) August 6, 2026 CB Avery Smith Smith spent several seasons learning from current Eagles Pro Bowler Quinyon Mitchell while both were at Toledo and despite going undrafted this year, he’s been showing out in camp on more than one occasion. He’s been sticky against all competition and could very well have just as many standout plays the past two weeks as any other defensive back. Even with guys like Nikko Reed and Eric Rogers still on the team after their impressive preseasons a year ago, Smith could very break into that group and force the Chargers to make a really tough choice. Which ones do you keep on the final roster and which ones can you risk possibly be claimed off waivers? All of them will have three opportunities to make their case and it’ll take at least one impressive outing by Smith to make sure that whole conversation gets started in the first place. Chargers S Derwin James Jr. on UDFA CB Avery Smith: "Confidence, swagger, he's throwing on the seat belt after he makes a play." "He don't shy away from any competition. Very smart, confident player." — Alex Insdorf (@alexinsdorf99) August 4, 2026

title: The Rams probably regret cutting this preseason hero
summary: There are several “what if” scenarios in recent Los Angeles Rams history that cut the fanbase to the bone. LA used a second-round pick on a gadget receiver in Tutu Atwell over an All-Pro interior lineman in Creed Humphrey. This spring they used the 13th overall selection on quarterback Ty Simpson rather than Makai Lemon, […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - AUGUST 09: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Stetson Bennett IV (13) prepares to take a snap from offensive lineman Willie Lampkin IV (62) in the third quarter of an NFL preseason football game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Los Angeles Rams, Saturday, Aug. 9, 2025, in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Tony Ding/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images There are several “what if” scenarios in recent Los Angeles Rams history that cut the fanbase to the bone. LA used a second-round pick on a gadget receiver in Tutu Atwell over an All-Pro interior lineman in Creed Humphrey. This spring they used the 13th overall selection on quarterback Ty Simpson rather than Makai Lemon, Kenyon Sadiq, or someone who could have helped in a 2026 Super Bowl push. And the latest example is the fact that Willie Lampkin is now excelling in training camp with the Philadelphia Eagles one year removed from the Rams releasing him. Let’s check in on reports from Eagles camp: The “little secret weapon”: Because it has become clear over the last couple of weeks that Lampkin is an NFL player and he’s pushing extremely hard for a spot on the Eagles’ 53-man roster. He has been turning the heads of his teammates and coaches along the way. “I think Willie’s done a phenomenal job,” starting left guard Landon Dickerson said. “He plays with great leverage, great feet. He’s a strong guy. “He’s kind of like our little secret weapon when it comes to the D-linemen. I just don’t think he’s your typical size for an offensive lineman, which can be a game-changer going against defensive linemen.”… Lampkin has been an absolute menace in 1-on-1 drills and has carried that success over to team drills. He is pushing hard for a roster spot and his versatility — he can play all three interior spots — makes him a valuable player. From head coach Nick Sirianni: 5'11" interior offensive lineman Willie Lampkin has been turning heads so far at Eagles training camp. pic.twitter.com/heSDzS7OPQ — NBC Sports Philadelphia (@NBCSPhilly) August 10, 2026 Lampkin was excellent last year for Rams Lampkin played in one-and-a-half exhibition games in 2025 for Los Angeles before suffering knee and ankle injuries. He showed flashes of elite play versus the Dallas Cowboys in his first ever NFL appearance. According to Pro Football Focus (PFF), Lampkin posted the below metrics while primarily playing at center and a little left guard: Offensive grade: 94.1 Run blocking grade: 92.2 Pass blocking grade: 78.6 Rams averaged 6.2 yards per carry on five middle-left runs The Rams’ gut-wrenching mistake The Rams are staring down the barrel of needing to soon sign both guards in Steve Avila and Kevin Dotson. There are no shortage of young players that LA must give new contracts. The Rams would have more flexibility if they had solid alternative options—someone like Lampkin. They simply do not have other viable paths currently. Les Snead and Sean McVay thought they could use Lampkin’s injury as an opportunity to stash him on the roster. They released him with a waived/injured designation and he would have converted to injured reserve if he went unclaimed. The Eagles saw his preseason performance and brought him to Philadelphia. Keeping Lampkin would have meant cutting someone else from the initial 53-man roster. That is tough to do for an injured player that may not be on the field soon, although Lampkin could have been moved to injured reserve after he made the first 53. The Rams thought they could sneak Lampkin onto the roster for 2026. The Eagles called LA’s bluff in a move that is very rarely seen. Less than 1-2% of players get claimed following a waived/injured designation. This is the latest advantage Philly found on the edge of roster building strategies. What’s done is done; however, the Rams probably wish they still had Willie Lampkin.

title: Key takeaways from Rams first depth chart
summary: On Wednesday afternoon, the Los Angeles Rams released their first depth chart ahead of the 2026 preseason and regular season. The depth chart always should be taken with a grain of salt considering teams are still conducting their evaluations ahead of preseason matchups. However, a depth chart can serve as a measuring stick and provide […]
full_text: On Wednesday afternoon, the Los Angeles Rams released their first depth chart ahead of the 2026 preseason and regular season. The depth chart always should be taken with a grain of salt considering teams are still conducting their evaluations ahead of preseason matchups. However, a depth chart can serve as a measuring stick and provide fans with some insight as to what the Rams may be thinking with their strategy, personnel, etc. Here are a few takeaways from the Rams depth chart release… TAKEAWAYS 1. Stetson Bennett is the back up to Matthew Stafford. Fans might have been hoping for Ty Simpson to be further along in the pecking order but the Rams are clearly taking his development at a controlled pace. Simpson will likely get the bulk of the preseason snaps with him landing on the third string 2. First Team Rotation at Tight End The Rams do not have a favorite at tight end, although Colby Parkinson is probably the guy. The team opted to list all four returning tight ends under the first string. Max Klare, the team’s second round rookie was on the second string. Davis Allen is still nursing a quad injury that he suffered at the beginning of training camp. 3. Punt Returner Solution Resolved? Xavier Smith, not Kyren Williams was listed as the team’s punt returner. Konata Mumpfield was listed as the second string. Kyren Williams was not even listed. Was KW simply trying out a week ago? Does this mean Xavier Smith’s job is safe? Who knows… 4. Linebacker Pecking Order Omar Speights still appears to still be Nate Landman’s running mate as Shaun Dolac was listed as Nate Landman’s backup. Stuard was listed as the second string behind Speights. 5. EDGE Rush Undrafted free agent Wesley Bailey was listed on the 4th string. He had received hype before training camp as a candidate to make the roster as an undrafted free agent. However, he has his work cut out for him as Keir Thomas II and Tomon Fox are ahead of him. 6. Jarquez Hunter Stock Down The Rams 4th round draft choice from the 2025 NFL Draft is listed with the 4th string…not exactly a ringing endorsement for the second year player. It would have been more welcoming to see his name listed alongside of Ronnie Rivers on the third team. 7. No Aaron Donald…Yet The Rams legend is not yet signed to the roster. Still things could change in a matter of 24 hours…as it is expected that Donald could officially rejoin the team this week. FINAL REACTION There are no real surprises for the Rams depth chart. Teams are unlikely to give away any more information as they want to protect their assets for when they have to cut players. Retaining players on the practice squad is a key method in today’s NFL. The Rams have never been a team to overzealous with their depth chart release so any major news from a depth chart release should be tempered for now.

full_text: The Los Angeles Rams have reached another important checkpoint of training camp, releasing their first unofficial depth chart ahead of the team’s opening preseason matchup. While the word “unofficial” is doing plenty of work here, the depth chart still provides an early glimpse into how the coaching staff currently views the roster and which players are positioned to receive opportunities when the preseason begins. Fans should be careful about reading too much into the initial listings. Around the NFL, teams are releasing their first preseason depth charts this week, and many of them include veteran players ahead of rookies and younger competitors even when the practice reps suggest a much closer competition. For the Rams, the biggest value of the depth chart may not be identifying who will ultimately start in Week 1. Instead, it gives fans a starting point for evaluating the battles that will dominate the preseason. OFFENSE DEFENSE SPECIAL TEAMS Ultimately, this first depth chart should be viewed as a starting point rather than a prediction of the final roster . Depth charts can change dramatically throughout August, particularly after preseason games expose strengths, weaknesses and unexpected performances.

title: Make 1 change to the Rams offense before the season starts
summary: The Los Angeles Rams enter the 2026 season with plenty of reasons to believe their offense can be one of the NFL’s best. Matthew Stafford remains at quarterback, Puka Nacua and Davante Adams give Sean McVay two proven weapons on the outside, and the backfield features one of the league’s more intriguing running back combinations […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams enter the 2026 season with plenty of reasons to believe their offense can be one of the NFL’s best. Matthew Stafford remains at quarterback, Puka Nacua and Davante Adams give Sean McVay two proven weapons on the outside, and the backfield features one of the league’s more intriguing running back combinations in Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. The Rams have also shown signs of evolving their offensive philosophy, with more attention being given to multiple-tight-end personnel packages. But if you could make one change to the Rams offense entering the season, what would it be? That’s the question. It doesn’t necessarily have to be a massive overhaul. In fact, the best change might be a relatively small adjustment that gets the most out of the personnel already on the roster. Option 1: Personnel Change One possibility would be returning to using more 11 personnel — one running back and one tight end — and getting three wide receivers on the field together more frequently. With Nacua and Adams occupying two of those spots, the third receiver role becomes extremely important. Finding consistency from that position could force defenses to respect the entire width of the field and create more room for Stafford, Nacua and Adams. The question is whether the Rams have enough separation and playmaking ability at WR3 to make that personnel grouping consistently dangerous. The opposite approach could be just as interesting. The Rams have multiple tight ends capable of contributing, and reports have indicated that McVay’s offense could lean more heavily into 12 and 13 personnel in 2026. That could give Stafford additional options in the middle of the field while also creating heavier formations for the running game. It could also allow the Rams to disguise their intentions more effectively before the snap. Option 2: Player Change Another change could simply be putting another player on the field that is not currently getting enough playing time. Kyren Williams remains the Rams’ RB1 and had 259 carries for 1,252 yards and 10 touchdowns in 2025. But Corum has shown enough to warrant a larger role, and the Rams have one of the league’s more intriguing running back duos. Instead of treating Corum primarily as a change-of-pace option, McVay could intentionally design portions of the game plan around him. Option 3: Find a Better WR3 Solution Maybe the biggest question is the third wide receiver. Nacua and Adams give the Rams an outstanding starting pair, but the offense could become significantly more dangerous if a legitimate WR3 emerges. The Rams’ current depth chart lists Jordan Whittington, Xavier Smith and Konata Mumpfield among the players competing for receiver opportunities behind the top names. Should the Rams sign someone else? Tyreek Hill? Josh Reynolds? Brandin Cooks? Keenan Allen? Option 4: Adding Insurance The Rams are still waiting to hear about whether the NFL will take action against Puka Nacua and Alaric Jackson regarding off field incidents. If the NFL does take action, the Rams star wide receiver and left tackle out via suspension. Might it be prudent for the Rams to sign someone to the roster before it is too late? Taylor Decker would the most logical option to fill a void. Option 5: Adjustments to Sean McVay’s Play Calling McVay doesn’t necessarily need different players. He might simply need to change how he uses them. More motion? More play-action? More opportunities for the tight ends? More creativity on early downs? Run the ball more? The Rams have enough talent that the biggest improvement could come from maximizing what is already there. So, if you could make ONE change to the Rams offense, what would it be?

title: Bears’ Johnson admits he got out-coached by Sean McVay
summary: The Los Angeles Rams were 3.5 point favorites to beat the Chicago Bears in the divisional round of the 2025 playoffs, but needed overtime to sneak past them and into the NFC Championship game. The Bears gave the Rams all they could handle in 19-degrees weather, but it’s a game that Chicago head coach Ben […]
full_text: Jan 18, 2026; Chicago, IL, USA; Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson looks on during warmups before an NFC Divisional Round game against the Los Angeles Rams at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Los Angeles Rams were 3.5 point favorites to beat the Chicago Bears in the divisional round of the 2025 playoffs, but needed overtime to sneak past them and into the NFC Championship game. The Bears gave the Rams all they could handle in 19-degrees weather, but it’s a game that Chicago head coach Ben Johnson still thinks he should have won. It’s a loss that’s been bothering Johnson all year, admitting that he didn’t understand how big of an advantage homefield would be for the Bears and that he didn’t have as good of a gameplan as Sean McVay. In a wide-ranging behind-the-scenes look with the Bears head coach, The Athletic’s Dan Pompei details some of the decisions that have haunted Johnson over the last eight months . He also wants to spend more time on game management, partly because of how he handled the Bears’ 20-17 overtime loss to the Rams in the divisional round of the playoffs. “I kick myself when I think about that game,” he says. Given his respect for Rams coach Sean McVay, MVP quarterback Matthew Stafford and the top-scoring offense in the NFL, Johnson anticipated a shootout. He was mentally unprepared to downshift to a more conservative attack to account for 25-mph winds, a wind chill of four below and snow. He regrets not attempting a field goal in the first quarter on fourth-and-2 from the Rams’ 21. Williams was intercepted on the play. “I should have changed the mindset,” he says. “I know now that the power of Soldier Field, particularly at that time of year, is a real thing. And it should be a major advantage for us, provided we recognize it and play with a certain style.” Only two minutes into the game, the Bears had driven to L.A.’s 21-yard line, largely aided by a 34-yard catch and run by Chicago receiver D.J. Moore. Perhaps little did Johnson know that big plays like that would be hard to come by over the rest of regulation and overtime. Johnson called a Caleb Williams passing play on fourth-and-2, resulting in an interception by Cobie Durant that was returned for 14 yards. (A pass Durant maybe should have let fall incomplete.) COBIE DURANT INTERCEPTION AND RETURN ON FOURTH DOWN #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/gujjd1TlKN — Jack (@MidwestLAFan) January 18, 2026 The Rams then ran a 14-play drive, including 10 passes by Matthew Stafford, capped off with a Kyren Williams touchdown run. The Bears answered with a touchdown drive of their own, but neither team would score a touchdown again until Williams’ scored again in the fourth quarter. Chicago needed a miraculous fourth down touchdown pass by Williams with :18 seconds left to force overtime. But what if Johnson had attempted that field goal to start the game instead? It’s a decision that’s been bothering Johnson for months. Will he do something differently if the Bears face the Rams in the playoffs again? He’d like to find out.

title: The Rams are the NFL’s second-most valuable franchise
summary: The Los Angeles Rams and Dallas Cowboys’ joint training camp matchup this week featured two of the NFL’s most valuable franchises. Sportico listed the Cowboys and Rams at spots No. 1 and 2, respectively, in its annual NFL team value rankings ahead of the 2026 season. According to the outlet, Los Angeles is valued at […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 8: Stan Kroenke of the Los Angeles Rams on the sideline during a game against the Philadelphia Eagles at SoFi Stadium on October 8, 2023 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams and Dallas Cowboys’ joint training camp matchup this week featured two of the NFL’s most valuable franchises. Sportico listed the Cowboys and Rams at spots No. 1 and 2, respectively, in its annual NFL team value rankings ahead of the 2026 season. According to the outlet, Los Angeles is valued at $12.7 billion, well behind the ‘Boys’ league-leading $15.5 billion valuation. The Dallas Cowboys are followed by the Los Angeles Rams at $12.7 billion, the New York Giants at $12 billion, the New England Patriots at $10.4 billion, and the New York Jets at $10.35 billion to round out the top five. https://t.co/MpfCGb2zdy pic.twitter.com/snnkJj0y01 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 12, 2026 At first glance, it’s surprising that the Patriots aren’t higher on the list. After all, they appeared in the Super Bowl in February, not the Rams, and they also have six Lombardi Trophies to their name. How odd. Dallas being the most valued NFL franchise for perhaps the umpteenth year in a row is not shocking. When you’re dubbed “America’s Team,” it’s only fair. Gross, I hated every bit of typing out that last sentence. However, it’s true, as the Cowboys are a household name. Even when they lose, they win. They always get a fair share of primetime slots throughout the season, simply because they’re the Cowboys. While it’s unlikely that any NFL team, including the Rams, can surpass Dallas in team value, the cost of owning a professional football team only continues to rise. ESPN’s Adam Schefter posted on social media that the average NFL team is now worth just over $9 billion, which is up from the 2025 average of $7.13 billion. That marks the largest year-over-year gain in franchise value since Sportico launched its valuations in 2020. Just think, the worst team in the league is worth that much. Well, unless I win the lottery or a major lawsuit, my dream of owning an NFL team went down the toilet. It always warms my heart to see the rich getting richer. Ah capitalism! Like most things associated with the NFL, expect those valuations to continue skyrocketing over the next several years. All you have to do is take a look at the teams that have recently been sold. The defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks are set to be sold for $9.6 billion, pending approval. That would be an NFL record, and should it go through, it would be 59% higher than the previous record of $6.05 billion for the Washington Commanders in 2023. The Rams sold for $750 million in 2010 , back when they still played in St. Louis. Between the move to Hollywood and another Lombardi in their trophy case, their value has only grown exponentially over time. L.A. is unlikely to surpass the Cowboys in team valuation, but it ultimately doesn’t matter. Since returning to Los Angeles, the Rams have transformed themselves into a destination for high-profile players, boosting their championship credibility. Imagine what another Super Bowl win within the next couple of years will do to their team value. Can you say cha-ching, cha-ching?

title: Puka Nacua left Rams-Cowboys practice with groin injury
summary: Puka Nacua left a joint practice against the Dallas Cowboys on Tuesday and although neither Sean McVay nor Matthew Stafford knew what happened at the time, Ian Rapoport later reported it as a “minor” groin injury. Reportedly Nacua is fine, but only time will tell if this causes the star receiver to miss any more […]
full_text: Westchester, - August 01: Wide receiver Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams during the Los Angeles Rams training camp on the campus of Loyola Marymount University in Westchester on Saturday, August 1, 2026. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images Puka Nacua left a joint practice against the Dallas Cowboys on Tuesday and although neither Sean McVay nor Matthew Stafford knew what happened at the time, Ian Rapoport later reported it as a “minor” groin injury. Reportedly Nacua is fine, but only time will tell if this causes the star receiver to miss any more practices moving forward. Elsewhere on the Rams’ roster, Myles Garrett missed his second straight day of practice with a knee injury. #Rams WR Puka Nacua, who left practice while walking with a trainer, is dealing with minor soreness in his groin, I'm told. The team is just being cautious. — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) August 11, 2026 The L.A. Rams have built a “super-team” this offseason, but they better hope none of these injuries become super serious. Puka Nacua injury: Rams star reportedly dealing with ‘minor’ groin soreness (ramswire) “According to Rapoport, Nacua is dealing with minor soreness in his groin that doesn’t appear to be serious. Still, any absence involving Nacua draws scrutiny given his track record. He suffered a significant right-knee injury that was later aggravated in the season opener in 2025, resulting in a PCL sprain and five games on injured reserve. In 2025, an ankle sprain against Baltimore briefly slowed him again, though he missed just one game before closing out a career year. Nacua is known for his aggressive play style, too, which sometimes leads to lots of bumps and bruises throughout the year.“ Rams’ Sean McVay Announces Puka Nacua News After Leaving Practice (athlonsports) “Nacua was elected to his first All-Pro team, and with the core of McVay-Stafford-Nacua intact, Los Angeles expects to make it back to the Super Bowl for the 2026 season. The team is currently training at its practice facility at the Warner Center in Woodland Hills, California. On Tuesday, the team received news about a potential injury to its star wide receiver. On the social media website X, ESPN’s Lindsey Thiry reported that Nacua left practice early with the training staff. Head coach McVay kept the information close to the vest, as McVay did not give an update on the potential injury to former BYU Cougar standout.“ Rams Star Puka Nacua Could Be Suspended For Week 1 (sports.yahoo.com) “The antisemism allegations followed an earlier incident in which Nacua made a gesture that “perpetuated harmful stereotypes against Jewish people” on a livestream in December. Nacua apologized, and the NFL and Rams publicly condemned his actions. Although he didn’t offer any updates on the legal situation, Nacua addressed his offseason to reporters two weeks ago. “There’s definitely trying to take accountability for the things that I know that I can continue to change and can grow in ways that I know that have helped me feel as best as I can when I step out here on the football field and outside of the football field,” Nacua said.“ Practice Points: Cowboys’ defense dominates Rams in joint practice (dallascowboys..com) “All eyes are on the Dallas Cowboys’ defense entering the 2026 season and, after their joint practice with the Los Angeles Rams, the optimism hovering over Christian Parker and his staff is feeling justified. The “iron sharpens iron” mantra that forces Parker’s group to face off daily against Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, and Javonte Williams, showed up in a big way when the new-look defense was tested for the first time against another team. And the fact that team is led by Matthew Stafford, schemed by Sean McVay and contains tons of firepower both downfield and in the backfield matters that much more. In the end, Parker’s defense owned the day, led by linebacker Justin Barron, who gave Stafford and Stetson Bennett pure hell in LA.“ From the Podium: Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford react to Rams’ joint practice with Cowboys (therams.com) “We’ve been going against each other for a long time. It’ll be good to be able to look at the film, see what we can learn. These are opportunities for us to grow, even though we don’t game plan it, we’re just testing our rules. But there was a lot of good stuff really from both sides, and I look forward to really looking at the film and diving into how we can learn from it.” – McVay The joint practice was the first opportunity to see a different defense and offense for the Rams after spending the last two weeks at LMU. Although the practice is unscripted for the offense, McVay still acknowledges the benefits that can come from examining the operations against a different defense.“ Rams Get Positive Puka Nacua Injury Update, Remain Cautious With Myles Garrett (si.com) “Nacua wasn’t the only player the Rams were cautious with on Tuesday. After missing three consecutive practices during training camp , Garrett returned to the field for the final two days. He also practiced when the team got back to Woodland Hills. However, Garrett was held out once again for the joint practice with the Cowboys due to some swelling in his knee. McVay said that Garrett felt 85 percent, but the team erred on the side of caution. “We just erred on the side of caution,” said McVay. “He wanted to be able to be out there, but we want to make sure that when he returns to play, he’s able to return to full performance and feel like himself. There’s nothing to be concerned about. It was just us erring on the side of caution.” Is Aaron Donald returning to Rams? Rumors, news and updates for Aug. 11 (usatoday) “As the Los Angeles Rams prepare for their first preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs on Saturday, Aug. 15, their biggest question mark remains the status of Aaron Donald and whether or not he will return for a potential run at the Super Bowl this season. Momentum seems to be pointing in the direction of Donald, one of the greatest defensive linemen of all-time, suiting up for the Rams again after walking away from the game three years ago, but neither he nor head coach Sean McVay have yet to say anything definitive. The three-time Defensive Player of the Year worked out with the team last week and was spotted running through drills with Braden Fiske and Desjuan Johnson at the Rams’ practice facility on Sunday, Aug. 9. McVay told reporters on Thursday that Donald flew out his speed trainer from Pittsburgh to Los Angeles.“ Cowboys star makes NSFW wager with Rams before heated joint practice (nypost) “There was no indication the Rams accepted his challenge—or that a Los Angeles player was even within earshot. It takes two sides to make a wager, especially when the proposed prize could be sitting inside a six-figure jewelry collection. Prescott has previously described trash talk as part of his leadership style , saying he deliberately provokes teammates who respond well to confrontation. “I start a lot of it,” Prescott said in 2023. “I open the door and make people feel comfortable to talk trash to me.” The Rams supplied a response once practice began.“ 10 Observations from Rams’ joint practice with Cowboys: Pass game and pass rush in focus (therams.com) “”I thought he was great,” McVay said when asked about Stafford’s performance. “There was one where just a little bit late over the middle, but I thought he kept the ball in play. I thought he saw coverage really well.” Stetson Bennett IV gets majority of second-team reps, Ty Simpson shines in his opportunities: Like in Rams Training Camp at LMU, Bennett took the majority of the second-team offense reps. He often received pressure from the Cowboys’ defensive front, but was still able to make plays down the field with a pair of interceptions mixed in by Barron over the middle. The rookie Simpson came in for a drive starting from midfield and…

title: 4 Keys To Watch For In Las Vegas Raiders Preseason Opener
summary: Thursday, August 13th, the Las Vegas Raiders open the 2026 NFL preseason at home against the Arizona Cardinals. Raider Nation’s first look at the new Raiders, the coaching staff and players alike. Heading into the first preseason game lets take a look at some position groups and key players to watch in the game. There […]
full_text: HENDERSON, NEVADA - JULY 29: DJ Glaze #71, Jackson Powers-Johnson #58, and Tyler Linderbaum #65 of the Las Vegas Raiders run through a drill during the first practice of the team's training camp at the Las Vegas Raiders Headquarters/Intermountain Health Performance Center on July 29, 2026 in Henderson, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Thursday, August 13th, the Las Vegas Raiders open the 2026 NFL preseason at home against the Arizona Cardinals. Raider Nation’s first look at the new Raiders, the coaching staff and players alike. Heading into the first preseason game lets take a look at some position groups and key players to watch in the game. There are many on offense, as it was an underperforming unit last season with a lot of new pieces. Fernando Mendoza Vincent Bonsignore, Host of The Morning Tailgate on Raider Nation Radio and senior NFL Columnist for the California Post, tweeted that the Raiders officially have a quarterback competition. Let’s be honest: no matter what happens, the future for the Raiders is Mendoza. If Bonsignore is correct and there is indeed a quarterback battle, then for such a philosophical pivot, Mendoza must be ahead of schedule. There's actually a real QB battle in @Raiders camp. I still believe Kirk gets the opener, but it's not etched in stone. Fernando has a real chance to win the job. https://t.co/yiwr3JgaDa — Vincent Bonsignore (@VinnyBonsignore) August 12, 2026 When Mendoza takes the field, his footwork will be on full display, as will his ability to run the offense from under center. With a firsthand view of his acclimation to NFL game speed, his quick processing and decision-making ability. Along with his ability to feel and evade the rush, will he overtake Cousins? Offensive line Rick Dennison, the Raiders’ new offensive line coach, is one of the best to ever do it. He has put together multiple Super Bowl-winning offensive lines. Dennison’s familiarity with head coach Klint Kubiak goes all the way back to when he coached for his dad, Gary Kubiak. Delmar Glaze, has had a good camp thus far and appears to be holding his own at the right tackle position. Last year was not the best for Glaze; under Brennan Carroll, he struggled with speed rushers. Often getting blown past out of his stance and chasing defenders rather than blocking them. Coaching makes a difference and if Glaze has a bounce-back year then things are looking up. Charles Grant , has got to be prepared to go this season. One can hope for the best with Kolton Miller’s health but the truth is the injuries are piling up. Grant will exit training camp the backup left tackle and swing tackle provided he has good preseason showings. A lot is being thrown at him as well. Spencer Burford , is slated to start at left guard according to the first unofficial depth chart. He has played under Kubiak in the past with the San Francisco 49ers and knows the system. He has a lot to prove as there are a ton of hungry guards on the Raiders looking to make their mark. Running backs Ashton Jeanty , had a hard time finding holes in his rookie campaign. In the offseason, he made a choice to alter his diet and change his physical composition. His goal was to improve his conditioning to accommodate the role he has set for him. Running backs with great cutting ability do well in Kubiak’s system and he will get fed the rock. Mike Washington Jr , has great tape at Arkansas University with a nearly identical body type to Darren McFadden. Washington’s one-cut-and-run ability with tremendous burst and great speed should do well in this offense. He also brings a lot more size to the table and some attitude to boot. We don’t want to get too excited just yet, but the silver and black have the beginnings of a good one-two punch as there is in the league. Should the offensive line be able to do its part, the running backs will certainly do theirs. Wide Receivers Tre Tucker , has shown promise and growth despite continuously being thrust into adverse situations. Surviving the coaching regimens of Josh McDaniels, Antonio Pierce and Pete Carroll is no small task. As if that wasn’t enough, he has had to rely on Geno Smith, Aidan O’Connell, Gardner Minshew and Jimmy Garoppolo to throw him the football. This offense should set him loose and with Kirk Cousins, he will have a much more capable quarterback throwing him the ball. Malik Benson , making noise in training camp is one thing; making the transition to Sundays is another altogether. Benson will get some run with the twos and an opportunity to continue to add to his resume. Getting paired with Mendoza will give us a great look at both. Proving himself against different competition will continue to free up playing time. Jalen Nailor , huge fan of his game once I threw on the tape and started watching. He got lost in Minnesota behind their 1 and 2 options, Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison. With the Raiders, he has as good a chance as any to be the guy here. Jack Bech , finished last season as a bit of an enigma. Averaging 11.2 yards per catch but was only targeted 29 times. Catching a total of 20 passes for 224 yards and dropped only one. He, too, has a lot to prove and the receiving room is crowded. Can he establish himself? We shall see.
