title: Las Vegas Raiders 53-man roster prediction ahead of preseason game against Arizona Cardinals
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are about to play their first preseason game of the 2026 NFL season, facing off against the Arizona Cardinals. That also means it’s time for the first attempt at who will be on the Raiders’ 53-man roster at the end of training camp. For simplicity, it’s assumed that 25 players on […]
full_text: Feb 10, 2026; Henderson, NV, USA; Las Vegas Raiders coach Klint Kubiak (left) and general manager John Spytek at introductory press conference at Intermountain Health Performance Center. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Las Vegas Raiders are about to play their first preseason game of the 2026 NFL season, facing off against the Arizona Cardinals . That also means it’s time for the first attempt at who will be on the Raiders’ 53-man roster at the end of training camp. For simplicity, it’s assumed that 25 players on each side of the ball (offense/defense) and three specialists will be on the team for the first roster prediction. Silver and Black Pride will publish a new prediction after each preseason game to provide updates based on how each player looks in the contests and the reports from training camp. Quarterback Starter: Kirk Cousins Backups: Fernando Mendoza (R), Aidan O’Connell Cut: Jacob Clark (R) The only real question at quarterback is what’s going to happen with O’Connell? He’s entering a contract year, and it’s no secret that Mendoza is the franchise’s future behind center, while Cousins is the bridge-gap starter. That could make O’Connell a trade candidate at the end of camp, especially if he plays well during the preseason. Or, as recently discussed in a mailbag column , the coaching staff might want to keep the four-year pro around as a backup to prevent Mendoza from having to play before he’s ready if something were to happen to Cousins. Running Back Starter: Ashton Jeanty Backups: Mike Washington Jr. (R), Connor Heyward (FB), Dylan Laube Cut: Roman Hemby (R) , Dare Ogunbowale It seems pretty clear that Jeanty and Washington will hold the top two spots in the Raiders’ backfield, and Heyward is the only fullback on the roster to make things simple. However, the running back room gets complicated when it comes to the final opening. Laube gets the nod right now because he can contribute on special teams and has the longest tenure in Las Vegas. But Hemby can easily take that role, and it’s worth noting that Ogubowale was signed after the coaching staff had a handful of practices to evaluate the position. Wide Receiver Starters: Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor, Malik Benson (R) Backups: Jack Bech, Dareke Young, E.J. Williams (R) Cut: Dont’e Thornton Jr., Chase Roberts (R), Shedrick Jackson, Phillip Dorsett II, Deven Thompkins The big question here is how many wideouts will the Raiders roster? I could see Klint Kubiak rolling with just five—with a couple on the practice squad—depending on how much 12 personnel he wants to run. On that note, the starters above are assuming 11 personnel. Also, wide receiver isn’t exactly a deep position group for the Silver and Black to complicate the projections at this stage. As far as the prediction goes, the big surprise would be Thornton getting cut. However, that seems to be getting less shocking every day. ESPN’s Ryan McFadden noted recently that the fourth-round pick has been working with the second- and third-team offenses while being “nonexistent whenever on the field and has had a hard time creating separation from defenders.” Tight Ends Starter: Brock Bowers Backups: Michael Mayer, Ian Thomas Cut: Carter Runyon, Patrick Gurd, Albert Okwuegbunam , Chris Myarick If Kubiak leans on 12 personnel, push Mayer up to the ‘starter(s)’ category. Heading into camp, I was hopeful that Runyon could beat out Thomas for the third tight end spot. But the former suffered an early injury and hasn’t been able to practice since. So, right now, the nine-year veteran has a significant advantage in making the team. Offensive Line Starters: Kolton Miller, Spencer Burford, Tyler Linderbaum, Jackson Powers-Johnson, DJ Glaze Backups: Charles Grant, Caleb Rogers, Jordan Meredith, Trey Zuhn III (R) Cut: Dalton Wagner, Will Putnam, Atonio Mafi, Kamar Missouri (R), Justin Pickett (R), Isaiah Jatta (R), Niklas Henning (R) Three out of the five Raiders’ starting offensive line spots were expected to be up for grabs this summer. However, Burford has taken all of the first-team snaps at left guard, and the right guard battle is leaning toward Powers-Johnson since he’s taken the majority of first-team reps at that spot. Granted, JPJ and Rogers have been rotating recently, but Rogers missed practice with an injury on Monday. At right tackle, it sounds like Glaze has had an up-and-down camp so far. But instead of Grant being the one to push the third-year pro, Zuhn has been getting opportunities to prove himself. It will be interesting to see how that plays out against the Cardinals. Edge Starters: Maxx Crosby, Malcolm Koonce Backups: Kwity Paye, Keryon Crawford (R), Cian Slone (R) Cut: Brennan Jackson, Jahfari Harvey, Patrick Johnson Koonce’s name has been brought up a handful of times as a standout during camp, even making some plays against the run. Meanwhile, Paye hasn’t generated much buzz and has been banged up, to explain the ‘starters’ above. Crawford has also battled injuries, returning to practice with a red, non-contact jersey on Monday, per The Athletic’s Sam Warren . Warren also noted that Paye returned to action on the same day. On a more positive note, Slone has been getting solid reviews to potentially earn a roster spot as an undrafted free agent. At this rate, it wouldn’t be too surprising if he’s ahead of the third-round pick on the depth chart. Defensive Tackle Starters: Thomas Booker IV, Adam Butler Backups: Tonka Hemingway, Jonah Laulu, JJ Pegues, Benito Jones Cut: Brandon Cleveland (R), Gary Smith II (R), Treven Ma’ae The ‘starters’ at defensive tackle are very fluid in Las Vegas. It’s a position group that lacks talent, and Hemingway has been one of the pleasant surprises from camp so far. Also, it sounds like Rob Leonard is going to use multiple fronts, not just the 3-4 scheme mentioned in the offseason, so the “first-string” defensive tackles could vary game to game. Ideally, a young defensive tackle like Cleveland and/or Smith steps up and can make the coaching staff feel comfortable moving on from older veterans Butler and Jones. However, Butler has been with the first-team defense, and there hasn’t been much buzz about the two rookies so far. Linebacker Starters: Nakobe Dean, Quay Walker Backups: Cody Lindenberg, Tommy Eichenberg, Segun Olubi Cut: Xavian Sorey Jr. (R), Buddy Johnson, Cameron McGrone Special teams is likely what will be the difference between who does and doesn’t make the team at linebacker. That’s how Olubi has carved out a four-year career to date, while Eichenberg and Lindenberg took the most and second-most special teams snaps, respectively, on last year’s team, per Pro Football Focus . So, the three backers listed as cuts have a chance to earn a roster spot, but it’s hard to put them in that category at the moment. Cornerback Starters: Eric Stokes, Darien Porter , Taron Johnson Backups: Hezekiah Masses (R), Jermod McCoy (R) Cut: Decamerion Richardson, Greedy Vance, Chigozie Anusiem, Caleb Offord (R), Devyn Perkins (R) From the sounds of it, the coaching staff will have some hard decisions to make at cornerback. Masses has been the star of training camp and is pushing Porter for a starting spot, while McCoy has arguably the most talent in the position group to factor into the mix when he isn’t on a pitch count anymore. Additionally, Vance has made a couple of interceptions off Mendoza to give the staff something to think about. That’s without mentioning that Johnson has been playing some safety to really throw the position group for a loop. In other words, expect to see some changes at this spot moving forward. Safety Starters: Jeremy Chinn, Isaiah Pola-Mao Backups: Treydan Stukes (R), Dalton Johnson (R) Cut: Tristin McCollum , Devin Lafayette (R) We still don’t have a good idea of who’s starting at free safety, and Johnson could factor into that mix. After a slow start to camp, Stukes has been getting more reps with the starting defense and…

Here are five things to watch: The quarterbacks: Itt remains to be seen how much we see of Kirk Cousins, Fernando Mendoza and Aidan O’Connell individually. But we should see plenty […]
full_text: HENDERSON, NEVADA - MAY 20: Head coach Klint Kubiak of the Las Vegas Raiders attends a news conference after an OTA offseason workout at the Las Vegas Raiders Headquarters/Intermountain Health Performance Center on May 20, 2026 in Henderson, Nevada. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders start the 2026 preseason Thursday when they host the Arizona Cardinals at Allegiant Stadium. Kickoff is at 5 p.m. PT. Here are five things to watch: The quarterbacks: Itt remains to be seen how much we see of Kirk Cousins, Fernando Mendoza and Aidan O’Connell individually. But we should see plenty of Mendoza, the No. 1 overall draft pick. His development will be the story of the preseason whether he’s truly in the mix to start early in the season or not. The coaching staff: This will be Klint Kubiak’s first ever game as a head coach. Yes, it’s just the preseason, but it will be interesting to see how the operation is run in this game. You can tell about of way a team is run even in the preseason. We show big flaws from the past two regimes in the past two preseasons. We’re looking for a smoother showing by Kubiak and his staff. The rookies: Mendoza may be the headliner, but he’s far from the only rookie who is creating excitement this summer. Let’s see how the entire rookie class performs including offensive lineman Trey Zuhn, running back Mike Washington, safety Treydan Stukes and cornerbacks Zeke Masses and Jermod McCoy, if he plays. The offensive line: We may not see many players on the first unit play in this game. but we want to see a better overall showing than last year. The Raiders’ offensive line was a root of a lot of their problems in 2o25. Improvement is expected under new offensive line coach Rick Dennison. Let’s see it in this game. Health: This is the biggest key of the preseason. No injuries, no injuries, no injuries.

title: Raiders roster 2026: Get to know Deven Thompkins
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders signed veteran wide receiver Deven Thompkins as a free agent recently. Let’s take a closer look at Thompkins: Size: 5-8, 155 pounds. NFL experience: Thompkins has played in 36 games in four NFL seasons. He was with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2022-23, the Carolina Panthers in 2024 and the Atlanta […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - DECEMBER 07: Atlanta wide receiver Deven Thompkins (83) prays prior to the start of the NFL game between the Seattle Seahawks and the Atlanta Falcons on December 7th, 2025 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders signed veteran wide receiver Deven Thompkins as a free agent recently. Let’s take a closer look at Thompkins: Size: 5-8, 155 pounds. NFL experience: Thompkins has played in 36 games in four NFL seasons. He was with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2022-23, the Carolina Panthers in 2024 and the Atlanta Falcons in 2025. He has 29 career receptions and 13 carries. He also has 42 punt returns and 45 kick returns. Draft status: He went undrafted in 2022 and joined the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2022, where he was with now Raiders’ general manager. (Photo by Doug Murray/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images As the National Football League inches closer to the start of the regular season less than one month from now, the league’s official website continues to release their list of the top-100 players as voted on by the players themselves. One Dolphins’ player found out his ranking this morning — and it’s his first time making the list. Dolphins running back, De’Von Achane, was named the 26th best player in the NFL according to his peers. The man who just signed a four-year, $64 million extension with Miami becomes just the second Dolphins player to make the list in 2026 — with linebacker Jordyn Brooks checking in at #67 not too long ago. Here’s what was said about Miami’s electric backfield weapon. “No player was more efficient on the ground in 2025 than Achane. The Dolphins tailback had a breakout year in his final go-around with Tua Tagovailoa and Mike McDaniel, totaling career bests in carries and rushing yards; his 5.7 yards per carry average led the NFL, though it didn’t even hold a candle to Achane’s 7.8 pace from his rookie year. After a Pro Bowl nod, the former third-round pick was the recipient of a four-year, $64 million extension , one of Jon-Eric Sullivan’s first big moves as Dolphins GM. How Achane will perform as the focal point of Jeff Hafley and Bobby Slowik’s Miami offense remains to be seen, but after a debut showing on the Top 100, there’s no doubt about the speedster’s place in the NFL.” It’s no secret that Achane will be the focal point of Miami’s offense in 2026. In a funny moment on the Rich Eisen Show this week, Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley joked he might have to carry Achane into Miami’s locker room himself after feeding the running back 40 touches per game this season. Hopefully Hafley’s help will not be needed in that regard, but it’s undeniable that Achane’s production this year will go a long way towards deciding how successful the Dolphins will be in 2026.

title: Kyler Murray QB1, The Merits of the Competition, and What’s Next for J.J. McCarthy
summary: The Minnesota Vikings have named Kyler Murray as their starting quarterback this season, as widely expected, ending the competition with J.J. McCarthy after two weeks of training camp. From the beginning, many/most were skeptical about the competition, figuring Murray would eventually be named the winner. And from Kevin O’Connell’s comments before the night practice on […]
full_text: The Minnesota Vikings have named Kyler Murray as their starting quarterback this season, as widely expected, ending the competition with J.J. McCarthy after two weeks of training camp. From the beginning, many/most were skeptical about the competition, figuring Murray would eventually be named the winner. And from Kevin O’Connell’s comments before the night practice on Sunday, indicating that the timeframe to make a decision on the starting quarterback had not changed, it appears that naming a starter after the night practice was the original plan. But now that the decision has been made, let’s look again at Kyler Murray as the Vikings’ starting quarterback, look back at the rationale and merits of the quarterback competition, and what may be next for J.J. McCarthy. Let’s begin with a review of the quarterback competition. Critiquing the Quarterback Competition From the moment the Vikings signed Kyler Murray, there seemed to be little doubt that he would be the starting quarterback this season. The reason was straightforward enough- Kyler Murray has the better track record as a starter when it comes to accuracy and just about every quarterback metric and has also demonstrated the minimum required skillset to be a quality starter in the NFL: processing ability, accuracy, poise in the pocket, and proper mechanics. J.J. McCarthy is still developing those fundamentals. More than anybody, Kevin O’Connell understood where each quarterback was at with their skillsets, but still he chose to have a competition rather than simply naming Kyler Murray the starting quarterback shortly after he was signed. So what was the rationale for doing so? What was he hoping to gain? Part of the rationale for having a competition was simply out of respect for J.J. McCarthy. When you have an incumbent starter on the roster, it is respectful to allow that player to compete for the starting job with any new acquisitions or others on the roster that have earned the right. Handing the starting job to Murray without any competition may have been seen as an indictment of his ability and potential growth since last season. Another reason for the competition may have been to give some motivation to McCarthy that may help accelerate his development. After all, he did not compete for the starting job in either his rookie or second season. Darnold was the presumed starter from the get-go his rookie year, and McCarthy was in his second year. The competition might also help Kyler Murray sharpen his tools, while also giving O’Connell the chance to see how well/quickly he learns the scheme before naming him the starter. The downside to having a competition is having the eventual starter- Murray- receive fewer reps in the offseason program and fewer first-team reps in training camp. Given the shorter training camps and offseason program compared to years ago, each rep in practice has become increasingly valuable in helping a new quarterback learn the scheme and develop rapport with his teammates, especially his receivers. O’Connell seemed to hedge against that downside by gradually shifting more of the first team reps to Murray during the first two weeks of training camp and maintaining his two-week deadline to name Murray the starter and give him all the first team reps going forward. Continuing the competition much beyond that would begin to compromise Murray’s ability to develop the rapport with the first team needed to be effective by the start of the regular season. All that led many to suspect that the competition wasn’t fair- it had a preordained result- and that McCarthy never really had much of a chance at winning the competition. And looking back on it now, that pretty clearly was the case. But compared to the alternative- no competition at all- this was perhaps the best solution considering the needs of McCarthy, Murray, and the team. In terms of gains from the quarterback competition, I’m not sure there was anything significant. McCarthy seemed very much like he was last year, so the competition factor didn’t appear to have the desired effect on him. Nor did it have much of a discernable effect on Murray either. He said early on in a press conference that he wasn’t really worried about the competition and was more focused on learning the offense. And so to the extent he had reduced reps the competition didn’t really help him. So, if that was indeed the case, it didn’t seem like the competition did much other than perhaps cushioning the blow a bit for McCarthy, which may be perceived positively in some ways by both McCarthy and the team. That isn’t nothing. In his first press conference since Murray was named the starter, McCarthy seemed to accept it gracefully and expressed his desire to remain with the Vikings and do whatever he can to help the QB room, team, and organization. What’s Next for Kyler Murray For both Kyler Murray and Kevin O’Connell, the bet in his signing with the Vikings is for Murray to be the next reclamation project after Sam Darnold. If Murray is able to deliver on that wager, with 2024 Darnold-like performance metrics or better, it’s unlikely the Vikings will let him walk like they did Darnold. It’s clear that O’Connell has better luck whispering to veterans than he does young and developing quarterbacks, so it’s unlikely he would stand in the way of extending Murray. New Vikings GM Nolan Teasley will also have a significant say in the matter, but he came into the league making two Super Bowl runs with a mobile quarterback that was too short in Russell Wilson so it wouldn’t be surprising if he was willing to sign off on extending Murray if he has a good season. At what price tag will be a question but it looks like the Vikings have built in room in their salary cap for a possible Murray extension. But more immediately, Murray needs to continue the path to learning the offense and developing rapport with his teammates and receivers. There have been plenty of growing pains over the course of the offseason program and training camp for Murray, as he’s worked through miscommunications, bad snaps, interceptions, and lack of timing/rapport with receivers at times- all while also battling a mostly dominant Brian Flores defense. It hasn’t all been bad by any means- he’s delivered some high-level throws as well- and his results aren’t much different than they were with Kirk Cousins and Sam Darnold before him as they too struggled with all of the above in 2023 and 2024, especially early in training camp. So panic is premature at this point. There is a month until the first regular season game and that is a lot of time for Murray to improve across the board. His first practices since being named the starter have been encouraging. And what kind of a season Murray will have, and how well he’ll fit in O’Connell’s scheme, will continue to be a subject of debate. At this point in 2024 expectations for Sam Darnold were low. He was expected to be a mediocre bridge quarterback until McCarthy was ready, probably in 2025 but maybe sooner. All those expectations proved to be wrong. For Murray, expectations are higher- in part because of the success of Darnold with the Vikings in 2024. There is also the fact that the Vikings won nine games last season with bottom-of-the-league quarterback performance. Murray simply being average may result in double-digit wins and a return to the playoffs. There is also the fact that Murray’s performance in the two seasons prior to joining the Vikings was much better than Darnold’s was, and in Murray’s last full season (2024) he basically equaled Darnold’s performance with the Vikings that year by most metrics: Overall PFF Grade Murray: 82.1. full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - AUGUST 16: New England Patriots running back JaMycal Hasty (39) returns a kickoff during the NFL preseason game between the New England Patriots and Minnesota Vikings on August 16th, 2025, in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New England Patriots are not done modifying their running back group. On Wednesday night, after already signing free agent Hassan Haskins and waiving rookie Myles Montgomery , they also brought in a second veteran. JaMycal Hasty, who already spent parts of the 2023 and 2024 seasons as well as last training camp in New England, has been re-signed after a workout. Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston was first to report the signing, with his agency since confirming the move. Hasty, 29, entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2020. The Baylor product was picked up by the 49ers and via the practice squad made his way onto the 53-man roster. He appeared in 22 total games over his two years with the club, but was cut ahead of the 2022 season. He joined the Jaguars as a waiver claim and delivered the most productive season of his career in his first year in Jacksonville, registering 66 touches, 320 yards, 3 touchdowns. Hasty failed to build on his success and was let go again by Jaguars during the 2023 regular season. This, in turn, allowed the Patriots to bring him in as a waiver claim of their own. Over his one and a half seasons in Foxborough, Hasty was used as a depth running back and kickoff return option. Overall, he played 17 games for the club between 2023 and 2024 and touched the ball 30 times for 128 yards and a touchdown while also averaging 23.8 yards on 10 kickoff returns. Hasty was let go by the Patriots ahead of last year’s roster cuts and subsequently spent the 2025 season on Miami’s practice squad. He was not retained after the season, and has remained unsigned since January. The Patriots will play the Colts in their preseason opener on Thursday night.

full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - JUNE 10: A general view of the Pariots new New Balance Athletics Center during New England Patriots Minicamp on June 10, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New England Patriots will play their first preseason game of 2026 on Thursday night. On the eve of the contest, another event took place on the franchise’s premises: the official opening of a new, state-of-the-art training facility. The New Balance Athletics Center as it is known for sponsorship reasons gives the team 160,000 square feet dedicated exclusively to football, the largest such space in the league. “Today is a very exciting day for the New England Patriots,” said Robert Kraft. “When our family purchased the Patriots in ‘94, we made a commitment to all our fans to do everything we could to build a first-class organization and give the team the right resources to compete at the highest level. For more than 30 years that commitment has guided us. It has meant investing not only in the team on the field but also the people, facilities and infrastructure that support the team every day. This building is the latest example of that commitment.” Welcome to the New England Patriots @newbalance Athletics Center! pic.twitter.com/x42n32Tcgl — New England Patriots (@Patriots) August 12, 2026 The Patriots started using the facility, which provides dedicated spaces for coaching, scouting, athletic training, strength and conditioning, sports science, nutrition, and recovery, earlier this offseason. To make room for the familiar free agent, the organization waived rookie rusher Myles Montgomery with an injury designation. Haskins, 26, entered the league with […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 12: Hassan Haskins #28 of the Los Angeles Chargers celebrates after an NFL football game against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium on October 12, 2025 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images A veteran of 44 NFL games arrived in Foxborough on the eve of the preseason opener. The New England Patriots announced the signing of running back Hassan Haskins on Wednesday. To make room for the familiar free agent, the organization waived rookie rusher Myles Montgomery with an injury designation. Haskins, 26, entered the league with the Tennessee Titans in the fourth round of the 2022 draft at pick No. 131 overall. The former first-team All-Big Ten selection did so after amassing 2,495 yards and 30 touchdowns from scrimmage at Michigan. He would overlap with head coach Mike Vrabel, running backs coach Tony Dews, vice president of player personnel Ryan Cowden and additional members of the current staff during his stint in Nashville. And at the league’s cutdown deadline in 2024, Haskins was claimed off waivers by the Los Angeles Chargers and fellow Wolverines product Jim Harbaugh. Staying in the AFC West through the 2025 campaign, Haskins stands with 76 carries for 229 yards, 18 catches for 119 yards, three touchdowns and one start in his NFL career. Logging 30 tackles and 28 kickoff returns, he has seen 371 snaps on offense and 683 snaps on special teams. In for a workout that also featured running backs JaMycal Hasty, Shane Watts and Leshon Williams, according to the league’s transaction wire, the 6-foot-2, 228-pound Haskins now joins Rhamondre Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson, Terrell Jennings, Lan Larison and Jam Miller on the August depth chart. The corresponding move would come in the backfield. Montgomery, 23, agreed to terms with the Patriots as part of the club’s undrafted class in May. The 5-foot-10, 205-pound running back spent three years at Cincinnati before transferring to Central Florida for his final two years of eligibility. An eventual team captain for the Knights, he played in 41 games altogether during his collegiate career while rushing for 1,546 yards and 11 touchdowns across 274 carries. As a result of the injury designation, Montgomery is on track to revert to New England’s injured reserve for the remainder of 2026. That follow-up transaction looms after clearing waivers. The preseason gets underway with a 7:30 p.m. ET kickoff against the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday.

title: Drake Maye is not worried about making Patriots receivers happy
summary: With the franchise quarterback in place, the next step in the New England Patriots’ roster construction process was surrounding him with as many weapon as possible. Looking at this year’s training camp, the team appears to have succeeded. In his third summer, Drake Maye gets to work with a top-tier running back duo, an intriguing […]
full_text: Foxborough, MA - July 28: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and wide receiver Mack Hollins shake hands at training camp on July 28, 2026. (Photo by Danielle Parhizkaran/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images With the franchise quarterback in place, the next step in the New England Patriots’ roster construction process was surrounding him with as many weapon as possible. Looking at this year’s training camp, the team appears to have succeeded. In his third summer, Drake Maye gets to work with a top-tier running back duo, an intriguing group of tight ends, and a wide receiver room that currently stands at seven roster-worthy players deep. Of course, the numbers create some problems that very well can be placed into the “first world” category: how do you keep all of the receiving talent involved and happy? For Maye, the answer is simple. You don’t, at least not by trying to spread the wealth in a traditional sense. “I think the best thing for that is winning,” he explained following Tuesday’s joint practice with the Indianapolis Colts. “Nobody really tries to complain when you win games. Nobody’s really that prideful in this sport about personal stats or achievements when we’re winning games. So, that’s our job as a team, to come together and try to win games. That’s the biggest thing that coach is preaching, and we’re trying to be second voices of him, and knowing ‘Protect the football team’ and doing things the right way. “But no, I think my job isn’t to try to make everybody happy. I think my job’s to have the offense move up and down the field, and score points.” In 2025 Maye and company managed to do that for the most part, finishing the regular season ranked second in scoring before a drop-off in the playoffs. In order to avoid a similar outcome this time around, the team decided to make some investments. Wide receivers Romeo Doubs and A.J. Brown were brought in via the free agency and trade markets, respectively, while tight end Eli Raridon was selected in the third round of the draft. Based on the summer so far, all three of them will be actively involved in the offensive operation come fall and winter. Doubs, Brown and Raridon are able players in their own rights and in some other years could have been the clear top trio in New England. In 2026, however, they are part of a group also featuring the likes of DeMario Douglas, Kayshon Boutte, Mack Hollins, Kyle Williams, Efton Chism, Hunter Henry, Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson — all of them either roster locks or close to it, and realistic candidates to end up playing a high number of snaps this year. “Our skill position room’s great, and we have a lot of depth and a lot of guys that really want to get in there and make plays,” said Maye. “That’s the best thing about it. It’s competitive in there. You have guys that are making plays all across the board, so it’s my job to get them the ball. They’re better runners than I am, so get them the football and let them do their thing.” And, to pick up on Maye’s logic, that is what ultimately will bring the happiness. Not him trying to keep count of targets.

title: Patriots 2026 scouting report for DT Christian Barmore
summary: The New England Patriots defense was one of the best in the NFL last season, in large part because of the performance in the trenches. The interior D-line in particular performed at a high level whiqle being led by one of the most disruptive starting duos in football: Milton Williams and Christian Barmore. Whereas the […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - JANUARY 25: New England Patriots defensive tackle Christian Barmore (90) celebrates after a second quarter sack against the Denver Broncos in the AFC Championship Game at Empower Field at Mile High on January 25, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New England Patriots defense was one of the best in the NFL last season, in large part because of the performance in the trenches. The interior D-line in particular performed at a high level whiqle being led by one of the most disruptive starting duos in football: Milton Williams and Christian Barmore. Whereas the former was a high-prized free agency pickup in 2025, the latter is one of the franchise’s premier home-grown talents. And with his medical issues behind him, Barmore now is back to his impactful ways. Hard facts Name: Christian Barmore Position: Defensive tackle/Interior defensive line Jersey number: 90 Opening day age: 27 (6/8/1999) Measurements : 6’4 1/8”, 315 lbs, 10” hand size, 33 5/8” arm length, 81 3/8” wingspan, 4.98s 40-yard dash, 7.81s 3-cone drill, 4.75s short shuttle, 8.39 Relative Athletic Score Experience NFL: New England Patriots (2021-) | College: Alabama (2018-20) A two-way lineman at Neumann Goretti High School in Philadelphia, Barmore received significant interest as a four-star defensive tackle recruit. He initially committed to Temple ahead of his senior season but later decommitted and saw Alabama,Georgia, LSU and Oregon join the almost 20 schools to offer him scholarships. He opted for the Crimson Tide, whom he joined in 2018. After sitting out his freshman campaign in Tuscaloosa, Barmore started six of 24 games over the next two seasons. Along the way, he registered 63 tackles, 10 sacks and three forced fumbles. A first-team All-SEC selection and National Champion as a sophomore, he opted to forgo his final two years of eligibility to enter the NFL Draft in 2021. Barmore was invited to the green room at the event, but ultimately had to wait until Day 2 of the draft to hear his name called: the Patriots traded up from the 46th to the 38th overall selection in the second round to bring him aboard. Since then, he has been a mainstay along their defensive line and one of their best defenders overall. In his five seasons since arriving in Foxborough, Barmore has appeared in a combined 70 regular season and playoff games with 32 starts. A well-rounded player, who has regularly been used both as a pass rusher and run defender, he notched 180 tackles including 25 for loss, 16.5 sacks — including a career-best 8.5 in 2023 — and a forced fumble. Unfortunately, however, he also struggled with his fair share of medical issues along the way. Barmore’s 2022 season was disrupted due to a nagging knee injury while he missed virtually all of 2024 due to blood clots. That same year, three months before the diagnosis, he signed a four-year, $84 million contract extension to become the highest-paid defender in Patriots history at the time. Scouting report Strengths: Standing at 6-foot-4, 315 pounds, Barmore offers tremendous size to occupy the interior of the defensive line. His build allows him to successfully play gap-control as a run defender while he also has the athleticism to penetrate upfield to blow up plays. His first-step quickness for his size is rare and he has the core strength to maintain his leverage and hold his position even against double teams. He also plays with anticipation and spatial awareness, displaying a high football IQ and good feel for putting himself in an advantageous position. He also is active in pursuit, As a pass rusher, Barmore is a handful for centers and guards alike. He gets a strong push on his bull rush and keeps his feet working to drive blockers back. His active hand technique and grip strength allow him to stay engaged throughout a rep, and he also has a wide array of counters in his toolbox; he can win by engaging his opponents head-first but also uses swim, chop and rip moves. He also has the natural length to get into offensive linemen’s chests and challenge their balance, and the high motor to make an impact even when not directly involved on the play side. Weaknesses: Barmore’s ability and productivity do not necessarily match; his sack numbers in particular are not in line with his levels of disruptiveness and his finishing has been uneven. The same is true for his tackling, which ran hot and cold in 2025. His at-times uneven consistency also extends to his pad level and play speed. He also comes with questions about his availability and stamina, and despite not being a heavily-flagged player has had some problems with temper and discipline. 2025 review Stats : 21 games (20 starts) | 842 defensive snaps (65.6%), 66 special teams snaps (12.0%) | 39 tackles, 12 missed tackles (23.5%), 6 TFLs | 58 QB pressures (3 sacks, 10 hits, 45 hurries) | 0 penalties Season recap: Barmore was limited to four games following his blood clots diagnosis, and ended the 2024 season on New England’s non-football injury/illness list. By the time 2025 came around, however, a lot had changed: not only did the Patriots change their head coach and a majority of their staff, Barmore himself was also cleared to return to action again. That showed from Day 1. When the Patriots started their voluntary offseason workout program in early April, he was among the players present. His availability, particularly in light of his medical issues the previous year, remained exemplary: he ended up appearing all 17 of his team’s regular season games as well as all four of its playoff contests, starting a combined 20 of them and playing a position-high 842 snaps. Together with free agency signings Milton Williams and Khyiris Tonga, Barmore formed one of the top interior trios in the NFL in 2025. And while his baseline stats do not necessarily reflect it — he posted just three sacks and zero turnovers — his impact on the group was profound. His 58 combined quarterback pressures ranked eighth among all NFL defensive tackles last season, and that is despite him being the regular target of double teams. In fact, his 17 pressures after being double-teamed ranked second, and fifth among all defenders regardless of position. Long story short, Barmore’s raw numbers might not reflect it, but he very much returned to his pre-blood clots levels of play in 2025 as a pass rusher. His run defense was a different story. He missed an uncharacteristically high number of tackles and saw a drop in production while Williams missed four games on injured reserve late during the regular season. His challenging moments did not stop there: he also started the Patriots’ game against the Browns on the bench for disciplinary reasons, had a heated halftime conversation with Mike Vrabel during a Week 17 game against the Jets, and was charged with assault and battery in December, a situation that eventually was solved in his favor. Despite the on- and off-field problems Barmore ran into in 2025, his season as a whole was a success. Considering that his outlooks was very much in question given his medical issues the previous year, he found a way to get back onto the field and contribute at a high level again. 2026 preview Position: 1-/3-technique defensive tackle | Ability: High quality starter | Contract: Signed through 2028 (2029 UFA) What will be his role? Barmore was an every-game starter for the Patriots in 2025 and played roughly two thirds of their defensive snaps on the year. While it remains to be seen whether the team opts for the same level of exposure this season, his role as a whole will not change dramatically: he will be a starting player along the defensive line, attacking the pocket as a pass rusher and run defender from multiple alignments but mostly operating between the nose and 3-technique spot. What is his growth potential? Despite already entering his sixth season in the NFL, the 27-year-old…

Also, because it’s shorter than an actual game, it’s a perfect opportunity for the starters to […]
full_text: Joint practices are always good ways for the team to evaluate its current players and coaching. During practice, it may be a bit more difficult to get it done, but adding some competition brings out the best in people. Also, because it’s shorter than an actual game, it’s a perfect opportunity for the starters to get some reps and stay away from a higher risk of injuries. So, it came as no surprise when, today, it was announced that the starters will be playing a good amount in tomorrow’s joint practice against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Saints had a short practice today. They’ll have a lot of starters vs starters in joint practice tomorrow against the Jaguars and Kellen Moore said as a result that means less snaps for the starters in preseason games — Katherine Terrell (@Kat_Terrell) August 12, 2026 With the starters getting some major playing time in the joint practice, the first preseason game is likely to feature more backups seeing the field. Still, players like Christen Miller, who fans are excited to see and could become a starter soon, should still have some playing time during the first preseason game. In the joint practice, it’s going to be very interesting to see the red zone playcalling, the offensive line blocking, how the pass defense is, and Tyler Shough against competition. It’s going to be our first real glimpse at some of the work the Saints have done this offseason.

summary: Welcome back to State of the NFC South! Tampa Bay Buccaneers Starting with the team that proved preseason expectations can go wrong, the Buccaneers were the surprise team of the NFC South last season. It’s not because they overperformed, but instead, disappointed and lost the division title. The team struggled with injuries, and the offense consistently […]
full_text: CANTON, OHIO - AUGUST 06: Ja'seem Reed #86 of the Carolina Panthers scores a 15-yard touchdown during the second quarter of the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame Game against the Arizona Cardinals at Tom Benson Hall Of Fame Stadium on August 06, 2026 in Canton, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to State of the NFC South! Tampa Bay Buccaneers Starting with the team that proved preseason expectations can go wrong, the Buccaneers were the surprise team of the NFC South last season. It’s not because they overperformed, but instead, disappointed and lost the division title. The team struggled with injuries, and the offense consistently regressed after OC Liam Coen left in the offseason. For 2026, the hope is the team can bounce back and get back to their winning ways, but already, there are some clear reasons why that won’t happen. Contract disputes with Baker Mayfield and a trade request from Vita Vea could derail what the Buccaneers want to accomplish, but in their first preseason game, we could see some players save their season. EDGE Rueben Bain Jr. was their first-round pick, and if he can be a star right away, the Buccaneers defense would be much better. Also, third-round pick Ted Hurst could become the “Mike Evans replacement” after the veteran left in free agency. Although their snaps may be limited, it will be great to see what they can do on the field. Carolina Panthers Unlike the Buccaneers, the Panthers actually did win the division in a bit of a shocking outcome, but ended up losing in the first round. After one of the best seasons in a while, the Panthers are looking to upgrade and compete in the playoffs for 2026. The pressure will be on Bryce Young to deliver, especially with a contract extension potentially right around the corner. For Preseason, the Panthers are the one team out of the division that has played a preseason matchup, which was the Hall of Fame game. Carolina ended up winning an extremely close battle with the Arizona Cardinals, and rookie QB Haynes King made the final play to get the victory. Rookie WR Chris Brazzell III went down with an injury that knocked him out for the season. First-round pick Monroe Freeling did not play in the preseason game as well. Atlanta Falcons With new HC Kevin Stefanski, the Falcons are in an interesting situation with their roster. It’s very youth-focused, and the potential is there, but Michael Penix Jr. still needs to prove to the coaching staff that they can rely on him, and the Falcons did not have a first-round pick in 2026 due to the James Pearce Jr. trade. Speaking of that trade, Pearce Jr. may be suspended for some of the 2026 season, and fellow 2025 first-round pick Jalon Walker will be out for the season with an injury. The draft class still has some talent, but this roster as a whole has a lot to prove in 2026. New Orleans Saints Even after finishing last season in 2025, the Saints have momentum going into this season. QB Tyler Shough showed the coaching staff he can be the starter, the offense is completely rebuilt to have little to no issues, and the defense has talent to be excited about. With those factors and a fourth-place schedule in the division, the season is set for the Saints to have a similar season to what the Panthers did last year, but injuries are becoming an issue. Some extremely important veterans on the roster have picked up injuries, and it’s already become the first big roadblock in the season. Still, the rookie class is extremely exciting, and the first preseason game against the Jaguars could be a perfect time for the young players to step up right away.

full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - DECEMBER 7: Charlie Smyth #39 of the New Orleans Saints warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on December 7, 2025 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images This Saturday, the New Orleans Saints will open the 2026 NFL preseason against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Caesars Superdome. The player to watch has endured a rough training camp to this point, and another poor performance this weekend could force New Orleans to explore other options at kicker: Charlie Smyth . Consistency has been the biggest issue for the 25-year-old Irishman throughout training camp, making Saturday’s preseason opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars an important opportunity for the young kicker. Smyth has shown the ability to make impressive kicks, and his leg power has never been the question, but stringing those successes together has been the challenge. For a player competing to become the Saints’ long-term answer at kicker, the team needs to see more reliability as the preseason gets underway. That makes Saturday’s performance particularly important. Another inconsistent outing could force New Orleans to seriously consider whether it has enough confidence in him heading into the regular season. Preseason games provide guys like Smyth with opportunities to solidify their roster spots, and he will need to take advantage of his chances. New Orleans already has Tanner Brown behind Smyth, giving the team another option internally. However, if neither kicker can establish themselves, the Saints could eventually turn their attention toward the veteran market. There are still plenty of opportunities for Smyth to change the conversation. A strong preseason could quiet concerns and allow him to maintain his position as the favorite. But if the struggles continue, the Saints may have little choice but to explore alternatives. For Smyth, Saturday is the first opportunity to show that he can be trusted when the games begin to count.

As the New Orleans Saints’ preseason opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars gets closer, it is time to begin previewing the offensive matchup for this week’s contest. Although it is unlikely for the starters to get much run in the first preseason game, this week will serve as an opportunity for Kellen Moore and the rest of the coaching staff to get a good look at some newcomers and rookies vying for roster spots in real-time action against an opponent other than their own teammates. With the Saints adding a bevy of new pass catchers to surround QB Tyler Shough, I would expect them to lean on the passing game early to give these players as much run as possible. Players like Jordyn Tyson, Bryce Lance, Barion Brown, Noah Fant, and Oscar Delp should get a fair amount of reps. Throughout training camp, there have been some doubters sharing their dismay with the offensive efficiency during practices. If the offense can perform and execute routine plays even with backups and reserves seeing the field, this game will serve as a platform to quiet some of the outside noise. Jaguars’ head coach Liam Coen has already announced that starters will not see the field versus New Orleans in week one, but that will not make this game any less important for either staff. The Jags made several key additions to their defensive units this offseason, including linebackers Amari Burney, Dennis Gardeck, and Jahlani Tavai, cornerback Montaric Brown, and defensive tackle Ruke Orhorhoro. Even though the Saints will not face Jacksonville during the regular season this year, it will still be good competition for New Orleans after the Jaguars finished first in the AFC South division in 2025 while taking a trip to the postseason, somewhere New Orleans has not been since 2020.

title: NY Giants practice report: Dominic Zvada’s 62-yard field goal wins the day
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — If he wasn’t already, undrafted free agent Dominic Zvada on Wednesday stamped himself as the clear favorite to win the placekicking competition against second-year kicker Ben Sauls. Zvada ended Wednesday’s practice with a 62-yard gamep-winning field goal in a tie game, final play of the game situation. That capped a day […]
full_text: Dominic Zvada | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — If he wasn’t already, undrafted free agent Dominic Zvada on Wednesday stamped himself as the clear favorite to win the placekicking competition against second-year kicker Ben Sauls. Zvada ended Wednesday’s practice with a 62-yard gamep-winning field goal in a tie game, final play of the game situation. That capped a day where Zvada went 7 of 7, also making kicks of 53 and 50 yards. Sauls went 5 of 6, making 50 and 53-yarders, but missing from 45 yards. “It was a great kick, great snap,” said head coach John Harbaugh. “Nice to see. It was exciting. It’s fun.” Zvada had made kicks from between 55 and 60 yards previously in camp, as had Sauls. This is the first time either kicker was good from beyond 60 yards. “He does have a big leg, but the bottom line is you’ve got to kick it straight consistently,” Harbaugh said. So having a big leg is a big deal. Kicking it straight consistently is a bigger deal. “I think both those guys have done that very well, and Ben has a very good leg too. I don’t want to imply that he doesn’t. Ben’s a very strong leg guy as well, but they’re both having really good camps.” Let’s go through more winners and losers. Winners The Jaxson Dart-Isaiah Likely connection — The second-year quarterback and his new tight end are forming an excellent connection. Likely caught several passes from Dart on Wednesday. In the end-of-game situation Harbaugh set up Wednesday to complete practice, it was clear Dart was looking for Likely whenever possible. Tremaine Edmunds — The massive inside linebacker dropped a potential pick 6 — a ball intended for Likely — when he jumped in front of the tight end on Dart’s first throw of practice. Two plays later, Edmunds batted down a pass from a scrambling Dart. Deonte Banks and Colton Hood — With Dru Phillips, Greg Newsome, and Paulson Adebo sidelined, Banks and Hood were the first-team cornerbacks. This represents a significant opportunity for both players. Banks was beaten deep by Malachi Fields, but he had good coverage and it took a leaping, one-handed grab. Hood batted away a deep pass from Jameis Winston intended for Dalen Cambre. Malachi Fields — Fields had a number of catches on Wednesday, including the long, one-handed grab at the goal line vs. Banks. Fields did lose a touchdown pass due to an offensive pass interference call, which explains why no defender was within five yards. Play a day Cambre — Dalen Cambre’s daily big play was a goal line touchdown catch from Winston on a quick out at the goal line. Bryan Hudson — I can’t really tell you how he is doing, but Hudson is getting first-team reps at center with John Michael Schmitz (concussion) and Lucas Patrick (knee) not practicing. Turbo Miller — He got a shout out on Wednesday from Harbaugh. “He’s explosive. He’s had catches. He caught one today long. He’s had runs where he’s shown acceleration,” Harbaugh said. Losers Ben Sauls — He’s not kicking poorly, but every miss makes it less and less likely he can win the competition with Zvada. Injury updates As previously mentioned, Phillips, Newsome, Adebo, Schmitz, and Patrick did not practice. Wide receivers JuJu Smith-Schuster (knee) and Jalin Hyatt (ankle/knee) did not practice. Running back Tyrone Tracy had a light workload. Saturday playing time Harbaugh would not answer whether or not quarterback Jaxson Dart will play Saturday in the preseason opener against the Minnesota Vikings. He did say that wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. will play. “He’s in a good place,” Harbaugh said. “He will play and I’m looking forward to seeing him play.” Schedule The Giants will practice on Thursday, then have Friday off before playing on Saturday.

title: NY Giants interested in Terrion Arnold because ‘we want to be aggressive in every way’
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants brought cornerback Terrion Arnold in for a free-agent visit on Wednesday despite the cornerback currently facing eight felony charges stemming from allegations that he orchestrated the kidnapping and beating of three men. Why would the Giants, a historically conservative organization, be willing to do that? “Because we […]
full_text: Terrion Arnold | Getty Images EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants brought cornerback Terrion Arnold in for a free-agent visit on Wednesday despite the cornerback currently facing eight felony charg es stemming from allegations that he orchestrated the kidnapping and beating of three men. Why would the Giants, a historically conservative organization, be willing to do that? “Because we want to be aggressive in every way, whatever we can do, find everything out we can about any situation player that can help us be better, probably. I would say that’s it,” head coach John Harbaugh said after practice on Wednesday. “The margins are tight in the National Football League. “We’re looking for players that can help us all the time, and he’s a player that can help us.” Whether the 23-year-old Arnold, who has also visited with the New Orleans Saints, Seattle Seahawks, and Houston Texans, will be available to help any NFL team could depend on how and when the legal process he is embroiled in plays out. Harbaugh said the Giants and other teams are aware that Arnold’s legal process “could take years” to play out. “I think you just have to decide where does the legal process stand, and what are we really talking about here,” said Harbaugh. “What does it look like, and you’ve got to, you have to make a judgment along those lines. You try to do the best you can to anticipate what that might be and see if it’s worth it.” Harbaugh said Arnold’s situation has been “studied very deeply” by the Giants organization. “I’ve got an overview of it. The organization has looked at it in depth. If there is a decision to be made on any player that you don’t want to go there with a player, then this organization, they won’t go there, and so that decision would also have to be made,” Harbaugh said. “Just understanding everything that goes on with that. It’s more than just what you read in the papers, though. I mean, you’ve got to find out exactly where everything stands, and I think I do know that our people do a great job of that.” Harbaugh said these are “case-by-case” situations. “One aspect is what’s best for your football team. The other aspect is what’s best for your organization and your people and doing the right thing.” Harbaugh said. “So there are certain situations that I know the Giants and Baltimore were the same way in the past where you just don’t go there with a player. Other situations where you understand the circumstances and you’re willing to do that.” The Giants have been dealing with injuries at cornerback. Dru Phillips and Greg Newsome have missed several practices with knee injuries, and Paulson Adebo has missed the last two practices. Harbaugh would not reveal Adebo’s injury, but said he is “day-to-day.” Pride of Detroit on Arnold I asked Jeremy Reisman of SB Nation’s Pride of Detroit about Arnold the player and Arnold the person. Here are his responses: Player: Hard to say. As the Lions defensive coordinator recently said, “Terrion Arnold had number one cornerback potential, but it was still untapped.” He was excellent last training camp, but then it didn’t carry over to the regular season. Just when it seemed like he was turning a corner midseason, he got injured and essentially lost the rest of the year. Person: Prior to this alleged incident in Florida, Arnold’s character was spotless. He came to the NFL with two notable stories regarding his character. One was the relationship he had forged with his high school janitor . The other was an iconic speech he gave about his mother at the NFL Combine . My personal interactions were all very pleasant, and I would consider him overly friendly in the locker room. That said, the allegations are pretty darn serious, and, if true, represent a very serious lack of judgment. I won’t try to predict what will happen with him legally, but I do think there’s a very good chance the NFL will reprimand him given the seriousness of eight felony charges.

title: OC Matt Nagy: Giants only ‘halfway through’ installing their offense
summary: More often than not throughout the early stages of New York Giants training camp, the defense has gotten the better of the offense during team periods. That is cause for alarm among some on the fan base . There are many who did not like the hiring of Matt Nagy as offensive coordinator, and aren’t […]
full_text: More often than not throughout the early stages of New York Giants training camp, the defense has gotten the better of the offense during team periods. That is cause for alarm among some on the fan base . There are many who did not like the hiring of Matt Nagy as offensive coordinator, and aren’t sure how the Giants’ offense is going to come together with multiple former head coaches or play callers on the staff. Nagy offered a hint regarding why the offense has not been better during first first media availability of training camp on Tuesday. As Nagy explains it, the offense we are seeing is far from complete, and far from polished. “We’re halfway through camp right now. We have still two and a half weeks. We’re halfway through our run install and halfway through our pass install, if it gives you any perspective,” Nagy said. “We still have a lot left, and we’re trying to just figure out, “Okay, what do we want to do as we go through it?” And we think we have a good idea.“ The Giants are still in the process of figuring out what they like and don’t like, and what they do and do not execute well. “When I say that, we have an idea of what we want to do,” Nagy said. “I’m talking play-wise – big picture we know – play-wise, you start to build a little bit of a library of what our guys do well. We’re not going to give them stuff that we just want to do because we want to do it. If we do something, it’s because they like it and they do a good job at it in any phase of the game. “So, putting all that together and cutting it loose, it’s [the season] going to be here quickly. So, getting as much stuff – the one thing Coach Harbs does is get a ton of reps of plays. So, whether it’s walkthrough, group install or competitive, we have a lot of stuff on tape right now that we’re able to pull and look at and decide what do we want to do.” The Giants are culling together an offense that leans on ideas from Harbaugh, Nagy, passing game coordinator Brian Callahan, senior offensive assistant Greg Roman, and other former head coaches and play callers on the offensive staff. “They’re still learning this offense. They’re learning it,” Nagy said. “There’s things that they’re familiar with, and there’s things that they’re not. There’s things that our staff is familiar with and things that they’re not, that I’m not. “We’re growing together in this process, and that’s the beauty of all of this. So, I just have a lot of trust in our offensive staff. I have a ton of trust in Coach Harbs, and I know he has a plan. I know internally what he wants, and now it’s growth every day.” ‘The number one question’ That would be what works for second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart, and what does not. “It’s the number one question we talked about when we got here with Coach Harbs and how we saw this thing,” Nagy said. “You go through it, every team, every new coordinator, every new head coach, every new quarterback. You’ve got to decide what’s best for that player and for our offense. But at the same point in time, we want to also look at schematically where do we see this thing going, and then trying to fit everything together.” Nagy said the Giants are going through the process of figuring out what pieces of their developing playbook Dart likes, and which ones need to be cast aside. “If there’s one or two plays where he might not be seeing it well, let’s figure out why you’re not. And if you’re not, let’s just get rid of the play. Let’s go to a different play. We’ve got enough plays,” Nagy said. “And so, we’re digging through that right now. We’re filtering through that to figure out, “What does he like? What’s he feel comfortable with?” “And so, now when we find those plays and we figure out what that is, now you’ve got to go execute and make them happen on the field, and I think that’s the biggest, probably, obstacle that we’re going through right now, which is fun as a coaching staff.” We do know that the offense will include a heavy dose of the run game, and that Dart will be asked to play under center more often. “I think most people will tell you – I played quarterback my entire life, and having a run game is the friendliest thing in the world,” Nagy said. “You want to be able to run the football. Everybody says it, but you’ve got to be able to do it. So, being under center is going to protect you with some of the play actions and different things you do. Jaxson’s had no issue with that. I mean, we’re doing a bunch of different things with it.” ‘Buckets and concepts’ Why are the Giants only halfway through the install of their playbook with just a bit more than a month to go before the regular season starts? “We spent Phase Two [of the offseason] just kind of trying to teach this thing ground up in buckets and phases, and not necessarily plays. So, we spent several weeks of just teaching the concepts and teaching, whether it’s run or pass, circles,” Nagy said. “We called it musical chairs, not positions. So, everybody had to know the concept. So, we weren’t running plays.” Now, of course, they are. And they are doing it against what Nagy termed a “crazy” defense. Nagy believes Dart is doing a good job handling it all. “Not only are we doing what we do, but now we get to see a crazy defense with Dennard [Wilson] and what he does,” Nagy said “So, you put it all together, and I think that every quarterback’s a little bit different, but my biggest thing with him was being able to get through these practices and get in – it sounds simple, but be able to get in the huddle, call the play, get up to the line of scrimmage, see the defense, and play fast. “He’s calling every play. He’s seeing it when he says it. He’s not just listening and memorizing it. When you can get to that point and you start seeing guys talk like this in the huddle, they’re speaking to the person, he’s there. So, he’s aced that part. Now we’ve got to get it to the part of seeing the defense and taking it to the next level, because the kid is super talented.”

And when he slid for the first down inbounds by the right sideline, a cheer erupted from the defense. “I clapped,” John Harbaugh said and smiled. “I applauded.” Peter Schrager on John Harbaugh “Think about a country club, or somewhere really fancy, a nice five star hotel and resort and take the exact opposite of that. title: The Science of “Ramping Up”: Why Aaron Glenn Playing Starters is a Calculated Risk Worth Taking
summary: For years, the conventional wisdom in NFL training camps was simple: wrap the starters in bubble wrap, hold them out of preseason games, save them for Week 1. And every September, like clockwork, the league watches soft-tissue injuries pile up anyway – hamstrings, calves, Achilles, all the non contact stuff that has nothing to do […]
full_text: For years, the conventional wisdom in NFL training camps was simple: wrap the starters in bubble wrap, hold them out of preseason games, save them for Week 1. And every September, like clockwork, the league watches soft-tissue injuries pile up anyway – hamstrings, calves, Achilles, all the non contact stuff that has nothing to do with getting hit and everything to do with a body that wasn’t ready to go full speed. There’s actually a real world test of this. In 2020, the NFL canceled the entire preseason because of COVID. No joint practices, no exhibition games, nothing. Researchers compared that season’s regular season injury numbers to 2018-19 and found soft-tissue injuries jumped hard. Hamstring, groin, calf, and quad injury rates all rose, several of them by statistically significant margins. Take away the ramp up period entirely, and the injuries didn’t drop. They got worse. That’s not a theory. That happened. The sports science explanation for why is the acute-to-chronic workload ratio, or ACWR basically a measure of how much a player’s workload in the last week compares to what his body has adapted to over the past month. Spike that ratio too fast, especially cutting straight from walkthroughs to live NFL speed, and soft tissue injury risk goes up. It’s worth saying: ACWR has real critics in the research world. Some have picked apart the math behind it, arguing it manufactures false correlations. So it’s not gospel. But the general principle underneath it bodies need a ramp, not a light switch, has more going for it than not, and the 2020 natural experiment is the strongest evidence for it we’re going to get without literally rerunning an NFL season twice. That’s the backdrop for what Aaron Glenn is doing with the Jets right now. He said Tuesday that all of Gang Green’s starters will play in Friday’s preseason opener against Tampa Bay, with the goal of getting each starter 25-30 combined reps across the three preseason games, probably averaging somewhere around 8-10 snaps a game, not a token appearance. He did the same thing last summer against Green Bay. Fans wince at this. Nobody wants to see a star player go down in a game that doesn’t count. But the idea that sitting starters out of preseason “protects” them doesn’t hold up well once you actually look at what happens to workload shielded players once the real season starts. Training camp practice, no matter how physical, still isn’t the same as live game speed, and there’s no way to fake that transition the body either gets exposed to it in August or it gets exposed to it in Week 1, and Week 1 is when it actually matters. This has extra weight for the Jets specifically. New play callers on both sides Aaron Glenn’s staff on defense, Frank Reich running the offense means starters need live reps in these systems that install periods and scripted practice can’t fully replicate. Geno Smith and the new look passing game are getting their first real look Friday night, and there’s value in that beyond just health. None of this means preseason snaps are risk-free. They’re not. Four Jets rookies have already gotten hurt during camp, before a single preseason game has been played, which is its own reminder that there’s no injury proof path through an NFL summer. Camp itself banged up plenty of players who never got near a preseason game, mostly guys on the roster bubble grinding for a job, which is a different risk profile than a starter getting a scripted 8-10 snaps. Whether it’s a joint practice in Florham Park or the lights at MetLife on Friday, the risk exists. The question was never whether to eliminate it. It’s whether ramping starters up gradually now is safer than throwing them into Week 1 cold. The data on the 2020 season says it probably is. At some point the Jets have to just play football. Better to shake off the rust in August, with two new coordinators still figuring out their calls, than in September when the wins start counting.

title: Eagles depth chart revealed ahead of first preseason game
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles’ first team-issued depth chart ahead of the 2026 NFL season is HERE! And now to immediately tamper the excitement: it doesn’t mean much. It’s not like this depth chart is carefully crated with insight from the front office and coaches. It literally says “Compiled by the Eagles Communications department” (AKA the PR […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JUNE 2: Grant Calcaterra #81 and Eli Stowers #87 of the Philadelphia Eagles look on during OTA offseason workouts at Jefferson Health Training Complex on June 2, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles ’ first team-issued depth chart ahead of the 2026 NFL season is HERE! And now to immediately tamper the excitement: it doesn’t mean much. It’s not like this depth chart is carefully crated with insight from the front office and coaches. It literally says “Compiled by the Eagles Communications department” (AKA the PR staff) at the top of the graphic. And it’s only issued to the public because it’s mandated by the NFL. “I was 22 years old and I was the one putting out the official depth chart…” A word of warning on “official” depth charts from @FG_Dolan on the Fantasy Feast podcast: pic.twitter.com/SPe93peCgQ — Ross Tucker Podcast (@RossTuckerPod) August 9, 2023 Even if this was the Eagles’ actual internal depth chart, there’s still plenty of time for things to change between now and roster cuts down to 53 players. There’s still a handful of training camp practices and three preseason games left. But for the sake of content, let’s put the cynicism aside and play along. OFFENSE QUARTERBACK — Jalen Hurts, Andy Dalton/Tanner McKee, Cole Payton RUNNING BACK — Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby, Will Shipley, Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele, Ja’Quinden Jackson WIDE RECEIVER — DeVonta Smith, Hollywood Brown, Johnny Wilson, Samori Toure, Brandon Hayes WIDE RECEIVER — Makai Lemon, Elijah Moore, Britain Covey/Quez Watkins WIDE RECEIVER — Dontayvion Wicks, Darius Cooper, Danny Gray TIGHT END — Dallas Goedert, Johnny Mundt, Eli Stowers, Grant Calcaterra, Cameron Latu, E.J. Jenkins, Stone Smartt LEFT TACKLE — Jordan Mailata, Fred Johnson, Myles Hinton, Hollin Pierce LEFT GUARD — Landon Dickerson, Michael Jordan, Myles Hinton CENTER — Cam Jurgens, Drew Kendall, Willie Lampkin RIGHT GUARD — Tyler Steen, Jake Majors, Micah Morris RIGHT TACKLE — Lane Johnson, Markel Bell, Cameron Williams, John Ojukwu DEFENSE EDGE DEFENDER* — Nolan Smith, Arnold Ebiketie, Jose Ramirez, Joshua Weru EDGE DEFENDER — Jalyx Hunt, A.J. Epenesa, Keyshawn James-Newby, Tarron Jackson DEFENSIVE TACKLE — Jalen Carter, Byron Young, Uar Bernard DEFENSIVE TACKLE — Jordan Davis, Ty Robinson, Zion Wilson DEFENSIVE TACKLE — Moro Ojomo, Gabe Hall, David Blay LINEBACKER — Zack Baun, Smael Mondon, Chance Campbell LINEBACKER — Jihaad Campbell, Jeremiah Trotter Jr., Deontae Lawson CORNERBACK — Riq Woolen, Jonathan Jones, Jakorian Bennett, Tariq Castro-Fields CORNERBACK — Quinyon Mitchell, Kelee Ringo, Ambry Thomas, Shaun Wade NICKEL CORNERBACK — Cooper DeJean, Michael Carter/Mac McWilliams, Kapena Gushiken SAFETY — Cooper DeJean, Michael Carter/Marcus Epps, J.T. Gray SAFETY — Andrew Mukuba, Andre’ Sam, Cole Wisniewski, Maximus Pulley *Note: Jonathan Greenard, who is on the active/physically unable to perform list, is not included on the depth chart. SPECIAL TEAMS PUNTER — Braden Mann KICKER — Jake Elliott HOLDER — Braden Mann LONG SNAPPER — Rocco Underwood PUNT RETURNER — Britain Covey, Makai Lemon, Elijah Moore KICK RETURNER — Will Shipley, Dameon Pierce, Tank Bigsby NOTES With Andy Dalton and Tanner McKee rotating QB2 reps, we already know there’s a backup quarterback battle going on. But here’s more confirmation. Dalton is listed first due to last name alphabetical order but he’s also arguably in the lead in reality. Will Shipley is going to be RB3 on this roster, whether you like it or not. Nothing shocking about how the wide receivers are listed but it is notable to see Lemon with the starters despite the fact he’s missed a lot of time in camp and didn’t stand out prior to getting hurt. Lemon might not actually be a Week 1 starter with the likes of Cooper and Moore having strong summers. Or at least there could be a heavier receiver rotation than there’s been in recent years. Whereas Lemon is listed with the starters, the Eagles aren’t even pretending that Stowers is a top two tight end right now. With the way the Eagles laid out tight end on this chart (see below), I don’t know that he’s even necessarily TE3. I tend to think Stowers might be a healthy scratch … early in the season, at least. It’ll be interesting to see if Fred Johnson — who hasn’t had a great summer — is the Eagles’ swing tackle or if he’s just the backup on the left side (assuming he makes the team) while Bell is the top backup on the right side. Seems like that battle between Big Fred and Bell is still ongoing. Hinton has been working more at guard than tackle this offseason. Michael Jordan is not actually the top backup at left guard. That’s Drew Kendall. Kendall is also the top backup at right guard. In terms of both the listing here and practice reps, Majors is higher on the depth chart than one would expect. Don’t think he’s playing well enough to make the roster … but maybe he sneaks on because the coaches like him? Ojukwu also gets more reps than you would expect and he’s been above Williams. No surprises with the defensive linemen or linebackers. Cornerback is interesting because McWilliams was first up at outside cornerback with Mitchell getting banged up on Tuesday. Of course, Jonathan Jones is also banged up. Gushiken has more often lined up at safety than nickel corner. Marcus Epps seems like a good bet to win the starting safety battle over Michael Carter II. But MC2 will still contribute as a dime defender in addition to providing depth at safety and nickel CB. Interesting to see Covey listed as the top punt returner. Makes sense in terms of him probably being the best option (assuming Cooper DeJean is off the table due to his defensive role). But not so sure Covey makes the roster. Shipley is listed as the top kick returner but Darius Cooper was also notably getting some reps in that role on Tuesday. What stands out to you? Let me know in the comments below.

summary: The Philadelphia Eagles made a slew of roster moves on Monday that included waiving undrafted rookie free agent signings Dae’Quan Wright and Jaedan Roberts. It didn’t take long for them to find new NFL homes. Wright was plucked off waivers by the Cleveland Browns, who rank sixth in the claiming order. Roberts is joining the […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JUNE 09: Philadelphia Eagles tight end Dae'Quan Wright #45 catches the ball during the Philadelphia Eagles off season minicamp on June 9th, 2026 at the Jefferson Health Training Complex in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles made a slew of roster moves on Monday that included waiving undrafted rookie free agent signings Dae’Quan Wright and Jaedan Roberts. It didn’t take long for them to find new NFL homes. Wright was plucked off waivers by the Cleveland Browns, who rank sixth in the claiming order. Roberts is joining the Atlanta Falcons, who rank 13th in the claiming order. The Eagles waiving Wright came as a surprise to me (and some other practice observes I talked to) since I thought he was one of their more intriguing UDFA additions . Wright was having a quiet camp while not getting many reps but he previously had a flash or two during the Eagles’ spring practices. I was interested to see him play in the preseason since he runs very hard after the catch. Alas, he’s in Cleveland now. As for Roberts, it looked like he suffered a season-ending injury earlier in camp but he got lucky and avoided that outcome. The Eagles already have a lot of offensive line depth, so, Roberts was expendable. In addition to this news, the Eagles officially released veteran running back Elijah Mitchell from injured reserve with an injury settlement. Mitchell recently got banged up in practice and was subsquently placed on IR.
