title: What have 2026 NFL rookies spent their first paychecks on?
summary: Jeremiyah Love, Drew Allar and Carnell Tate are among the NFL rookies who just got their first pro contracts. How did they spend their new money?
full_text:
For NFL rookies, that first paycheck represents more than just a payday. After years of working toward the league -- which kicks off Thursday with a full slate of Week 1 preseason games  -- many first-year players have used that money on long-awaited purchases and priorities.

 For some rookies, it's a new car. For others, it's a house or an opportunity to take care of their parents. And then there are those who aren't ready to spend a dime.

 Buffalo Bills fourth-round pick Skyler Bell , who said NIL money at UConn helped him buy his first car, is already eyeing his next ride -- "maybe like an AMG [Mercedes] or something."  New Orleans Saints sixth-round pick Barion Brown has a different approach: "Nah, I'm a sixth-round guy, man. I've got to save every penny I can get!"

 Here's a look at what some of the NFL's top rookies told ESPN's NFL Nation they have done or plan to do with their first professional paycheck.

 

 
 Jump to a category: 
 Savings, investing | Homes, goods 
 Sports equipment | Apparel | Family 
 Travel, vehicles | Electronics | Exotic pets 

 
 

 

 Savings and investing 

 

 Jeremiyah Love , RB, Arizona Cardinals 
 Round 1, No. 3 | Age: 21 

 Love hasn't been shy about how he's going to spend his rookie contract, which is worth a fully guaranteed $53.9 million over four years -- or rather, how he won't be spending his rookie contract. Love said he plans to live off his endorsement money and not spend his NFL paychecks. He has deals with PayPal, New Balance and Celsius. Reports put Love's NIL valuation at Notre Dame at around $600,000, which Love said allows him to live off what he already makes and not new money.

 "I'm not going to touch the money," he said. "I'm probably going to put it all away and live normally like I've been doing now."

 

 

 Arvell Reese , LB/Edge, New York Giants 
 Round 1, No. 5 | Age: 20 

 Reese also won't being spending big, even though his deal includes $47.8 million guaranteed. "I just signed it and then went to the hotel and then just got ready for the practice the next day," Reese said. "I don't really got [anything] to buy right now. I already got everything. I got a car and an apartment. So, I'm good right now."

 

 

 Malachi Lawrence , Edge, Dallas Cowboys 
 Round 1, No. 23 | Age: 23 

 "I got a truck, a [Ram] TRX, that was my first purchase, but that was with NIL. It wasn't with my bonus," Lawrence said.

 So, what about his NFL money?

 "I haven't spent really any of that yet. I think like 70% of the players after the NFL go bankrupt or something like that, and I want to be in that 30%."

 
 

 Peter Woods , DT, Kansas City Chiefs 
 Round 1, No. 29 | Age: 21 

 "I wouldn't say there is [anything specific I want to buy]," Woods said. "Nah, I'm just kind of letting my money make money right now. I had a pretty blessed college situation [at Clemson]. It's a different landscape [now]. It allows me to kind of be disciplined in that area. I'm not really worried about it, for real."

 
 

 Zachariah Branch , WR, Atlanta Falcons 
 Round 3, No. 79 | Age: 22 

 The Falcons' rookie wide receiver wants to be frugal, the way his parents taught him to be. Branch said he has already spent "a little bit" of his NFL money but on an investment in the stock market. Specifically, S&P 500 companies. "I think I'm all good right now," said Branch, a third-round pick. "I don't think I'm in a position to get to doing certain things that's not smart. I'm trying to create generational wealth. So, whatever comes it may come, but right now I think I'm good on the investments and just food, family."

 

 Eventually, the Georgia product said he wants to get into real estate. His father, Sheva, is a prominent realtor in the family's hometown of Las Vegas. "Trying to get some properties and things like that to expand my real estate portfolio," Branch said.

 

 

 Homes and household goods 

 

 Blake Miller , OT, Detroit Lions 
 Round 1, No. 17 | Age: 22 

 Miller isn't looking to purchase anything crazy but is looking to buy a home. "I'm trying to be smart with it and not be a big, big spender," Miller told ESPN. "But, I guess a place to live would be it." Miller, who was selected by Detroit as the 17th pick, learned the value of being smart with his finances from his parents and by managing his money at Clemson from 2022 to 2025, where he started all 54 games of his career.

 "Obviously being in college in the whole NIL era, that helped a little bit because I kind of was there when it was getting going and you get to see the progression of it," Miller said. "Like guys now, you don't just get a big chunk of money deposited in your account. You're still making good money, but it's not as crazy as it is now. So, I feel like that kind of helped me be able to deal with more and more money, and then my parents as well set a good example. They're always there with questions or anything, and they're really helpful."

 

 

 Jadarian Price , RB, Seattle Seahawks 
 Round 1, No. 32 | Age: 22 

 With some of the $8.7 million in signing bonus money he received as the 32nd pick in the draft, Price bought his family a new house in his hometown of Denison, Texas. It was something he has wanted to do since he was young and his biggest goal once he reached the NFL. "Checked that off the list," he said. His family's reaction? "A bunch of smiles," Price said.

 

 

 Treydan Stukes , S, Las Vegas Raiders 
 Round 2, No. 38 | Age: 24 

 "I actually got a house," Stukes said. "I went the real estate route. That was the big purchase, and everything else went into the savings [account]."

 
 

 Jacob Rodriguez , LB, Miami Dolphins 
 Round 2, No. 43 | Age: 23 

 "I went and got a bed," Rodriguez said of his first purchase. "I went and got a mattress. So, you know, in college for a little bit, when I was a walk-on, I slept on the ground in my brother's apartment. And so, like, I'd never slept good when I was 13 and on, and so then I moved to the college, like 3-inch mattress or whatever. So I never bought a mattress until I was [drafted] because I always said my first purchase is going to be a bed. So, I bought a nice Tempur-Pedic."

 

 

 Brandon Cisse , CB, Green Bay Packers 
 
 Round 2, No. 52 | Age: 21 

 Cisse's first paycheck wasn't his first payday. "I had mostly all my stuff already thankfully because of my NIL deals and stuff like that," he said. "But I was able to purchase a house for my family. At the time I purchased the house, I was having a daughter. Now she's here, so that's why I wanted to buy a house here in Green Bay." His daughter was born July 17, just before training camp opened.

 
 

 

 Antonio Williams , WR, Washington Commanders 
 Round 3, No. 71 | Age: 22 

 

 The third-round pick from Clemson made one big purchase. "My first big purchase was a home about 10 minutes away from the [Commanders'] facility. I'm not a big spender. I feel that was a good investment. No cars, nothing crazy, man. I didn't want to make any dumb decisions."

 

 Sports equipment 

 

 Caleb Lomu , OT, New England Patriots 
 
 Round 1, No. 28 | Age: 21 

 

 "I'm not really a guy who spends too much money, but one of the first things I got was a new golf set," Lomu said. "I'm big into golf. I love playing some golf. I had to get some longer ones. I kind of outgrew my old set."

 

 Family support 

 

 Jordyn Tyson , WR, New Orleans Saints 
 
 Round 1, No. 8 | Age: 22 

 "I sent my dad some money. I looked at his USAA account. ... I was like, let me give Pops some money. [I didn't tell him.] When he saw me, he just gave me a hug," Tyson said. "For myself, I bought a house. I'd say that was the big thing."

 

 

 Zion Young , Edge, Baltimore Ravens 
 Round 2, No. 45 | Age: 22 

 Young, who is the youngest of 11 siblings, used the money to help his parents. "My parents have [had] a house full of kids my whole life," Young said. "The first thing I wanted to do was put a little money in their pockets and pay for some [house] renovations."…

title: 2026 Atlanta Falcons training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Falcons training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Atlanta Falcons ' camp is taking place in Flowery Branch, Georgia, and Falcons reporter Marc Raimondi has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Falcons camp. We will update this file often. How will the QB battle play out between  Michael Penix Jr . and  Tua Tagovailoa for QB1? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Falcons stories 
 
 Sources: Falcons, RB Robinson reach 3-year deal worth up to $75M 
 Falcons sign Matthew Bergeron to four-year, $96M extension 
 Falcons' Jalon Walker tore ACL, out for season 
 Wife of DC Ulbrich dies of cancer 
 
 
 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 Falcons practice Wednesday was a short one, mainly consisting of two-minute drills, with the team's first preseason game coming up Friday.

 Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa had some success, but was unable to get the ball into the end zone. He was 5-of-9 passing in the 11-on-11, two-minute drill sessions. Tagovailoa was intercepted on the final play of the session by safety Jammie Robinson on a pass that appeared to be meant for tight end  Kyle Pitts Sr ..

 Tagovailoa nearly had a beautiful touchdown pass down the right side to wide receiver  Olamide Zaccheaus , but the ball was slightly overthrown.

 Cooper Rush , who will back up Tagovailoa in the exhibition Friday, was 5-of-10 and also unable to score a touchdown.

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa has been a full participant in practice for about a week now. And his performances have really turned the corner since late last week.

 Tagovailoa was 7-of-7 passing in 11-on-11 team sessions Tuesday. The tight back issue seems to be in the rearview mirror and Tagovailoa is starting to show comfortability with this new offense under head coach Kevin Stefanski and offensive coordinator Tommy Rees.

 "Oh, he's getting better every day," Falcons quarterbacks coach Alex Van Pelt said Tuesday. "I think he's becoming more comfortable with the system and the play calls and protection adjustments and everything. It's tough always to come into a new system. So, picking that up -- missing the first part of camp set him back just a little bit -- but really the last three or four days he's really come on."

 
 The Falcons defense is dealing with some injuries. Safety Jessie Bates III (back), inside linebacker Divine Deablo , defensive back Natrone Brooks and cornerback Avieon Terrell all missed practice Tuesday. Defensive tackle  Da'Shawn Hand  has been out since last week. 
 The Falcons signed veteran running back Trey Sermon to add depth behind Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr ., who has gotten some run as a kick returner. Sermon will complete with Tyler Goodson , Nathan Carter and Cash Jones to make the 53-man roster. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 Quarterback Michael Penix Jr . is still not cleared for 11-on-11 sessions, but he has mostly been sharp in practice lately.

 On Monday, Penix was 9-of-11 passing during a 7-on-7 series, including a beautiful completion to tight end  Kyle Pitts Sr . down the right sideline. The throw was right in the bucket and would have gone for a big gain. Penix did get picked off by cornerback Clark Phillips III on his final throw.

 Tua Tagovailoa was 4-of-6 in 11s and working more on pushing the ball down the field.

 Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said he has not yet made a decision on whether Tagovailoa will play in the team's first preseason game Friday against the Denver Broncos . As for Penix, he can't play in any game until he is cleared for 11s in practice, Stefanski said.

 More observations: 

 
 The Falcons signed defensive end Cameron Sample , who was waived last week by the San Francisco 49ers . Sample will provide depth off the edge after second-year standout Jalon Walker went down with a torn ACL last week. 
 Right tackle Jawaan Taylor was activated from the reserve/physically unable to perform list. He is likely to be the team's starting right tackle. The Falcons have been rotating Michael Jerrell , Brandon Walton and rookie seventh-rounder Ethan Onianwa in that spot. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa had his best practice of camp, though it did not last long. The practice, that is.

 Lightning halted the Falcons' open practice at Lanier High School in Sugar Hill, Georgia, early on Saturday night. There was still more than 30 minutes left when things were called on the field of a packed stadium.

 Tagovailoa was 6-of-8 passing in 11-on-11 drills, including his best two passes of training camp: a 30-yarder with touch to wide receiver Jahan Dotson and a play-action rollout lob to wide receiver Drake London .

 Tagovailoa returned to full practices earlier this week after dealing with a tight back to start camp.

 
 

 
 
 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa hit running back Bijan Robinson on a wheel route that would have gone for a 90-yard touchdown or so during an 11-on-11 session Friday. The series was situational. The Falcons offense was backed up against the opposite goal line and Tagovailoa floated it nicely to Robinson, who had complete daylight.

 It was just another play in another practice this summer here in Flowery Branch, Georgia. But it also felt like more than that, something symbolic. Like a sigh of relief.

 For the first time this training camp, Tagovailoa and Robinson were both full participants in practice. Tagovailoa has been dealing with a tight back and Robinson was a hold-in before signing a three-year contract extension Wednesday that is worth up to $75 million. Robinson got his first carries in 11s Friday.

 More observations: 

 
 Quarterback Michael Penix Jr . is still not cleared for 11s, but has looked sharper lately in 7-on-7 work. On Friday, he was 6-of-9 in the red zone, helped out by a diving catch from wide receiver Keelan Marion . 
 Matt Ryan, the team's president of football and former franchise quarterback, threw to wide receivers Drake London and Jahan Dotson separated from everyone else during a drill Friday. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Michael Penix Jr . explained his current situation in the clearest way possible Wednesday.

 "If I can't be on the field," Penix said, "how am I going to be the starter?"

 Penix has been on the field. He has done individual drills and 7-on-7 sessions. But what the Falcons third-year quarterback means is that he has yet to be cleared for 11-on-11 work. And until he does, there cannot be any kind of quarterback competition.

 That is not necessarily news. The Falcons coaching staff made that clear in the spring. But back then there was some expectation Penix would be fully ready for training camp. That has not been the case and Penix said it could be another several weeks before he's good to go.

 Tua Tagovailoa (tight back) took another step toward a full return Wednesday with more work in 11s. He went 5-of-7 passing. At this juncture, it's fair to say Tagovailoa will be the team's Week 1 starter unless something major changes.

 More observations: 

 
 Edge rusher Jalon Walker was officially confirmed as out for the season with a torn ACL after getting injured Tuesday at practice. It's a major blow for a pass rush that was depending him on to make a major impact. He had 5.5 sacks as a rookie last season. 
 Running back Bijan Robinson officially put pen to paper on his three-year extension, which is worth up to $75 million. He is still limited in practice and has not done any 11s as the team ramps him up.

title: Ranking NFL quarterbacks by trait: Best arm, accuracy, more
summary: Does Josh Allen have the league's strongest arm? Is Lamar Jackson still the most unstoppable QB rusher? And where does Caleb Williams stand among the best improvisers?
full_text:
You're going to hear us talk about quarterbacks a lot on " NFL Live " over the course of the 2026 season . There will be debates about all of them, from the best in the game to the borderline starters. But for a third straight year , I'm narrowing the focus here in the preseason . Who are the best signal-callers in the NFL at individual skills?

 Does anyone boast a better arm than Josh Allen ? Does Joe Burrow or Matthew Stafford have the more refined mechanics? Is Lamar Jackson still the gold standard in QB rushing?

 I ranked the top 10 quarterbacks by seven different traits: arm strength, ball placement, mechanics, decision-making, pocket presence, second-reaction creativity and rushing ability. These lists are based on current performance and expectations for the 2026 season. It is how I would rank the QB group at this exact moment. I included only starters  and leaned on what I see on tape to form the rankings.

 

 
 Jump to a section: 
 Arm strength  | Ball placement  |  Mechanics 
 Decision-making  |  Pocket presence 
 Second reaction | Rushing ability 

 
 

 Arm strength 
 1. Josh Allen , Bills 
2. Justin Herbert , Chargers 
3. Caleb Williams , Bears 
4. Matthew Stafford , Rams 
5. Patrick Mahomes , Chiefs 
6. Baker Mayfield , Buccaneers 
7. Drake Maye , Patriots 
8. Joe Burrow , Bengals 
9. Lamar Jackson , Ravens 
10. Dak Prescott , Cowboys 

 There are different kinds of arm strength. Everyone immediately looks at deep balls -- the 60-yard Hail Marys down the sideline. It's all about who can throw the rock the furthest, right? You need a live arm to connect on those shot plays, no doubt. But I focus more on passes into tight windows in the intermediate areas of the field and the pure power throws from what I call "funny body" positions. Quarterbacks don't have the strong base to fall back on here; there is no loading up and driving through the pass. Instead, they need to rely almost entirely on their arm to get the ball where it needs to go with velocity.

 Allen is still No. 1 in this department. His ability to get zip on his throws from uncomfortable positions really stands out. He just flicks his wrist, and the ball is suddenly in his receiver's hands on a rope. Not every QB1 can do that, and yet he does it with consistency.

 

 But there are some challengers for his top spot this year. Herbert gets real pop on his throws by driving it. No one has completed more tight-window balls over the past five years than Herbert (162). Williams got legit consideration for No. 1, too. He made some miraculous passes from unorthodox positions in 2025, including a 40-plus-yard strike to the end zone late in the divisional round  -- while back-pedaling.

 Mahomes can wing it with the best of them, and Stafford and Maye are both elite on downfield balls. Stafford completed 37 passes of 20 or more air yards last season, easily the most in the NFL. And I also want to call out Mayfield -- I still think he has the most slept-on arm in the NFL. The one quarterback I really wanted to get into the top 10 was Trevor Lawrence . He also has some underrated arm talent and makes difficult throws look easy. Hey, it's tough to limit these lists to just 10 guys.

 

 

 Ball placement 
 1. Matthew Stafford , Rams 
2. Drake Maye , Patriots 
3. Sam Darnold , Seahawks 
4. Joe Burrow , Bengals 
5. Jared Goff , Lions 
6. Jordan Love , Packers 
7. Josh Allen , Bills 
8. Lamar Jackson , Ravens 
9. Brock Purdy , 49ers 
10. Dak Prescott , Cowboys 

 How do you find the best quarterbacks in ball placement? Their receivers are never truly considered "covered."

 I say this every year in this space, but it's worth refreshing: Accuracy and ball placement aren't the same thing. Accuracy means putting the ball on the receiver so he can make the play. Ball placement means putting the ball on the receiver in the perfect spot so he can make the play -- and no one else can. The names at the top of this list -- including some MVP candidates last season in Stafford and Maye -- routinely keep the ball away from the defender. It's all about precision.

 Let's start by addressing a big shift at the top. Burrow was the top-ranked QB in ball placement on each of the past two lists I've put together. He's now No. 4. He's still extremely good in this area, able to pin the ball to his receivers. But injuries did cost him more than half of the 2025 season, and it opened the door for some others to move up the list a little bit. Fair or not, I'm factoring in time on task. And Stafford came out every Sunday and fired bull's-eyes with conviction.

 If you're looking at the stats, Maye would have a pretty good case to be the new No. 1, too. He settles for second here, but there's no knocking his league-best 72.0% completion rate and 9.1% completion rate above expectation (per NFL Next Gen Stats). And unlike every other QB in the top five, he wasn't playing with an All-Pro receiver. Maye was especially good with trajectory going downfield, dropping it in a bucket. I can't wait to see what he does with A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs in 2026.

 Goff is sneaky good in this trait, and we see it at all levels of the field. Purdy displays incredible touch, layering the ball in. His 10.7% off-target rate was fourth-best in the NFL last season. Love and Prescott have an impressive ability to float the pass in and set their receiver up for yards after the catch. It's another list that was hard to sort through at the bottom, but I think every name on here is deserving.

 Tua Tagovailoa has been a mainstay in the ball placement top 10, and he was all the way up at No. 2 in 2024 when I first started doing this annual project. But he has declined a bit here, and his QB1 battle in Atlanta disqualifies him, anyway. Geno Smith also slid out after making the list in back-to-back years; he didn't look like the same quarterback last season at 35 years old.

 

 

 

 Mechanics 
 1. Matthew Stafford , Rams 
2. Joe Burrow , Bengals 
3. Daniel Jones , Colts 
4. Jared Goff , Lions 
5. Dak Prescott , Cowboys 
6. C.J. Stroud , Texans 
7. Caleb Williams , Bears 
8. Jayden Daniels , Commanders 
9. Josh Allen , Bills 
10. Lamar Jackson , Ravens 

 It's neck and neck between Stafford and Burrow. Things that matter here:

 
 Clean, smooth throwing motions from start to finish 
 Strong bases that keep the QB in rhythm and firm 
 Repeatable processes that don't change from rep to rep, even when things get chaotic around the QB 
 
 That last one is key for Stafford and Burrow. Defenses don't know what's coming because every throw looks exactly the same coming out. It's amazing consistency. The tight connection between Stafford's upper and lower body allows him to pull off all those no-look throws. Defenses can't tell the difference until his release, and bam, the ball is going somewhere unexpected.

 You might be surprised to see Jones at No. 3. I was, too. But watching the tape again, I was taken aback by how good his mechanics were in Indianapolis last season. The Colts ran many different forms of RPOs, and that means his mechanics need to be sound. They were.

 Goff, Prescott and Stroud are such pure passers, with beautiful, natural motions. Daniels' mechanics have shades of Stroud. And I was impressed with how much Williams improved here last season. He might be more known for the off-platform plays, but he's solid from a mechanics standpoint. I had a hard time leaving Justin Herbert off. He probably should be on the list. Aaron Rodgers was also a tough cut, even in Year 22.

 

 

 Decision-making with the football 
 1. Josh Allen , Bills 
2. Matthew Stafford , Rams 
3. Jordan Love , Packers 
4. Drake Maye , Patriots 
5. Jayden Daniels , Commanders 
6. Dak Prescott , Cowboys 
7. Lamar Jackson , Ravens 
8. Joe Burrow , Bengals 
9. Patrick Mahomes , Chiefs 
10. Jalen Hurts , Eagles

title: 2026 Baltimore Ravens training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Ravens training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Baltimore Ravens ' camp is taking place at Under Armour Performance Center in Baltimore, and Ravens reporter Jamison Hensley has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Ravens camp. We will update this file often. Can new coach Jesse Minter get  Lamar Jackson  and the Ravens to the Super Bowl? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Ravens camp 
 
 Zay Flowers, Ravens agree to four-year, $140M extension 
 Derrick Henry, entering 11th year, not thinking about retirement 
 Ravens waive rookie Diego Pavia to make room for Ethan Pocic 
 Ravens' Madubuike (neck) practices for 1st time in 10 months 
 
 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 The Baltimore Ravens ' cornerback depth is being tested this week after both of their starting cornerbacks exited practice early.

 A day after Nate Wiggins was carted off the field with a knee injury, Marlon Humphrey walked off the practice field midway through Wednesday's practice with a trainer. It is unclear what he injured.

 Ravens defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver said after practice that he expects both Wiggins and Humphrey to return soon.

 "We would love to have those guys [Wiggins and Humphrey] out there," Weaver said. "Thoughts and prayers that they get back as fast as they can."

 With Wiggins and Humphrey not on the field, the Ravens' most experienced cornerbacks are Chidobe Awuzie and T.J. Tampa . Baltimore also have promising young corners in rookie Chandler Rivers ,  Bilhal Kone  and Keyon Martin .

 In Wednesday's play of the day, Rivers dislodged the ball from wide receiver Xavier Guillory , knocking the ball high in the air. Martin pulled in the loose ball for a turnover.

 "There are a bunch of guys I think that could step in if needed," Weaver said.

 Other observations: 

 
 Pro Bowl defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike participated in positional drills for the first time in training camp. Madubuike, who underwent neck surgery in April, had been limited to individual drills for the first two weeks of camp. "He looks phenomenal," Weaver said. "I know he wants to be just doing everything he can to be back out there, and when he is out there, I expect him to look like the Nnamdi we have grown to know and love throughout the years." 
 Rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane continues his hot streak. He caught a 45-yard touchdown from Lamar Jackson in a one-on-one drill and then boxed out Tampa for a 35-yard catch downfield. 
 Tight end Mark Andrews had his best day of camp, catching a touchdown pass from Lamar Jackson in the red zone. 
 Lamar Jackson showed leadership after he misconnected with wide receiver LaJohntay Wester in the red zone. Jackson first talked to Wester about his route and then took him to a tablet where they could rewatch the play again. 
 The Ravens placed No. 3 QB Skylar Thompson on injured reserve and signed QB Austin Reed , who was with offensive coordinator Declan Doyle at the Bears' training camp last season. With Lamar Jackson not playing in Saturday's preseason opener, the expectation is for Tyler Huntley to start and undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano to play a bulk of the game.

 
 
 
 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Pro Bowl wide receiver Zay Flowers surprisingly returned to practice after suffering a quad contusion on Saturday. He missed one practice.

 Flowers ran before Tuesday's practice and participated in positional drills. He looked fast and smooth cutting around the cones before heading early into the team facility.

 "That was all part of the plan as he's working back just through the soreness of the quad," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "I expect him to be Zay here any day."

 In other encouraging injury news, starting nose tackle Travis Jones was activated off the Physically Unable to Perform list and practiced for the first time this summer. He worked in positional drills after missing the first two weeks of training camp with a pectoral injury.

 "He's been chomping at the bit," Minter said. "He'll be a guy that in the first few days we'll probably have to hold him back, which is sometimes a good thing. But, 'Trav' looks amazing striking the sled. He's been putting in a ton of work off the field, in the weight room [and in] conditioning. I expect big, big things from 'Trav'."

 Other observations: 

 
 
 Ravens QB   Lamar Jackson   and other "established players" won't play in Saturday's preseason opener against the   Philadelphia Eagles , Minter said. Jackson hasn't played in the preseason since 2021. 
 Ravens kicker   Tyler Loop   had another perfect day, making all seven of his kicks. Loop is now 33 of 35 (94.2%) in training camp and has made all eight of his tries beyond 50 yards. 
 Minter said he hasn't decided how the Ravens will handle challenges. The NFL will allow head coaches to designate a member of their sideline staff to throw the red flag. "That's certainly something to think about -- it could be helpful in certain situations, potentially," Minter said. "But, we'll figure that out as we get closer to the game. I may try it a couple different ways, even in the preseason, and see what gives us the best opportunity as a team." 
 

 
 Sunday, Aug. 9 
 Putting on full pads for the fourth time in training camp, the Ravens had one of their most physical practices of the summer. It was also their sloppiest.

 Baltimore's first, second and third offenses totaled eight false starts during the two-hour practice. The Ravens' starting offense jumped offside twice during a red-zone drill.

 Ravens coach Jesse Minter indicated the offense was trying to mix up the quarterback cadence on Sunday to keep the defense on its heels.

 "I think it's a great message of just the focus and the details that's required for that to become a real weapon and not something that puts you behind the chains like it did a few times today," Minter said.

 Other observations:  

 
 Just like he's done all camp, rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane had a couple more big plays, including working back to make a 15-yard grab in front of cornerback Marlon Humphrey . But Lane's most impressive play Sunday was his block on the perimeter that helped running back Derrick Henry gain some extra yards. 
 Minter reiterated that wide receiver Zay Flowers won't miss much time after leaving Saturday's practice with a quad contusion. "I feel good that he'll be back out there being Zay pretty soon," Minter said. 
 Safety Jaylinn Hawkins has made it difficult for wide receivers to go over the middle. On Saturday, Hawkins' collision with Flowers caused him to leave practice with a quad contusion. A day later, Hawkins crashed into Rashod Bateman to force an incompletion. Asked if there is a lesson for Hawkins to learn, Minter said, "I really don't want to put that on him. When you're a safety and you're breaking on the ball, there's just a little bit of an awareness of not trying to have the body-on-body collisions. We certainly want Jaylinn to play with the mindset that he plays with. So we'll continue to just be really, really careful about that." 
 Starting nose tackle Travis Jones "will be starting to work back in real, real soon," Minter said. Jones is on the Physically Unable to Perform list with a pectoral injury. Defensive end Calais Campbell participated in team drills for the first time in camp. Both Jones and Campbell should be ready for the Sept. 13 season opener. 
 Kicker Tyler Loop was 8-of-8 on field goal attempts, including three from beyond…

title: Bills, fans get first look inside new Highmark Stadium
summary: ESPN chronicled the Buffalo Bills' "Return of the Blue & Red night" on Saturday, the first public event held at the new Highmark Stadium.
full_text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- For decades, questions have lingered around Western New York: When and where would the Buffalo Bills move? Los Angeles? Toronto?

 The answer proved to be the other side of Abbott Road.

 The first public event held at the Bills' new Highmark Stadium was Saturday's training camp practice -- more specifically the annual "Return of the Blue & Red" night. It offered members of the team and 51,807 fans (a team record for a practice, per the Bills) a first look at the $2.2 billion stadium. 

 The Bills' new home is now open after three years of construction. Saturday's practice was filled with blue, red and even some gray sights on what many described as a "bittersweet night." 

 ESPN chronicled the evening through photographs.

 

 

 QB1's new look 

 Quarterback Josh Allen 's first steps in uniform onto the new field was a highly anticipated moment. Photographers and videographers gathered by the tunnel more than a half-hour before he came out.

 Allen is known for wearing custom items for this particular stadium practice.

 But new year, new stadium, new look.

 Allen came out of the tunnel wearing the team's new alternate "Nickel City" uniform  that has been surrounded in controversy. The quarterback vocally supported  the look on the opening day of training camp.

 Before practice, Allen played catch with fans all the way around the track of the stadium. As he threw his final passes, a sign that read, "the house that Allen Built" was visible in the stands behind him.

 Backup quarterbacks Kyle Allen and Shane Buechele , as well as punter Tommy Doman Jr ., joined Allen in wearing the uniform, while the rest of the offense wore the team's home blue jerseys and the defense was in the away whites.

 "I don't know if your quarterbacks are always the best models to show how it looks like. I made fun of Kyle Allen," coach Joe Brady joked. "It's taken me a long time to let [the defensive line] know not to touch the red jerseys in practice. ... I said, 'Look, if you touch a gray jersey today, you don't have to worry about me being the mad one. There's 50,000 fans that are going to be pretty mad at you.'"

 The quarterbacks finished the practice unscathed. 

 

 

 Hello, grass 

 The new stadium features a big change that players are overwhelmingly in favor of -- going from artificial turf to natural grass.

 "Perfect," right tackle Spencer Brown said of the grass. "I love it. I might sleep out here tonight actually."

 The field is made up of Kentucky Bluegrass cultivated by Tuckahoe Turf Farms in New Jersey. While the night practice was held on a humid summer night (and was hit by a brief, but strong, rain shower) -- winter will come.

 

 When it does, the field's underground heating coils will activate to prevent freezing. There are also snowmelt systems on the artificial turf and track that surround it. There are four natural grass kicking areas cut into the artificial turf that surrounds the grass field. Those allow specialists to work from the sidelines on the same playing surface that is on the field.

 There were moments when players had to stomp grass chunks back into place, but the reception after the practice was all positive.

 "It's my No. 1 favorite thing, honestly," tight end Dawson Knox said. "I mean, people probably won't understand, but playing on grass vs. playing on turf is a huge difference. And I think I can speak for literally every player on this team, we love the grass. This is beautifully done. I mean, hats off to whoever did this grass, because it's perfect."

 

 

 The Family Circle 

 The much-anticipated bison family statues were in place a month ahead of the practice, but this was the stainless-steel statues' time to shine, quite literally.

 Four hours before the practice, an orderly line of people waited for their chance to take a photo with the bison and the stadium behind. But soon after, the line broke apart and fans took photos from every angle. 

 The bison reside in The Family Circle, where fans congregated and immersed themselves in signage. All of the members of the team's wall of fame from the previous stadium are recognized here -- outside of O.J. Simpson . There are also blank canvases, ready to honor current and future Bills.

 The team livestreamed the bison statues onto the jumbotrons in the stadium, and the statues were lit up in blue and red at the conclusion of the practice.

 
 

 

 'Take it all in' 

 Knox arrived at the stadium four hours early.

 He walked around the field, taking in all the sights or as he described, "taking myself on a little tour." The veteran tight end made sure to note all of the details. "It's the coolest place I've ever played football in," Knox said after practice.

 Other players and staff members took the field well ahead of the day's events with looks of awe and wonderment.

 Brady's goal with this practice was for his players to go through a game-like setting in the stadium. That's why a 7 p.m. start time was chosen. But he also wanted players to arrive early, as Knox did, to focus on practice when practice began.

 "The lights, how does the wind feel, just the grass, the environment, take it all in," Brady said. "So that hey, now when we get out to practice, we're not thinking about all the other potential distractions."

 The coach himself took some time before the practice to take in the field with his son, Jordan, 3, sporting a Josh Allen shirt, of course.

 "To get to run around with him, those are the moments that I made sure I tried to take that in," Brady said. "And then, all right, now it's time to go."

 
 

 

 A bag of Wegmans chips 

 The old Highmark Stadium is largely erased from the Orchard Park skyline. What is left is the rubble from the upper deck as the underground portions of the stadium continue to be filled.

 Before the doors opened for practice, many fans took the opportunity to peer through the fence at what is left of the former home of the team.

 "Bittersweet" was uttered time and time again.

 The SanFilippo family sat by their car in the parking lot with the rubble of the past behind them and their eyes on the future. They had multiple sets of season tickets at the old stadium and ultimately kept just three seats total from their 1963 package that originated with Andy SanFilippo's father.

 Andy remarked how he can't look back at the old stadium that holds "great memories." He renewed his own season tickets when Jim Kelly came to Buffalo and kept them over the past couple of decades.

 Bills apparel in full display, Buffalo pride and Wegmans chips in hand, they all agreed on a sadness in seeing the old stadium go while also acknowledging that they were "excited' to see the new venue for the first time.

 
 

 

 Nods to Buffalo 

 Bills owner Terry Pegula made very clear to the team's senior vice president of design, Frank Cravotta, what he wanted.

 "[Pegula] said, 'Frank, when you plop me down in my new stadium, I better know immediately that I'm in Buffalo,'" Cravotta said. "We have such a proud history. We have such great stories to tell."

 That includes placing the world's largest folding table in the 100 level, on which a fan placed a Josh Allen sticker during the event. There is the large-scale model of the Peace Bridge, which connects Buffalo to Fort Erie, Ontario, that fans can walk under. A full-size camper bus is on the 300 level.

 Food vendors are labeled with different Buffalo neighborhoods, and some represent local restaurants, such as Southern Junction, a BBQ restaurant with a South Asian influence.

 There is also an art program that includes more than 45 creators and teams who crafted pieces that are displayed throughout the stadium. The art depicts a variety of Bills-specific touches, and some reflect Western New York.

 
 

 

 'Welcome to Highmark Stadium' 

 The first fans heard warm greetings from a ticket scanner as they entered the gates near the M&T Club, phones up in the air to record their…

title: 2026 Carolina Panthers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our updates from Panthers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Carolina Panthers ' camp is taking place in Charlotte, North Carolina, and we'll have the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Panthers camp. We will update this file often. Will QB Bryce Young and the Panthers take another step forward after making the playoffs in 2025? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan has gotten "bigger and stronger" this offseason, according to head coach Dave Canales . And that improved physique was on display throughout Wednesday's practice in Charlotte.

 McMillan started the day with a nifty double move against starting cornerback Mike Jackson in one-on-one drills. McMillan was able to create increased separation with his route progression after beating Jackson off the line. The wideout then hauled in the ball for a touchdown a few paces in front of Jackson.

 "At the line of scrimmage, just hasn't really had an issue this camp," Canales said. "Getting off the line, I think that he's really translating all the work he did in the offseason. ... I'm really excited where he's at."

 Later, during team drills, the connection between quarterback Bryce Young and McMillan was apparent.

 Young was picked off by Jackson on an early rep while targeting McMillan. But following that miscue, the starting quarterback connected with McMillan on more than a handful of tosses.

 Other observations: 

 
 Along with Jackson's interception against Young in team drills, safety  Demani Richardson  intercepted a pass from backup QB Kenny Pickett in 11-on-11 drills. 
 Left guard Damien Lewis (calf) returned to practice in pads after missing several workouts during the first two weeks of camp. He took part in individual drills. He isn't expected to play against the Buffalo Bills on Saturday, per Canales. 
 Outside linebacker Pat Jones (illness) was a new absence. Defensive end Derrick Brown (knee soreness) also missed practice. Brown hasn't worked with his teammates in a week. 
 Rookie right tackle Monroe Freeling , the team's first-round pick, had a pair of strong reps against outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips , the team's prized free-agent addition, in individual pass rush drills. Following the first rep, veteran lineman Brady Christensen clapped in approval. After the second try, offensive line coach Joe Gilbert loudly praised Freeling's technique. 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 A competition is brewing at inside linebacker next to one of the Carolina Panthers ' biggest offseason additions.

 Trevin Wallace is competing with veteran Claudin Cherelus for the second starting linebacker job opposite All-Pro defender Devin Lloyd , head coach Dave Canales confirmed Monday. 

 The Panthers signed Lloyd to a three-year, $41.9 million deal in March to lead their defense. However, when defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero uses a base set, the play-caller will deploy two inside linebackers, which is why the competition becomes paramount for the unit. Wallace, a 2024 third-round pick, has been limited to 25 games (20 starts) during his first two seasons. He has sustained back-to-back season-ending shoulder ailments and underwent surgery for the latest setback after landing on injured reserve in December of last year. 

 Despite his injury struggles over the past two years, Wallace was expected to be the first man up next to Lloyd. Now, he'll need to earn that spot in the lineup. Both Wallace and Cherelus played in the first half during Thursday's 33-30 win over the Arizona Cardinals in the Hall of Fame game in Canton, Ohio.

 Other observations: 

 
 Several players were forced to break up a tussle between center Luke Fortner and cornerback Mike Jackson in the middle of the scrum following an 11-on-11 rep. At one point, Fortner and Jackson, while hanging onto each other, slammed down to the ground. The bout was quickly separated, but backup offensive tackle Stone Forsythe was also pushed to the ground.  
 Canales acknowledged that the defense bounced back on Monday after being one-upped by the offense on Sunday. Backup linebacker Bam Martin-Scott , rookie cornerback Cam Miller and nickel corner Corey Thornton got hands on passes for deflections in coverage during team drills.  
 Backup Kenny Pickett had some nice moments. He made an excellent sideline toss to running back Trevor Etienne with safety Isaiah Simmons closely guarding his inside shoulder. Pickett located the ball perfectly to Etienne, who snagged the ball roughly 25 yards down the field, with Simmons' right arm barely missing a pass breakup. 
 Third-string quarterback Kyle Trask , who was added Sunday, made an excellent sideline throw to training camp standout Ja'seem Reed in team drills. The wide receiver has been getting open with regularity and has become a favorite of the depth QBs. 
 Left guard Damien Lewis (calf) and defensive end Derrick Brown (knee soreness) worked off to the side with trainers. Brown has missed the past two practices, while Lewis has been sidelined for more than a week. 
 
 

 Legette suffers apparent stinger, avoids concussion 
Panthers wide receiver Xavier Legette suffered a "stinger" on a hard fall during Tuesday's practice, according to coach Dave Canales , who added that the third-year player does not have a concussion.
 Legette was trying to make a catch in the corner of the end zone when he came down hard on the back of his head. Trainers rushed to his side and Legette was later seen wiggling his fingers in the air in front of trainers before boarding a cart.

 It was the latest scare in what has been an injury-riddled start to training camp for the Panthers, who have already lost starting linebacker Nic Scourton and rookie wide receiver Chris Brazzell II for the season. Read more 

 
 

 Pickett to start Thursday's preseason game 
 Panthers quarterback Kenny Pickett will start Thursday night's Pro Football Hall of Fame Game against the Arizona Cardinals  ( 8 p.m. ET, NBC ), per ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter . Pickett, No. 2 on the depth chart behind  Bryce Young , will lead a Carolina team that doesn't plan to play any of its starters Thursday night, including rookie offensive tackle  Monroe Freeling .

 Panthers coach Dave Canales added Pickett, 28, to develop behind Young, the No. 1 pick of the 2023 draft. Pickett replaced 38-year-old Andy Dalton , who was traded in March to the Philadelphia Eagles for a 2027 seventh-round draft pick. -- ESPN Staff 

 
 Panthers VP says decision on Young deal 'collaborative' 
 The Panthers remain tight-lipped about the long-term contractual future of quarterback  Bryce Young  as he prepares to enter his fourth NFL season.

 Panthers executive vice president of football operations Brandt Tilis said Monday he felt Young "ascended" to a new level last season, while adding that the 25-year-old's ceiling is still "unknown."

 After being benched early in his second season, the No. 1 overall pick in 2023 responded by throwing for 3,011 yards with 23 touchdowns and 11 interceptions last year while going 8-8 as a starter and leading the Panthers to an NFC South championship. Read more 

 
 Fans show up for scrimmage; injuries cast a shadow 
The Panthers scrimmaged in front of approximately 40,000 fans at Bank of America Stadium on Friday night in their first appearance on their home turf since losing in the opening round of last season's playoffs. Injuries continue to be the story of the team's training…

title: Lakers' $12 billion purchase tops record U.S. sports team sales
summary: The Lakers have been sold for a staggering $12 billion fee. It's a North American sports franchise record. Here are others that sold for big money.
full_text:
Another American sports franchise has been sold for yet another record price.

 

 On Wednesday morning, news broke that Josh Kushner and Bob Iger had agreed to purchase majority ownership of the Los Angeles Lakers from Mark Walter for a staggering $12 billion, sources told ESPN's Ramona Shelburne . It's the largest sale of a professional sports franchise in the world. It's also the second time in recent memory the Lakers have broken that record -- Walter purchased them from the Buss family in June 2025 for $10 billion .

 This deal adds to a recent surge in franchise sale prices. Here's a list of some of the most expensive franchise purchases in U.S. sports:

 

 Los Angeles Lakers 
 Sale price: $12 billion 

 A little more than a year after their previous sale, the Lakers changed hands again, this time going from Mark Walter to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger. Kushner and Iger had made overtures toward an NBA franchise in Las Vegas, but made an unexpected pivot to buy the team from Walter for $2 billion more than he paid in 2025.

 

 Los Angeles Lakers 
 Sale price: $10 billion 

 Mark Walter, who previously owned a minority stake in the Lakers and has interests in the Los Angeles Dodgers , the WNBA's Los Angeles Sparks , the Billie Jean Cup, the Cadillac Formula 1 team and the Professional Women's Hockey League officially bought the team for a record $10 billion in October 2025 . The Buss family, who previously owned the team for 46 years, retained a minority stake in the franchise.

 

 Boston Celtics 
 Sale price: $6.1 billion 

 Bill Chisholm, managing partner at Symphony Technology Group agreed to purchase the Boston Celtics from the Grousbeck family for $6.1 billion in March 2025. It marked the largest sale of an American sports franchise at the time, surpassing the mark of $6.05 billion set by the Washington Commanders in 2023. The deal came within a year of the Celtics winning the 2024 championship.

 

 Washington Commanders 
 Sale price: $6.05 billion 

 

 This sale came after a period of turmoil and multiple investigations into former owner Dan Snyder, who was fined $60 million after attorney Mary Jo White released her findings. The new owners were a group led by Josh Harris , who -- along with David Blitzer as part of the Harris-Blitzer Sports Entertainment group -- also owns the Philadelphia 76ers and New Jersey Devils . The team finished the 2023 season with a 4-13 record but went 12-5 in 2024 after drafting quarterback  Jayden Daniels .

 

 Denver Broncos 
 Sale price: $4.65 billion 

 The Walton-Penner group's $4.65 billion purchase of the Broncos in 2022 was the record sale price for an NFL team by more than $2 billion before the sale of the Commanders. Previously, former Carolina Panthers owner Jerry Richardson had sold his franchise to billionaire David Tepper for $2.275 billion in 2018. 

 Rob Walton's net worth is $57.9 billion, according to Forbes . His cousin and another Walmart heir, Ann Walton, is the wife of Los Angeles Rams owner Stan Kroenke. Kroenke also owns three Colorado sports teams: the NBA's Denver Nuggets , NHL's Colorado Avalanche and MLS'  Colorado Rapids .

 

 Phoenix Suns and Mercury 
 Sale price: $4 billion 

 The combined sale, which received league approval in February, set a high-water mark for NBA franchises at the time by more than $1.5 billion compared to what the Brooklyn Nets sold for in 2019. New owner Matt Ishbia was a walk-on for Michigan State and part of the Spartans' 2000 national championship team.

 

 Dallas Mavericks 

 Sale price: $3.5 billion 

 One of the most visible owners in the league, Mark Cuban served as the majority owner of the Mavericks since 2000 before selling to the Adelson and Dumont families of the Las Vegas Sands casino in 2023.

 

 Charlotte Hornets 

 Sale price: $3 billion 

 After a 13-year run as owner, NBA legend Michael Jordan agreed to sell his majority stake in the Hornets in the summer of 2023. The buyers were a group led by Gabe Plotkin and Rick Schnall, the former having previously been a minority owner of Charlotte. 

 

 New York Mets 
 Sale price: $2.4 billion 

 

 The Mets had the honor of having the most expensive team sale in American sports until the Broncos came along. In 2020, hedge fund manager Steve Cohen purchased the Mets for $2.4 billion . The Los Angeles Dodgers previously held the mark for the most expensive MLB team sale when they sold for $2 billion in 2012.

 Cohen is the founder of Point 72 Asset Management and now-defunct SAC Capital Advisors.

 

 Brooklyn Nets 
 Sale price: $2.35 billion 

 In 2019, Alibaba co-founder Joe Tsai bought the Nets for $2.35 billion from Russian billionaire Mikhail Prokhorov. Tsai already had secured 49% ownership from Prokhorov in 2018 but accelerated the timeline for full ownership. Along with the then-record purchase for Brooklyn, Tsai also purchased Barclays Center, the Nets' home arena, in a separate transaction for roughly $1 billion.

 Brooklyn isn't the only New York-based sports team Tsai owns. He bought the WNBA's New York Liberty franchise in January 2019 .

 

 Carolina Panthers 
 Sale price: $2.275 billion 

 

 The Panthers became available for sale following the 2017 NFL season after sexual harassment and workplace misconduct accusations  were made against Richardson. Tepper, whose net worth is $16.7 billion according to Forbes , bought the team for $2.275 billion . Before taking over Carolina, Tepper had a 5% ownership stake in the Pittsburgh Steelers .

 The Appaloosa founder also spent $325 million in 2019 to bring MLS its 30th team, Charlotte FC .

 

 Houston Rockets 
 Sale price: $2.2 billion 

 Former Rockets owner Leslie Alexander sold the team to Texas native and billionaire Tilman Fertitta for $2.2 billion in 2019. Fertitta grew up in Galveston, Texas, and was a regular attendee at Houston's games before buying the franchise.

 According to his website , he is the sole owner of Fertitta Entertainment, which owns the restaurant giant Landry's, the Golden Nugget Casinos and Hotels and the Rockets. Fertitta also has his own TV show on CNBC called "Million Dollar Buyer."

The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Cleveland Browns  camp is taking place at the CrossCountry Mortgage Campus and Browns reporter Daniel Oyefusi has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Browns camp. We will update this file often. The biggest question for Cleveland remains who will be the starting QB? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Browns stories 
 
 What are the Browns looking for in their QB competition? 
 Jerry Jeudy clarifies viral video, says he talked to Browns QBs 
 AJ Epenesa grateful to be Eagle after 'weird' Browns situation 
 Deshaun Watson: Preseason is 'great opportunity' after injuries 
 Deion Sanders gives Browns 'insight' on Shedeur Sanders 
 GM Andrew Berry 'hopeful' Browns can reunite with Jadeveon Clowney 
 Sources: Browns, Grant Delpit agree to 3-year, $48M extension 
 
 
 Wednesday, Aug. 12 
 The Browns are hoping quarterback  Deshaun Watson 's return to health will mean a return to the Pro Bowl form he displayed with the Texans, but Watson said Wednesday that "my game has definitely changed."

 "I'm different, man," Watson said before practice. "I think ever since I've been here early on, bringing up Houston was cool, but I'm 30 now. I had some injuries and things like that. So, my game has definitely changed. But the mentality in how I play and how I approach it doesn't."

 Watson was one of the NFL's top dual-threat passers in Houston, but suspension and injuries have limited him to just 19 games since Cleveland traded for him in March 2022.

 "I think you have to be who you are because if you try to be something you're not, you're not going to play at the highest level of your skill set," coach Todd Monken said. "So it's just the way it is with him; he's going to have to play or utilize his athleticism in order to play at the top of his skill set. ... But one of the superpowers is his athleticism. I mean, that always has been. So you can't take that away or you've basically taken away a part of what made him special."

 More observations: 

 
 In a lighter practice ahead of the team's preseason opener against the Bears, Watson and Shedeur Sanders led successful two-minute drills to cap the session. Both quarterbacks connected on deep passes during their possession. Sanders had a deep completion to wide receiver Isaiah Bond , who made a diving catch. Watson lofted a pass to receiver Luke Floriea along the offense's sideline. 
 Teven Jenkins and Tyre Phillips split snaps at right guard with the No. 1 offense. 
 Cornerback Denzel Ward and offensive tackle Izavion Miller returned to practice. Cornerback Tyron Herring left practice with a member of the team's medical staff during individual drills. 
 Fifteen players did not practice: Joe Royer , Cedric Tillman (new absence), D'Angelo Ross , Myles Bryant , Michael Burton , Carson Schwesinger , Mike Hall, Parker Brailsford , Elijah Chatman , Zak Zinter , Elgton Jenkins , Dae'Quan Wright , Jack Stoll , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis . Veteran edge rusher Tyus Bowser had a tryout with the Browns on Wednesday, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. 
 
 
 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Four days before their preseason opener against the Chicago Bears on Saturday, the Browns listed " Deshaun Watson  OR Shedeur Sanders " at starting quarterback in their first unofficial depth chart.

 Coach Todd Monken has yet to announce which quarterback will start in Chicago, but spoke about the value the preseason adds for evaluating the two passers.

 "It does, in terms of getting the ball out, got to learn to get the ball out. Got to learn how to slide," Monken said. "You're not going to be able to just run around. I do want playmaking ability, so there is a balance there between playmaking ability and taking some sacks. You're going to have to live with that to an extent.

 "The other part is stacking plays, where it matters, because they got the scoreboard on in terms of points you put on the board. In terms of the flow of the game, that's a big part of it. We're going to be on the road. The ebbs and flows of positive plays and negative plays, overcoming that. I think there's a part of the quarterback's body language, how they are around the team. Do I sense, 'Hey, that's over. I've moved on to the next play.' So there's a number of things you get to evaluate once you get to the closest we have in terms of games, which is preseason."

 With rookie Spencer Fano securing a starting role at left tackle, Monken said the only starting position on the offensive line up in the air is right guard. Teven Jenkins and KT Leveston have been rotating at the spot.

 "I think Teven has the advantage there from experience," Monken said.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Special teams coordinator Byron Storer said the team is "definitely taking a hard look at" punters Wes Pahl and Nik Constantinou , but "It's Corey [Bojorquez]'s job to lose." 
 Monken said he is "hopeful" that defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr . will return to practice "soon." Hall hasn't practiced since Aug. 3. 
 On the second-team offensive line, the Browns moved Dawand Jones from left tackle to right tackle and rookie Austin Barber from right tackle to left tackle. 
 Cornerback Damarri Mathis left practice on the back of a cart after he sustained an injury in coverage during a 1-on-1 drill. The team later placed Mathis on injured reserve. 
 Defensive tackle Travis Bell left practice early with a member of the team's medical staff. 
 Fifteen players did not practice Tuesday: Joe Royer ,  D'Angelo Ross , Denzel Ward (new absence), Myles Bryant , Michael Burton , Carson Schwesinger ,  Mike Hall Jr ., Parker Brailsford , Izavion Miller , Elijah Chatman , Zak Zinter , Jack Stoll , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis , Maliek Collins . 
 The Browns claimed tight end Dae'Quan Wright off waivers from the Eagles, per the NFL transaction wire. 
 The Browns had three tight ends in for a tryout today, per the NFL transaction wire: Sal Cannella , Matt Lauter and  Jermaine Terry II . 
 

 

 

 
 Monday, Aug. 10 
 Coach Todd Monken explained the change in the quarterback rotation last Saturday.

 Though Monken said before the practice that Shedeur Sanders would get a "majority" of first-team reps, he said he was later informed that Sanders had received more padded practices with the starters than Watson in the week. So Monken changed the order of reps.

 Sanders practiced with the starting offense Monday, while Watson led the No. 2 offense.

 "As long as we're still sharing reps, it's a competition," Monken said.

 Monken also said he has not decided which quarterback will start the preseason opener in Chicago on Saturday, but he intends to start Watson in one of the first two preseason games and Sanders in the other.

 "I'd like to get our starters out there for the first series together [in the preseason opener]," Monken said.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Both Watson and Sanders threw short touchdowns during red zone 11-on-11 team drills, but it was overall a mistake-filled practice for the offense. Monken ended a two-minute drill for the No. 1 offense after three consecutive pre-snap penalties. The head coach then called it a day after back-to-back pre-snap infractions for the No. 2 offense. 
 Monken made two notable non-quarterback personnel changes, as rookie left tackle Spencer Fano and rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston practiced with the first-team offense. Fano had been alternating days at starting left tackle with Dawand Jones . Monken…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Denver Broncos camp is taking place in Englewood, Colorado, and Broncos reporter Jeff Legwold has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Broncos camp. We will update this file often as we track the Broncos' push toward getting to the Super Bowl after falling one game short last season. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Broncos camp 
 
 Broncos opting to sit QB Bo Nix for preseason opener 
 Why 2026 is a crucial season for Nix and the Broncos 
 Payton to talk to Taysom Hill about interest in Broncos 
 Nix won't be afraid to run on repaired ankle 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 
 Since Bo Nix will not play in Friday's preseason opener in Atlanta, there will be a chance for Jarrett Stidham and Sam Ehlinger to continue what has been one of the most spirited position battles of camp. On a team that returns 20 of 22 starters on offense and defense from the AFC Championship Game and returns most of the backups, too, Stidham and Ehlinger have had a heated battle to be the No. 2 quarterback. And Friday might be their best chance to show what they can do given Nix is expected to play some snaps in the Broncos' two other preseason games.

 Coach Sean Payton said after Wednesday's practice that each of the quarterbacks will play a half against the Falcons. Stidham is expected to start the game and play the first half.

 "They're focused on like their best stuff, they're competing against the 31 other quarterbacks (in the league) like any other position," Payton said. "... It's a great room, they get along well."

 Ehlinger, who led the team with 412 yards passing last preseason, has been consistently lauded by Payton for his work in camp and has routinely moved the second- and third-team offenses in practices. Stidham led the quarterbacks in touchdown passes last preseason, with four in three games.

 More observations: 

 
 Payton expects most of the healthy starters to get about 15 plays against the Falcons and said some of the injured players will remain back in Denver to continue to rehab their injuries. Wide receivers Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims Jr ., who are both working back from leg injuries in camp, are expected to be among the group that remains in Denver. 
 When asked why he, unlike many other coaches, will likely have several starters play in all three preseason games, Payton said: "[You're] trying to win everything, I just believe in that." 
 Veteran center Michael Deiter , who was carted off the field during Tuesday's practice, will miss the remainder of the season with a thigh injury that will require surgery. "[I] feel bad for him and where he's at," Payton said. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Broncos owner/CEO Greg Penner, who had not spoken publicly since the league meetings in March, covered a variety of topics with local media on Tuesday. At one point he was asked about his expectations for the season, and he made it clear a team that returns all but two starters from the AFC Championship Game has the same expectations from him as the next year's team and the ones that come after that.

 "Our goal is to compete for championships every year and if we put ourselves in that position every year, we're going to be successful and win Super Bowls," he said.

 He also talked about the new five-year deal for coach Sean Payton that Payton signed in June, saying: "I've been really pleased with what he's built here, the culture, the performance on the field (and) it enabled us to line up he and [general manager] George [Paton's] contracts now. George has done a fantastic job building this roster."

 More observations: 

 
 Center is suddenly a trouble spot, as injuries continue to happen at the position. The Broncos' top two centers -- Luke Wattenberg and Alex Forsyth -- have missed time in camp and on Tuesday Michael Deiter -- who was signed for depth in the offseason after spending seven seasons in Miami, Houston and Washington -- was carted to the locker room. Calvin Throckmorton slid in as the first-team center, with undrafted rookie free agent Gavin Ortega providing depth. All-Pro guard Quinn Meinerz played some center early in his NFL career and could shift over if needed, but moving one of the NFL's best guards to another position is not ideal. 
 Sam Ehlinger continues to flash in his quest for the No. 2 quarterback job. He has consistently moved the offense in team drills during camp, and his throw to undrafted rookie wide receiver Kolbe Katsis for a touchdown in situational red zone work with the third-team offense was one of the best plays of the day. 
 Running back J.K. Dobbins , who left Monday's practice with what Sean Payton referred to as a soft tissue injury, returned to practice Tuesday. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 A recent spate of what Sean Payton called "soft-tissue" injuries prompted the coach to adjust the end of practice. After the two-and-half-hour workout, Payton had the strength and conditioning staff add a longer, more formal warm-down period. Payton said he expected to continue to have the players go through the longer warm down in the days ahead.

 

 "Got to get a handle on some of the soft-tissue stuff. ... Strains, hamstring or groins, [we] continue to fight through that," Payton said. "I don't think it's heat related. ... You always try to look at your pre-practice routine, your hydration obviously."

 Running back J.K. Dobbins left the practice field with an injury and did not return. Wide receivers Marvin Mims Jr . -- who returned to practice Monday -- and Jaylen Waddle have also had similar injuries in recent weeks.

 More observations: 

 
 Payton said he will play most, if not all, of the healthy starters for at least some snaps in Friday's preseason opener in Atlanta. Payton said the coaches hadn't yet formalized the snap counts yet, but that he wanted regulars to get at least some work. "You have to build callouses," he said. 
 Quarterback Bo Nix hopes first-year offensive coordinator Davis Webb will be on the sideline during games to call plays instead of in the coaches' box. Payton said Monday he and Webb hadn't yet discussed the gameday setup yet, but that he expected Webb to call plays from the sideline. "I always loved quarterback-to-playcaller when they're on the sideline with me," Nix said. "You get the feel of the game a little differently. ... They get to feel the emotions of a game on the sideline. ... I like when the playcaller is right there, and when I come off I can have that eye-to-eye conversation." 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 When the Broncos went through a scripted scrimmage, it was safety Brandon Jones who was 3-of-4 in field goal attempts.

 Why? Broncos special teams coach Darren Rizzi said most of the Australian punters he has worked with in his long coaching career, including the Broncos' Jeremy Crawshaw , have not kicked field goals.

 So the Broncos need a contingency plan in case  Wil Lutz gets injured in a game. And with Lutz and several Broncos coaches, including Sean Payton, in Canton, Ohio, to see Drew Brees be enshrined into the Hall of Fame, it was Jones getting the kicks.

 Rizzi said Jones' longest made field goal was 39 yards, but Jones said he made a 50-yarder in OTAs. At one point, as Jones moved into position before the snap, the crowd of several thousand people chanted his name.
