title: Future of QB Bo Nix, Broncos will be defined by 2026 season
summary: Nix has been a winner for the Broncos in his two NFL seasons, but is he truly their next alpha franchise QB? This season could give us the answer.
full_text:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- Sometimes when Denver Broncos coach Sean Payton begins to answer a question, his mind is already on things yet to come. There have been a few moments in training camp when he has mentioned the work to be done by quarterback Bo Nix in his "fourth year."

 Payton certainly knows Nix is actually in his third NFL season, but the accidental bobble fits since folks have been in a hurry to assess the 26-year-old quarterback from the moment the Broncos selected him  with the No. 12 pick of the 2024 draft.

 Nix has been on the fast track since arriving in Denver. He was named the team's starter during his first NFL preseason and immediately found himself with the immense expectations that come from quarterbacking a franchise that has won three Super Bowls and been led by the likes of Hall of Famers John Elway and Peyton Manning.

 And as Payton has often said about Nix, "I'm glad he's on our team. ... I like where he's headed."

 

 But the clock is ticking for Nix and the Broncos, who have a 25-11 record (including postseason) in two seasons with him as the starter. They enter the third season of Nix's financially friendly rookie contract on a quest to win the franchise its fourth Super Bowl title. But that's not all that's on the line.

 The Broncos need to decide whether Nix is truly Denver's next franchise quarterback -- and if he's worthy of a big-money, long-term contract that will significantly alter the team's roster and salary cap situation. They have to juggle Nix's ability to win games and play at his highest level in the clutch with a growing list of ankle injuries and some red-flag moments in his play.

 For his part, Nix has remained calm, focused and quietly driven to make a giant step in where he wants his career to go this season.

 "Year 1, I'm trying to just not mess up for the team," Nix said. "I feel like Year 3, I'm trying to make plays for the team. It's just quite the different feeling. It's just a confidence-level thing."

 
 THE BRONCOS HAVE won 69.4% of their games with Nix as their starting quarterback. They have made playoff trips in his two seasons as a starter (after missing the postseason the previous eight seasons) and are the defending AFC West champions . And the Broncos went 14-3 last season, including an NFL-record 12 comeback wins and an 11-2 record in one-score games.

 Yes, the defense is elite. But Nix has done his part. He is only the third quarterback in league history to throw for at least 3,500 passing yards and 25 touchdown passes in his first two seasons (Manning and the Los Angeles Chargers ' Justin Herbert are the others). Nix has the most team wins, passing touchdowns, rushing touchdowns and total touchdowns among the six first-round quarterbacks selected in 2024, besting the likes of Caleb Williams , Drake Maye and Jayden Daniels . His QBR in the red zone last season also was fourth best in the league (82.6), and he led the NFL in winning drives (seven).

 He also embodies one of Payton's foundational principles in quarterback play: don't take sacks. Though Nix led the league in pass attempts (612) and dropbacks (667) last season, he was sacked the ninth-fewest times among the league's starters. And much of his late-game success is derived from his ability to move out of trouble and get a play to what Payton calls "the second act."

 "It's one of his superpowers," Payton said. "It's hard to sack some quarterbacks; he's one of them. That was something you saw on college tape. In our league when you take a sack, you just do the analytics on what your points become in that drive ... and it all drops dramatically."

 

 His ability to extend plays, his leadership style, day-to-day demeanor and overall approach to the job are among the first things his teammates list when asked why they believe Nix is "The Guy."

 "Bo just walks in the room like he's ready for anything," running back J.K. Dobbins said. "And he is. He ain't trying to walk like that, you know what I mean? That's just that thing about him. You're never going to feel you're out of it with Bo. People can say whatever they want about Bo, about this and that, but Bo's our guy. We all know it."

 How the Broncos built their roster shows how much their decision-makers agree with Dobbins. Since Nix was drafted, the Broncos have spent more than $300 million in guaranteed-at-signing money to secure standouts such as defensive tackle  Zach Allen , guard  Quinn Meinerz , edge rusher Nik Bonitto , wide receiver  Courtland Sutton , cornerback  Pat Surtain II and offensive tackle  Garett Bolles to long-term extensions. They're returning 20 of 22 offensive and defensive starters from last season's AFC Championship Game , and they re-signed 17 of 21 players who were scheduled to be unrestricted, restricted or exclusive rights free agents. And when their internal reviews revealed a need in their passing game, they sent first-, third- and fourth-round picks to the Miami Dolphins in March to acquire wide receiver Jaylen Waddle .

 All of these moves were made to build the kind of depth chart around Nix "that can help a quarterback develop," as Payton has said.

 "The 'next step' is kind of cliché," the coach added when asked of Nix's progression. "He just finished winning 14 games and having a really good season. Do I think he's going to continue to improve? ... I think there are certain areas for us offensively that can help with the quarterback, a consistent run game throughout the year. There are some things that we can do to help him."

 
 THE BRONCOS SPENT what first-year offensive coordinator Davis Webb called "some long hours in the offseason" going through each Nix game of the past two seasons to evaluate what he has done well as a starter and the areas where progress needs to be made.

 Though Payton has consistently praised his QB's decision-making, processing and ability to avoid sacks and turnovers, Nix hasn't been particularly accurate, especially on downfield throws. He also resides near the middle of the pack among the league's starting quarterbacks in explosive pass plays.

 "We were really trying to evaluate ... the last two years, how his first read on plays marries up the second read, depth-wise, playcall-wise, where we are at that point in the game,'' Webb said. "... It's noticeable the strides he's making, hanging on [the first read], getting to two, to three."

 Nix was 26th in the league in completion percentage over expectation (minus-2.1%) last season, per NFL Next Gen Stats, and he was 12th in the league in completions of 20 or more yards (47 -- 25 behind league-leader Matthew Stafford 's 72). Nix also completed 44.1% of his pass attempts of 10 or more air yards, along with 36.1% of attempts for 20 or more air yards.

 

 Defensive coaches in the league have found other areas to exploit. Some who have faced Nix over the past two years say they want to present looks that force him to look toward the middle of the field, an area he hasn't shown comfort attacking.

 When his 2026 pass chart is fully separated into sections of the field, his lowest attempt totals come between the hashmarks (40 attempts). His highest volume comes outside the numbers (234 attempts).

 "We'll do that a lot in the spring self-scout," Payton said. "Then we'll look at -- 'All right, what are the things that maybe we need to be better at?' But yes, we'll look at hit charts, we'll look at the analytics."

 There are also questions about Nix's long-term health . He has shown exceptional durability so far, given that he started a then-record 61 college games in five seasons at Auburn and Oregon. He has sat out only one game as an NFL starter -- last season's AFC Championship Game.

 So by any definition, Nix has been reliable. But the fractured right ankle sustained in the Broncos' divisional round win over the Buffalo Bills means Nix has sustained ankle fractures in high school, college and the NFL. He has had three ankle surgeries in his two…

title: Is rookie Brandon Cisse a lock to start at CB for Packers?
summary: Keisean Nixon entered camp as the presumptive starter on the left side, but second-rounder Brandon Cisse has shined.
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- When training camp opened, there appeared to be one cornerback spot settled.  Keisean Nixon , who started every game last season and was one of three Green Bay Packers to play more than 1,000 snaps on defense, had the left side spot locked down.

 That would leave three players to fight for the right cornerback spot: returning starter Carrington Valentine , veteran free agent Benjamin St-Juste and rookie second-round pick Brandon Cisse .

 Two weeks into camp, everything about the cornerback position appears to have flipped.

 

 Going into Thursday's preseason opener at the Pittsburgh Steelers ( 7 p.m. ET, NFL Network ), Cisse looks like he has the inside track to a starting spot and Nixon might be in a fight for the other. Cisse has been a regular with the defensive starters at right cornerback ever since Valentine dropped out of practice because of a hamstring injury Aug. 2.

 It's both a validation of what the Packers thought they had when they used their top draft pick (No. 52 overall) on Cisse and a question about whether they need to upgrade from Nixon, who despite leading the NFL with 15 pass breakups also led all defensive backs in penalties (13, including those accepted and declined), according to ESPN Research.

 

 "Everything's a competition right now," coach Matt LaFleur said of the cornerbacks. "So we're going to put different guys in different situations in different spots and see how they respond."

 Day after day, Cisse has gone up against the Packers' top receivers and held his own. In one practice this week, Cisse broke up a pass intended for receiver  Christian Watson on the sideline but also gave up a completion to Watson. It's all part of the learning process for the rookie.

 "I think it's helped me tremendously to go against somebody that talented every day," Cisse said. "It helps that his locker is right next to mine, being able to pick his brain and him being able to pick my brain on certain techniques that he may see.

 "Every day just trying to make sure you go against somebody like that is going to make you a lot better. I'm going to be able to challenge him because he wants to be the best and I want to be the best. That's kind of what I strive for is to try and learn from him and continue to grow and try to take on that matchup. He's somebody I look up to in ways. He's been great to me ever since I got here."

 

 Cisse claims he'd be lying if he said he expected to start on opening day against the Minnesota Vikings .

 "I didn't think like that," he said.

 He might be too humble to do so.

 "My job as a rookie is just to sit back and learn," Cisse said. "I understand my role. I just try to be a professional about my business every day and just try to come in and be a pro, work out my daily habits, and just soak up as much information from everybody around me. Because those guys have been in the fire and I'm still a young guy who needs to learn every day. So I just trying to be a sponge."

 One of those guys he has tried to learn from is safety Javon Bullard .

 Bullard, who was also a second-round pick, quickly worked his way into a starting role as a rookie two years ago.

 "I think what really makes him special is just his willingness to learn from people, different coaches, different teammates," Bullard said. "He's really a sponge. I think it's crucial for a young player to come in and learn because you learn with experience. He's a great football player nonetheless, but that experience matters in this league. And I think he's coming in here and just being a sponge, soaking up that knowledge from any and everybody, and I think he's going to be special. He's going to make a lot of plays for us for sure."

 

 If there was a picture in the dictionary next to "ideal teammate," Cisse's headshot might be there.

 "He is an A-plus human and he loves football," LaFleur said. "I think every time he goes out there there's a lot of good things, and then there's a lot of teachable moments. But I think he's a guy that the sky's the limit for him."

 As for a potential cornerback pairing of Cisse and Nixon, that's still to be determined. For two days of practice this week, Nixon appeared to be facing a demotion. He took reps with the second- and third-string defensive units. But in the final practice in advance of the preseason opener, Nixon was back with the first group.

 Still, it's not off the table that if the Packers decide Nixon isn't a starter, they might want to move on. Nixon has expressed a desire to be paid like a No. 1 cornerback, but the Packers haven't budged. He's in the final year of a contract that will pay him $5 million this season, which is on the low end for a veteran starter at his position.

 St-Juste, who signed a two-year, $10 million contract in March, also has been impressive and could find his way into a significant role with or without Nixon around.

 But for now, it appears the most settled thing about the cornerback spot is Cisse.

 "Obviously we took him where we took him," new defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon said. "He's got the skill set that we're looking for, and he's doing a good job of when he makes a mistake -- mistakes are going to happen, especially for young guys in a new scheme, this a new scheme for him as it is all our guys -- mistakes are OK, just don't make it the same mistake again."

title: 2026 Green Bay Packers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Packers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Green Bay Packers ' camp is taking place in Green Bay, Wisconsin, and Packers reporter Rob Demovsky has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Packers camp. We will update this file often. Will the revamped WR corps help QB Jordan Love and the offense take another step? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Thursday.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news out of Packers camp 
 
 Aaron Rodgers wishes game at Lambeau, discusses retirement return 
 Packers QB Love expected to play in first preseason game 
 Micah Parsons: Playing vs. Cowboys in Week 6 'realistic' 
 Packers RT changes last name to Bako-Bewele to honor heritage 
 Packers star TE Tucker Kraft activated off PUP after ACL recovery 
 Packers CEO: Team needs financial bump to stay competitive 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 Three weeks and 11 practices into training camp, and something's missing: fighting.

 
There hasn't even been so much as a scuffle or shoving match.

 
This is training camp No. 7 for veteran safety Xavier McKinney and when asked if this is the deepest into training camp he has ever gone without seeing a fight, McKinney didn't hesitate.

 
"Hell yeah," he said. "For sure."

 
But McKinney doesn't think that's a bad thing. Nor is it a sign that the players are not competitive enough.

 
"I think we're past that, to be honest," McKinney said. "I think we have a bigger goal, and that bigger goal is to get over this hump that we've been kind of dealing with these last couple years. We're not focused on fighting. Nobody's trying to get kicked out of practice. Nobody's trying to have practice stop early. We're just trying to focus on our technique. We're trying to find ways where we can improve as individuals. We want to be the best group that we can possibly be. We want to be better than what we were last year."

 
The Packers also haven't had a joint practice yet. So even McKinney said all bets are off when the Cardinals come to town for a practice Aug. 26.

 
"That always happens," McKinney said.

 Other observations: 

 
 Just when it looked like the injury list would keep getting longer, a few key players returned to practice. Receivers Matthew Golden (toe) and Jayden Reed (ankle) were back after missing two practices. So was tight end Josh Whyle (neck). All took part in team (11-on-11) periods. Cornerback Carrington Valentine , who dropped out of practice Aug. 2 because of a hamstring injury, returned for individual drills only. The only new addition to the DNP list was rookie edge Dani Dennis-Sutton , but it was because of an illness. 
 The Packers had a pair of new defensive backs on the field after signing Trey Dean III and Travion Fluellen . They both worked with the safeties during individual drills. Safety Javon Bullard (foot) remained out. 
 After taking reps with both the second- and third-string defenses Monday, Keisean Nixon was back at his regular left cornerback spot with the No. 1 defense. In fact, he worked exclusively with that group and appeared to be on the field for every snap that the starters took. Brandon Cisse continued to work as the No. 1 right cornerback. 
 Trey Smack went 4-for-5 during a field goal period. His miss was wide right on a 45-yarder. He hit the right upright on a 41-yarder but it still went through. He's now 20-for-28 (71.4%) during camp. 
 A day after the NFL said it will allow head coaches to designate a member of their sideline staff to initiate replay challenges , coach Matt LaFleur said he doesn't plan to pass off the red challenge flag. "I probably should give it up based on past actions," LaFleur joked. "So no, I'll probably hold the challenge flag." 
 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 

 It was the kind of practice that would have excited a young, backup quarterback.

 But what about a 37-year-old going into his 16th NFL season?

 
"Oh yeah, the game still excites me," Tyrod Taylor said.

 
In what was perhaps Taylor's best practice since he signed with the Packers this offseason, he completed passes of all varieties. There was a deep post to Kisean Johnson . A quick-hitting slant to Will Sheppard for a first down. A 20-yarder to Sheppard down the left sideline. A big gain over the middle to J. Michael Sturdivant .

 
It didn't matter to Taylor that it was all with backup receivers -- many of whom might not make the team.

 
"There's a healthy rotation of guys that's going in and out with the group that I'm running with, and it's just up to me to communicate, get them in the right position but also give them a chance to make plays," Taylor said. "We've got a ton of playmakers at our skill positions."

 
The Packers had one of the best backup quarterbacks in the NFL last season with Malik Willis , who signed with the Dolphins as a free agent. Now, they have one of the most experienced.

 "I'm a firm believer that your actions speak louder than your words, especially early on," said Taylor, who has played in 100 career games (with 62 starts) for seven teams. "It's about me coming in, being myself, preparing on the field, off the field, being ready for the opportunities and taking advantage of them as well, and then gradually growing into more of a vocal leader and speaking on things when they fit."

 Other observations: 

 
 As if it weren't unusual enough to see cornerback Keisean Nixon with the second-string defense Sunday, it was even more surprising to see him taking snaps with the third-stringers Monday. In the very next period, he was back with the No. 1 defense, but it's a baffling way to handle a player who last season was considered the team's No. 1 cornerback. When Nixon wasn't with the starters, Benjamin St-Juste was in his spot along with rookie Brandon Cisse on the other side. Could it be a sign the Packers are thinking about demoting Nixon? "There's always competition," coach Matt LaFleur said. "All these guys got to be prepared for that. As far as the substitution, that's not something that I'm always micromanaging. A lot of that's on the position coach." 
 Though starting linebackers Edgerrin Cooper (foot) and Zaire Franklin (rest) returned to practice, the offense was still without two of its top receivers, Matthew Golden (toe) and Jayden Reed (ankle). Without running back Josh Jacobs (groin) and with tight end  Tucker Kraft (knee) not yet doing 11-on-11 periods, the primary skill position players with the No. 1 offense were MarShawn Lloyd at running back; Christian Watson , Bo Melton , Skyy Moore , Savion Williams and Isaiah Neyor at receiver; and  Messiah Swinson and Drake Dabney at tight end. 
 Add safety Javon Bullard to the injury list. He had a walking boot on his right foot during practice but said afterward that the issue was just a bruise that won't impact his availability for the start of the season. Kitan Oladapo played in Bullard's usual spot in the slot in the nickel package. 
 Two of the biggest plays of the day came from players fighting to make the roster. Cornerback Jaylin Simpson ended practice with a goal-line interception off undrafted rookie quarterback Kyron Drones . Meanwhile, Melton came down with a true 50-50 ball on a deep throw from Jordan Love . It looked like Nixon might have been in position to break it up or even intercept it before Melton came back for the ball and snagged it. "I just wanted it to be like a 80/20 or 100/0," Melton said. "My ball or nobody's." 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 
 If the Packers were looking for someone to emerge behind their top three…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action.  Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 Although he wasn't selected in the NFL draft, Chiefs rookie right tackle Kahlil Benson was confident he'd be able to compete for a roster spot. Benson, however, has impressed the Chiefs enough so far into their training camp that he has a chance to win a starting spot on the offensive line. Benson will get his opportunity to make a strong first impression Saturday when the Chiefs host the Los Angeles Rams for their preseason opener.

 "Honestly, I kept my head down and knew my time was going to come," Benson said after Wednesday's practice. "I really just stayed humbled, stayed faithful and just kept praying to God that I was ready to be on-call when it was that time."

 Against the Rams, Benson is expected to play two positions in the first half: right tackle and right guard. This week, Benson has taken all his reps at right guard since starter Trey Smith has been out with a hip injury. When the second-team offense enters the game, Benson is expected to slide to the right tackle spot. Showing quality versatility could be a factor in Benson winning the right tackle role over five-year veteran Jaylon Moore .

 "I don't really feel like it's a challenge," Benson said of switching positions. "You've got to be able to adjust when it's time and your number is being called. You just never know what could happen."

 More conversations: 

 
 Three players left the field before Wednesday's practice ended. The Chiefs said linebacker Nick Bolton left with an illness, tight end Jared Wiley sustained a strained hamstring and rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods had an ankle injury that occurred late in a team period. 
 The players who missed Wednesday's practice were Smith (hip), cornerback  L'Jarius Sneed  (rest), linebacker Drue Tranquill (lower back spasms) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee). 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 One player fans should be interested to see in Saturday's preseason opener against the Los Angeles Rams is receiver Andrew Armstrong .

 A second-year player who was cut last year by the Miami Dolphins , Armstrong joined the Chiefs in January and has been impressive throughout training camp. When fellow receivers Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy were out last week, Armstrong had several highlights with quarterback Patrick Mahomes and the rest of the first-team offense.

 "I've been out there being the best I can be and learning," Armstrong said after Tuesday's practice. "One of the main goals is being trustworthy for the quarterback. I'm trying to build that with [Mahomes].

 "This has been my favorite team since I was a little kid. I really wanted to be around a serious environment and this is an extremely serious environment. I love that."

 Armstrong is in a tight competition with second-year player Jalen Royals for the sixth and potential final receiver spot on the initial 53-man roster. If Armstrong performs well against the Rams, he could gain a sizable lead in the battle.

 "Oh, it's going to feel great, just looking and seeing all the red," Armstrong said of playing inside Arrowhead Stadium. "It's different playing on a [video] game than in real life. I know it's going to feel amazing."

 More observations: 

 
 The players who missed Tuesday's practice were right guard Trey Smith (hip), cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (rest), linebacker Drue Tranquill (lower back spasms) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee). 
 Before Tuesday's practice, the Chiefs agreed to sign defensive end Emmanuel Ogbah to a one-year deal. A 10-year veteran, Ogbah was with the Chiefs in 2019, the year the team won the Super Bowl. "I always had an affection for E," defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo said. "I've always periodically been in touch with him. If he's part of our group, I'll be excited about that." 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 With just seven practices left in training camp, Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes appears to be close to having his full complement of receivers on the field. For the first time in camp, Monday's on-field work featured Mahomes' top four receivers -- Rashee Rice , Xavier Worthy , Tyquan Thornton and rookie Cyrus Allen .

 Worthy, who missed last week's practices with a sprained right shoulder, was the lone receiver who didn't participate in the 7-on-7 and 11-on-11 reps. He could be a full participant later this week ahead of the preseason opener Saturday against the Los Angeles Rams .

 In the 7-on-7 period inside the red zone, Allen showed his ability to improvise in the middle of one play to get behind linebacker Nick Bolton for an 11-yard touchdown. A few minutes later, Rice caught a 6-yard touchdown pass in the back of the end zone against tight coverage from Nohl Williams .

 Mahomes had several reps with his top three receivers being Rice, Thornton and Allen alongside tight end Travis Kelce and running back  Kenneth Walker III .

 More observations: 

 
 The players who missed practice were right guard Trey Smith (hip), cornerback  L'Jarius Sneed  (rest), linebacker Drue Tranquill (lower-back spasms) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee). 
 For the first time in camp, rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane was in pads and cleared to participate in 7-on-7 periods, although he was still wearing a noncontact yellow jersey for the shoulder injury he sustained in May that forced him to miss the mandatory minicamp in June. In Monday's practice, Delane had two quality reps, where he covered Kelce and the other against Thornton inside the red zone. "He did a nice job with that," Reid said of Delane. 
 For the third straight practice, Kahlil Benson , the undrafted rookie from Indiana, had his reps at right guard in place of Smith. Jaylon Moore , the five-year veteran, played at right tackle with the first-team offense. "I think it's good for him to have some flexibility to do both [positions]," Reid said of Benson, who began camp at right tackle. "We worked him a little bit in there in OTAs and liked what we saw. This gives him real competition in there now where [defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo] is throwing a lot of different things at you, so you have to be able to adjust. It'll do nothing but help him, even at the tackle spot once he jumps back there." 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 More than halfway through camp, the Chiefs finally had a practice where multiple players had physical altercations. Coach Andy Reid doesn't want his players to fight, but he designs the Chiefs' camp to push the players, both physically and mentally.

title: Jonas Brothers to perform at NFL's first regular-season game in Australia
summary: The Jonas Brothers will be part of the entertainment lineup for the NFL's first regular-season game in Australia.
full_text:
MELBOURNE, Australia -- The Jonas Brothers will perform at halftime of the NFL's Week 1 game between the San Francisco 49ers and the Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in Australia.

 

 The NFL announced the headliners for the halftime show Wednesday. The game will air on Netflix in the U.S. on Sept. 10. The Jonas Brothers will be part of the entertainment lineup for the league's international schedule this season, which includes games in seven countries and on four continents.

 "We couldn't be more excited to perform at halftime during the NFL's first-ever regular-season game in Australia," the Jonas Brothers said in a statement. "Playing at the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground in front of such passionate Australian fans is an incredible honor."

 

 The Jonas Brothers -- Nick, Joe and Kevin -- have sold more than 20 million albums and recently landed a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

 Tim Tubito, the NFL's senior director of global game presentation and entertainment, said the league's first regular-season game in Australia is a landmark for the NFL.

 "The Jonas Brothers are global entertainers whose music connects across generations, making them the ideal artists to help us celebrate this historic game in Melbourne," Tubito said. "We look forward to delivering a memorable halftime performance for our fans in Australia and those watching around the world."

summary: Follow our daily updates from Vikings training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Minnesota Vikings ' camp is taking place in Eagan, Minnesota, and Vikings reporter Kevin Seifert has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Vikings camp. We will update this file often. Who will win the starting quarterback battle between incumbent J.J. McCarthy and free agent addition Kyler Murray ? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Thursday.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Vikings stories 

 
 What Kyler Murray as QB1 means for Vikings, J.J. McCarthy 
 Vikings, O'Neill reach $96M extension 
 Top Vikings storylines after minicamp, from QBs to new GM 
 Will Vikings start Caleb Banks, other rookies on defense? 
 Jefferson says decision on Vikings starting QB 'coach's call' 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 While the world has been focused on the Vikings' quarterback competition, another part of their offense has been more quietly under development. 
Coaches are in the process of tweaking the team's run game to give it more variety and, they hope, more production. Once pads came on at the start of the second week of training camp, Vikings running backs have ripped through the line of scrimmage on a regular basis, especially via outside zone concepts. 
"We're running the football very, very well against a really good defense right now," coach Kevin O'Connell said this week. 
On one play Wednesday, running back Jordan Mason followed a block from right tackle Brian O'Neill to reach the sideline and sprint for a touchdown. As Mason was running, O'Neill, right guard Joe Huber and center Blake Brandel sprinted after him in celebration.

 Other observations:

 
 Right guard Will Fries again sat out practice, with Huber taking his place with the first team. 
 Rookie safety Jakobe Thomas participated in individual drills, but his absence from team drills continued. 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 After his first public practice with the Vikings this spring, Kyler Murray uttered a four-word phrase that hovered over the team's quarterback competition all summer.

 "My confidence," Murray said in May, "is unshakeable."

 That helps explain why Murray didn't sound much different Tuesday after coach Kevin O'Connell named him the team's starter as the third week of training camp began. Murray said he did not expect to be handed the job and acknowledged that not every practice this summer has gone smoothly as he split reps with J.J. McCarthy .

 "There's going to be good days," Murray said. "There's going to be bad days. We're facing adversity every single day. But I'm definitely getting more comfortable as each day goes."

 Murray had a sharp practice Tuesday while taking all of the first-team reps for the first time since Week 5 of last season when he was with the Arizona Cardinals . McCarthy said he would address the decision publicly Wednesday.

 More observations:  

 
 Right guard Will Fries did not practice Tuesday. He was replaced on the first team by second-year guard Joe Huber . 
 

 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 

 As the third week of training camp began in the evening, Minnesota Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell was not ready to name a winner in the QB1 competition between Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy .

 "Nothing has really changed from a standpoint of the timeline and things like that," O'Connell said before the Vikings took the field at TCO Stadium for their annual night practice. "So we'll see how the reps continue to go and when we feel like we're at that place, we're going to make sure we communicate that both in house and internally and obviously to you guys as soon as possible."

 The Vikings have a scheduled off day Monday to reset the competition if they desire. Murray entered training camp as the favorite for the job, and sources say they believe he still is. Asked Sunday where Murray is in the offensive system compared to where he thought he would be at this point, O'Connell said: "I think mentally he's definitely probably ahead of where I thought." O'Connell went on to say there are some parts of the offense that are new to everyone.

 
 It was a rough practice for the offense as defensive pressure made it difficult for quarterbacks Kyler Murray or J.J. McCarthy to get into a rhythm. Murray threw two interceptions, to cornerbacks James Pierre and Isaiah Rodgers , the latter when he was scrambling and tried to get the ball to Justin Jefferson on the sideline. McCarthy continued his theme of hitting deep out routes, including another to receiver Myles Price . McCarthy completed a deep pass to Jefferson down the right sideline but it forced Jefferson to slow down to bring it in, and he struggled later in a red zone drill. 
 Part of the protection issue was caused by the absence of left tackle Christian Darrisaw , who took a veteran's rest day. The Vikings also rested rookie defensive lineman Caleb Banks , who remains on a maintenance plan to ensure full recovery from a broken left foot. 
 Defensive linemen Levi Drake Rodriguez and Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins also sat out the practice, giving rookie nose tackle Domonique Orange extensive first-team action. 
 Safety Jay Ward is in the latter stages of the concussion protocol, O'Connell said. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 Two members of the Vikings' draft class -- both Day 3 picks -- made splash plays during a low-key practice.

 Rookie tailback Demond Claiborne ran about 70 yards off left tackle using a nifty jump cut to get outside. Claiborne, a sixth-round pick from Wake Forest, has mostly worked with the third team behind Aaron Jones Sr . and Jordan Mason . He could also get some work as a kick returner during the preseason.

 Meanwhile, cornerback Charles Demmings -- a fifth-round pick from Stephen F. Austin -- broke up a J.J. McCarthy pass intended for receiver Tai Felton near the goal line. For Demmings, it was the latest in a series of pass breakups, including two earlier in camp while he was defending Justin Jefferson . The Vikings seem to have their top three cornerbacks set with Byron Murphy Jr ., Isaiah Rodgers and James Pierre , and it is always dangerous to get too excited when a rookie makes splash plays. But to this point, he has demonstrated he could provide an immediate contribution this season should defensive coordinator Brian Flores need him. 

 Other observations: 

 
 Veteran Jamal Adams said he appreciates the Vikings giving him a chance to work at safety, the position the New York Jets drafted him as in 2017, and that his new number of 32 is "definitely a better feeling" than the number he opened camp with (54). But Adams agreed it was likely he will also resume his linebacker duties at times in Flores' scheme. "I think it's going to be a little bit of everything, just being versatile in a lot of ways," he said. 
 Adams continued to get first-team work at safety in some packages with fellow safeties Jay Ward and Jakobe Thomas sitting out team drills. 
 Right tackle Brian O'Neill appeared to be taking a veteran's rest day. 
 Receiver Jordan Addison (left thumb) caught passes from quarterbacks for the first time since he suffered the injury while working in some team drills. 
 The Vikings will have their annual night practice Sunday at TCO Stadium. 
 

 

 
 Friday, Aug. 7 
 NFL training camps can be tediously routine at times, but some days close observers can be surprised.

 The Vikings changed linebacker Jamal Adams ' jersey number from 54 to 32 and worked him in some of their safety specialty packages during full-team drills. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores…

title: 2026 New England Patriots training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Patriots training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The New England Patriots ' camp is taking place in Foxborough, Massachusetts, and Patriots reporter Mike Reiss has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Patriots camp. We will update this file often. Will Drake Maye  start another MVP-like campaign in Year 3? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Patriots camp 
 
 Patriots TE Hunter Henry signs extension worth up to $20M 
 Has Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez found his voice? 
 A.J. Brown on injury: 'Thumb out of place, you keep going' 
 Patriots' Brown knows Vrabel's rip comes from 'great place' 
 Kraft: Patriots' Gonzalez has offer to be 'highest-paid' CB ever 
 Too many receivers? A look at the Patriots' crowded WR room 
 
 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 
 The Patriots' had an official ribbon-cutting ceremony for their new 160,000-square-foot New Balance Athletics Center on Wednesday, with owner Robert Kraft and coach Mike Vrabel among those sharing remarks before VP of football operations and strategy John Streicher led a behind-the-scenes tour.

 "There's not a better place to teach and prepare our players," Vrabel said.

 The facility includes a 15,000-square-foot weight room; 11,000 square feet of dining and kitchen space; a 10,500-square-foot virtual reality room; 3,700 square feet dedicated to hydrotherapy; and a state of the art draft room.

 The 160,000 square feet is more than double the amount the team previously occupied at Gillette Stadium.

 On one notable part of the tour, Streicher stopped at QB Drake Maye 's locker and explained the thought that went in to selecting the details of each locker -- which includes two separate areas to dry shoulder pads/helmets and cleats.

 Maye's locker is directly next to WR A.J. Brown 's, and across from CB Christian Gonzalez 's, with whom he has regularly engaged in back-and-forth locker room banter in recent years.

 

 More: 

 
 The Patriots waived undrafted rookie RB Myles Montgomery with an injury designation Wednesday and signed RB Hassan Haskins , a 2022 fourth-round draft pick of the Titans. The Patriots host the Colts in the preseason opener Thursday, and with top-of-the-depth-chart RBs Rhamondre Stevenson , TreVeyon Henderson and Terrell Jennings not expected to play, Haskins could get carries right away after Lan Larison and rookie Jam Miller . 
 

 

 

 
 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Quarterback Drake Maye isn't expected to play in Thursday's preseason opener against the Colts, coach Mike Vrabel said Tuesday.

 "That's where my mindset is right now, standing here today," Vrabel said before Tuesday's joint practice with the Colts in Foxborough. "That can always change, but I wouldn't anticipate that happening right now."

 Vrabel noted that Tuesday's practice essentially takes the place of the game for Maye & Co.

 "That's really the only reason that we do these joint practices. It will be a lot of the front-line players and whoever's available [in the practice]. Some of the guys that maybe will not get as much work will get extensive work in the game on Thursday," he said.

 The plan for practice was to have the offense take 24 full-team reps, which Vrabel pointed out was more than Maye & Co. would likely see in a preseason game.

 Maye's final rep in practice wasn't to his liking, as he threw an end zone interception to Colts safety Cam Bynum on a second-down play in the two-minute drill. Otherwise, he was pleased with the Patriots' effort, energy and execution.

 "We challenged our guys to be consistent throughout the day, and I think they responded to that," Maye said.

 More observations: 

 
 Starting CB Christian Gonzalez missed his first practice of training camp. It might have been related to his final play of Monday's practice, when he landed hard in the end zone while defending WR Romeo Doubs . Gonzalez has also been in negotiations with the team on a contract extension. 
 With Gonzalez and fellow starting CB Carlton Davis III not practicing, and top backup Charles Woods also out, any evaluation of the pass defense came with a caveat. The Colts were without two top WRs, however. 
 The Colts' first units on offense/defense won the end-of-practice two-minute drill, while the Patriots' second units were victorious -- QB Tommy DeVito connecting with WR Mack Hollins on a long TD and S John Saunders Jr . notching an INT. 
 DeVito had another deep ball earlier in practice as speedy WR Kyle Williams got behind the defense and tracked the ball well. 
 With the Patriots' first-unit offense on one field and the first-unit defense on the other, Vrabel stayed with the offense. That left assistant head coach Terrell Williams and coordinator Zak Kuhr to lead the defensive field. 
 WR A.J. Brown had an active practice, with Maye looking in his direction often. He was charted with five receptions. 
 Starting LB Christian Elliss limped off early in practice. 
 RB Rhamondre Stevenson as a reliable pass catcher in the red zone has been a theme in recent days. He had another TD catch from Maye that had the crowd buzzing. 
 Colts DT Grover Stewart powered into LG Alijah Vera-Tucker on one play and got his hands up to bat down a pass. 
 OLB Elijah Ponder had the Patriots' most decisive PBU, getting his hands up at the line to swat away a pass from QB Daniel Jones . 
 Owners Robert Kraft (Patriots) and Carly Irsay-Gordon (Colts) watched practice together at one point. 
 Former Patriots safety Devin McCourty was in attendance to sign autographs. 
 

 

 
 Monday, Aug. 10 
 First-round draft pick Caleb Lomu has been a full participant in all 13 training camp practices, and he shared insight Monday on the top thing he has learned.

 "The biggest thing is really focusing on not so many things. On defense, these guys are coming off the ball, they know their assignment, and everyone on the field has to know what they're doing. If you're thinking about multiple things, and if you hesitate at all for a quick second, the guy on the other side of the line is going to beat you.

 "Coming out here, at first I was thinking a lot and that caused me to play a little slower. I realized you can't think too much. You have to trust in what you learned in the classroom and go out and play ball."

 The 28th pick, Lomu had mostly been working at right tackle until the team's 12th practice last Friday, which was an intrasquad scrimmage. He flipped more to the left side that day, and that continued Monday in a practice held in shorts and light shoulder pads, as he was the backup left tackle behind Will Campbell .

 Lomu played left tackle at Utah, so he noted changing sides has been an adjustment with the different footwork and hand placement, among other things. But he said he feels comfortable on both sides.

 He shared that his primary focus at practice Monday was playing with "tight hands" and not giving up his chest to pass rushers. He appeared to have one of his better days in drills.

 More observations: 

 
 WR Romeo Doubs caught a leaping TD from QB Drake Maye to cap off a "game-ending" drive despite being blanketed by CB Christian Gonzalez . Doubs crashed to the ground, and fellow WRs Efton Chism III and Kayshon Boutte gave him a mock-CPR celebration by pumping his chest. 
 Chism showed strong hands at the catch point, leaping over CB Marcellas Dial Jr . to catch a TD pass from QB Tommy DeVito to produce another offensive highlight. 
 CB Kindle Vildor had one of the top defensive plays of the day,…

summary: Follow our daily updates from Saints training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  New Orleans Saints ' camp is taking place in Metairie, Louisiana, and Saints reporter Katherine Terrell has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Saints camp. We will update this file often. Kellen Moore enters his second season as head coach, and expectations are higher after  Tyler Shough  impressed while starting the final nine games of the 2025 campaign. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Saints news 
 
 Drew Brees' greatness, as seen through eyes of teammates, coaches 
 Saints place WR Ja'Lynn Polk, 24, on reserve/retired list 
 Saints starting DT Bryan Bresee to have season-ending ACL surgery 
 The legacy of Taysom Hill in New Orleans: 'There's only one' 
 WR Chris Olave signing four-year extension 
 
 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 
 The Saints took a step back in anticipation of Thursday's joint practice session against the Jacksonville Jaguars . The Saints will practice against three different teams over the course of camp, and tomorrow's practice will essentially function as their preseason game. The starters won't play in Saturday's game, but they will get extensive time against the Jaguars' first-team tomorrow. The Saints had a short, non-padded inside practice to get ready for that.

 They still ran some 11-on-11 drills with a few highlights -- Isaac Yiadom broke up a Spencer Rattler pass to Bryce Lance , continuing to work through the play until the ball came out. Some teammates rushed over to celebrate the play. In the next team session, Lance caught a touchdown from Rattler in the end zone, making the catch over Jordan Howden and Elliott Davison before spiking the ball in celebration. They'll be back in pads tomorrow against Jacksonville.

 More observations: 

 
 There were multiple bad snaps among all their units, including a high snap from Erik McCoy to Tyler Shough . That comes a day after the offense had several penalties. Moore said the team is a work in progress. "We need to play more consistent football. We have to get there and that's what this time of the year is about," Moore said. 
 The Saints ended practice with red zone work, scoring a touchdown off a handoff to  Travis Etienne Jr . up the middle. Shough's two passes in the four-play session were incomplete, including an attempt to Juwan Johnson on the run with pressure from Chase Young . 
 The Saints experimented with multiple combinations, including an offensive line shuffle ( Cesar Ruiz got a few snaps at center again) and also moving Jonas Sanker around the field, while cornerback Jayden Price got some first-team reps. Moore said Price's consistency has been impressive and he earned more opportunities because of it. 
 The Saints brought former Lions CB Terrion Arnold in for a visit and said they're still gathering information on him. Arnold was released by the Lions after he was arrested on felony charges of armed robbery and kidnapping. His case is still ongoing. 
 Devaughn Vele got a rest day while Davon Godchaux was a new absence after rolling an ankle on Tuesday.  Cameron Jordan  remained absent with a hamstring injury. 
 The Saints did not attempt field goal kicks during their practice session Wednesday. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Offense and defense went at each other in an unscripted red zone scenario to end practice. The first side to 18 points won, with four points given to the defense if they held the offense to a field goal, three points to the offense for a made field goal, and seven points for a touchdown or turnover.

 The defense went up 4-3 after Charlie Smyth kicked a field goal for the first unit. Tanner Brown kicked a field goal for the second team after after  Martin Emerson Jr . broke up a Spencer Rattler pass on third down. With the defense up 8-6, Carl Granderson almost picked off Tyler Shough and then did manage to snag the ball three plays later, before punting it in celebration. That put the defense up 13-6, and Zach Wilson took advantage of an offsides penalty to throw a touchdown to Barion Brown to tie things up.

 The first-team offense took over with a chance to win outright, but Quincy Riley picked off Shough in the end zone, giving the defense the win. Coach Kellen Moore said the idea was to create a competitive environment. "It's just play ball and defense has the opportunity to score and obviously they won the day in the red zone," he said.

 Other observations:  

 
 The Saints first-team offense had multiple false starts during team periods. 
 Shough threw a touchdown to Juwan Johnson with Kool-Aid McKinstry in coverage during an early team period. 
 The two kickers had previously alternated practices, now they'll alternate kicks during practice moving forward. Brown went 7-of-7 and Smyth went 5-of-6. 
 Devin Neal worked off to the side with an athletic trainer. Rejzohn Wright left with a hip injury, Davon Godchaux left with an ankle injury.  
 Jeremiah Wright returned to practice, while  Cameron Jordan  did not practice with a hamstring injury. Kendre Miller ,  Chris Rumph II and John Ridgeway III  did not practice. 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 
 

 Sunday's practice featured the most 11-on-11 work yet, and it was an up-and-down day for the first-team offense.

 Quarterback Tyler Shough got off to a quick start with completions to Chris Olave , Devaughn Vele and Jordyn Tyson in his first session. He was able to roll out and find Olave after an incompletion to Juwan Johnson . Later, Shough had three straight completions to Johnson, Olave and Tyson after a miss to Olave, but the offense was flagged for a false start, and then Shough was sacked on the next play. Shough targeted Olave downfield on the next session but couldn't connect and then was sacked before a completion to Travis Etienne Jr . His next period had completions to Etienne and Olave before he ran it himself for a first down. The unit finished the day working specifically on third down, and Shough had a completion to Noah Fant , incompletions to Vele and Barion Brown (with good coverage by Kool-Aid McKinstry ), and a completion to Tyson.

 Other observations:  

 
 Cesar Ruiz was back at starting right guard after playing second-team center Saturday. 
 Reserve guard Dillon Radunz is done for the season with a torn ACL. 
 Defensive end Cameron Jordan has a hamstring issue that could cause him to miss time in training camp. He was not at practice Sunday. 
 Kicker Charlie Smyth had his second straight three-miss day. After missing three kicks in a row during his last practice session Thursday, he went 4-of-7, missing from 47 and 56 yards and then missing a 50-yard field goal in the two-minute drill. 
 Alvin Kamara and Zach Wood were back at practice after attending Drew Brees' Hall of Fame ceremony (Jordan attended as well). 
 Rookie Bryce Lance had the play of the day, scoring a touchdown after a deep pass by Spencer Rattler . Running back CJ Donaldson had an impressive run with the third-team offense. 
 Quarterback Zach Wilson threw a deep touchdown to Ronnie Bell with the third-team offense. 
 John Ridgeway III  and Pete Werner left early with injuries. 
 Olave and Julian Blackmon practiced after both dealt with injuries in Saturday's practice. 
 Devin Neal , Kendre Miller , Christen Miller , Jeremiah Wright , Rejzohn Wright , Bub Means (personal) didn't practice.

title: 2026 New York Giants training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Giants training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The New York Giants' camp is taking place at The Greenbrier in White Sulphur Springs, West Virginia, and Giants reporter Jordan Raanan has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Giants camp. We will update this file often. How will the Giants handle increased expectations and a new coach? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Thursday.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Giants camp 
 
 Cam Skattebo admits doing 'dumb things,' will save backflips for TDs 
 Nabers 'looked good' in 1st practice since knee injury 
 Giants have spoken with Skattebo after Fanatics Fest flip 
 2026 New York Giants training camp preview 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 The kicking competition continues: Ben Sauls went 5-of-6 on field goal attempts in Wednesday's practice. Rookie Dominic Zvada went 7-of-7, including a 61-yarder to end practice.

 Overall in camp, Zvada is now 48-of-51 on kicks. Sauls is 41-of-48.

 "They're both having really good camps," coach John Harbaugh said.

 Running back Cam Skattebo and tight end Isaiah Likely peer-pressured Harbaugh into having Zvada attempt the 61-yard kick after the offense repeatedly sputtered in end-of-game situations. There were 10 seconds remaining on the clock and Harbaugh had the offense out on the field ready to run a play from the 44-yard line.

 He reconsidered. Zvada drilled the kick with plenty of room to spare (it clanked off the back fence) as the offense went wild.

 At this point, it seems a fait accompli that the Giants will carry a kicker with little to no experience come Week 1.

 Other observations:  

 
 Odell Beckham Jr . caught a pair of passes in live drills after a couple of quiet days. Harbaugh said Beckham will play in Saturday's preseason opener against the Vikings. 
 Harbaugh took the high road on whether QB Jaxson Dart will play. He decided to intentionally "dodge" that question. 
 Backup cornerback Art Green had a really strong practice. He knocked down a handful of passes. It comes at a time when the Giants are looking for someone to step up at cornerback. 
 CBs Dru Phillips (knee), Greg Newsome II (knee) and Paulson Adebo worked on the side at Wednesday's practice. Harbaugh said Adebo was "day to day." 
 G Francis Mauigoa was a full participant after being limited Tuesday. 
 WRs Juju Smith-Schuster (knee) and Jalin Hyatt (leg), C John Michael Schmitz Jr. (concussion), C/G Lucas Patrick (knee) and DB DJ James did not practice. 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 It was another rough afternoon for the Giants' offense. The unit sputtered and failed to hit any downfield throws during a practice without full pads.

 During one red zone drill, quarterback Jaxson Dart threw touchdown passes to Theo Johnson and Malachi Fields on two of the first three plays. He followed with five straight incompletions, including an interception at the goal line by Arvell Reese .

 These are the learning curves with a new offense.

 "[Tuesday] was an average practice, maybe below average," offensive coordinator Matt Nagy said. "It wasn't good enough. [Dart] knows that, we know that. We'll put it on tape, but we also talk about success through struggles and ... there's going to be some struggles as we go through this now in training camp and during the season. But how do we react?"

 The season starts in just over a month. The Giants are combining the offenses of Nagy, quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman. They're putting as much as possible on tape and plan to pare it down to accommodate the talent.

 The clock is ticking.

 Other observations: 

 
 Reese's interception included a circus catch. He dropped into coverage, sprinted to the flat and put an arm in the air. The ball hit off the back of Reese's hand, and he tipped it to himself for the interception at the goal line. It was the latest highlight for the No. 5 pick. "He's been impressive," defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson said. 
 CB Paulson Adebo and WR Jalin Hyatt missed practice. That left three of the Giants' top cornerbacks (Adebo,  Greg Newsome II  and Dru Phillips ) on the sideline. Big opportunity for rookie Colton Hood and Deonte Banks . 
 Outside linebacker Abdul Carter (hand) returned to practice after sitting out Monday. Rookie guard Francis Mauigoa  participated only in individual drills after getting banged up Monday. 
 Second-year tight end  Thomas Fidone II  is catching everything these days. He had another highlight-reel diving catch deep down the middle of the field from Jameis Winston . He later added two more catches during live drills, including a touchdown in the red zone. It's going to be hard for the Giants to leave Fidone off the roster. 
 
 

 Aug. 10 
 The Giants' biggest problem last season was their run defense. It was close to historically bad while allowing 5.3 yards per carry.

 It's hard to succeed that way. New coach John Harbaugh is well aware. He and defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson have made it a priority to stop the run this season.

 So far, so good. Veteran nose tackle  DJ Reader  has been a force in the middle throughout training camp. First-round pick Arvell Reese 's physical approach has been a major asset. That was again the case in live drills during Monday's practice, which was the latest reminder that the Giants appear to have made serious gains on this front.

 "It's just technique and mentality," outside linebacker Brian Burns said. "We just really put an emphasis on being in our gap but also having ... a mean mentality when it comes to the run. We've got some goals that we want to reach this year."

 More observations: 

 
 OLB Abdul Carter missed practice because of a hand injury. Harbaugh did not think it was serious. 
 CB  Greg Newsome II  (knee), CB Dru Phillips (knee), WR  JuJu Smith-Schuster  (knee), C John Michael Schmitz Jr. (concussion) and G/C Lucas Patrick (knee) also missed practice. OLB Chauncey Golston left practice because of a neck/head injury. 
 Giants kickers made all 13 of their field goal and extra point attempts. Ben Sauls was 7-of-7, and  Dominic Zvada was 6-of-6. Both have had nice camps. 
 

 

 
 Aug. 8 

 The Giants finished their 12 days in West Virginia with another physical practice filled with goal-line and run-game work. It was a typical John Harbaugh workout. No easy days.

 Harbaugh thinks it's going to make a difference for a team that won seven games combined the past two seasons.

 "Well, I think we got a lot better. That's probably what we got out of it. We improved tremendously," Harbaugh said. "We're much further along than we were when we started. I think we can look back and say that we've come a long way."

 The trip helped with team building and camaraderie.

 "I would give it an A, A-plus for that. It's been really everything," Harbaugh said. "We've been able to focus on the task at hand. There's really no distractions out here. It's a beautiful setting. It's a beautiful resort. Everything has been excellent. And the guys have been able to lock in on the football. The fields have held up extremely well. I mean, every little thing has been good. It's not lavish by any stretch in terms of the facility, but it's everything we could want. Maybe that's even better."

 

 Other observations: 

 
 RB Cam Skattebo returned to practice after stretching out his leg the previous day. He participated in all 10 practices in West Virginia as he returns from a fractured ankle last year. 
 Defensive lineman Darius…

title: 2026 New York Jets training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Jets training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  New York Jets  camp is taking place at the Atlantic Health Training Facility in Florham Park, New Jersey, and Jets reporter Rich Cimini has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Jets camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Thursday.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Jets camp 
 
 Jets CB Stiggers taken to hospital after collapsing at practice 
 No. 2 pick Bailey living up to hype, bringing 'juice' to Jets 
 Rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq to miss time after hernia setback 
 Jets' Smith rues being 'distraction' after dispute with girlfriend 
 2026 Jets training camp preview 
 
 
 Wednesday, Aug. 12 
 Baker Mayfield beat the Jets with a two-minute drill last season in Week 3, setting up a game-winning field goal for the Buccaneers as time expired, and he did it again on Wednesday in the second of two joint practices.

 The Bucs' QB burned the Jets with three straight completions, hitting Dennis Houston with a short TD pass with three seconds left in a two-minute drill.

 "Baker does a really good job in that situation, and I wanted to see exactly how our guys operated in that situation," said Jets coach Aaron Glenn, adding that he could've helped the players with better defensive calls.

 It was another uneven day for the Jets, who had some hiccups in their own two-minute drive -- a drop by RB Braelon Allen , a holding call on RT Armand Membou and a false start. QB Geno Smith completed only two of seven passes on the drive, which ended with a missed field goal (61 yards) by Jason Sanders .

 "I felt like we could've made a few more plays," Smith said.

 The same could be said of the entire two-day experience. The Bucs, a playoff team in three of Todd Bowles' four seasons as coach, proved themselves the superior team.

 Silver lining for the Jets: This was a learning experience, a not-so-subtle reminder they still have a lot of work to do. Their young players got quality work, which should benefit them in the long run.

 More observations: 

 
 CB Qwan'tez Stiggers , who passed out during Tuesday's practice and was taken to a hospital, is in concussion protocol. Glenn said Swiggers experienced "symptoms" on Tuesday, but didn't elaborate except to say "something must have happened." Before collapsing and briefly losing consciousness, he was involved in a fight with some Tampa Bay players. He lost his helmet in the skirmish (it was flung by Bucs RT Luke Goedeke ). Stiggers was released from the hospital on Tuesday night. 
 Edge rusher Joseph Ossai , removed from the PUP list, is expected to start practicing next week. Rookie CB D'Angelo Ponds (calf), who hasn't practiced at all, also could return, although that seems less certain. Ponds' hopes of landing a starting job for Week 1 are fading by the day. 
 The two teams didn't fight as much as they did on Tuesday. This time, there were only a couple of scuffles. WR Tim Patrick and LG Dylan Parham were involved in "dust ups," as Glenn likes to call them. 
 Free agent CB Terrion Arnold visited the Giants on Wednesday, but there was no meeting with the Jets, a source said. They inquired about Arnold when he was released by the Detroit Lions , but their interest -- if there was any interest beyond due diligence -- appears to have cooled. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Quarterback Geno Smith and the rest of the starters will play Friday night against the Buccaneers in the preseason opener, coach Aaron Glenn announced Tuesday.

 They can use the work.

 The first-team offense struggled in Tuesday's joint practice with the Bucs, as Smith was intercepted twice (one returned for a touchdown). The offense, learning new coordinator Frank Reich's system, is trending downward after an encouraging start to camp.

 The Jets were out of sync and allowed the Bucs to control the line of scrimmage, with running back  Breece Hall saying, "They beat us up a little today." And, no, he wasn't alluding to the four fights that marred practice.

 There was a spark in a red zone period late in practice, with Smith throwing touchdowns to tight end  Mason Taylor and wide receiver  Garrett Wilson (on a deflection). But it's clear the starting unit -- hardly devoid of talent -- has a way to go. Smith finished 10-for-16 in 11 on 11 periods.

 Glenn said the starters will play about 25 to 30 snaps in the preseason, though he's not sure how that will be divided over the three games. The Jets are installing new offensive and defensive systems. That's one of the reasons why Glenn wants to play his starters.

 Another reason: While many coaches prefer to be cautious, concerned about injuries, Glenn believes the best way to prep for the regular season is to actually play in the preseason.

 "Everybody's playing," he said.

 This isn't a new philosophy. A year ago, starting QB Justin Fields played 28 snaps in the preseason.

 

 More observations: 

 
 If you had to pick a "winner" in the joint practice, it would be the Bucs, who brought more energy and physicality at the outset. The two teams will do it again Wednesday. 
 WR Isaiah Williams , one of the stars of camp, has played his way into a bigger role. Before camp, he was viewed as a return specialist and No. 4 receiver, but that isn't the case anymore. Williams, who made three receptions in the joint practice, could leapfrog first-round pick Omar Cooper Jr ., who has experienced "little pitfalls," receivers coach Shawn Jefferson said. "That's part of being a rookie." 
 Wilson made one of the best plays of the day, catching the tipped pass in the red zone and evading what seemed like half of Tampa Bay's defense to find the end zone. 
 Rookie David Bailey had another impressive day as a pass rusher, making at least one sack and multiple QB pressures. He still needs work against the run, though. 
 Dane Belton , who had a pass breakup, may have the best ball production of any safety in camp. Glenn called him a "ball magnet." He's definitely pushing Andre Cisco for the starting job opposite Minkah Fitzpatrick . 
 Remember last year, when we made a big deal out of "live" tackling in training camp because it's uncommon in the NFL? Well, there won't be live tackling this summer. Glenn said he now prefers "thud" -- when defenders wrap up ball carriers but don't bring them to the ground. Glenn said "thud" promotes better technique and reduces injury. 
 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 The Jets ended the first phase of training camp with a controlled instrasquad scrimmage.

 There was a scary moment near the end, when prized rookie edge rusher David Bailey walked off gingerly, favoring his left ankle.

 Afterward, coach Aaron Glenn confirmed it was an ankle injury, adding that Bailey likely will be listed as day-to-day. He was able to jog back to the sideline after being examined in the medical tent.

 Bailey, drafted No. 2 overall, continued his strong camp, recording one sack and at least two pressures, unofficially. He probably should've had another sack, but the officials let the play continue.

 This was one of those good news-bad news days. Glenn's new-look defense looked terrific, while the offense struggled, especially in the red zone.

 There were plenty of self-inflicted mistakes. QB Geno Smith started hot, leading a 65-yard touchdown drive and completing his first five passes, but the starting offense unraveled after that. There were five penalties and two sacks.

 Penalties were a bugaboo last season. Glenn noted that most of the…

title: 2026 Seattle Seahawks training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Seahawks training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Seattle Seahawks ' camp is taking place in Renton, Washington, and Seahawks reporter Brady Henderson has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Seahawks camp. We will update this file often. What is new with the defending Super Bowl champions? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Thursday.

 
 Camp previews for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Seahawks camp 
 
 WR Tory Horton healthy after cracking tibia last season 
 Seattle Pro Bowl DL Williams confirms deal talks 
 Seattle's Nick Emmanwori has ankle surgery, expected to play W1 
 Who are the Khoslas? Meet the family set to buy the Seahawks 
 
 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 There was nothing noteworthy to come from the Seahawks' 16th practice of training camp, with players wearing shorts and T-shirts during a 55-minute walk-through. But there was a development with  Terrion Arnold . 
 
After working out for the Seahawks on Sunday, then visiting the New Orleans Saints on Tuesday, the second-year cornerback continued his free agent tour by meeting with the New York Giants  on Wednesday. If the Seahawks are going to truly pursue Arnold, who is facing eight felony charges in Florida in connection with a kidnapping and robbery in early February, then it sounds like they'll have competition. 
 
Coach Mike Macdonald's comments on Arnold earlier this week made it clear that Seattle's interest is much more than simply the team's usual due diligence. That was reinforced on the second episode of "Hard Knocks," which showed general manager John Schneider eagerly relaying to Macdonald what Seahawks quarterback Jalen Milroe told him about Arnold while vouching for his college teammate. 
 
In another clip, Schneider was shown asking another front office member about instances of an NFL team acquiring a player with an outstanding legal case, as if trying to gauge the potential blowback. 
 
There are other questions the Seahawks likely have to ponder: 
 
When might Arnold be available should he land on the NFL commissioner's exempt list? How might the team's soon-to-be owners feel about a controversial signing if it were to happen before they'd be in position to sign off on it? And would Arnold fit into the tight-knit culture that has been part of the reigning Super Bowl champions' secret sauce? 
 
Defensive tackle Leonard Williams was asked about the possibility of adding a player with off-the-field issues to Seattle's locker room. 
 
"We have such a culture and way about ourselves here that if you don't fall in line with the way our team is, you're just going to get steamrolled and not fit in, to be honest," Williams said. "I think guys instantly come into this building and they see that we stand out in different ways in terms of the way we practice, the way we communicate, the way we show respect and want to get better. If you're not following all of our principles and guidelines, you're going to stand out really easily. You're either just going to fall in line or not end up here."

 Other observations:

 
 The Seahawks have a full-length practice Thursday and a shorter one Friday before their preseason opener Saturday against the Dallas Cowboys at Lumen Field. 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 Good news came on the injury front on Tuesday via safety Nick Emmanwori passing his physical, a significant step in his return from July ankle surgery.

 Then came bad news, with the team announcing that second-year fullback Robbie Ouzts will go on injured reserve, ending his season because of the neck issue that kept him out of the NFC Championship Game and Super Bowl.

 It's no small thing given new coordinator Brian Fleury's stated desire to run a good chunk of his offense with two backs on the field at the same time. Fleury came from the San Francisco 49ers , who ran an NFL-high 491 plays last season out of two-back formations, according to ESPN Research. Since 2022, coach Kyle Shanahan's offense leads the league in snaps with two backs.

 "I like using two backs because it can change the formation strength after the snap as opposed to the whole defense being able to identify it before the snap," Fleury said last week. "It creates some fit problems. It's becoming less and less common across the league, so it's more difficult to prepare for. Those are the elements I like about it. I'm more of an old-school traditionalist because of my upbringing in football and so I'm always going to want to play with two backs at some point. I like the guys we have in that role right now."

 At that point, it wasn't known yet that Ouzts would have to miss the season. Brady Russell , a converted tight end, is the Seahawks' next man up at fullback. They also signed Brock Lampe last week.

 General manager John Schneider has a long history of late-summer additions, so the Seahawks could potentially find their replacement for Ouzts via a trade or waiver claim. Or, as Fleury said, they could find creative ways to get a second back on the field.

 "It doesn't have to be a traditional fullback," Fleury said last week. "We've found ways to use receivers in lead blocking roles, other tight ends, even other running backs. We'll find a way to get it done."

 More observations: 

 
 Rookie RB Jadarian Price missed his fourth straight practice. Coach Mike Macdonald has described his issue as lower-body soreness and said Seattle's first-round pick should be back in a matter of days. 
 Tuesday's practice again got contentious. During an 11-on-11 period, S Ty Okada hit WR Tory Horton on a screen pass. Horton took exception, pushing Okada. G Christian Haynes came to Horton's defense and ended up going to the ground with Okada. There were no flare-ups after that, and Okada was laughing about the altercation with fellow defensive backs on the sideline moments later. 
 Okada came down with an interception when CB Josh Jobe deflected a QB  Sam Darnold pass to WR Cooper Kupp near the goal line. 
 

 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 The Seahawks might have more NFL-caliber safeties than they'll be able to keep, and the players who are vying for roster spots have been making plays.

 AJ Finley and Rodney Thomas II both had interceptions during Seattle's annual practice at Lumen Field on Saturday. D'Anthony Bell got in on the action Monday as the team returned to work following an off day.

 In an 11-on-11 period, No. 3 quarterback Jalen Milroe was trying to hit tight end Elijah Arroyo on an out route when Bell jumped in front of the throw and intercepted it in stride for what might have been a pick-six in an actual game.

 "It was great to see him make a play today," coach Mike Macdonald said. "He's doing a good job. There's a lot of competition for the job that he's trying to earn himself, so it's a process. One day at a time, but D-Bell is doing a good job."

 Ty Okada still looks like the heavy favorite to replace free agent departure Coby Bryant in the starting lineup opposite Julian Love . Rookie Bud Clark is a lock to make the team after Seattle drafted him No. 64. The Seahawks were optimistic immediately after Nick Emmanwori had ankle surgery in July that he'd be back in time for Week 1, so it would take an unforeseen issue with his recovery to keep him off the 53-player roster to begin the season.

 Working in Bell's favor is the fact that he has been the primary backup to Emmanwori as the third safety in big nickel packages. He's also a strong special teams player. Bell blocked a punt last season and played the fourth-most special teams snaps…
